The training and validation .csv files share no common genes — Ciclops fails silently, producing ./training splits with only sample-name and label columns and missing gene expression columns SHAP analysis is the goal with regression models (gpr, lr) — SHAP is only implemented for LightGBM, XGBoost, and Random Forest You need a guaranteed-default hyperparameter configuration — hyperparameters are not fixed and must be tuned by the user for a better fit http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Run Ciclops' 10-fold cross-validation on a training transcriptome dataset (e.g., GSE151189 RNA-seq) and evaluate the trained models on an external cross-platform test set (e.g., GSE59098 microarray), collecting per-fold and bootstrapped 95% CI performance metrics from ./performance/. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101583
skills.summary: Run Ciclops' 10-fold cross-validation on a training transcriptome dataset (e.g., GSE151189 RNA-seq) and evaluate the trained models on an external cross-platform test set (e.g., GSE59098 microarray), collecting per-fold and bootstrapped 95% CI performance metrics from ./performance/.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The training and validation .csv files share no common genes — Ciclops fails silently, producing ./training splits with only sample-name and label columns and missing gene expression columns SHAP analysis is the goal with regression models (gpr, lr) — SHAP is only implemented for LightGBM, XGBoost, and Random Forest You need a guaranteed-default hyperparameter configuration — hyperparameters are not fixed and must be tuned by the user for a better fit

skills.description: Use when multiple PC-regression-derived scGRNs have been built from random cell subsamples (e.g., 10 networks x 500 cells) and edge-weight noise must be smoothed before downstream comparison or recall evaluation.
skills.name: tensor-decomposition-network-denoising
skills.search_text: tensor-decomposition-network-denoising Use when multiple PC-regression-derived scGRNs have been built from random cell subsamples (e.g., 10 networks x 500 cells) and edge-weight noise must be smoothed before downstream comparison or recall evaluation. Input is a single, already-denoised GRN with no replicate/subsampled layers to smooth across The goal is comparing highly dissimilar samples, since scTenifoldNet (including its denoising step) is designed for 'comparing highly similar samples, such as two populations of cells of the same type' Input is normalized or QC-processed expression data rather than the raw counts matrix expected by the scTenifoldNet pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Denoises multilayer single-cell gene regulatory networks (scGRNs) built by PC regression from subsampled scRNA-seq data using CANDECOMP/PARAFAC (CP) low-rank tensor decomposition, then recovers regulatory relationships with ~25% higher recall than the individual noisy networks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100139
skills.summary: Denoises multilayer single-cell gene regulatory networks (scGRNs) built by PC regression from subsampled scRNA-seq data using CANDECOMP/PARAFAC (CP) low-rank tensor decomposition, then recovers regulatory relationships with ~25% higher recall than the individual noisy networks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single, already-denoised GRN with no replicate/subsampled layers to smooth across The goal is comparing highly dissimilar samples, since scTenifoldNet (including its denoising step) is designed for 'comparing highly similar samples, such as two populations of cells of the same type' Input is normalized or QC-processed expression data rather than the raw counts matrix expected by the scTenifoldNet pipeline

skills.description: Use when you have constructed multiple candidate scGRNs per condition (e.g., 10 networks from 500-cell subsamples via pcNet/makeNetworks) and need a single denoised network per condition before aligning conditions or testing differential regulation.
skills.name: tensor-denoising-of-multilayer-networks
skills.search_text: tensor-denoising-of-multilayer-networks Use when you have constructed multiple candidate scGRNs per condition (e.g., 10 networks from 500-cell subsamples via pcNet/makeNetworks) and need a single denoised network per condition before aligning conditions or testing differential regulation. You have only a single pre-built GRN per condition (no multilayer/subsampled network stack) — the CP tensor approximation requires a tensor of multiple network layers to denoise You want to compare highly dissimilar samples rather than two populations of cells of the same type; scTenifoldNet as a whole is designed for highly similar samples Input is still raw single-cell count data — QC (scQC) and normalization (cpmNormalization) and network construction (makeNetworks) must precede tensor denoising http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Denoises the multilayer set of single-cell gene regulatory networks (scGRNs) built from subsampled cells using CANDECOMP/PARAFAC (CP) low-rank tensor decomposition, which smooths edge weights across networks so downstream manifold alignment and differential regulation testing operate on a single robust network per condition. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100139
skills.summary: Denoises the multilayer set of single-cell gene regulatory networks (scGRNs) built from subsampled cells using CANDECOMP/PARAFAC (CP) low-rank tensor decomposition, which smooths edge weights across networks so downstream manifold alignment and differential regulation testing operate on a single robust network per condition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a single pre-built GRN per condition (no multilayer/subsampled network stack) — the CP tensor approximation requires a tensor of multiple network layers to denoise You want to compare highly dissimilar samples rather than two populations of cells of the same type; scTenifoldNet as a whole is designed for highly similar samples Input is still raw single-cell count data — QC (scQC) and normalization (cpmNormalization) and network construction (makeNetworks) must precede tensor denoising

skills.description: Use when a trained Keras model's hidden-layer outputs have rank > 2 (e.g., CNN feature maps from dict-encoded protein sequences) and you need a 2-D UMAP embedding to inspect representations layer by layer.
skills.name: tensor-dimensionality-reduction-pooling
skills.search_text: tensor-dimensionality-reduction-pooling Use when a trained Keras model's hidden-layer outputs have rank > 2 (e.g., CNN feature maps from dict-encoded protein sequences) and you need a 2-D UMAP embedding to inspect representations layer by layer. The layer of interest lies in a branch of the built model — layerUMAP cannot capture hidden outputs from branch layers; capture them manually in a Jupyter Notebook instead. The hidden-layer output tensor already has rank ≤ 2 (e.g., a dense layer output), where no pooling/flatten reduction step is needed before UMAP. The task requires model training or prediction rather than hidden-representation visualization — use autoBioSeqpy's running.py or predicting.py pipelines directly instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reduce high-rank hidden-layer activation tensors from trained autoBioSeqpy/Keras models to a 2-D sample-by-feature matrix (via max/min/avg pooling or flatten), then embed with UMAP for layer-wise visualization of learned biological-sequence representations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105530
skills.summary: Reduce high-rank hidden-layer activation tensors from trained autoBioSeqpy/Keras models to a 2-D sample-by-feature matrix (via max/min/avg pooling or flatten), then embed with UMAP for layer-wise visualization of learned biological-sequence representations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The layer of interest lies in a branch of the built model — layerUMAP cannot capture hidden outputs from branch layers; capture them manually in a Jupyter Notebook instead. The hidden-layer output tensor already has rank ≤ 2 (e.g., a dense layer output), where no pooling/flatten reduction step is needed before UMAP. The task requires model training or prediction rather than hidden-representation visualization — use autoBioSeqpy's running.py or predicting.py pipelines directly instead.

skills.description: Use when you have communication scores from multiple contexts (e.g., 12 BALF COVID-19 samples: 3 control, 3 moderate, 6 severe) and need to deconvolve them into context-driven communication patterns simultaneously.
skills.name: tensor-factorization-decomposition
skills.search_text: tensor-factorization-decomposition Use when you have communication scores from multiple contexts (e.g., 12 BALF COVID-19 samples: 3 control, 3 moderate, 6 severe) and need to deconvolve them into context-driven communication patterns simultaneously. When analyzing a single sample or context — use regular cell2cell for single-context CCC inference instead of tensor decomposition When the communication tensor contains many missing values — the implemented decomposition algorithm is not optimized for missing values, so only shared cell types and LR pairs should be included and members missing in some contexts are dropped When using raw (unnormalized) counts as the expression representation — they yield less consistent decompositions (mean 1-CorrIndex ≈ 0.77 vs ≈ 0.86 for log(CPM+1), non-zero fraction, ComBat, Scanorama) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Decompose 4D cell-cell communication tensors (LR pairs × sender cell types × receiver cell types × contexts) with non-negative Tensor Component Analysis (TCA) in Tensor-cell2cell to extract latent, context-dependent communication modules as interpretable factors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31369-2
skills.summary: Decompose 4D cell-cell communication tensors (LR pairs × sender cell types × receiver cell types × contexts) with non-negative Tensor Component Analysis (TCA) in Tensor-cell2cell to extract latent, context-dependent communication modules as interpretable factors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When analyzing a single sample or context — use regular cell2cell for single-context CCC inference instead of tensor decomposition When the communication tensor contains many missing values — the implemented decomposition algorithm is not optimized for missing values, so only shared cell types and LR pairs should be included and members missing in some contexts are dropped When using raw (unnormalized) counts as the expression representation — they yield less consistent decompositions (mean 1-CorrIndex ≈ 0.77 vs ≈ 0.86 for log(CPM+1), non-zero fraction, ComBat, Scanorama)

skills.description: Use when you have per-context communication scores (e.g., CellChat LR-pair scores for control/moderate/severe COVID-19 BALF samples) and need to deconvolve them into factors that vary jointly across LR pairs, cell types, and patient contexts.
skills.name: tensor-factorization-of-communication-scores
skills.search_text: tensor-factorization-of-communication-scores Use when you have per-context communication scores (e.g., CellChat LR-pair scores for control/moderate/severe COVID-19 BALF samples) and need to deconvolve them into factors that vary jointly across LR pairs, cell types, and patient contexts. You only need communication inference in a single sample or context — use a standard CCC tool (e.g., CellChat) rather than tensor decomposition Your communication tensor contains many missing LR pairs or cell types per context; the implemented algorithm is not optimized for missing values You aim to include cell types not shared across all samples — the case-study tensors only contain cell types shared across all samples http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Decompose a 4D ligand-receptor x sender x receiver x context communication tensor (e.g., the 12 x 189 x 6 x 6 BALF COVID-19 tensor built from CellChat Human-2020-Jin scores) with Tensor-cell2cell at a fixed rank (e.g., rank=10, non-negative, init='svd') to extract context-dependent communication factors whose loadings correlate with phenotypic severity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31369-2
skills.summary: Decompose a 4D ligand-receptor x sender x receiver x context communication tensor (e.g., the 12 x 189 x 6 x 6 BALF COVID-19 tensor built from CellChat Human-2020-Jin scores) with Tensor-cell2cell at a fixed rank (e.g., rank=10, non-negative, init='svd') to extract context-dependent communication factors whose loadings correlate with phenotypic severity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need communication inference in a single sample or context — use a standard CCC tool (e.g., CellChat) rather than tensor decomposition Your communication tensor contains many missing LR pairs or cell types per context; the implemented algorithm is not optimized for missing values You aim to include cell types not shared across all samples — the case-study tensors only contain cell types shared across all samples

skills.description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq count matrices (preprocessed with scanpy/anndata, HVG-selected) where dropout events are high and cell-cell topology should be preserved, or when reproducing scMGCA's multinomial decoder training.
skills.name: tensorflow-autoencoder-training
skills.search_text: tensorflow-autoencoder-training Use when clustering scRNA-seq count matrices (preprocessed with scanpy/anndata, HVG-selected) where dropout events are high and cell-cell topology should be preserved, or when reproducing scMGCA's multinomial decoder training. If the goal is denoising with a zero-inflated negative binomial model (e.g., DCA-style ZINB loss) rather than the multinomial-with-dropout formulation scMGCA uses If the input is already a reduced feature/PCA table rather than a raw count matrix, since the pipeline expects a normalized expression matrix with HVG selection and cell-graph construction If cell-cell topological structure is irrelevant to the analysis, e.g., simple marker-gene-based annotation on already-clustered data http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train the scMGCA graph convolutional autoencoder in TensorFlow: two GCN encoder layers learn cell-cell topology from a cell-PPMI graph, a multinomial-based decoder with Bernoulli dropout simulation reconstructs the scRNA-seq count distribution, and KL-divergence self-optimization refines cluster assignments. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36134-7
skills.summary: Train the scMGCA graph convolutional autoencoder in TensorFlow: two GCN encoder layers learn cell-cell topology from a cell-PPMI graph, a multinomial-based decoder with Bernoulli dropout simulation reconstructs the scRNA-seq count distribution, and KL-divergence self-optimization refines cluster assignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the goal is denoising with a zero-inflated negative binomial model (e.g., DCA-style ZINB loss) rather than the multinomial-with-dropout formulation scMGCA uses If the input is already a reduced feature/PCA table rather than a raw count matrix, since the pipeline expects a normalized expression matrix with HVG selection and cell-graph construction If cell-cell topological structure is irrelevant to the analysis, e.g., simple marker-gene-based annotation on already-clustered data

skills.description: Use when a generative model for scRNA-seq must output expression vectors constrained to a target per-cell library size, and the architecture requires a custom differentiable layer rather than an off-the-shelf normalization op.
skills.name: tensorflow-custom-layer-implementation
skills.search_text: tensorflow-custom-layer-implementation Use when a generative model for scRNA-seq must output expression vectors constrained to a target per-cell library size, and the architecture requires a custom differentiable layer rather than an off-the-shelf normalization op. Input expression vectors are already library-size normalized or the downstream analysis does not require a fixed total read count per generated cell The model is not built in TensorFlow (e.g. a Matlab or other-framework implementation such as SUGAR) and the op cannot be made differentiable in the training graph Implements a custom, differentiable TensorFlow layer — here the library-size normalization (LSN) output layer of the scGAN/cscGAN generator — so the generator explicitly emits cells with a fixed total read count (phi = 20,000), matching the training data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-14018-z
skills.summary: Implements a custom, differentiable TensorFlow layer — here the library-size normalization (LSN) output layer of the scGAN/cscGAN generator — so the generator explicitly emits cells with a fixed total read count (phi = 20,000), matching the training data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression vectors are already library-size normalized or the downstream analysis does not require a fixed total read count per generated cell The model is not built in TensorFlow (e.g. a Matlab or other-framework implementation such as SUGAR) and the op cannot be made differentiable in the training graph

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq subpopulation is too sparse for reliable downstream analysis (e.g. classifier F1 degradation after downsampling) and synthetic cell generation with a GAN is needed.
skills.name: tensorflow-gan-training-workflow
skills.search_text: tensorflow-gan-training-workflow Use when a scRNA-seq subpopulation is too sparse for reliable downstream analysis (e.g. classifier F1 degradation after downsampling) and synthetic cell generation with a GAN is needed. When data is still in raw mtx/tsv format and has not been converted to .h5/.h5ad — convert first with the provided Jupyter notebook. When the goal is conditional generation on side information other than cell type (e.g. case/control samples), which the authors left untested for future work. When you need a benchmarked best generator for quality comparison and your task is not augmentation — the paper reports cscGAN outperforms current methods, but other generators like SUGAR may suit manifold-based generation goals. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train conditional single-cell GAN (cscGAN) models with TensorFlow to generate realistic scRNA-seq cells of defined types, enabling augmentation of sparse subpopulations (e.g. downsampled PBMC cluster 2) for downstream classifier robustness. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-14018-z
skills.summary: Train conditional single-cell GAN (cscGAN) models with TensorFlow to generate realistic scRNA-seq cells of defined types, enabling augmentation of sparse subpopulations (e.g. downsampled PBMC cluster 2) for downstream classifier robustness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When data is still in raw mtx/tsv format and has not been converted to .h5/.h5ad — convert first with the provided Jupyter notebook. When the goal is conditional generation on side information other than cell type (e.g. case/control samples), which the authors left untested for future work. When you need a benchmarked best generator for quality comparison and your task is not augmentation — the paper reports cscGAN outperforms current methods, but other generators like SUGAR may suit manifold-based generation goals.

skills.description: Use when implementing or reproducing a multi-loss GAN (adversarial + cycle + correspondence) in TensorFlow 1.x-style graph/session mode where generator and discriminator must be optimized in a strict per-iteration order with logged diagnostics.
skills.name: tensorflow-graph-session-execution
skills.search_text: tensorflow-graph-session-execution Use when implementing or reproducing a multi-loss GAN (adversarial + cycle + correspondence) in TensorFlow 1.x-style graph/session mode where generator and discriminator must be optimized in a strict per-iteration order with logged diagnostics. You need eager execution / interactive debugging rather than a pre-built static graph executed via sess.run You are aligning more than two modalities — the number of required generators grows quadratically, so the networks would have to be made small or trained separately You only need distributional alignment without point-wise geometry preservation; the correspondence/geometry loss machinery (and its choice of point distance) is not plug-and-play http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Structures scMMGAN training as a TensorFlow graph built in advance (losses, optimizers) and executed inside a tf.Session, so that generator optimization (train_op_G) runs before discriminator optimization (train_op_D) each iteration with periodic loss sanity checks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100577
skills.summary: Structures scMMGAN training as a TensorFlow graph built in advance (losses, optimizers) and executed inside a tf.Session, so that generator optimization (train_op_G) runs before discriminator optimization (train_op_D) each iteration with periodic loss sanity checks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need eager execution / interactive debugging rather than a pre-built static graph executed via sess.run You are aligning more than two modalities — the number of required generators grows quadratically, so the networks would have to be made small or trained separately You only need distributional alignment without point-wise geometry preservation; the correspondence/geometry loss machinery (and its choice of point distance) is not plug-and-play

skills.description: Use when building a supervised binary classifier (viral vs. human) over fixed-length sequence fragments (e.g., 48 bp RNA-seq reads) with TensorFlow/Keras, or when retraining baseline models on an identical training split for a fair benchmark.
skills.name: tensorflow-keras-model-training
skills.search_text: tensorflow-keras-model-training Use when building a supervised binary classifier (viral vs. human) over fixed-length sequence fragments (e.g., 48 bp RNA-seq reads) with TensorFlow/Keras, or when retraining baseline models on an identical training split for a fair benchmark. Reads must be classified for organisms other than human/viral — the model's predictions for sequences from other organisms are not defined, and the authors defer such models to future work The task is predicting viral contigs from an already-trained model rather than training — use the packaged virnatrap-predict command on *_unmapped.fastq files instead Only one model needs to be run with no fair-comparison requirement — retraining all baselines on the same split is unnecessary overhead http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train a TensorFlow/Keras deep learning model to discriminate viral RNAseq reads from human transcripts, as in viRNAtrap: 48 bp fragments of positive (viral) and negative (human) transcripts are split into training/test sets, and the trained model is persisted as an .hdf5 checkpoint for later read prediction and contig assembly. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36336-z
skills.summary: Train a TensorFlow/Keras deep learning model to discriminate viral RNAseq reads from human transcripts, as in viRNAtrap: 48 bp fragments of positive (viral) and negative (human) transcripts are split into training/test sets, and the trained model is persisted as an .hdf5 checkpoint for later read prediction and contig assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads must be classified for organisms other than human/viral — the model's predictions for sequences from other organisms are not defined, and the authors defer such models to future work The task is predicting viral contigs from an already-trained model rather than training — use the packaged virnatrap-predict command on *_unmapped.fastq files instead Only one model needs to be run with no fair-comparison requirement — retraining all baselines on the same split is unnecessary overhead

skills.description: Use when constructing a denoising autoencoder in TensorFlow/Keras to learn latent embeddings from raw scRNA-seq count matrices, explicitly modeling zero inflation (dropout) via a zero-inflated negative binomial reconstruction loss.
skills.name: tensorflow-keras-network-construction
skills.search_text: tensorflow-keras-network-construction Use when constructing a denoising autoencoder in TensorFlow/Keras to learn latent embeddings from raw scRNA-seq count matrices, explicitly modeling zero inflation (dropout) via a zero-inflated negative binomial reconstruction loss. The input is already a low-dimensional feature/embedding table rather than a raw scRNA-seq count matrix requiring dropout-aware denoising The goal is consensus clustering of existing embeddings — that is handled by the separate bipartite graph ensemble clustering module (BC.m/BGEC.m), not the autoencoder A non-TensorFlow/Keras deep learning stack is mandated, since network.py, loss.py and utils.py are implemented in TensorFlow 2.6.0/Keras 2.6.0 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Build and train the single-cell Dual Denoising Autoencoder network of scBGEDA in TensorFlow/Keras: a Gaussian-noise-corrupted encoder projects scRNA-seq counts into a 32-dimensional latent space Z, with a ZINB master decoder and an MSE follower decoder trained by the combined loss L_h = lambda*L1 + gamma*L2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad075
skills.summary: Build and train the single-cell Dual Denoising Autoencoder network of scBGEDA in TensorFlow/Keras: a Gaussian-noise-corrupted encoder projects scRNA-seq counts into a 32-dimensional latent space Z, with a ZINB master decoder and an MSE follower decoder trained by the combined loss L_h = lambda*L1 + gamma*L2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a low-dimensional feature/embedding table rather than a raw scRNA-seq count matrix requiring dropout-aware denoising The goal is consensus clustering of existing embeddings — that is handled by the separate bipartite graph ensemble clustering module (BC.m/BGEC.m), not the autoencoder A non-TensorFlow/Keras deep learning stack is mandated, since network.py, loss.py and utils.py are implemented in TensorFlow 2.6.0/Keras 2.6.0

skills.description: Use when a raw scRNA-Seq count matrix needs deep-learning-based denoising/imputation and you must reconstruct the AutoClass architecture (autoencoder + classifier branch with pre-clustering) in TensorFlow.
skills.name: tensorflow-neural-network-training
skills.search_text: tensorflow-neural-network-training Use when a raw scRNA-Seq count matrix needs deep-learning-based denoising/imputation and you must reconstruct the AutoClass architecture (autoencoder + classifier branch with pre-clustering) in TensorFlow. When a strong distribution assumption is acceptable and a simpler method such as DCA (zero-inflated negative binomial), SAVER, or scImpute suffices for a single noise type like dropouts When no raw count matrix is available (e.g. input is already a normalized/feature table) and the take_norm + count-based pipeline cannot be applied as described http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Build and train the AutoClass composite network in TensorFlow (>=2.0): an autoencoder with a classifier branch attached to the bottleneck that uses virtual class labels from K-means pre-clustering, combining reconstruction and classification losses to denoise scRNA-Seq count matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29576-y
skills.summary: Build and train the AutoClass composite network in TensorFlow (>=2.0): an autoencoder with a classifier branch attached to the bottleneck that uses virtual class labels from K-means pre-clustering, combining reconstruction and classification losses to denoise scRNA-Seq count matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a strong distribution assumption is acceptable and a simpler method such as DCA (zero-inflated negative binomial), SAVER, or scImpute suffices for a single noise type like dropouts When no raw count matrix is available (e.g. input is already a normalized/feature table) and the take_norm + count-based pipeline cannot be applied as described

skills.description: Use when starting from raw 10x scRNAseq data from an infected sample and you need cellranger-produced host-aligned outputs plus the unaligned read pool ready for pathogen alignment and UMI quantification (e.g., HIV, SARS-CoV-2 samples).
skills.name: tenx-scrnaseq-sample-preparation
skills.search_text: tenx-scrnaseq-sample-preparation Use when starting from raw 10x scRNAseq data from an infected sample and you need cellranger-produced host-aligned outputs plus the unaligned read pool ready for pathogen alignment and UMI quantification (e.g., HIV, SARS-CoV-2 samples). Input is already a cellranger output folder with unaligned reads extracted — proceed directly to pathogen alignment (scPathoQuant) rather than re-running sample preparation Data is not 10x single cell scRNAseq output (e.g., bulk RNAseq or plate-based scRNAseq) — cellranger count and 10x matrix assumptions do not hold The goal is quantifying host transcript expression only, with no pathogen/genome-of-interest component — standard cellranger processing suffices without the unaligned-read extraction step http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Prepares 10x Genomics scRNAseq sample outputs so pathogen-derived reads can be aligned and quantified: run cellranger count against the host genome, retain the unaligned reads (e.g., from possorted_genome_bam.bam), and stage the cellranger output folder plus a pathogen reference genome folder (FASTA and optional GTF) for tools like scPathoQuant. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae145
skills.summary: Prepares 10x Genomics scRNAseq sample outputs so pathogen-derived reads can be aligned and quantified: run cellranger count against the host genome, retain the unaligned reads (e.g., from possorted_genome_bam.bam), and stage the cellranger output folder plus a pathogen reference genome folder (FASTA and optional GTF) for tools like scPathoQuant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cellranger output folder with unaligned reads extracted — proceed directly to pathogen alignment (scPathoQuant) rather than re-running sample preparation Data is not 10x single cell scRNAseq output (e.g., bulk RNAseq or plate-based scRNAseq) — cellranger count and 10x matrix assumptions do not hold The goal is quantifying host transcript expression only, with no pathogen/genome-of-interest component — standard cellranger processing suffices without the unaligned-read extraction step

skills.description: Use when a pre-computed CCI dataset of enriched ligand-receptor int-pairs must be linked to Gene Ontology and pathway terms, e.g. to build InterCellar's function-verse ranked-term annotation table.
skills.name: term-enrichment-ranking
skills.search_text: term-enrichment-ranking Use when a pre-computed CCI dataset of enriched ligand-receptor int-pairs must be linked to Gene Ontology and pathway terms, e.g. to build InterCellar's function-verse ranked-term annotation table. Input is raw scRNA-seq data or a full interaction reference database rather than pre-computed inferred ligand-receptor interactions; InterCellar's workflow builds upon pre-computed interactions uploaded as CCI data. Goal is classic statistical over-representation analysis (p-values) on a single gene list, rather than annotating int-pairs under the all-components-enriched rule. Goal is comparing interactions across multiple datasets/conditions to highlight condition-specific communication patterns — that is the multiple-condition comparison functionality, not function-verse annotation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Annotates enriched ligand-receptor int-pairs from a CCI dataset with GO and pathway terms using biomaRt (Ensembl) and graphite (KEGG, Reactome, Biocarta, PID:NCI-Nature, Panther, PharmGKB), then ranks terms by occurrence. Core rule: a term is assigned to an int-pair only when ALL components, including multi-subunit complex members, are enriched by that term. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-02986-2
skills.summary: Annotates enriched ligand-receptor int-pairs from a CCI dataset with GO and pathway terms using biomaRt (Ensembl) and graphite (KEGG, Reactome, Biocarta, PID:NCI-Nature, Panther, PharmGKB), then ranks terms by occurrence. Core rule: a term is assigned to an int-pair only when ALL components, including multi-subunit complex members, are enriched by that term.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw scRNA-seq data or a full interaction reference database rather than pre-computed inferred ligand-receptor interactions; InterCellar's workflow builds upon pre-computed interactions uploaded as CCI data. Goal is classic statistical over-representation analysis (p-values) on a single gene list, rather than annotating int-pairs under the all-components-enriched rule. Goal is comparing interactions across multiple datasets/conditions to highlight condition-specific communication patterns — that is the multiple-condition comparison functionality, not function-verse annotation.

skills.description: Use when generating synthetic benchmark data for enrichment methods where ground-truth active pathways must reflect realistic inter-pathway redundancy (e.g. shared genes), so performance can be evaluated as a function of pathway-similarity structure.
skills.name: term-similarity-based-pathway-sampling
skills.search_text: term-similarity-based-pathway-sampling Use when generating synthetic benchmark data for enrichment methods where ground-truth active pathways must reflect realistic inter-pathway redundancy (e.g. shared genes), so performance can be evaluated as a function of pathway-similarity structure. When the goal is enrichment analysis on real experimental p-values rather than constructing synthetic benchmarks with known positives When pathways in the database are assumed independent and similarity structure should not influence the ground truth (rho effectively 0 with uniform sampling suffices) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 A simulation technique from the pareg workflow that builds a synthetic pathway database with pronounced pathway clustering, computes a pairwise Jaccard term-similarity matrix, and then uses similarity-aware sampling of active pathways so that ground-truth positive gene sets are correlated rather than drawn independently. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad522
skills.summary: A simulation technique from the pareg workflow that builds a synthetic pathway database with pronounced pathway clustering, computes a pairwise Jaccard term-similarity matrix, and then uses similarity-aware sampling of active pathways so that ground-truth positive gene sets are correlated rather than drawn independently.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is enrichment analysis on real experimental p-values rather than constructing synthetic benchmarks with known positives When pathways in the database are assumed independent and similarity structure should not influence the ground truth (rho effectively 0 with uniform sampling suffices)

skills.description: Use when after thresholding root/terminal probabilities (Pr, Pt) at 0.99 on the La Manno-style stationary states, the selected terminal cells must be partitioned into terminal regions to initialize trajectory simulations.
skills.name: terminal-region-clustering-assignment
skills.search_text: terminal-region-clustering-assignment Use when after thresholding root/terminal probabilities (Pr, Pt) at 0.99 on the La Manno-style stationary states, the selected terminal cells must be partitioned into terminal regions to initialize trajectory simulations. Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable from the velocity field — the authors state they do not recommend trajectory inference in that case (e.g. fuzzy root-cell probability distributed without a discernible pattern in the hepatocyte zonation data). The underlying RNA velocity estimation itself is faulty (e.g. time-dependent degradation rates in the scvelo-simulated data), which led to spurious root/terminal state inference, making the resulting regions meaningless. Supervised root/terminal state annotations are already provided — use them directly instead of re-clustering. Groups the terminal cells selected by scvelo/Cytopath stationary-state estimation (terminal probability Pt ≥ 0.99) into terminal regions, using a user-supplied clustering when available or an internally computed Louvain clustering, so each terminal region seeds one set of Cytopath Markov-chain trajectory simulations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Groups the terminal cells selected by scvelo/Cytopath stationary-state estimation (terminal probability Pt ≥ 0.99) into terminal regions, using a user-supplied clustering when available or an internally computed Louvain clustering, so each terminal region seeds one set of Cytopath Markov-chain trajectory simulations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable from the velocity field — the authors state they do not recommend trajectory inference in that case (e.g. fuzzy root-cell probability distributed without a discernible pattern in the hepatocyte zonation data). The underlying RNA velocity estimation itself is faulty (e.g. time-dependent degradation rates in the scvelo-simulated data), which led to spurious root/terminal state inference, making the resulting regions meaningless. Supervised root/terminal state annotations are already provided — use them directly instead of re-clustering.

skills.description: Use when a fitted DIPM tree (e.g. from dipm() on the MASS::anorexia weight-change data) contains terminal sister leaves whose optimal treatment assignments coincide and you want a smaller tree that preserves all treatment recommendations.
skills.name: terminal-sister-node-merging
skills.search_text: terminal-sister-node-merging Use when a fitted DIPM tree (e.g. from dipm() on the MASS::anorexia weight-change data) contains terminal sister leaves whose optimal treatment assignments coincide and you want a smaller tree that preserves all treatment recommendations. The object is a DIPM forest (multiple trees, ntree > 1) rather than a single fitted tree, since pmprune operates on a tree object The task requires changing the treatment recommendation or refitting split points — pmprune only collapses sister leaves with identical optimal treatments and does not alter any recommendation Simplifies a fitted DIPM classification tree by removing terminal sister nodes that share the same optimal treatment, via the dipm package's pmprune function, so the tree structure collapses without altering any treatment recommendation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac041
skills.summary: Simplifies a fitted DIPM classification tree by removing terminal sister nodes that share the same optimal treatment, via the dipm package's pmprune function, so the tree structure collapses without altering any treatment recommendation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The object is a DIPM forest (multiple trees, ntree > 1) rather than a single fitted tree, since pmprune operates on a tree object The task requires changing the treatment recommendation or refitting split points — pmprune only collapses sister leaves with identical optimal treatments and does not alter any recommendation

skills.description: Use when a single-cell omics dataset (AnnData with PCA in obsm['X_pca']) needs pseudotime, automated terminal state prediction, and lineage/branch probabilities, especially for tree-like, cyclic, or disconnected topologies.
skills.name: terminal-state-and-lineage-reconstruction
skills.search_text: terminal-state-and-lineage-reconstruction Use when a single-cell omics dataset (AnnData with PCA in obsm['X_pca']) needs pseudotime, automated terminal state prediction, and lineage/branch probabilities, especially for tree-like, cyclic, or disconnected topologies. The goal is only clustering or dimensionality reduction without ordering of cells along trajectories or fate detection The dataset has no meaningful differentiation dynamics or trajectory structure (e.g. a static cell atlas of unrelated cell types) Cells require time/trajectory labels along a known schedule — VIA's disconnected/time-aware variant needs t_diff_step-compatible labeled times, which are not available here http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstruct single-cell trajectories, pseudotime, and cell fates using VIA's PARC-based cluster-graph and lazy-teleporting random walks, which automate terminal state detection and lineage (branch probability) assignment across scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, cytometry, and imaging modalities. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25773-3
skills.summary: Reconstruct single-cell trajectories, pseudotime, and cell fates using VIA's PARC-based cluster-graph and lazy-teleporting random walks, which automate terminal state detection and lineage (branch probability) assignment across scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, cytometry, and imaging modalities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is only clustering or dimensionality reduction without ordering of cells along trajectories or fate detection The dataset has no meaningful differentiation dynamics or trajectory structure (e.g. a static cell atlas of unrelated cell types) Cells require time/trajectory labels along a known schedule — VIA's disconnected/time-aware variant needs t_diff_step-compatible labeled times, which are not available here

skills.description: Use when a dandelionR trajectory run on a pseudobulked VDJ feature space (pb.milo) needs an explicit root and terminal states before DiffusionMap/DPT and markovProbability can be invoked.
skills.name: terminal-state-and-root-cell-definition
skills.search_text: terminal-state-and-root-cell-definition Use when a dandelionR trajectory run on a pseudobulked VDJ feature space (pb.milo) needs an explicit root and terminal states before DiffusionMap/DPT and markovProbability can be invoked. The trajectory is cyclic (e.g. B cell receptor editing), which cannot be represented by absorbing Markov chains with fixed absorbing terminal states The data topology is not bifurcating or linear — the destiny-based diffusion map is only suitable for bifurcation or linear topologies, limiting this root/tip strategy The input is still single cells or lacks a pseudobulked VDJ feature-space PCA (e.g. no vdjPseudobulk output), since extreme-cell selection is defined on the pseudobulk embedding http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Defines the root cell and terminal (branch-tip) states geometrically from the pseudobulk VDJ feature-space PCA embedding, so that destiny's DPT and the Palantir-style absorbing Markov chain can compute pseudotime and branch probabilities. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2025.06.047
skills.summary: Defines the root cell and terminal (branch-tip) states geometrically from the pseudobulk VDJ feature-space PCA embedding, so that destiny's DPT and the Palantir-style absorbing Markov chain can compute pseudotime and branch probabilities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trajectory is cyclic (e.g. B cell receptor editing), which cannot be represented by absorbing Markov chains with fixed absorbing terminal states The data topology is not bifurcating or linear — the destiny-based diffusion map is only suitable for bifurcation or linear topologies, limiting this root/tip strategy The input is still single cells or lacks a pseudobulked VDJ feature-space PCA (e.g. no vdjPseudobulk output), since extreme-cell selection is defined on the pseudobulk embedding

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq (or CyTOF/scATAC) data requires automated identification of end-state cell fates and branch probabilities without manually assigning terminal states, especially for rare lineages in multifurcating or disconnected trajectories.
skills.name: terminal-state-auto-detection
skills.search_text: terminal-state-auto-detection Use when scRNA-seq (or CyTOF/scATAC) data requires automated identification of end-state cell fates and branch probabilities without manually assigning terminal states, especially for rare lineages in multifurcating or disconnected trajectories. Terminal states are already known and must be imposed exactly — supply user-defined terminal states instead of relying on auto-detection Data is raw counts without a PCA representation or any graph-ready low-dimensional embedding The analysis goal is purely visualization of an existing trajectory rather than fate/lineage detection http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Automatically detect terminal cell fates/lineages in single-cell trajectory inference using VIA's lazy-teleporting random walks on a PARC cluster-graph, without user-defined terminal states. Enables discovery of rare or elusive fates (e.g., the ~3% delta-cell population in E15.5 pancreatic endocrinogenesis) that other TI methods miss. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25773-3
skills.summary: Automatically detect terminal cell fates/lineages in single-cell trajectory inference using VIA's lazy-teleporting random walks on a PARC cluster-graph, without user-defined terminal states. Enables discovery of rare or elusive fates (e.g., the ~3% delta-cell population in E15.5 pancreatic endocrinogenesis) that other TI methods miss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Terminal states are already known and must be imposed exactly — supply user-defined terminal states instead of relying on auto-detection Data is raw counts without a PCA representation or any graph-ready low-dimensional embedding The analysis goal is purely visualization of an existing trajectory rather than fate/lineage detection

skills.description: Use when a pre-processed anndata object with cluster annotations and an RNA velocity field is available and you must determine which populations are terminal fates (e.g. which endocrine populations are absorbing states for Ngn3-low EP progenitors).
skills.name: terminal-state-identification-markov-chain
skills.search_text: terminal-state-identification-markov-chain Use when a pre-processed anndata object with cluster annotations and an RNA velocity field is available and you must determine which populations are terminal fates (e.g. which endocrine populations are absorbing states for Ngn3-low EP progenitors). When no RNA velocity field is available or velocity profiles are not robust — FateCompass can bias transitions with a gradient of differentiation potential instead, but that mode requires prior biological knowledge that is hard to supply (e.g. cancer studies) When the goal is transcription-factor activity inference rather than terminal-state/fate-probability identification — the linear gene-regulation model steps (tf_activities.m, bootstrapping.m) address a different question http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identify terminal (absorbing) cell states of a differentiation landscape by building a discrete Markov process on a KNN graph over single-cell transcriptomics, with edges directed by scVelo-derived RNA velocity, and estimating fate/absorption probabilities toward candidate terminal populations. Applied in FateCompass and benchmarked against CellRank on the mouse E15.5 pancreas dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100512
skills.summary: Identify terminal (absorbing) cell states of a differentiation landscape by building a discrete Markov process on a KNN graph over single-cell transcriptomics, with edges directed by scVelo-derived RNA velocity, and estimating fate/absorption probabilities toward candidate terminal populations. Applied in FateCompass and benchmarked against CellRank on the mouse E15.5 pancreas dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no RNA velocity field is available or velocity profiles are not robust — FateCompass can bias transitions with a gradient of differentiation potential instead, but that mode requires prior biological knowledge that is hard to supply (e.g. cancer studies) When the goal is transcription-factor activity inference rather than terminal-state/fate-probability identification — the linear gene-regulation model steps (tf_activities.m, bootstrapping.m) address a different question

skills.description: Use when benchmarking how robustly a trajectory-inference method recovers rare terminal cell fates (e.g., mDC, pDC) under varying KNN/ncomps parameters, and when validating detected lineages by marker gene trends.
skills.name: terminal-state-lineage-f1-evaluation
skills.search_text: terminal-state-lineage-f1-evaluation Use when benchmarking how robustly a trajectory-inference method recovers rare terminal cell fates (e.g., mDC, pDC) under varying KNN/ncomps parameters, and when validating detected lineages by marker gene trends. The goal is simulating synthetic trajectories rather than evaluating terminal-state detection on a real annotated dataset — use dynverse/dyntoy to generate toy data instead. The dataset has disconnected or cyclic topology requiring via_wrapper_disconnected with multiple roots and preserve_disconnected=True rather than a single-root hematopoiesis tree. Input is raw count data without precomputed PCA — the workflow assumes PCA is already stored in adata.obsm['X_pca']. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A robustness-and-validation skill for VIA-based terminal state detection on the 5780-cell human CD34+ hematopoiesis scRNA-seq dataset: sweep KNN and principal-component parameters, score per-lineage F1 recovery of rare dendritic, megakaryocyte, erythroid, monocyte and B-cell fates, and validate rare lineages with marker-gene pseudotime trends (IRF8, CSF1R, CD123). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25773-3
skills.summary: A robustness-and-validation skill for VIA-based terminal state detection on the 5780-cell human CD34+ hematopoiesis scRNA-seq dataset: sweep KNN and principal-component parameters, score per-lineage F1 recovery of rare dendritic, megakaryocyte, erythroid, monocyte and B-cell fates, and validate rare lineages with marker-gene pseudotime trends (IRF8, CSF1R, CD123).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is simulating synthetic trajectories rather than evaluating terminal-state detection on a real annotated dataset — use dynverse/dyntoy to generate toy data instead. The dataset has disconnected or cyclic topology requiring via_wrapper_disconnected with multiple roots and preserve_disconnected=True rather than a single-root hematopoiesis tree. Input is raw count data without precomputed PCA — the workflow assumes PCA is already stored in adata.obsm['X_pca'].

skills.description: Use when validating Cytopath trajectory inference outputs on a dataset with known terminal cell identities (e.g. pancreatic endocrinogenesis alpha/delta states) and expected co-occurring processes such as cell cycling.
skills.name: terminal-state-recovery-validation
skills.search_text: terminal-state-recovery-validation Use when validating Cytopath trajectory inference outputs on a dataset with known terminal cell identities (e.g. pancreatic endocrinogenesis alpha/delta states) and expected co-occurring processes such as cell cycling. Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors explicitly do not recommend Cytopath trajectory inference in this situation The underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty or unrepresentative (e.g. time-invariant rate assumptions violated), as Cytopath inference becomes meaningless The dataset has no independent marker-based or annotated terminal identities against which endpoint recovery can be checked http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Validation procedure for Cytopath trajectory inference that checks whether consensus trajectories terminate in biologically annotated endocrine terminal states (alpha, beta, gamma, delta) and whether interlaced processes such as cell cycling at the onset of differentiation are recapitulated by correlating cell cycle phase with individual simulation steps. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Validation procedure for Cytopath trajectory inference that checks whether consensus trajectories terminate in biologically annotated endocrine terminal states (alpha, beta, gamma, delta) and whether interlaced processes such as cell cycling at the onset of differentiation are recapitulated by correlating cell cycle phase with individual simulation steps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors explicitly do not recommend Cytopath trajectory inference in this situation The underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty or unrepresentative (e.g. time-invariant rate assumptions violated), as Cytopath inference becomes meaningless The dataset has no independent marker-based or annotated terminal identities against which endpoint recovery can be checked

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data with RNA velocity should be resolved into directed differentiation trajectories whose endpoints are known terminal cell states (e.g. annotated alpha/beta/gamma/delta endocrine clusters), especially with cycling or convergent topologies.
skills.name: terminal-state-supervised-simulation
skills.search_text: terminal-state-supervised-simulation Use when scRNA-seq data with RNA velocity should be resolved into directed differentiation trajectories whose endpoints are known terminal cell states (e.g. annotated alpha/beta/gamma/delta endocrine clusters), especially with cycling or convergent topologies. When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors explicitly do not recommend performing Cytopath trajectory inference in this case. When the underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty (e.g. time-dependent degradation rates, multiple regulatory regimes per gene), which yields spurious root/terminal inference as shown for the erythroid gastrulation dataset. When a topology-constrained tree inference is needed for fully static data without RNA velocity — Cytopath relies on velocity-derived transition probabilities. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Run Cytopath's Markov chain simulations on an RNA velocity field while supervising terminal states with annotated cell fates (e.g. alpha, beta, gamma, delta endocrine cells), so that the inferred trajectories terminate in biologically validated endpoints. This recovers directed differentiation paths, including complex topologies such as the circular cell-cycle structure feeding into endocrinogenesis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Run Cytopath's Markov chain simulations on an RNA velocity field while supervising terminal states with annotated cell fates (e.g. alpha, beta, gamma, delta endocrine cells), so that the inferred trajectories terminate in biologically validated endpoints. This recovers directed differentiation paths, including complex topologies such as the circular cell-cycle structure feeding into endocrinogenesis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors explicitly do not recommend performing Cytopath trajectory inference in this case. When the underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty (e.g. time-dependent degradation rates, multiple regulatory regimes per gene), which yields spurious root/terminal inference as shown for the erythroid gastrulation dataset. When a topology-constrained tree inference is needed for fully static data without RNA velocity — Cytopath relies on velocity-derived transition probabilities.

skills.description: Use when you have a discrete cluster-target label per cell (CSV) and want to test whether one of three specific clusters is transitional between the other two, by converting per-class errors into simplex coordinates and a confusion score.
skills.name: ternary-simplex-coordinate-mapping
skills.search_text: ternary-simplex-coordinate-mapping Use when you have a discrete cluster-target label per cell (CSV) and want to test whether one of three specific clusters is transitional between the other two, by converting per-class errors into simplex coordinates and a confusion score. The question involves more or fewer than three clusters at a time — the confusion score is defined only per class triple No prior discrete cluster assignment exists for the cells (the workflow is supervised and starts from user-defined class labels) The goal is pseudotime ordering of individual cells rather than testing transitional relationships between three specific clusters Maps three putatively related clusters into ternary (simplex) plot coordinates from one-vs-rest logistic-regression class probabilities and cross-validation error estimates, and computes a confusion score (0–1) per class triple to test whether one cluster is a transitional state between the other two (e.g. 0.06 for C5-C6-C7 vs 0.72 for C2-C3-C4). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05988-7
skills.summary: Maps three putatively related clusters into ternary (simplex) plot coordinates from one-vs-rest logistic-regression class probabilities and cross-validation error estimates, and computes a confusion score (0–1) per class triple to test whether one cluster is a transitional state between the other two (e.g. 0.06 for C5-C6-C7 vs 0.72 for C2-C3-C4).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question involves more or fewer than three clusters at a time — the confusion score is defined only per class triple No prior discrete cluster assignment exists for the cells (the workflow is supervised and starts from user-defined class labels) The goal is pseudotime ordering of individual cells rather than testing transitional relationships between three specific clusters

skills.description: Use when you have a table of TESLA pMHC pairs with predicted binding/immunogenicity scores and experimental immunogenicity labels, and need a significance test comparing score distributions between groups.
skills.name: tesla-benchmark-pairwise-group-comparison
skills.search_text: tesla-benchmark-pairwise-group-comparison Use when you have a table of TESLA pMHC pairs with predicted binding/immunogenicity scores and experimental immunogenicity labels, and need a significance test comparing score distributions between groups. The data are not peptide-MHC pairs scored by DeepHLApan/TSNAD v2.0 with paired experimental immunogenicity labels — the test requires labeled groups to compare You are scoring neoantigen candidates in a discovery pipeline (use the binding score >0.5 and immunogenic score >0.5 filter instead of a group-comparison test) The score distributions require paired/matched samples — the Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann-Whitney-type) test used here assumes independent groups http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3407 Statistical skill for testing whether TSNAD v2.0 / DeepHLApan predicted immunogenicity scores discriminate immunogenic from non-immunogenic peptide-MHC pairs on the 608-pair TESLA benchmark, using Wilcoxon rank-sum tests on the full set and on the immunogenic-score>0.5 subset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.016
skills.summary: Statistical skill for testing whether TSNAD v2.0 / DeepHLApan predicted immunogenicity scores discriminate immunogenic from non-immunogenic peptide-MHC pairs on the 608-pair TESLA benchmark, using Wilcoxon rank-sum tests on the full set and on the immunogenic-score>0.5 subset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not peptide-MHC pairs scored by DeepHLApan/TSNAD v2.0 with paired experimental immunogenicity labels — the test requires labeled groups to compare You are scoring neoantigen candidates in a discovery pipeline (use the binding score >0.5 and immunogenic score >0.5 filter instead of a group-comparison test) The score distributions require paired/matched samples — the Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann-Whitney-type) test used here assumes independent groups

skills.description: Use when benchmarking antigen specificity prediction or clustering against a clonotype-level TCR-only baseline, or when a Bayesian TCR functional landscape estimate supervised by scRNA-Seq is required on preprocessed T cell data.
skills.name: tessa-functional-landscape-model-execution
skills.search_text: tessa-functional-landscape-model-execution Use when benchmarking antigen specificity prediction or clustering against a clonotype-level TCR-only baseline, or when a Bayesian TCR functional landscape estimate supervised by scRNA-Seq is required on preprocessed T cell data. The goal is a cell-level multimodal embedding fusing transcriptome and TCR — tessa uses a clonotype-level approach that fuses cells with identical TCRs and loses within-clonotype phenotype information No antigen specificity annotation or reference atlas is available to supervise the model The task requires only TCR sequence analysis without scRNA-Seq supervision http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Executes tessa (TCR functional landscape estimation), Zhang et al.'s Bayesian model supervised with scRNA-Seq, to predict and cluster antigen specificity from TCR sequences, serving as the baseline against mvTCR in benchmark comparisons. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49806-9
skills.summary: Executes tessa (TCR functional landscape estimation), Zhang et al.'s Bayesian model supervised with scRNA-Seq, to predict and cluster antigen specificity from TCR sequences, serving as the baseline against mvTCR in benchmark comparisons.

skills.description: Use when comparing feature-selecting sparse regression methods on high-dimensional omics data and you need a reproducible summary of average test MSE and selected feature counts across repeated random splits.
skills.name: test-mse-and-feature-count-aggregation
skills.search_text: test-mse-and-feature-count-aggregation Use when comparing feature-selecting sparse regression methods on high-dimensional omics data and you need a reproducible summary of average test MSE and selected feature counts across repeated random splits. The goal is feature selection or subspace recovery on a single dataset without a benchmarking comparison — use suffPCR directly (suffPCR(X, y, d=1:3)) rather than the aggregation protocol Data are low-dimensional or features are uncorrelated, where sparse PCA-based regression offers no advantage over standard regression You lack a held-out test fold — averaging test MSE requires a 40/30/30-style train/validation/test split; validation-fold lambda selection plus test-fold evaluation is essential http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Benchmark protocol for evaluating sparse regression methods (SuffPCR vs. SPC, Lasso, Elastic Net, SPCA, DSPCA) on high-dimensional microarray data by averaging test-set prediction MSE and the number of selected features across repeated random train/validation/test splits, as in Table 2 of the SuffPCR paper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac033
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol for evaluating sparse regression methods (SuffPCR vs. SPC, Lasso, Elastic Net, SPCA, DSPCA) on high-dimensional microarray data by averaging test-set prediction MSE and the number of selected features across repeated random train/validation/test splits, as in Table 2 of the SuffPCR paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is feature selection or subspace recovery on a single dataset without a benchmarking comparison — use suffPCR directly (suffPCR(X, y, d=1:3)) rather than the aggregation protocol Data are low-dimensional or features are uncorrelated, where sparse PCA-based regression offers no advantage over standard regression You lack a held-out test fold — averaging test MSE requires a 40/30/30-style train/validation/test split; validation-fold lambda selection plus test-fold evaluation is essential

skills.description: Use when comparing penalized or latent-factor regression methods in a p >> n setting and you need unbiased out-of-sample generalization error (test MSE) plus feature-recovery quality on a synthetic or held-out benchmark.
skills.name: test-set-prediction-error-evaluation
skills.search_text: test-set-prediction-error-evaluation Use when comparing penalized or latent-factor regression methods in a p >> n setting and you need unbiased out-of-sample generalization error (test MSE) plus feature-recovery quality on a synthetic or held-out benchmark. skills.summary: Evaluate high-dimensional regression methods (SuffPCR vs. Lasso, Elastic Net, Ridge, SPC, AIMER, ISPCA, FPS-PCR, Oracle) on an independent test set by recording test MSE alongside feature-selection precision/recall and ROC curves, mirroring the paper's synthetic benchmark (Algorithm 3 data, n=100, p=1000).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is only in-sample fit or training-set residual diagnostics — this skill requires an independent test set disjoint from both training and validation data.
