skills.description: Use when you have a multi-sample, multi-condition single-cell atlas with a fitted GEDI model and prior TF-gene networks, and need to test whether TF activity gradients (e.g., SPI1, CEBPA, SP1) concord with the disease vector field in a defined cell type.
skills.name: tf-activity-gradient-concordance-analysis
skills.search_text: tf-activity-gradient-concordance-analysis Use when you have a multi-sample, multi-condition single-cell atlas with a fitted GEDI model and prior TF-gene networks, and need to test whether TF activity gradients (e.g., SPI1, CEBPA, SP1) concord with the disease vector field in a defined cell type. Input is not a multi-sample, multi-condition count matrix with sample-level covariates — GEDI's sample-specific manifold parameters (Qi) require a condition contrast to model No prior TF-gene network is available for the TFs of interest, since TF activity inference depends on DoRothEA high-confidence sets A, B, and C The analysis goal is non-linear manifold learning or counterfactual perturbation prediction, which GEDI currently does not support http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A GEDI-based analysis that tests whether transcription factor (TF) activity gradients align with the transcriptomic vector field of a condition (e.g., severe COVID-19) within specific cell types such as HLA-DRlo S100Ahi monocytes, using prior knowledge gene regulatory networks (DoRothEA) to infer TF activities. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50963-0
skills.summary: A GEDI-based analysis that tests whether transcription factor (TF) activity gradients align with the transcriptomic vector field of a condition (e.g., severe COVID-19) within specific cell types such as HLA-DRlo S100Ahi monocytes, using prior knowledge gene regulatory networks (DoRothEA) to infer TF activities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a multi-sample, multi-condition count matrix with sample-level covariates — GEDI's sample-specific manifold parameters (Qi) require a condition contrast to model No prior TF-gene network is available for the TFs of interest, since TF activity inference depends on DoRothEA high-confidence sets A, B, and C The analysis goal is non-linear manifold learning or counterfactual perturbation prediction, which GEDI currently does not support

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq counts (dgCMatrix) are available together with a TF-gene regulatory prior (e.g., DoRothEA sets A/B/C) and per-TF activity scores per cell are needed, or when TF activities must be validated against TF perturbation labels.
skills.name: tf-activity-inference-from-scrna-seq
skills.search_text: tf-activity-inference-from-scrna-seq Use when raw scRNA-seq counts (dgCMatrix) are available together with a TF-gene regulatory prior (e.g., DoRothEA sets A/B/C) and per-TF activity scores per cell are needed, or when TF activities must be validated against TF perturbation labels. Only a pre-computed feature/expression table without raw counts and without a TF-gene regulatory prior is available — GEDI's knowledge-informed C-matrix formulation requires both The analysis targets nonlinear manifold structure — GEDI currently supports only linear manifold learning, with optional hyperellipsoid restriction The goal is differential expression between defined clusters rather than continuous, sample-aware TF activity inference along cell states http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 Infers transcription factor (TF) activities in single cells by embedding a weighted DoRothEA regulatory prior matrix as a knowledge-informed constraint (C matrix) in the GEDI generative model, and benchmarks the resulting activities against eight decoupleR methods using AUROC against TF perturbation labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50963-0
skills.summary: Infers transcription factor (TF) activities in single cells by embedding a weighted DoRothEA regulatory prior matrix as a knowledge-informed constraint (C matrix) in the GEDI generative model, and benchmarks the resulting activities against eight decoupleR methods using AUROC against TF perturbation labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a pre-computed feature/expression table without raw counts and without a TF-gene regulatory prior is available — GEDI's knowledge-informed C-matrix formulation requires both The analysis targets nonlinear manifold structure — GEDI currently supports only linear manifold learning, with optional hyperellipsoid restriction The goal is differential expression between defined clusters rather than continuous, sample-aware TF activity inference along cell states

skills.description: Use when you have a non-overlapping candidate region bed-file with per-cell-type activity columns and need gene-level TF affinity features for downstream modelling such as INVOKE expression prediction.
skills.name: tf-affinity-summarisation-per-gene
skills.search_text: tf-affinity-summarisation-per-gene Use when you have a non-overlapping candidate region bed-file with per-cell-type activity columns and need gene-level TF affinity features for downstream modelling such as INVOKE expression prediction. You only need the enhancer-gene interaction scores themselves — run STARE's separate ABC-scoring part independently instead of the gene-level affinity summarisation. Your regions lack an activity signal and only promoter-proximal regions matter — use promoter-mode (no bed-file scaling) rather than the activity-scaled ABC-mode summarisation. You want TF-gene scores from raw peaks with TEPIC's own window-based assignment, length normalisation and peak-count features instead of STARE's mapping-dependent scalers. http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Summarises region-level TRAP TF affinities (computed over 818 non-redundant PFMs from JASPAR 2022, HOCOMOCO v11 and Kheradpour & Kellis) into a per-gene per-TF affinity matrix, with the summation scaling determined by the chosen region-gene mapping (gene window, ABC, gABC or custom existing_abc mapping). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad062
skills.summary: Summarises region-level TRAP TF affinities (computed over 818 non-redundant PFMs from JASPAR 2022, HOCOMOCO v11 and Kheradpour & Kellis) into a per-gene per-TF affinity matrix, with the summation scaling determined by the chosen region-gene mapping (gene window, ABC, gABC or custom existing_abc mapping).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need the enhancer-gene interaction scores themselves — run STARE's separate ABC-scoring part independently instead of the gene-level affinity summarisation. Your regions lack an activity signal and only promoter-proximal regions matter — use promoter-mode (no bed-file scaling) rather than the activity-scaled ABC-mode summarisation. You want TF-gene scores from raw peaks with TEPIC's own window-based assignment, length normalisation and peak-count features instead of STARE's mapping-dependent scalers.

skills.description: Use when you have fine-mapped GWAS/SCZ variants with genomic coordinates and need to predict which transcription factors' binding affinities are disrupted by the risk allele versus the reference allele, specifically to prioritize variants with large (≥20-fold) motif affinity changes.
skills.name: tf-binding-affinity-pwm-scanning
skills.search_text: tf-binding-affinity-pwm-scanning Use when you have fine-mapped GWAS/SCZ variants with genomic coordinates and need to predict which transcription factors' binding affinities are disrupted by the risk allele versus the reference allele, specifically to prioritize variants with large (≥20-fold) motif affinity changes. When the question is linking variants to genes they regulate (use GrID-Net peak-gene linking instead) rather than predicting within-locus TF binding changes. When variants are not fine-mapped or lack confident genomic coordinates in GRCh38/hg38, since allele-specific sequence extraction requires exact variant positions. When you only have gene-level expression or chromatin accessibility data and no variant-level genomic coordinates. http://edamontology.org/topic_3125 http://edamontology.org/topic_3511 Predicts allele-specific transcription-factor binding affinity changes by scanning risk and reference allele sequences (flanked by ±20 bp genomic context from GRCh38/hg38) with FIMO against PWM libraries (HOCOMOCO v11 Full Collection, JASPAR CORE Non-Redundant v2, CIS-BP v2), then computing risk/reference fold changes per variant–TF pair to identify ≥20-fold binding disruptions in noncoding SCZ variants. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Predicts allele-specific transcription-factor binding affinity changes by scanning risk and reference allele sequences (flanked by ±20 bp genomic context from GRCh38/hg38) with FIMO against PWM libraries (HOCOMOCO v11 Full Collection, JASPAR CORE Non-Redundant v2, CIS-BP v2), then computing risk/reference fold changes per variant–TF pair to identify ≥20-fold binding disruptions in noncoding SCZ variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the question is linking variants to genes they regulate (use GrID-Net peak-gene linking instead) rather than predicting within-locus TF binding changes. When variants are not fine-mapped or lack confident genomic coordinates in GRCh38/hg38, since allele-specific sequence extraction requires exact variant positions. When you only have gene-level expression or chromatin accessibility data and no variant-level genomic coordinates.

skills.description: Use when fitting TFvelo gene dynamics or any per-gene model that needs a priori candidate TF regulators per target gene from ENCODE/ChEA, with a capped number of TFs per gene.
skills.name: tf-database-candidate-selection
skills.search_text: tf-database-candidate-selection Use when fitting TFvelo gene dynamics or any per-gene model that needs a priori candidate TF regulators per target gene from ENCODE/ChEA, with a capped number of TFs per gene. The dataset already contains curated, experimentally validated TF-gene regulatory edges and database-derived candidates would add noise The analysis goal is splicing-based velocity (scVelo) rather than TF-expression-based velocity, where TF-target priors are not part of the model The target gene has no TF hits in ENCODE or ChEA, so no regulatory prior is available for initialization http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Selects candidate transcription factors for each target gene from curated TF-target databases (ENCODE and ChEA by default in TFvelo), then initializes TF weights for gene-dynamics fitting. This links per-gene velocity models to known regulation instead of treating genes independently. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45661-w
skills.summary: Selects candidate transcription factors for each target gene from curated TF-target databases (ENCODE and ChEA by default in TFvelo), then initializes TF weights for gene-dynamics fitting. This links per-gene velocity models to known regulation instead of treating genes independently.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset already contains curated, experimentally validated TF-gene regulatory edges and database-derived candidates would add noise The analysis goal is splicing-based velocity (scVelo) rather than TF-expression-based velocity, where TF-target priors are not part of the model The target gene has no TF hits in ENCODE or ChEA, so no regulatory prior is available for initialization

skills.description: Use when you have scATAC-seq peaks linked to target genes and need to filter the universe of TFs down to a per-target-gene candidate pool before inferring a TF–gene network (e.g. as the base GRN input for scGATE).
skills.name: tf-dna-binding-motif-scanning
skills.search_text: tf-dna-binding-motif-scanning Use when you have scATAC-seq peaks linked to target genes and need to filter the universe of TFs down to a per-target-gene candidate pool before inferring a TF–gene network (e.g. as the base GRN input for scGATE). You already have a curated base GRN parquet from external hints — skip motif scanning and go straight to read_base_GRN() summarization. You need large-scale de novo inference over many genes: scGATE with its refined candidate TFs applies only to a small (<200) subset of genes, and >5 TFs per logic gate is impractical. Your goal is predicting logic gates without regulatory context — leave base_GRN empty rather than building a motif-based one. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Scans accessible chromatin peak sequences from scATAC-seq data for TF DNA binding motifs to assign candidate regulatory TFs to each peak, producing a peak-based TF–gene candidate table (base GRN parquet) that scGATE consumes as its refined candidate TF pool. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180
skills.summary: Scans accessible chromatin peak sequences from scATAC-seq data for TF DNA binding motifs to assign candidate regulatory TFs to each peak, producing a peak-based TF–gene candidate table (base GRN parquet) that scGATE consumes as its refined candidate TF pool.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a curated base GRN parquet from external hints — skip motif scanning and go straight to read_base_GRN() summarization. You need large-scale de novo inference over many genes: scGATE with its refined candidate TFs applies only to a small (<200) subset of genes, and >5 TFs per logic gate is impractical. Your goal is predicting logic gates without regulatory context — leave base_GRN empty rather than building a motif-based one.

skills.description: Use when you have a paired/single-cell multiome Seurat object with an ATAC peak assay and need per-cell TF activity scores (e.g., to select candidate TFs and compute TF-gene correlations for eGRN construction along a pseudotime trajectory).
skills.name: tf-motif-activity-estimation-with-chromvar
skills.search_text: tf-motif-activity-estimation-with-chromvar Use when you have a paired/single-cell multiome Seurat object with an ATAC peak assay and need per-cell TF activity scores (e.g., to select candidate TFs and compute TF-gene correlations for eGRN construction along a pseudotime trajectory). Input lacks a single-cell chromatin accessibility assay (e.g., RNA-only data) — chromVAR deviation scores require ATAC peaks over which to scan motifs The analysis targets a non-human genome or requires motif sets outside JASPAR2020; the tutorial binds the pipeline to hg38 (BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38) and JASPAR2020 CORE matrices You only need bulk peak counts or differential accessibility rather than per-cell TF activity to build a regulatory network http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Estimates per-cell transcription factor activity from scATAC-seq peaks by matching JASPAR2020 motifs against hg38 (AddMotifs) and computing chromVAR deviation scores (RunChromVAR), as wrapped by scMEGA on Seurat/Signac objects. The resulting 'chromvar' assay feeds downstream TF selection and TF-gene correlation steps for enhancer-based GRN inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad003
skills.summary: Estimates per-cell transcription factor activity from scATAC-seq peaks by matching JASPAR2020 motifs against hg38 (AddMotifs) and computing chromVAR deviation scores (RunChromVAR), as wrapped by scMEGA on Seurat/Signac objects. The resulting 'chromvar' assay feeds downstream TF selection and TF-gene correlation steps for enhancer-based GRN inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks a single-cell chromatin accessibility assay (e.g., RNA-only data) — chromVAR deviation scores require ATAC peaks over which to scan motifs The analysis targets a non-human genome or requires motif sets outside JASPAR2020; the tutorial binds the pipeline to hg38 (BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38) and JASPAR2020 CORE matrices You only need bulk peak counts or differential accessibility rather than per-cell TF activity to build a regulatory network

skills.description: Use when building a GRN from single-cell multiome (snRNA-seq + snATAC-seq) data where candidate TF–gene interactions must be filtered by enhancer–promoter linkage plus TF motif occurrence in linked peaks, as in scMEGA's eGRN assembly.
skills.name: tf-motif-binding-evidence-integration
skills.search_text: tf-motif-binding-evidence-integration Use when building a GRN from single-cell multiome (snRNA-seq + snATAC-seq) data where candidate TF–gene interactions must be filtered by enhancer–promoter linkage plus TF motif occurrence in linked peaks, as in scMEGA's eGRN assembly. Input is single-omic (e.g., scRNA-seq only) with no ATAC peaks, motif matrix, or peak-to-gene links — the enhancer-based criterion cannot be evaluated. You want a purely co-expression/correlation-based GRN without cis-regulatory evidence; scMEGA will drop TF–gene pairs lacking a bound, linked enhancer. Bulk multi-omics data without per-cell pairing/trajectory, since scMEGA's workflow depends on single-cell multiome objects and pseudo-time (AddTrajectory) context. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 scMEGA's enhancer-based rule for assembling a gene regulatory network: a TF–gene edge is retained only when the gene has at least one linked enhancer (peak-to-gene link) and the TF's motif is present (bound) on one of those linked enhancers, additionally supported by TF–gene correlation. This grounds inferred TF targets in cis-regulatory evidence rather than co-expression alone. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad003
skills.summary: scMEGA's enhancer-based rule for assembling a gene regulatory network: a TF–gene edge is retained only when the gene has at least one linked enhancer (peak-to-gene link) and the TF's motif is present (bound) on one of those linked enhancers, additionally supported by TF–gene correlation. This grounds inferred TF targets in cis-regulatory evidence rather than co-expression alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-omic (e.g., scRNA-seq only) with no ATAC peaks, motif matrix, or peak-to-gene links — the enhancer-based criterion cannot be evaluated. You want a purely co-expression/correlation-based GRN without cis-regulatory evidence; scMEGA will drop TF–gene pairs lacking a bound, linked enhancer. Bulk multi-omics data without per-cell pairing/trajectory, since scMEGA's workflow depends on single-cell multiome objects and pseudo-time (AddTrajectory) context.

skills.description: Use when scMM latent dimensions from single-cell multiomics (e.g. CITE-seq transcriptome + surface protein, or ATAC-seq accessibility) lack biological interpretation and you need to link each latent dimension to enriched TF motifs via decoded pseudocells.
skills.name: tf-motif-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: tf-motif-enrichment-analysis Use when scMM latent dimensions from single-cell multiomics (e.g. CITE-seq transcriptome + surface protein, or ATAC-seq accessibility) lack biological interpretation and you need to link each latent dimension to enriched TF motifs via decoded pseudocells. The trained model is not scMM and you have no access to its decoder, since pseudocell decoding requires the mixture-of-experts decoder The analysis goal is crossmodal prediction or data integration between modalities rather than interpreting what individual latent dimensions encode Input is raw count data that has not yet been trained through scMM — motif enrichment here operates on decoded pseudocell accessibility, not primary counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Associates individual latent dimensions of the trained scMM mixture-of-experts model with transcription factor regulatory programs by aggregating chromatin accessibility peaks from pseudocells generated along each latent dimension and testing those peaks for transcription factor motif enrichment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100071
skills.summary: Associates individual latent dimensions of the trained scMM mixture-of-experts model with transcription factor regulatory programs by aggregating chromatin accessibility peaks from pseudocells generated along each latent dimension and testing those peaks for transcription factor motif enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trained model is not scMM and you have no access to its decoder, since pseudocell decoding requires the mixture-of-experts decoder The analysis goal is crossmodal prediction or data integration between modalities rather than interpreting what individual latent dimensions encode Input is raw count data that has not yet been trained through scMM — motif enrichment here operates on decoded pseudocell accessibility, not primary counts

skills.description: Use when scATAC-seq cells have been assigned to DC3 subpopulations and you need to rank transcription factors as key regulators per subpopulation from open-chromatin motif enrichment plus FPKM expression evidence.
skills.name: tf-motif-enrichment-scoring
skills.search_text: tf-motif-enrichment-scoring Use when scATAC-seq cells have been assigned to DC3 subpopulations and you need to rank transcription factors as key regulators per subpopulation from open-chromatin motif enrichment plus FPKM expression evidence. Input is a bulk-only sample without single-cell data to derive subpopulation assignments and merged subpopulation-specific peaks/expression. Only one subpopulation exists, so differential expression versus 'at least one other subpopulation' and expression-specificity fold changes cannot be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A method for identifying subpopulation-specific key transcription factor regulators by combining Homer motif enrichment scores (geometric mean of -log10 p-value and fold change) on MACS2-called peaks with expression and differential-expression filters, then ranking TFs by a multiplicative importance score. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-12547-1
skills.summary: A method for identifying subpopulation-specific key transcription factor regulators by combining Homer motif enrichment scores (geometric mean of -log10 p-value and fold change) on MACS2-called peaks with expression and differential-expression filters, then ranking TFs by a multiplicative importance score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a bulk-only sample without single-cell data to derive subpopulation assignments and merged subpopulation-specific peaks/expression. Only one subpopulation exists, so differential expression versus 'at least one other subpopulation' and expression-specificity fold changes cannot be computed.

skills.description: Use when you have VIA pseudotime, terminal states, and single-cell branch probabilities on scATAC-seq (or analogous single-cell) data and need to visualize TF-motif activity dynamics along lineages and validate the hierarchy.
skills.name: tf-motif-pseudotime-trend-visualization
skills.search_text: tf-motif-pseudotime-trend-visualization Use when you have VIA pseudotime, terminal states, and single-cell branch probabilities on scATAC-seq (or analogous single-cell) data and need to visualize TF-motif activity dynamics along lineages and validate the hierarchy. Input is raw scRNA-seq counts without pseudotime or branch-probability outputs from VIA — trend curves along pseudotime require TI outputs first The trajectory topology is disconnected or cyclic and no root/terminal-state strategy has been established; use via_wrapper_disconnected instead of the standard wrapper for lineage trend rendering You only need fate-detection accuracy benchmarking (F1 scores vs. SlingShot/Palantir/STREAM/Monocle3) without visualization of gene dynamics http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Compute transcription-factor/motif trend curves along VIA-inferred pseudotime (e.g., GATA1, CEBPD, IRF8 in scATAC-seq hematopoiesis) and render the cluster-level trajectory graph overlaid on a single-cell embedding such as UMAP. This visualizes temporal gene-regulatory dynamics along inferred lineages rather than just computing abstract pseudotime. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25773-3
skills.summary: Compute transcription-factor/motif trend curves along VIA-inferred pseudotime (e.g., GATA1, CEBPD, IRF8 in scATAC-seq hematopoiesis) and render the cluster-level trajectory graph overlaid on a single-cell embedding such as UMAP. This visualizes temporal gene-regulatory dynamics along inferred lineages rather than just computing abstract pseudotime.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw scRNA-seq counts without pseudotime or branch-probability outputs from VIA — trend curves along pseudotime require TI outputs first The trajectory topology is disconnected or cyclic and no root/terminal-state strategy has been established; use via_wrapper_disconnected instead of the standard wrapper for lineage trend rendering You only need fate-detection accuracy benchmarking (F1 scores vs. SlingShot/Palantir/STREAM/Monocle3) without visualization of gene dynamics

skills.description: Use when building a candidate TF–target regulatory mask from bulk ATAC-seq peaks and a PWM motif database (e.g. CisBP), to serve as an epigenetic prior for GRN inference methods such as scKINETICS.
skills.name: tf-motif-scanning-with-pwms
skills.search_text: tf-motif-scanning-with-pwms Use when building a candidate TF–target regulatory mask from bulk ATAC-seq peaks and a PWM motif database (e.g. CisBP), to serve as an epigenetic prior for GRN inference methods such as scKINETICS. The input is already a curated TF–target interaction list or a pre-built binary GRN mask — no motif scanning or peak-to-gene mapping is needed. You lack peak sequences or genomic coordinates (e.g. only differential expression data), since motif scanning requires ATAC-seq peak DNA sequence. You need a validated or literature-supported GRN rather than a permissive candidate prior mask for subsequent EM-based inference. http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Construct a candidate TF–target gene regulatory network mask by scanning ATAC-seq peak sequences with position weight matrices from CisBP, then mapping motif-containing peaks to target genes. This provides the epigenetic prior mask that scKINETICS uses to constrain its expectation-maximization inference of regulator-target impacts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Construct a candidate TF–target gene regulatory network mask by scanning ATAC-seq peak sequences with position weight matrices from CisBP, then mapping motif-containing peaks to target genes. This provides the epigenetic prior mask that scKINETICS uses to constrain its expectation-maximization inference of regulator-target impacts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a curated TF–target interaction list or a pre-built binary GRN mask — no motif scanning or peak-to-gene mapping is needed. You lack peak sequences or genomic coordinates (e.g. only differential expression data), since motif scanning requires ATAC-seq peak DNA sequence. You need a validated or literature-supported GRN rather than a permissive candidate prior mask for subsequent EM-based inference.

skills.description: Use when you have a fitted scKINETICS model (GRN matrix A plus original per-cell velocities) and need single-cell TF activity scores to identify regulators of a state-transition process, e.g. acinar-to-ductal metaplasia.
skills.name: tf-perturbation-velocity-scoring
skills.search_text: tf-perturbation-velocity-scoring Use when you have a fitted scKINETICS model (GRN matrix A plus original per-cell velocities) and need single-cell TF activity scores to identify regulators of a state-transition process, e.g. acinar-to-ductal metaplasia. You only have raw single-cell expression data and no fitted scKINETICS model — the method requires the learned GRN matrix A and original velocities, not expression alone The goal is expression-based TF activity inference (e.g. regulon scoring on counts alone) — this score derives from velocity changes, so a low-expression TF like Ptf1a is exactly the case where expression-based scoring would fail You need true experimental knockout validation — this is purely in silico perturbation via zeroing GRN columns http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 An in silico transcription-factor ablation procedure built on scKINETICS: each TF's regulatory influence is removed from the learned gene regulatory network, per-cell transcriptional velocities are recomputed, and the perturbation effect is quantified as a per-cell cosine distance to assign single-cell TF activity scores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: An in silico transcription-factor ablation procedure built on scKINETICS: each TF's regulatory influence is removed from the learned gene regulatory network, per-cell transcriptional velocities are recomputed, and the perturbation effect is quantified as a per-cell cosine distance to assign single-cell TF activity scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have raw single-cell expression data and no fitted scKINETICS model — the method requires the learned GRN matrix A and original velocities, not expression alone The goal is expression-based TF activity inference (e.g. regulon scoring on counts alone) — this score derives from velocity changes, so a low-expression TF like Ptf1a is exactly the case where expression-based scoring would fail You need true experimental knockout validation — this is purely in silico perturbation via zeroing GRN columns

skills.description: Use when converting a gene expression matrix (e.g., TCGA tumor/normal or LINCS drug-induced profiles) into a GSFM active matrix and you need network-level FM activity via TF regulation, complementing GSFM_Up/Down and GSFM_ssGSEA.
skills.name: tf-regulatory-weight-normalization
skills.search_text: tf-regulatory-weight-normalization Use when converting a gene expression matrix (e.g., TCGA tumor/normal or LINCS drug-induced profiles) into a GSFM active matrix and you need network-level FM activity via TF regulation, complementing GSFM_Up/Down and GSFM_ssGSEA. Normal samples are unavailable (e.g., certain rare diseases), since differential correlation-based TF-target filtering (|r| > 0.2, P < 0.05 between tumor and normal) cannot be performed The analysis goal is per-gene differential expression rather than multi-level functional module activity scoring The FMs under study have no significantly enriched TFs or are not well-aligned with the disease under study, making the TF-regulatory quantifier uninformative http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Computes the GSFM_TF quantifier, a transcriptional regulatory network-level activity score for each functional module (FM), by weighting TF expression with normalized regulation weights (Ratio_Module x Ratio_TF, standardized to sum to 1 within each module) derived from high-confidence TF-target interactions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.apsb.2024.08.017
skills.summary: Computes the GSFM_TF quantifier, a transcriptional regulatory network-level activity score for each functional module (FM), by weighting TF expression with normalized regulation weights (Ratio_Module x Ratio_TF, standardized to sum to 1 within each module) derived from high-confidence TF-target interactions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Normal samples are unavailable (e.g., certain rare diseases), since differential correlation-based TF-target filtering (|r| > 0.2, P < 0.05 between tumor and normal) cannot be performed The analysis goal is per-gene differential expression rather than multi-level functional module activity scoring The FMs under study have no significantly enriched TFs or are not well-aligned with the disease under study, making the TF-regulatory quantifier uninformative

skills.description: Use when you need biologically interpretable cell-level attention over TF regulons from a trained TOSICA model — e.g., to order cells in pseudotime by regulon attention or compare regulon dominance between cell states or disease conditions.
skills.name: tf-regulon-masked-attention-interpretation
skills.search_text: tf-regulon-masked-attention-interpretation Use when you need biologically interpretable cell-level attention over TF regulons from a trained TOSICA model — e.g., to order cells in pseudotime by regulon attention or compare regulon dominance between cell states or disease conditions. When only a generic cell-type label is needed without interpretability — other annotation tools suffice When reference and query gene sets (var_names) cannot be made consistent and identically ordered, since TOSICA requires this When the goal requires pathway-level (GO/Reactome) rather than TF-regulon-level token interpretability — use human_gobp or human_reactome masks instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Uses TOSICA's multi-head self-attention with tokens masked by transcription-factor gene sets (TF.gmt) so that attention weights are traceable to TF regulons, then treats the attention matrix as an interpretable embedding for trajectory and regulon-dominance analyses (e.g., NF1-to-CEBP transition in osteoarthritis chondrocytes). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-35923-4
skills.summary: Uses TOSICA's multi-head self-attention with tokens masked by transcription-factor gene sets (TF.gmt) so that attention weights are traceable to TF regulons, then treats the attention matrix as an interpretable embedding for trajectory and regulon-dominance analyses (e.g., NF1-to-CEBP transition in osteoarthritis chondrocytes).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a generic cell-type label is needed without interpretability — other annotation tools suffice When reference and query gene sets (var_names) cannot be made consistent and identically ordered, since TOSICA requires this When the goal requires pathway-level (GO/Reactome) rather than TF-regulon-level token interpretability — use human_gobp or human_reactome masks instead

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether single-cell co-expression network edges are biologically supported, by overlapping inferred TF–gene edges against known ChIP-seq TF–target interactions across cell types.
skills.name: tf-target-chipseq-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: tf-target-chipseq-overlap-analysis Use when evaluating whether single-cell co-expression network edges are biologically supported, by overlapping inferred TF–gene edges against known ChIP-seq TF–target interactions across cell types. When gold-standard TF–target edges are available or the dataset is simulated with a known true network — direct accuracy metrics are preferable to ChIP-seq overlap For cell types with fewer than 100 cells, which fall outside the Tabula Muris analysis scope When the goal is to assign directionality or edge type (regulatory vs co-regulatory) — scLink edges are undirected statistical dependencies http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Validates cell type-specific gene networks inferred by scLink on Tabula Muris Smart-seq2 data by computing the proportion of inferred TF–gene edges that match a pooled ChIP-seq TF–target reference built from ENCODE, ChEA, and Harmonizome. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.11.006
skills.summary: Validates cell type-specific gene networks inferred by scLink on Tabula Muris Smart-seq2 data by computing the proportion of inferred TF–gene edges that match a pooled ChIP-seq TF–target reference built from ENCODE, ChEA, and Harmonizome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When gold-standard TF–target edges are available or the dataset is simulated with a known true network — direct accuracy metrics are preferable to ChIP-seq overlap For cell types with fewer than 100 cells, which fall outside the Tabula Muris analysis scope When the goal is to assign directionality or edge type (regulatory vs co-regulatory) — scLink edges are undirected statistical dependencies

skills.description: Use when preprocessing scRNA-seq data for TFvelo and each target gene needs a curated candidate TF set drawn from ENCODE/ChEA regulatory pairs before fitting TF-based gene dynamics.
skills.name: tf-target-database-annotation-filtering
skills.search_text: tf-target-database-annotation-filtering Use when preprocessing scRNA-seq data for TFvelo and each target gene needs a curated candidate TF set drawn from ENCODE/ChEA regulatory pairs before fitting TF-based gene dynamics. The dataset already contains spliced/unspliced counts and you intend to run standard splicing-based scVelo dynamical modeling instead of TF-based modeling No ENCODE/ChEA TF-target database has been downloaded/decompressed — the candidate-TF restriction step cannot be performed and the pipeline should not be run until 'unzip ENCODE.zip' completes The goal is gene-level normalization only (e.g. standalone scanpy QC) rather than annotating target genes with TF candidates for regulatory modeling http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Restrict candidate transcription factors for each target gene to curated regulatory pairs from the ENCODE and ChEA TF-target databases prior to dynamic velocity modeling in TFvelo, ensuring gene dynamics are modeled from biologically grounded TF regulation rather than splicing information. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45661-w
skills.summary: Restrict candidate transcription factors for each target gene to curated regulatory pairs from the ENCODE and ChEA TF-target databases prior to dynamic velocity modeling in TFvelo, ensuring gene dynamics are modeled from biologically grounded TF regulation rather than splicing information.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset already contains spliced/unspliced counts and you intend to run standard splicing-based scVelo dynamical modeling instead of TF-based modeling No ENCODE/ChEA TF-target database has been downloaded/decompressed — the candidate-TF restriction step cannot be performed and the pipeline should not be run until 'unzip ENCODE.zip' completes The goal is gene-level normalization only (e.g. standalone scanpy QC) rather than annotating target genes with TF candidates for regulatory modeling

skills.description: Use when evaluating a co-expression inference method on scRNA-seq data (e.g., AD snRNA-seq or COVID PBMC) by checking that its significant co-expressed gene pairs capture known TRRUST transcription factor-target relationships more than benchmark methods.
skills.name: tf-target-enrichment-evaluation
skills.search_text: tf-target-enrichment-evaluation Use when evaluating a co-expression inference method on scRNA-seq data (e.g., AD snRNA-seq or COVID PBMC) by checking that its significant co-expressed gene pairs capture known TRRUST transcription factor-target relationships more than benchmark methods. The goal is functional annotation of co-expression gene modules rather than benchmarking the co-expression inference method itself — use GO enrichment via clusterProfiler::enrichGO instead. Input co-expressions are inferred across mixed cell types without subsetting, violating the CS-CORE recommendation to subset by cell type to avoid Simpson's paradox. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Benchmarks cell-type-specific co-expression inference by testing whether inferred co-expressed gene pairs are enriched for known transcription factor-target pairs from TRRUST, comparing CS-CORE against competitors (rho-sctransform, rho-analytic PR, SpQN). It serves as a biological-relevance validation that complements cross-dataset reproducibility. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40503-7
skills.summary: Benchmarks cell-type-specific co-expression inference by testing whether inferred co-expressed gene pairs are enriched for known transcription factor-target pairs from TRRUST, comparing CS-CORE against competitors (rho-sctransform, rho-analytic PR, SpQN). It serves as a biological-relevance validation that complements cross-dataset reproducibility.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is functional annotation of co-expression gene modules rather than benchmarking the co-expression inference method itself — use GO enrichment via clusterProfiler::enrichGO instead. Input co-expressions are inferred across mixed cell types without subsetting, violating the CS-CORE recommendation to subset by cell type to avoid Simpson's paradox.

skills.description: Use when computing the network-level GSFM_TF column of a GSFM active matrix, i.e., when a gene expression matrix and a curated TF-target regulatory database (Garcia-Alonso et al.) must be combined to quantify FM activity at the transcriptional regulatory network level.
skills.name: tf-target-enrichment-fisher-testing
skills.search_text: tf-target-enrichment-fisher-testing Use when computing the network-level GSFM_TF column of a GSFM active matrix, i.e., when a gene expression matrix and a curated TF-target regulatory database (Garcia-Alonso et al.) must be combined to quantify FM activity at the transcriptional regulatory network level. When no TF-target regulatory database or TF expression data is available for the tumor type — GSFM_TF cannot be computed and only the gene-level (GSFM_Up, GSFM_Down) or pathway-level (GSFM_ssGSEA) quantifiers apply. When the goal is gene-level or pathway-level FM activity only — use GSFM_Up/GSFM_Down or GSFM_ssGSEA instead of the network-level GSFM_TF. When the input is already a transformed FM active matrix (e.g., output of STEP 2); this skill operates on the raw gene expression matrices. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies transcription factors (TFs) whose validated target genes are significantly enriched within each functional module (FM) via one-tailed Fisher exact tests, then computes the GSFM_TF quantifier as the regulation-weighted average expression of significantly regulated TFs. This supplies the transcriptional regulatory network-level dimension of the four biologically interpretable quantifiers (BIQs) in the GSFM transformation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.apsb.2024.08.017
skills.summary: Identifies transcription factors (TFs) whose validated target genes are significantly enriched within each functional module (FM) via one-tailed Fisher exact tests, then computes the GSFM_TF quantifier as the regulation-weighted average expression of significantly regulated TFs. This supplies the transcriptional regulatory network-level dimension of the four biologically interpretable quantifiers (BIQs) in the GSFM transformation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no TF-target regulatory database or TF expression data is available for the tumor type — GSFM_TF cannot be computed and only the gene-level (GSFM_Up, GSFM_Down) or pathway-level (GSFM_ssGSEA) quantifiers apply. When the goal is gene-level or pathway-level FM activity only — use GSFM_Up/GSFM_Down or GSFM_ssGSEA instead of the network-level GSFM_TF. When the input is already a transformed FM active matrix (e.g., output of STEP 2); this skill operates on the raw gene expression matrices.

skills.description: Use when you need to validate that a fitted gene-wise LASSO model over candidate TFs recapitulates known regulatory databases, e.g. by one-sided t-test enrichment of non-zero-weight TFs in ENCODE/ChEA TF-target sets.
skills.name: tf-target-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: tf-target-enrichment-testing Use when you need to validate that a fitted gene-wise LASSO model over candidate TFs recapitulates known regulatory databases, e.g. by one-sided t-test enrichment of non-zero-weight TFs in ENCODE/ChEA TF-target sets. When no spliced/unspliced-independent TF-based velocity model has been fitted — enrichment testing presumes per-gene non-zero LASSO TF weights against scVelo velocities When your TF database is not ENCODE/ChEA or TFs were not selected via --TF_databases with --max_n_TF cap, since the enrichment statistic is defined against those candidate sets When the dataset is very large: TFvelo is slower than scVelo and parallelization over CPUs is required, making the full fit-then-test workflow costly http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Statistically tests whether transcription factors with non-zero LASSO weights, fitted to predict scVelo RNA velocity from TF abundances, are enriched in ENCODE TF-target relationships, validating TF-based velocity estimation on the pancreas dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45661-w
skills.summary: Statistically tests whether transcription factors with non-zero LASSO weights, fitted to predict scVelo RNA velocity from TF abundances, are enriched in ENCODE TF-target relationships, validating TF-based velocity estimation on the pancreas dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no spliced/unspliced-independent TF-based velocity model has been fitted — enrichment testing presumes per-gene non-zero LASSO TF weights against scVelo velocities When your TF database is not ENCODE/ChEA or TFs were not selected via --TF_databases with --max_n_TF cap, since the enrichment statistic is defined against those candidate sets When the dataset is very large: TFvelo is slower than scVelo and parallelization over CPUs is required, making the full fit-then-test workflow costly

skills.description: Use when the goal is to functionally interpret scRNAseq cell clusters by encoding them with a TF-target-biased (e.g., TRRUST) autoencoder latent space and to identify which clusters the TF network can reconstruct (mean QCC and QCM >= 0.5 across runs).
skills.name: tf-target-network-encoded-representation
skills.search_text: tf-target-network-encoded-representation Use when the goal is to functionally interpret scRNAseq cell clusters by encoding them with a TF-target-biased (e.g., TRRUST) autoencoder latent space and to identify which clusters the TF network can reconstruct (mean QCC and QCM >= 0.5 across runs). The task is generic clustering or normalization of raw scRNAseq counts — SCA requires a reference clustering and log10-transformed counts and is meant for functional mining, not primary processing. You need a well-defined score for a non-TF latent space or expect all clusters to be reconstructed — SCA by design reconstructs only clusters where the encoding space drives cell aggregation, so absence of QCC/QCM >= 0.5 for other clusters is expected, not a failure. miRNAs must be quantified alongside mRNAs — it is currently not possible to quantify miRNAs together with mRNAs at single-cell level, so TF-miRNA circuit inputs cannot be used directly. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Encodes single-cell RNAseq clusters in a latent space whose hidden layers are biased by experimentally validated transcription-factor target networks (e.g., TRRUST), via a Sparsely-Connected Autoencoder (SCA) implemented in rCASC, and scores reconstruction of clusters with QCC and QCM metrics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-020-00162-6
skills.summary: Encodes single-cell RNAseq clusters in a latent space whose hidden layers are biased by experimentally validated transcription-factor target networks (e.g., TRRUST), via a Sparsely-Connected Autoencoder (SCA) implemented in rCASC, and scores reconstruction of clusters with QCC and QCM metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is generic clustering or normalization of raw scRNAseq counts — SCA requires a reference clustering and log10-transformed counts and is meant for functional mining, not primary processing. You need a well-defined score for a non-TF latent space or expect all clusters to be reconstructed — SCA by design reconstructs only clusters where the encoding space drives cell aggregation, so absence of QCC/QCM >= 0.5 for other clusters is expected, not a failure. miRNAs must be quantified alongside mRNAs — it is currently not possible to quantify miRNAs together with mRNAs at single-cell level, so TF-miRNA circuit inputs cannot be used directly.

skills.description: Use when you have a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix plus a candidate list of TFs (optionally a base GRN .parquet from scATAC-seq/motif data) and need directed, cell-type-specific TF-target edges with Bayes-Factor-ranked Boolean logic gates.
skills.name: tf-target-network-inference
skills.search_text: tf-target-network-inference Use when you have a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix plus a candidate list of TFs (optionally a base GRN .parquet from scATAC-seq/motif data) and need directed, cell-type-specific TF-target edges with Bayes-Factor-ranked Boolean logic gates. You need large-scale network inference from scratch: scGATE is applicable only to a small (<200) subset of genes with a refined list of candidate TFs based on external hints. The regulatory logic involves more than 5 TFs per target: decoding high-order Boolean logic beyond k=5 regulators is prone to overfitting. You need temporal/pseudotime-aware inference along differentiation trajectories — scGATE does not yet handle pseudotime-sorted single-cell data or temporal delays. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Infer directed TF-to-target-gene regulatory networks from single-cell RNA-seq data using scGATE's Hill-function and Bayesian logic-gate framework, optionally refined by a base GRN derived from scATAC-seq peaks and TF binding motifs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180
skills.summary: Infer directed TF-to-target-gene regulatory networks from single-cell RNA-seq data using scGATE's Hill-function and Bayesian logic-gate framework, optionally refined by a base GRN derived from scATAC-seq peaks and TF binding motifs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need large-scale network inference from scratch: scGATE is applicable only to a small (<200) subset of genes with a refined list of candidate TFs based on external hints. The regulatory logic involves more than 5 TFs per target: decoding high-order Boolean logic beyond k=5 regulators is prone to overfitting. You need temporal/pseudotime-aware inference along differentiation trajectories — scGATE does not yet handle pseudotime-sorted single-cell data or temporal delays.

skills.description: Use when you have a small (<200 gene) scRNA-seq matrix, a candidate TF list, and an optional scATAC-seq/motif-derived base GRN parquet, and you need a directed, BF-ranked TF–target network for a specific tissue or cell type.
skills.name: tf-target-network-inference-bayes-factor-ranking
skills.search_text: tf-target-network-inference-bayes-factor-ranking Use when you have a small (<200 gene) scRNA-seq matrix, a candidate TF list, and an optional scATAC-seq/motif-derived base GRN parquet, and you need a directed, BF-ranked TF–target network for a specific tissue or cell type. Input spans more than ~200 genes or lacks a refined candidate TF list — the paper states scGATE 'is currently applicable to a rather small (<200) subset of genes with a refined list of candidate regulatory TFs based on external hints' Data are pseudotime-sorted along differentiation trajectories or you need to model temporal delays — scGATE does not yet handle these You expect to capture regulation by large protein complexes or high-order logic (>5 regulators) — overfitting makes this unreliable and such interactions are missed by the model and the ground truth http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Infer directed TF–gene regulatory networks from preprocessed scRNA-seq count matrices with scGATE (R 4.1.3), fitting a Hill activation function within a Bayesian EM framework and ranking candidate edges by Bayes Factor (BF_score). A base GRN from scATAC-seq peaks and TF binding motifs constrains candidate TFs per target gene. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180
skills.summary: Infer directed TF–gene regulatory networks from preprocessed scRNA-seq count matrices with scGATE (R 4.1.3), fitting a Hill activation function within a Bayesian EM framework and ranking candidate edges by Bayes Factor (BF_score). A base GRN from scATAC-seq peaks and TF binding motifs constrains candidate TFs per target gene.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spans more than ~200 genes or lacks a refined candidate TF list — the paper states scGATE 'is currently applicable to a rather small (<200) subset of genes with a refined list of candidate regulatory TFs based on external hints' Data are pseudotime-sorted along differentiation trajectories or you need to model temporal delays — scGATE does not yet handle these You expect to capture regulation by large protein complexes or high-order logic (>5 regulators) — overfitting makes this unreliable and such interactions are missed by the model and the ground truth

skills.description: Use when building a candidate TF-target prior network from ATAC-seq peak sets (e.g. scKINETICS epigenetic prior), where TF motif scan results must be converted to a binary TF-by-gene mask restricted to expressed genes.
skills.name: tf-target-prior-mask-construction
skills.search_text: tf-target-prior-mask-construction Use when building a candidate TF-target prior network from ATAC-seq peak sets (e.g. scKINETICS epigenetic prior), where TF motif scan results must be converted to a binary TF-by-gene mask restricted to expressed genes. Target genes cannot be cross-referenced with a single-cell expression dataset to filter for expressed genes, since the mask is intended to be restricted to expressed genes Only single-cell ATAC data without a compatible bulk peak set is available, as the described pipeline operates on bulk ATAC-seq peaks The goal is data-driven GRN inference without epigenetic priors, e.g. inference relying only on gene-gene co-expression or phenotypic manifold constraints http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Construct a binary TF-by-gene candidate regulatory mask to serve as the epigenetic prior for scKINETICS, by scanning bulk ATAC-seq peaks with TF position-weight matrices and mapping motif-containing peaks to genes near their TSS. This grounds GRN inference in chromatin accessibility rather than co-expression alone. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Construct a binary TF-by-gene candidate regulatory mask to serve as the epigenetic prior for scKINETICS, by scanning bulk ATAC-seq peaks with TF position-weight matrices and mapping motif-containing peaks to genes near their TSS. This grounds GRN inference in chromatin accessibility rather than co-expression alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Target genes cannot be cross-referenced with a single-cell expression dataset to filter for expressed genes, since the mask is intended to be restricted to expressed genes Only single-cell ATAC data without a compatible bulk peak set is available, as the described pipeline operates on bulk ATAC-seq peaks The goal is data-driven GRN inference without epigenetic priors, e.g. inference relying only on gene-gene co-expression or phenotypic manifold constraints

skills.description: Use when a synthetic benchmark has known signed TF-target weights (e.g., 10 TFs per target gene) and you must quantify recovery of regulatory weights, velocities, and edges via Spearman correlation, F1, and AUROC.
skills.name: tf-target-weight-inference-evaluation
skills.search_text: tf-target-weight-inference-evaluation Use when a synthetic benchmark has known signed TF-target weights (e.g., 10 TFs per target gene) and you must quantify recovery of regulatory weights, velocities, and edges via Spearman correlation, F1, and AUROC. Input is real scRNA-seq data without splicing information but with no ground-truth regulatory weights — there is nothing to validate the inferred weights against; use TFvelo's standard run/analysis demo workflow instead The goal is runtime benchmarking on large-scale datasets — TFvelo is known to be slower than scVelo, and this synthetic validation does not address efficiency Genes whose dynamics TFvelo is known to fit poorly (cf. Fig. S14) are the focus — weight recovery metrics may not be meaningful for those genes http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates that TFvelo reconstructs ground-truth gene regulatory dynamics from synthetic multi-TF benchmark data by scoring inferred TF weights, RNA velocities, and thresholded TF–target edges against signed ground truth, and benchmarks them against scVelo's EM baseline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45661-w
skills.summary: Validates that TFvelo reconstructs ground-truth gene regulatory dynamics from synthetic multi-TF benchmark data by scoring inferred TF weights, RNA velocities, and thresholded TF–target edges against signed ground truth, and benchmarks them against scVelo's EM baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real scRNA-seq data without splicing information but with no ground-truth regulatory weights — there is nothing to validate the inferred weights against; use TFvelo's standard run/analysis demo workflow instead The goal is runtime benchmarking on large-scale datasets — TFvelo is known to be slower than scVelo, and this synthetic validation does not address efficiency Genes whose dynamics TFvelo is known to fit poorly (cf. Fig. S14) are the focus — weight recovery metrics may not be meaningful for those genes

skills.search_text: tf-tg-regulatory-relationship-merging Use when an initial GRN adjacency matrix inferred from expression data must be refined before Boolean Network conversion, and curated database interactions are available for the organism. The organism is absent from OmniPath, Signor, SignaLink, and TRRUST (typical for non-model microbes); the databases will contribute no edges and refinement cannot rely on verified interactions The goal is Boolean Network logic-rule setting rather than GRN refinement — that step uses the Cell Collective database search instead No additional knowledge of the genome (e.g., annotated GenBank file) is available, since refining steps cannot be performed without it http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Merges verified transcription factor–target gene regulatory interactions retrieved from curated databases (OmniPath, Signor, SignaLink, TRRUST) into an MI-inferred GRN, using name translation and explicit conflict-resolution rules to produce the final adjacency matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2024.01.013
skills.summary: Merges verified transcription factor–target gene regulatory interactions retrieved from curated databases (OmniPath, Signor, SignaLink, TRRUST) into an MI-inferred GRN, using name translation and explicit conflict-resolution rules to produce the final adjacency matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism is absent from OmniPath, Signor, SignaLink, and TRRUST (typical for non-model microbes); the databases will contribute no edges and refinement cannot rely on verified interactions The goal is Boolean Network logic-rule setting rather than GRN refinement — that step uses the Cell Collective database search instead No additional knowledge of the genome (e.g., annotated GenBank file) is available, since refining steps cannot be performed without it

skills.search_text: tfidf-log-count-matrix-preprocessing Use when comparing synthetic single-cell count matrices (e.g., from scReadSim or SCAN-ATAC-Sim) against real scATAC-seq counts in a shared low-dimensional space to compute mixing metrics such as miLISI. Input is raw sequencing reads or a BAM/BED file without a peak-by-cell count matrix — construct count matrices first (e.g., via Utility.scATAC_bam2countmat) before applying this preprocessing The analysis target is read-sequence fidelity rather than cell-embedding mixing — use summary statistics (peak-wise mean, variance, CV, zero proportion; cell-wise library size, zero proportion) with KS tests instead Data are already normalized embeddings — TF-IDF + log transform would distort an already-reduced representation http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Preprocess scATAC-seq peak-by-cell read count matrices (real and synthetic) with TF-IDF followed by logarithmic transformation, then embed them in a shared PCA/UMAP space to quantify how well synthetic cells mix with real cells (miLISI). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43162-w
skills.summary: Preprocess scATAC-seq peak-by-cell read count matrices (real and synthetic) with TF-IDF followed by logarithmic transformation, then embed them in a shared PCA/UMAP space to quantify how well synthetic cells mix with real cells (miLISI).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads or a BAM/BED file without a peak-by-cell count matrix — construct count matrices first (e.g., via Utility.scATAC_bam2countmat) before applying this preprocessing The analysis target is read-sequence fidelity rather than cell-embedding mixing — use summary statistics (peak-wise mean, variance, CV, zero proportion; cell-wise library size, zero proportion) with KS tests instead Data are already normalized embeddings — TF-IDF + log transform would distort an already-reduced representation

skills.search_text: tfidf-normalization-of-scatac-counts Use when a raw scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix (AnnData with cells as n_obs and peaks as n_vars) must be prepared as encoder input for a cross-modality translator such as scButterfly before modality-specific pretraining. skills.search_text: thresholding-based-radius-binary-search Use when a large single-cell RNA-seq expression matrix (rows = cells, columns = genes/PCs) must be reduced to a fixed-size representative subset that preserves rare cell states and covers the transcriptomic space, rather than uniform subsampling. When the goal is unbiased random subsampling rather than data-dependent, distance-based representative selection — uniform subsampling is simpler, though it risks overlooking rare cell states. When cells lack a meaningful distance measure or the input is not a sample-by-feature numeric matrix (rows must be cells, columns genes/PCs). When downstream analysis requires the full dataset's raw counts rather than a reduced sketch, or depends on algorithmic assumptions incompatible with a metric-space sphere model (the article notes compatibility was only tested with Louvain and Monocle 2). http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Implements Sphetcher's spherical thresholding scheme: a radius is guessed and binary-searched while a disk-friendly greedy set-cover step selects sphere centers, yielding a fixed-size sketch of cells that evenly covers the transcriptomic space. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101126
skills.summary: Implements Sphetcher's spherical thresholding scheme: a radius is guessed and binary-searched while a disk-friendly greedy set-cover step selects sphere centers, yielding a fixed-size sketch of cells that evenly covers the transcriptomic space.

When downstream analysis requires the full dataset's raw counts rather than a reduced sketch, or depends on algorithmic assumptions incompatible with a metric-space sphere model (the article notes compatibility was only tested with Louvain and Monocle 2).

skills.search_text: til-subtype-composition-quantification Use when a scRNA-seq query of T cells (e.g. tetramer+ CD8 TILs or LCMV P14 cells) needs cell subtype frequencies, or when comparing perturbation effects on T cell state proportions (e.g. KO vs WT). skills.name: time-course-correlation-change-analysis
skills.search_text: time-course-correlation-change-analysis Use when a single scRNA-seq dataset spans multiple time points (e.g. GSE75748 definitive endoderm 0/12/24/36/72/96 h) and the goal is to quantify co-expression correlation changes or hub-gene degree shifts between time points. Data come from a single condition or time point with no temporal contrast — per-time-point correlation-change comparison is undefined The goal is directed regulatory or causal edges between genes — scLink edges are undirected statistical dependencies Gene list is very large — the article suggests instead dividing genes into modules based on scLink's correlation and applying scLink separately to each module http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Detect changes in gene co-expression and network structure across a differentiation or perturbation time course by fitting scLink penalized Gaussian graphical models per time point and comparing robust correlation matrices and adjacency-derived degrees across marker-gene pairs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.11.006

skills.description: Use when the input is a time-course scRNA-seq expression matrix (cells sacrificed at each time point, no cell-to-cell correspondence) and the goal is per-cell lineage tracing, cell fate prediction, or dynamic gene-network/critical-gene discovery.
skills.name: time-course-scrna-seq-data-processing
skills.search_text: time-course-scrna-seq-data-processing Use when the input is a time-course scRNA-seq expression matrix (cells sacrificed at each time point, no cell-to-cell correspondence) and the goal is per-cell lineage tracing, cell fate prediction, or dynamic gene-network/critical-gene discovery. The data are a single time point or lack a temporal design — optimal transport alignment between adjacent time points and trajectory construction are not applicable. Only a bulk population-average trajectory is needed and per-cell resolution is unnecessary; the article notes most existing methods already construct such bulk trajectories. Expression data are so low-dimensional or small-sample that classical alignment measures (Euclidean distance, Pearson correlation) remain valid, making the OT-based alignment unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 End-to-end CellST pipeline that turns time-course scRNA-seq expression matrices (e.g. 38,731 cells x 11,588 genes zebrafish embryogenesis Drop-seq data) into individual cell fate trajectories and dynamic gene networks, instead of a single bulk pseudotime trajectory. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ailsci.2023.100068
skills.summary: End-to-end CellST pipeline that turns time-course scRNA-seq expression matrices (e.g. 38,731 cells x 11,588 genes zebrafish embryogenesis Drop-seq data) into individual cell fate trajectories and dynamic gene networks, instead of a single bulk pseudotime trajectory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are a single time point or lack a temporal design — optimal transport alignment between adjacent time points and trajectory construction are not applicable. Only a bulk population-average trajectory is needed and per-cell resolution is unnecessary; the article notes most existing methods already construct such bulk trajectories. Expression data are so low-dimensional or small-sample that classical alignment measures (Euclidean distance, Pearson correlation) remain valid, making the OT-based alignment unnecessary.

skills.name: time-course-simulation-design
skills.search_text: time-course-simulation-design Use when benchmarking circadian or cell-cycle phase-inference methods on droplet-based scRNA-seq data and you need controlled simulations with ground-truth phases across library sizes, cell counts, and sampling conditions. Evaluating on real experimental scRNA-seq data where no ground-truth single-cell circadian phases exist — the theoretical optimum comparison is only possible under a known generative model Plate-based scRNA-seq studies where sparse-droplet library-size effects (median UMIs of 3000–20000) are not the concern being benchmarked Non-circadian oscillatory processes (e.g., cell cycle) where the ~20-gene core clock gene set and 24 h sinusoidal assumption do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Design simulated circadian time-course scRNA-seq benchmark datasets with known ground-truth cell phases, generated from Tempo's Negative Binomial generative model, to quantify how closely a phase-inference method approaches the theoretical optimum. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34185-w
skills.summary: Design simulated circadian time-course scRNA-seq benchmark datasets with known ground-truth cell phases, generated from Tempo's Negative Binomial generative model, to quantify how closely a phase-inference method approaches the theoretical optimum.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating on real experimental scRNA-seq data where no ground-truth single-cell circadian phases exist — the theoretical optimum comparison is only possible under a known generative model Plate-based scRNA-seq studies where sparse-droplet library-size effects (median UMIs of 3000–20000) are not the concern being benchmarked Non-circadian oscillatory processes (e.g., cell cycle) where the ~20-gene core clock gene set and 24 h sinusoidal assumption do not apply

skills.description: Use when analyzing time-series scRNA-seq data where cell asynchrony must be corrected via pseudotime and the goal is to identify genes or cell subclusters whose abundance fluctuates significantly over pseudotime.
skills.name: time-dependent-covariate-modeling
skills.search_text: time-dependent-covariate-modeling Use when analyzing time-series scRNA-seq data where cell asynchrony must be corrected via pseudotime and the goal is to identify genes or cell subclusters whose abundance fluctuates significantly over pseudotime. Data are not time-series or no pseudotime/trajectory information is available — the time-dependent covariate requires ordered cells along a trajectory The analysis goal is static differential expression between predefined conditions rather than fluctuations along pseudotime (e.g. plain Monocle or tradeSeq-style DE suffices) Trajectory inference has not been performed and 'full'-mode preprocessing (gene filtering, scran normalization, root-type selection) is outside the user's scope http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 scTITANS' time-dependent covariate analysis fits a curve for each gene's relative abundance (and each subcluster's cell counts) along Monocle3-derived pseudotime, tests the complete model against a flat-line null with an F statistic, and assigns bootstrap-derived q-values to call time-varying genes and subclusters in time-series scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.07.016
skills.summary: scTITANS' time-dependent covariate analysis fits a curve for each gene's relative abundance (and each subcluster's cell counts) along Monocle3-derived pseudotime, tests the complete model against a flat-line null with an F statistic, and assigns bootstrap-derived q-values to call time-varying genes and subclusters in time-series scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not time-series or no pseudotime/trajectory information is available — the time-dependent covariate requires ordered cells along a trajectory The analysis goal is static differential expression between predefined conditions rather than fluctuations along pseudotime (e.g. plain Monocle or tradeSeq-style DE suffices) Trajectory inference has not been performed and 'full'-mode preprocessing (gene filtering, scran normalization, root-type selection) is outside the user's scope

skills.description: Use when a time-series RNA-Seq count table has been discretized and pairwise mutual information computed for candidate edges, and undirected edges must be oriented TF->TG with a regulation sign.
skills.name: time-lag-edge-direction-sign-estimation
skills.search_text: time-lag-edge-direction-sign-estimation Use when a time-series RNA-Seq count table has been discretized and pairwise mutual information computed for candidate edges, and undirected edges must be oriented TF->TG with a regulation sign. Input expression data are not time series (no adjacent time-point pairs exist, so MSD-based time lag cannot be estimated) You only need undirected co-regulation scores — plain mutual information tools such as ARACNE or minet suffice without the lag/orientation step You need a fully refined network with TF binding motifs and curated database interactions — this skill only produces the initial, MI-based GRN before refinement http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Orients candidate TF-target edges in an initial GRN inferred by mutual information (as in Augusta) and assigns positive/negative regulation signs using the transcriptional time lag, identified via the most significant difference (MSD) among adjacent pairs of time points in the expression time series. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2024.01.013
skills.summary: Orients candidate TF-target edges in an initial GRN inferred by mutual information (as in Augusta) and assigns positive/negative regulation signs using the transcriptional time lag, identified via the most significant difference (MSD) among adjacent pairs of time points in the expression time series.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression data are not time series (no adjacent time-point pairs exist, so MSD-based time lag cannot be estimated) You only need undirected co-regulation scores — plain mutual information tools such as ARACNE or minet suffice without the lag/orientation step You need a fully refined network with TF binding motifs and curated database interactions — this skill only produces the initial, MI-based GRN before refinement

skills.description: Use when a MAPiT-transformed pseudotime trajectory must be validated against ground-truth real-time kinetics, e.g. geminin trajectories reconstructed from static flow cytometry that should match single-cell time-lapse microscopy data (Paper Fig 2).
skills.name: time-lapse-microscopy-trajectory-comparison
skills.search_text: time-lapse-microscopy-trajectory-comparison Use when a MAPiT-transformed pseudotime trajectory must be validated against ground-truth real-time kinetics, e.g. geminin trajectories reconstructed from static flow cytometry that should match single-cell time-lapse microscopy data (Paper Fig 2). The trajectory is a pseudotime ordering that has not yet been transformed to the real-time scale with MAPiT.m and preMAPiT.m — comparison would be meaningless on the pseudotime axis. The process has no independent real-time reference measurement (e.g. no time-lapse microscopy data and no labelled sampling timepoints); the paper notes such validation was only envisioned for label data. The analysis target is the spheroid spatial scale, where validation instead requires sliced spheroid cross-sections quantified by confocal microscopy (MAPiT_Spheroid_Validation.m), not time-lapse kinetics. Validation strategy in which a MAPiT-reconstructed marker trajectory (e.g. geminin kinetics from static flow cytometry of unsynchronised NCI-H460/geminin cells) is compared against independently measured single-cell time-lapse microscopy kinetics to confirm the recovered real-time scale. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-60400-z
skills.summary: Validation strategy in which a MAPiT-reconstructed marker trajectory (e.g. geminin kinetics from static flow cytometry of unsynchronised NCI-H460/geminin cells) is compared against independently measured single-cell time-lapse microscopy kinetics to confirm the recovered real-time scale.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trajectory is a pseudotime ordering that has not yet been transformed to the real-time scale with MAPiT.m and preMAPiT.m — comparison would be meaningless on the pseudotime axis. The process has no independent real-time reference measurement (e.g. no time-lapse microscopy data and no labelled sampling timepoints); the paper notes such validation was only envisioned for label data. The analysis target is the spheroid spatial scale, where validation instead requires sliced spheroid cross-sections quantified by confocal microscopy (MAPiT_Spheroid_Validation.m), not time-lapse kinetics.

skills.search_text: time-resolved-gene-module-annotation Use when you have subject- and time-point-specific gene modules from multi-subject dynamic network inference (e.g. 79 donors x 4 time points) and need to identify which GO biological processes dominate at each stimulation time point. skills.name: time-series-scrnaseq-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: time-series-scrnaseq-differential-expression-analysis Use when raw UMI count matrices from time-course scRNA-seq experiments (e.g., GSE52529 HSMM, GSE67310 MEF, GSE126954 CEED) need DEG and differential subcluster identification along pseudotime rather than per-timepoint comparisons. skills.summary: Loads and manipulates the curated TISCH-derived tumor scRNA-seq training corpus (2,157,387 cells aggregated across 93 datasets) consumed by MetaTiME's ICA-based MeC discovery module (metatime.mecmapper), enabling cohort-level operations such as leave-one-out retraining and component-stability comparison against the full-set reference of 86 meta-components.

skills.search_text: tissue-mapping-rate-statistical-comparison Use when RNA-seq reads from multiple tissue groups have been aligned (e.g., STAR Log.final.out files) and you need to quantify whether mapping-quality metrics such as % uniquely mapped or % 'too short' reads differ systematically by tissue. skills.summary: Extracts per-sample STAR alignment statistics (uniquely mapped, unmapped 'too short', and chimeric read percentages) from a two-pass RNA-seq pipeline and tests whether mapping quality differs across tissue groups (liver, abdominal fat, breast muscle) using a one-way ANOVA and a chimeric-vs-unmapped regression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is allele-specific expression testing from VCF files — that is handled by the VADT pipeline, not alignment-metric comparison. skills.description: Use when preparing multi-tissue RNA-seq genotype and transcript expression matrices (e.g. GTEx V7) for sQTL mapping and you must decide which tissues/samples pass a minimum sample-size threshold for powered within-tissue QTL testing.
skills.name: tissue-sample-cohort-selection
skills.search_text: tissue-sample-cohort-selection Use when preparing multi-tissue RNA-seq genotype and transcript expression matrices (e.g. GTEx V7) for sQTL mapping and you must decide which tissues/samples pass a minimum sample-size threshold for powered within-tissue QTL testing. Working with a single pre-defined tissue cohort whose sample size was already fixed by the study design — no per-tissue sample-size selection is needed Input expression/genotype data are not organized by tissue group (e.g. pooled cohorts or cell-line panels), so the tissue-wise >=70-sample criterion does not apply The downstream tool enforces different sample-size or tissue-criterion thresholds (e.g. GTEx V8 pipelines in broadinstitute/gtex-v8) — do not reuse the V7 48-tissue cutoff http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Selects GTEx V7 tissue sample cohorts for sQTL mapping by retaining only tissues with at least 70 samples, as required by the sqtlseeker2-nf preprocessing criterion, before applying sQTLseekeR2 gene, transcript and variant filters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2
skills.summary: Selects GTEx V7 tissue sample cohorts for sQTL mapping by retaining only tissues with at least 70 samples, as required by the sqtlseeker2-nf preprocessing criterion, before applying sQTLseekeR2 gene, transcript and variant filters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Working with a single pre-defined tissue cohort whose sample size was already fixed by the study design — no per-tissue sample-size selection is needed Input expression/genotype data are not organized by tissue group (e.g. pooled cohorts or cell-line panels), so the tissue-wise >=70-sample criterion does not apply The downstream tool enforces different sample-size or tissue-criterion thresholds (e.g. GTEx V8 pipelines in broadinstitute/gtex-v8) — do not reuse the V7 48-tissue cutoff
