skills.description: Use when matched bulk RNA-seq replicates (e.g. GSE52529 Trapnell myoblast bulk data with three biological replicates) must be normalized to define true-zero / expression-level bins against which scRNA-seq dropout imputation is judged.
skills.name: tmm-bulk-rnaseq-normalization
skills.search_text: tmm-bulk-rnaseq-normalization Use when matched bulk RNA-seq replicates (e.g. GSE52529 Trapnell myoblast bulk data with three biological replicates) must be normalized to define true-zero / expression-level bins against which scRNA-seq dropout imputation is judged. There are no matched bulk RNA-seq replicates available to define biologically-silent (true-zero) genes, e.g. only a single-cell matrix with no ground-truth reference. The bulk data are single-end samples without biological replicates, making median-across-replicates and composition-bias checking unreliable. The goal is standalone differential expression between bulk conditions rather than building reference expression bins for evaluating scRNA-seq imputation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Normalize matched bulk RNA-seq replicates with TMM followed by log2 transformation to detect and correct composition bias, so that gene-level bulk expression bins (e.g. biologically-silent zero-expression genes from Trapnell myoblast GSE52529) provide a trustworthy reference for evaluating single-cell zero retention. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-34688-x
skills.summary: Normalize matched bulk RNA-seq replicates with TMM followed by log2 transformation to detect and correct composition bias, so that gene-level bulk expression bins (e.g. biologically-silent zero-expression genes from Trapnell myoblast GSE52529) provide a trustworthy reference for evaluating single-cell zero retention.
skills.when_to_use_negative: There are no matched bulk RNA-seq replicates available to define biologically-silent (true-zero) genes, e.g. only a single-cell matrix with no ground-truth reference. The bulk data are single-end samples without biological replicates, making median-across-replicates and composition-bias checking unreliable. The goal is standalone differential expression between bulk conditions rather than building reference expression bins for evaluating scRNA-seq imputation.

skills.description: Use when you have classified tncRNA reads (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, 5'tRH, 3'tRH) mapped to tRNA loci plus flanks and want to test whether cleavage is precise/codon-dependent rather than random tRNA degradation, or to find a conserved tRF-5::tRNA interface motif.
skills.name: tncrna-cleavage-position-composition-analysis
skills.search_text: tncrna-cleavage-position-composition-analysis Use when you have classified tncRNA reads (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, 5'tRH, 3'tRH) mapped to tRNA loci plus flanks and want to test whether cleavage is precise/codon-dependent rather than random tRNA degradation, or to find a conserved tRF-5::tRNA interface motif. The goal is general tncRNA identification/annotation from raw sRNA-seq FASTQ rather than post-classification cleavage-position analysis — run the tncRNA Toolkit mapping/classification steps first The input reads are not uniquely attributable to a single tRNA locus (ambiguous multi-mapped reads were discarded if aligned more than 50 times, so unfiltered alignments would confound cleavage-position tallies) The analysis targets miRNA/piRNA/rRNA-derived small RNAs (e.g. via SPORTS1.0) rather than tRNA-derived fragments http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies nucleotide composition at tncRNA cleavage positions and groups counts by anticodon to test codon-dependent, non-random tRNA cleavage, then scores tRF-5::tRNA interface alignments to compile conserved cleavage motifs (e.g. AG::TGG) across angiosperms. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Quantifies nucleotide composition at tncRNA cleavage positions and groups counts by anticodon to test codon-dependent, non-random tRNA cleavage, then scores tRF-5::tRNA interface alignments to compile conserved cleavage motifs (e.g. AG::TGG) across angiosperms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is general tncRNA identification/annotation from raw sRNA-seq FASTQ rather than post-classification cleavage-position analysis — run the tncRNA Toolkit mapping/classification steps first The input reads are not uniquely attributable to a single tRNA locus (ambiguous multi-mapped reads were discarded if aligned more than 50 times, so unfiltered alignments would confound cleavage-position tallies) The analysis targets miRNA/piRNA/rRNA-derived small RNAs (e.g. via SPORTS1.0) rather than tRNA-derived fragments

skills.summary: Aggregates per-sample tncRNA classification outputs from the tncRNA Toolkit (tncRNAs.py) into per-species and per-subtype (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, 5'tRH, 3'tRH) totals of unique reads and distinct loci, reconciling with the 43,153 tncRNAs reported across 2,448 sRNA-seq samples from six angiosperms.

skills.description: Use when small RNA-seq reads have been mapped to a tRNA-masked artificial genome (BAM + reference FASTA available) and per-tncRNA nucleoside modification annotations (e.g. m3C, pseudouridine, dihydrouridine, m2G) are needed.

skills.search_text: tncrna-feature-annotation Use when small RNA-seq reads have been mapped to a tRNA-masked artificial genome (BAM + reference FASTA available) and per-tncRNA nucleoside modification annotations (e.g. m3C, pseudouridine, dihydrouridine, m2G) are needed. When the goal is to detect or quantify tncRNAs themselves rather than annotate their modification sites — use the upstream tncRNA prediction step of the tncRNA Toolkit (tRNAscan-SE + bowtie1 artificial-genome mapping) instead. When sequencing data is conventional RNA-seq rather than small RNA-seq — the article notes switching to tRNA-seq is needed to overcome modification biases, so calls from biased RNA-seq would be unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Predicts modified nucleoside sites on tRNA-derived non-coding RNAs (tncRNAs) using HAMR v1.2 with the eukaryotic tRNA modification model, retaining only calls on mature tRNA bodies and 50 bp leader/trailer flanks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Predicts modified nucleoside sites on tRNA-derived non-coding RNAs (tncRNAs) using HAMR v1.2 with the eukaryotic tRNA modification model, retaining only calls on mature tRNA bodies and 50 bp leader/trailer flanks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to detect or quantify tncRNAs themselves rather than annotate their modification sites — use the upstream tncRNA prediction step of the tncRNA Toolkit (tRNAscan-SE + bowtie1 artificial-genome mapping) instead. When reads have not been mapped to the tRNA-masked artificial genome with 50 nt flanks; modification calls would not be restricted to tRNA plus leader/trailer contexts. skills.description: Use when you have classified per-sample tncRNA catalogs (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, 5'tRH, 3'tRH) plus progenitor mature tRNA sequences with 50 bp flanks, and the goal is to distinguish specific endoribonucleolytic cleavage from random tRNA degradation and recover a conserved cleavage motif.

The goal is de novo tncRNA detection from raw FASTQ files (use the tncRNA Toolkit prediction pipeline instead — this skill operates on already-classified tncRNA catalogs) Analyzing non-plant or single-species datasets where the angiosperm-wide conservation of the interface motif cannot be assessed Random-degradation behavior is expected a priori (e.g. degraded total RNA libraries) — the codon-dependent non-uniformity test would not be interpretable http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 A skill for testing whether plant tncRNA generation is codon-dependent and whether tRF-5 cleavage at the tRF-5::tRNA interface is governed by a conserved nucleotide motif across angiosperms. skills.description: Use when a CSV of pre-computed log2 fold changes and adjusted p-values per gene must be screened for extreme variations across pairwise antibiotic-vs-control conditions (e.g., VAN, CPT, DEL, LZD vs untreated) using dual fold-change and significance cut-offs.
skills.name: tnseq-log2fold-change-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: tnseq-log2fold-change-threshold-filtering Use when a CSV of pre-computed log2 fold changes and adjusted p-values per gene must be screened for extreme variations across pairwise antibiotic-vs-control conditions (e.g., VAN, CPT, DEL, LZD vs untreated) using dual fold-change and significance cut-offs. The dataset lacks pre-computed fold-change and adjusted p-value columns — the README states 'your dataset should contain pre-computed fold change values (and related adjusted p-values) as columns in the CSV file' A standard four-way plot suffices and no extreme-value stratification is needed — 'multiplication factor' set to 1 'will produce a four-way plot, not the scorecard' Only one experimental condition is available, since the scorecard compares pairwise conditions and merges information across comparisons A data-driven filtering step from the Scorecard Python library that selects extreme (or moderate) expression variations in Tn-seq/RNA-seq pairwise comparisons by screening log2 fold changes and adjusted p-values, instead of preselecting genes. Applied to Staphylococcus aureus USA300 transposon insertion sequencing data it isolates quadrant-assigned genes such as VAN-linked down-regulated loci and over-expressed SAUSA300_RS03525, SAUSA300_RS04560, SAUSA300_RS08475. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00284-025-04435-3

skills.description: Use when you have a ranked list of predicted peptide-MHC candidates and an external gold-standard set of experimentally validated immunogenic labels (e.g., TESLA syn21048999), and you need to quantify whether top-k selection enriches true immunogenic neoantigens above baseline.

skills.search_text: top-k-candidate-benchmark-evaluation-against-validated-labels Use when you have a ranked list of predicted peptide-MHC candidates and an external gold-standard set of experimentally validated immunogenic labels (e.g., TESLA syn21048999), and you need to quantify whether top-k selection enriches true immunogenic neoantigens above baseline. You lack experimentally validated immunogenic labels for the candidate pMHCs — ranking alone cannot be scored and the 6.1% baseline comparison is not possible Your candidates have not passed the DeepHLApan binding/immunogenic score >0.5 and TPM >= 1 filters, so top-k lists would be dominated by low-confidence pairs You need de novo immunogenicity prediction (e.g., TCR-pMHC binding modeling), which TSNAD v2.0 explicitly does not provide http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Benchmarks a neoantigen prediction pipeline by ranking candidate peptide-MHC pairs per peptide length by DeepHLApan binding score, forming top-10/20/30/40/50 candidate lists, and scoring them against TESLA-validated immunogenic pMHC labels to compare achieved positive rates with the 6.1% TESLA baseline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.016
skills.summary: Benchmarks a neoantigen prediction pipeline by ranking candidate peptide-MHC pairs per peptide length by DeepHLApan binding score, forming top-10/20/30/40/50 candidate lists, and scoring them against TESLA-validated immunogenic pMHC labels to compare achieved positive rates with the 6.1% TESLA baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You lack experimentally validated immunogenic labels for the candidate pMHCs — ranking alone cannot be scored and the 6.1% baseline comparison is not possible Your candidates have not passed the DeepHLApan binding/immunogenic score >0.5 and TPM >= 1 filters, so top-k lists would be dominated by low-confidence pairs You need de novo immunogenicity prediction (e.g., TCR-pMHC binding modeling), which TSNAD v2.0 explicitly does not provide

skills.description: Use when you need to show that a cell-communication network's top-ranked ligand–receptor pairs depend on the edge-weighting metric (expression vs. specificity), e.g. to expose housekeeping-edge inflation in expression-ranked networks.
skills.name: top-ranked-pair-comparison-across-weightings
skills.search_text: top-ranked-pair-comparison-across-weightings Use when you need to show that a cell-communication network's top-ranked ligand–receptor pairs depend on the edge-weighting metric (expression vs. specificity), e.g. to expose housekeeping-edge inflation in expression-ranked networks. Your ligand–receptor pairs involve heteromeric complexes — NATMI does not model heteromeric complexes, heterodimerization, or co-receptor requirements You need downstream signalling consequences or spatial-context-aware communication predictions — NATMI is not designed for these (use NicheNet, SoptSC, or spatial tools instead) You need global (cross-dataset) specificity values — the specificity weights NATMI computes are local/dataset-specific and a Human Cell Atlas-based global reference was not yet available http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A NATMI-based analysis skill that ranks ligand–receptor communication edges by two alternative edge weights (mean expression vs. specificity) and compares the resulting top-20 lists, demonstrating that weighting choice substantially changes which ligand–receptor pairs and cell-type pairs appear most important. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18873-z
skills.summary: A NATMI-based analysis skill that ranks ligand–receptor communication edges by two alternative edge weights (mean expression vs. specificity) and compares the resulting top-20 lists, demonstrating that weighting choice substantially changes which ligand–receptor pairs and cell-type pairs appear most important.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your ligand–receptor pairs involve heteromeric complexes — NATMI does not model heteromeric complexes, heterodimerization, or co-receptor requirements You need downstream signalling consequences or spatial-context-aware communication predictions — NATMI is not designed for these (use NicheNet, SoptSC, or spatial tools instead) You need global (cross-dataset) specificity values — the specificity weights NATMI computes are local/dataset-specific and a Human Cell Atlas-based global reference was not yet available

skills.description: Use when a per-sample parameter/feature matrix (rows = parameters, columns = samples) must be reduced to its most variable features before training or evaluating a cross-cohort classifier on sample-level labels.
skills.name: top-variable-feature-selection-sample-level
skills.search_text: top-variable-feature-selection-sample-level Use when a per-sample parameter/feature matrix (rows = parameters, columns = samples) must be reduced to its most variable features before training or evaluating a cross-cohort classifier on sample-level labels. When classification is at the single-cell level rather than the sample level — this selection is designed for per-sample parameter matrices When the parameter matrix already contains few features (selection by SD adds no value and may drop discriminative low-variance features) When the task is differential expression or integration itself rather than ML-based prediction of sample characteristics http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Selects the top-N most variable sample-specific parameters (by standard deviation across samples) from a parameter matrix such as GEDI's Q matrix, to reduce noise before training a sample-level classifier like the SVM used for COVID-19 vs. healthy prediction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50963-0
skills.summary: Selects the top-N most variable sample-specific parameters (by standard deviation across samples) from a parameter matrix such as GEDI's Q matrix, to reduce noise before training a sample-level classifier like the SVM used for COVID-19 vs. healthy prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When classification is at the single-cell level rather than the sample level — this selection is designed for per-sample parameter matrices When the parameter matrix already contains few features (selection by SD adds no value and may drop discriminative low-variance features) When the task is differential expression or integration itself rather than ML-based prediction of sample characteristics

skills.description: Use when preparing raw scRNA-seq count matrices (cells x genes) as input to EDGE or a similar ensemble feature-extraction method, and you need log-normalization plus a top-variable-gene filter to reduce dimensionality of the candidate gene space.
skills.name: top-variable-gene-selection
skills.search_text: top-variable-gene-selection Use when preparing raw scRNA-seq count matrices (cells x genes) as input to EDGE or a similar ensemble feature-extraction method, and you need log-normalization plus a top-variable-gene filter to reduce dimensionality of the candidate gene space. Input is already log-normalized and gene-filtered (e.g., a cells-by-genes log matrix from a prior pipeline step) — re-filtering could discard signal genes The dataset is simulated with Splatter and fewer than 500 genes exist — the 500-gene top-variable filter is unnecessary and the real-dataset 1000-gene rule does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Preprocesses scRNA-seq count matrices by library-size normalization (scaling to median totals, log2(x+1) transformation) and restricting to the most variable genes (1000 for real datasets, 500 for simulated) before running EDGE feature gene identification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19465-7
skills.summary: Preprocesses scRNA-seq count matrices by library-size normalization (scaling to median totals, log2(x+1) transformation) and restricting to the most variable genes (1000 for real datasets, 500 for simulated) before running EDGE feature gene identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already log-normalized and gene-filtered (e.g., a cells-by-genes log matrix from a prior pipeline step) — re-filtering could discard signal genes The dataset is simulated with Splatter and fewer than 500 genes exist — the 500-gene top-variable filter is unnecessary and the real-dataset 1000-gene rule does not apply

skills.description: Use when you have a fitted GEDI model's sample-specific manifold parameter matrix (Q) and need a sample-level 2D embedding showing that samples cluster by one covariate after regressing out another.
skills.name: top-variable-parameter-selection
skills.search_text: top-variable-parameter-selection Use when you have a fitted GEDI model's sample-specific manifold parameter matrix (Q) and need a sample-level 2D embedding showing that samples cluster by one covariate after regressing out another. When the analysis target is cell-level latent embedding rather than sample-level manifold parameters — GEDI's cell embeddings come from the model itself, not this post-hoc procedure When a covariate group has only one sample (the workflow restricts to technologies with rowSums > 1) When sample-specific translation vectors Δoi have not been excluded — including them confounds the manifold-parameter encoding http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A post-hoc procedure for encoding and visualizing GEDI-learned sample-specific manifold parameters: regress out a covariate (technology or donor), select the top 20 most variable parameters, run PCA via SVD, and embed with UMAP to reproduce Fig. 2a/2d-style sample embeddings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50963-0
skills.summary: A post-hoc procedure for encoding and visualizing GEDI-learned sample-specific manifold parameters: regress out a covariate (technology or donor), select the top 20 most variable parameters, run PCA via SVD, and embed with UMAP to reproduce Fig. 2a/2d-style sample embeddings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis target is cell-level latent embedding rather than sample-level manifold parameters — GEDI's cell embeddings come from the model itself, not this post-hoc procedure When a covariate group has only one sample (the workflow restricts to technologies with rowSums > 1) When sample-specific translation vectors Δoi have not been excluded — including them confounds the manifold-parameter encoding

skills.description: Use when a fitted CODAL/MIRA topic model is available and you need per-topic gene rankings from the beta matrix to test whether a topic captures a specific cell-type identity program or to interpret topics biologically.
skills.name: topic-association-matrix-extraction
skills.search_text: topic-association-matrix-extraction Use when a fitted CODAL/MIRA topic model is available and you need per-topic gene rankings from the beta matrix to test whether a topic captures a specific cell-type identity program or to interpret topics biologically. The model has not been fitted yet — this skill operates on an already-trained CODAL/MIRA topic model's beta matrix, not raw counts The question is batch correction or cell-state integration itself rather than interpreting topics as gene programs (use CODAL integration skill instead) The gene set of interest lacks ontology annotation or cell-type-specific log-fold changes, so the enrichment/correlation validation is impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extracts the Ntopics x Ngenes topic association matrix (beta) from a fitted CODAL/MIRA expression topic model so individual topics can be linked to gene-level signatures (e.g., ranking Topic 14's top 200 genes for ontology enrichment and log-fold-change correlation). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39494-2
skills.summary: Extracts the Ntopics x Ngenes topic association matrix (beta) from a fitted CODAL/MIRA expression topic model so individual topics can be linked to gene-level signatures (e.g., ranking Topic 14's top 200 genes for ontology enrichment and log-fold-change correlation).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model has not been fitted yet — this skill operates on an already-trained CODAL/MIRA topic model's beta matrix, not raw counts The question is batch correction or cell-state integration itself rather than interpreting topics as gene programs (use CODAL integration skill instead) The gene set of interest lacks ontology annotation or cell-type-specific log-fold changes, so the enrichment/correlation validation is impossible

skills.description: Use when an interpretable scRNA-seq topic model (MIRA/CODAL) has been fitted and you need a gene set representing one topic's biological program, plus a background, to test motif or pathway enrichment among topic-ranked genes.
skills.name: topic-based-gene-set-selection
skills.search_text: topic-based-gene-set-selection Use when an interpretable scRNA-seq topic model (MIRA/CODAL) has been fitted and you need a gene set representing one topic's biological program, plus a background, to test motif or pathway enrichment among topic-ranked genes. The gene set is already defined by an external source (e.g. curated marker list or differential expression table) — ranking by topic contribution would duplicate or distort it No interpretable topic model has been fitted, or topic loadings are confounded by batch effects because technical correction (CODAL) was not applied The question requires genome-wide genes rather than the HVG-filtered panel (genes failing the 30-count filter are absent from the model and cannot be ranked) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Extracts a biologically coherent gene set by ranking genes on their contribution to a single interpretable topic in a CODAL/MIRA expression topic model (e.g. the top 200 genes of topic 4, upregulated in proerythroblast cells), retaining the remaining highly variable genes as a matched background set for downstream enrichment testing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39494-2
skills.summary: Extracts a biologically coherent gene set by ranking genes on their contribution to a single interpretable topic in a CODAL/MIRA expression topic model (e.g. the top 200 genes of topic 4, upregulated in proerythroblast cells), retaining the remaining highly variable genes as a matched background set for downstream enrichment testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene set is already defined by an external source (e.g. curated marker list or differential expression table) — ranking by topic contribution would duplicate or distort it No interpretable topic model has been fitted, or topic loadings are confounded by batch effects because technical correction (CODAL) was not applied The question requires genome-wide genes rather than the HVG-filtered panel (genes failing the 30-count filter are absent from the model and cannot be ranked)

skills.description: Use when scETM topics have been flagged as differentially expressed (e.g., AD topics 12 and 58 at permutation p ≤ 1e-5) and their biological character must be confirmed from gene loadings.
skills.name: topic-gene-loading-interpretation
skills.search_text: topic-gene-loading-interpretation Use when scETM topics have been flagged as differentially expressed (e.g., AD topics 12 and 58 at permutation p ≤ 1e-5) and their biological character must be confirmed from gene loadings. When no topics have been called significant by the differential abundance test — loading inspection is most meaningful for pre-selected topics When the goal is batch correction or cell-type clustering rather than topic interpretability (tools like Harmony or Scanorama are more appropriate) When the gene embedding matrix ρ was fixed (trainable_gene_emb_dim = 0 in p-scETM) and topic-gene associations are constrained by external pathway sets rather than learned from data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Interpret scETM-learned topics by inspecting the topic gene loadings (varm['rho']) and topic embeddings (uns['alpha']) to characterize topics as biologically meaningful, disease-related pathways — e.g., confirming mitochondrial gene enrichment for topic 58 in the Alzheimer's Disease differential analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25534-2
skills.summary: Interpret scETM-learned topics by inspecting the topic gene loadings (varm['rho']) and topic embeddings (uns['alpha']) to characterize topics as biologically meaningful, disease-related pathways — e.g., confirming mitochondrial gene enrichment for topic 58 in the Alzheimer's Disease differential analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no topics have been called significant by the differential abundance test — loading inspection is most meaningful for pre-selected topics When the goal is batch correction or cell-type clustering rather than topic interpretability (tools like Harmony or Scanorama are more appropriate) When the gene embedding matrix ρ was fixed (trainable_gene_emb_dim = 0 in p-scETM) and topic-gene associations are constrained by external pathway sets rather than learned from data

skills.description: Use when you have an Ntopics x Ngenes topic association matrix (beta) from a fitted CODAL/MIRA topic model and need to interpret an individual topic as a gene program, e.
skills.name: topic-gene-ranking
skills.search_text: topic-gene-ranking Use when you have an Ntopics x Ngenes topic association matrix (beta) from a fitted CODAL/MIRA topic model and need to interpret an individual topic as a gene program, e. The topic model was not fit with CODAL/MIRA and no beta (topic association) matrix exists — topic weights from non-interpretable latent embeddings cannot be ranked as gene programs. No ontology-defined gene membership set exists for the target cell type, since the Fisher's exact contingency table requires a defined gene universe and ontology-member counts. You want batch-effect correction itself rather than interpretation of an already-fitted topic model — use CODAL integration as a preprocessing step instead. Ranks genes by their weight in a specific topic (e.g., Topic 14) from a fitted CODAL/MIRA expression topic model β matrix, retains the top 200 genes per the paper's convention, and tests whether that gene set is enriched for ontology-defined cell-identity programs (e.g., HuBMAP CD16+ monocyte genes) via a one-sided Fisher's exact test. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39494-2
skills.summary: Ranks genes by their weight in a specific topic (e.g., Topic 14) from a fitted CODAL/MIRA expression topic model β matrix, retains the top 200 genes per the paper's convention, and tests whether that gene set is enriched for ontology-defined cell-identity programs (e.g., HuBMAP CD16+ monocyte genes) via a one-sided Fisher's exact test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The topic model was not fit with CODAL/MIRA and no beta (topic association) matrix exists — topic weights from non-interpretable latent embeddings cannot be ranked as gene programs. No ontology-defined gene membership set exists for the target cell type, since the Fisher's exact contingency table requires a defined gene universe and ontology-member counts. You want batch-effect correction itself rather than interpretation of an already-fitted topic model — use CODAL integration as a preprocessing step instead.

skills.description: Use when you have trained an scETM model (e.g. 100-topic model on HP, AD, or MDD AnnData) and need interpretable per-topic gene rankings to test topics against known pathway gene sets via GSEA.
skills.name: topic-gene-scoring-from-embeddings
skills.search_text: topic-gene-scoring-from-embeddings Use when you have trained an scETM model (e.g. 100-topic model on HP, AD, or MDD AnnData) and need interpretable per-topic gene rankings to test topics against known pathway gene sets via GSEA. Input is raw counts or cell embeddings only — gene scoring requires the learned rho and alpha matrices from a trained scETM model, not cell-level data The model variant is p-scETM with the gene embedding matrix rho fixed to a pathways-by-genes matrix, since pathway structure is already imposed and scoring against the same gene sets is circular Genes in the scRNA-seq data do not sufficiently overlap the pathway gene sets after filtering (pathways must contain more than 5 genes to be kept) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Score genes for each topic learned by the scETM embedded topic model by combining the learned gene embedding matrix (rho) with the topic embedding matrix (alpha), producing per-topic gene rankings suitable for downstream gene set enrichment analysis of pathway associations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25534-2
skills.summary: Score genes for each topic learned by the scETM embedded topic model by combining the learned gene embedding matrix (rho) with the topic embedding matrix (alpha), producing per-topic gene rankings suitable for downstream gene set enrichment analysis of pathway associations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw counts or cell embeddings only — gene scoring requires the learned rho and alpha matrices from a trained scETM model, not cell-level data The model variant is p-scETM with the gene embedding matrix rho fixed to a pathways-by-genes matrix, since pathway structure is already imposed and scoring against the same gene sets is circular Genes in the scRNA-seq data do not sufficiently overlap the pathway gene sets after filtering (pathways must contain more than 5 genes to be kept)

skills.description: Use when STdeconvolve has produced per-topic transcriptional profiles (beta) and cell-type proportions (theta) from multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST data and the recovered topics must be biologically labeled via marker genes.
skills.name: topic-marker-gene-annotation
skills.search_text: topic-marker-gene-annotation Use when STdeconvolve has produced per-topic transcriptional profiles (beta) and cell-type proportions (theta) from multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST data and the recovered topics must be biologically labeled via marker genes. When a suitable single-cell RNA-seq reference exists and supervised methods like SPOTlight, RCTD, or spatialDWLS provide cell-type identities directly When topics cannot be matched to any known marker genes because the tissue or cell types are poorly characterized When the ST data cover sub-cellular pixel resolution or thin structures spanning only a few pixels, where deconvolution itself is unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 Annotate deconvolved cell-type transcriptional profiles (LDA beta topics) from STdeconvolve by inspecting top genes per topic and matching them to known marker genes, e.g. Myh6 for atrium, Myh7 for ventricle, Apoa2 for liver, Hba.a2 for blood vessels, and Purkinje/Bergmann glia signatures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30033-z
skills.summary: Annotate deconvolved cell-type transcriptional profiles (LDA beta topics) from STdeconvolve by inspecting top genes per topic and matching them to known marker genes, e.g. Myh6 for atrium, Myh7 for ventricle, Apoa2 for liver, Hba.a2 for blood vessels, and Purkinje/Bergmann glia signatures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a suitable single-cell RNA-seq reference exists and supervised methods like SPOTlight, RCTD, or spatialDWLS provide cell-type identities directly When topics cannot be matched to any known marker genes because the tissue or cell types are poorly characterized When the ST data cover sub-cellular pixel resolution or thin structures spanning only a few pixels, where deconvolution itself is unreliable

skills.description: Use when analyzing Perturb-Seq/CROP-seq expression profiles plus per-cell perturbation labels (control labeled 'CTRL') to quantitatively prioritize individual gene perturbation effects at single-cell granularity.
skills.name: topic-model-based-perturbation-effect-ranking
skills.search_text: topic-model-based-perturbation-effect-ranking Use when analyzing Perturb-Seq/CROP-seq expression profiles plus per-cell perturbation labels (control labeled 'CTRL') to quantitatively prioritize individual gene perturbation effects at single-cell granularity. Input is raw FASTQ data — MUSIC starts from the gene expression profile, not fastq data Perturbations with perturbed cells lower than 30 (default) — MUSIC does not consider them in ranking Perturbations whose corresponding gene expression values are all zero among all the cells — they are filtered directly before ranking http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 MUSIC's topic-modeling pipeline that ranks gene perturbation effects from single-cell CRISPR screening data: after QC, imputation (SAVER) and cell filtering, it builds topic models on the entire screen dataset, automatically selects the optimal topic number, computes cell-level topic distributions, and prioritizes perturbations via overall and topic-specific rankings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10216-x
skills.summary: MUSIC's topic-modeling pipeline that ranks gene perturbation effects from single-cell CRISPR screening data: after QC, imputation (SAVER) and cell filtering, it builds topic models on the entire screen dataset, automatically selects the optimal topic number, computes cell-level topic distributions, and prioritizes perturbations via overall and topic-specific rankings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ data — MUSIC starts from the gene expression profile, not fastq data Perturbations with perturbed cells lower than 30 (default) — MUSIC does not consider them in ranking Perturbations whose corresponding gene expression values are all zero among all the cells — they are filtered directly before ranking

skills.description: Use when preparing pooled CRISPR screening combined with single-cell RNA-seq data (Perturb-seq/CROP-seq/CROP-seq expression profile + sgRNA perturbation assignments) for topic modeling, and you must remove cells with invalid sgRNA edits and under-represented perturbations.
skills.name: topic-model-input-preprocessing
skills.search_text: topic-model-input-preprocessing Use when preparing pooled CRISPR screening combined with single-cell RNA-seq data (Perturb-seq/CROP-seq/CROP-seq expression profile + sgRNA perturbation assignments) for topic modeling, and you must remove cells with invalid sgRNA edits and under-represented perturbations. Input is raw FASTQ or fastq-level data — MUSIC's starting point is a gene expression profile, not fastq data Data is already filtered/QC-passed and has fewer than 30 cells per perturbation — the 30-cell minimum would incorrectly drop intended perturbations CRISPRi (CRISPR interference) screens — MUSIC's off-target analysis only supports knockout data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 MUSIC's data preprocessing step that cleans single-cell CRISPR screening data (e.g. CROP-seq expression_profile.txt plus perturb_information.txt) before topic model building by filtering perturbed cells with invalid edits and filtering perturbations represented by too few cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10216-x
skills.summary: MUSIC's data preprocessing step that cleans single-cell CRISPR screening data (e.g. CROP-seq expression_profile.txt plus perturb_information.txt) before topic model building by filtering perturbed cells with invalid edits and filtering perturbations represented by too few cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ or fastq-level data — MUSIC's starting point is a gene expression profile, not fastq data Data is already filtered/QC-passed and has fewer than 30 cells per perturbation — the 30-cell minimum would incorrectly drop intended perturbations CRISPRi (CRISPR interference) screens — MUSIC's off-target analysis only supports knockout data

skills.description: Use when you have raw scRNA-seq count data in an AnnData object with batch_indices (and optionally cell_types) and need unsupervised cell embeddings for clustering, batch integration, or downstream benchmarking against methods like Harmony, LIGER, scVI, or Scanorama.
skills.name: topic-model-unsupervised-training
skills.search_text: topic-model-unsupervised-training Use when you have raw scRNA-seq count data in an AnnData object with batch_indices (and optionally cell_types) and need unsupervised cell embeddings for clustering, batch integration, or downstream benchmarking against methods like Harmony, LIGER, scVI, or Scanorama. The input is already a reduced embedding or feature table — scETM requires raw cells-by-genes count data in AnnData format The analysis requires correcting multiple categorical batch variables or numerical/continuous covariates (e.g. subject age) — the current model handles only a single categorical batch variable Multi-omic integration (scRNA-seq with protein or scATAC-seq) is needed — this is not yet implemented in scETM http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train the scETM generative topic model on a cells-by-genes AnnData matrix without cell-type supervision, using batched gradient descent via UnsupervisedTrainer, to produce interpretable cell, gene, and topic embeddings for single-cell RNA-seq clustering and integration. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25534-2
skills.summary: Train the scETM generative topic model on a cells-by-genes AnnData matrix without cell-type supervision, using batched gradient descent via UnsupervisedTrainer, to produce interpretable cell, gene, and topic embeddings for single-cell RNA-seq clustering and integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a reduced embedding or feature table — scETM requires raw cells-by-genes count data in AnnData format The analysis requires correcting multiple categorical batch variables or numerical/continuous covariates (e.g. subject age) — the current model handles only a single categorical batch variable Multi-omic integration (scRNA-seq with protein or scATAC-seq) is needed — this is not yet implemented in scETM

skills.description: Use when fitting graded LDA topic models to single-cell CRISPR screening (Perturb-seq/CROP-seq/CRISP-seq) expression data and you must choose the optimal topic number in a data-driven manner rather than fixing it arbitrarily.
skills.name: topic-number-model-selection
skills.search_text: topic-number-model-selection Use when fitting graded LDA topic models to single-cell CRISPR screening (Perturb-seq/CROP-seq/CRISP-seq) expression data and you must choose the optimal topic number in a data-driven manner rather than fixing it arbitrarily. When the analysis is a standard cell-type clustering task rather than perturbation-effect topic modeling of single-cell CRISPR screening data — ordinary LDA topic-count heuristics or clustering metrics are more appropriate When expression values are not normalized/rounded for topic modeling or the input is raw FASTQ data — MUSIC requires gene expression profiles as input, not fastq When perturbations with fewer than 30 perturbed cells or invalid edits have not yet been filtered — topic modeling on unfiltered data yields unreliable topic profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Data-driven selection of the optimal number of topics for graded LDA topic models fitted to single-cell CRISPR screening data in MUSIC, by scoring candidate models (topic_number = 4:6) with topic specificity, purity, and their combination. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10216-x
skills.summary: Data-driven selection of the optimal number of topics for graded LDA topic models fitted to single-cell CRISPR screening data in MUSIC, by scoring candidate models (topic_number = 4:6) with topic specificity, purity, and their combination.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis is a standard cell-type clustering task rather than perturbation-effect topic modeling of single-cell CRISPR screening data — ordinary LDA topic-count heuristics or clustering metrics are more appropriate When expression values are not normalized/rounded for topic modeling or the input is raw FASTQ data — MUSIC requires gene expression profiles as input, not fastq When perturbations with fewer than 30 perturbed cells or invalid edits have not yet been filtered — topic modeling on unfiltered data yields unreliable topic profiles

skills.description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq count matrix (genes × cells) and want robust, interpretable latent topics via penalized LDA, e.g. reproducing the pLDA vignette simulation and exporting topic-word distributions.
skills.name: topic-word-probability-estimation
skills.search_text: topic-word-probability-estimation Use when you have a scRNA-seq count matrix (genes × cells) and want robust, interpretable latent topics via penalized LDA, e.g. reproducing the pLDA vignette simulation and exporting topic-word distributions. Data are not scRNA-seq counts where cells can be modeled as documents of gene 'words' (the LDA document–word analogy does not fit) The goal requires annotated cell-type labels rather than unsupervised latent topics http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fits a penalized Latent Dirichlet Allocation (pLDA) model to scRNA-seq count data, treating genes as words, cells as documents, and latent biological functions as topics, and exports the estimated topic-word probability matrix and per-cell topic proportions. The penalty increases robustness of the estimation so the fitted topics are interpretable with biological functions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s12561-021-09304-8
skills.summary: Fits a penalized Latent Dirichlet Allocation (pLDA) model to scRNA-seq count data, treating genes as words, cells as documents, and latent biological functions as topics, and exports the estimated topic-word probability matrix and per-cell topic proportions. The penalty increases robustness of the estimation so the fitted topics are interpretable with biological functions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not scRNA-seq counts where cells can be modeled as documents of gene 'words' (the LDA document–word analogy does not fit) The goal requires annotated cell-type labels rather than unsupervised latent topics

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA/ATAC/ADT modalities must be reduced to a structure-preserving latent space (e.g., PCA-reduced PBMC RNA, LSI-reduced PBMC ATAC, BM RNA/ADT matrices) before manifold alignment or benchmarking projection methods.
skills.name: topological-autoencoder-embedding
skills.search_text: topological-autoencoder-embedding Use when single-cell RNA/ATAC/ADT modalities must be reduced to a structure-preserving latent space (e.g., PCA-reduced PBMC RNA, LSI-reduced PBMC ATAC, BM RNA/ADT matrices) before manifold alignment or benchmarking projection methods. The data already has a latent embedding and only modality alignment is needed — use run_scTopoGAN directly on existing manifolds You need cell-type labels or supervised structure in the projection — topoAE is an unsupervised, per-modality embedding method Modalities are already low-dimensional in a shared space — computing a new topoAE embedding discards it http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes low-dimensional manifold embeddings (8-dimensional latents) of single-cell modalities using a Topological Autoencoder (topoAE), the first stage of the scTopoGAN pipeline before topology-guided GAN alignment. topoAE better preserves original data structure in low-dimensional representations than regular AE, VAE, and UMAP. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad171
skills.summary: Computes low-dimensional manifold embeddings (8-dimensional latents) of single-cell modalities using a Topological Autoencoder (topoAE), the first stage of the scTopoGAN pipeline before topology-guided GAN alignment. topoAE better preserves original data structure in low-dimensional representations than regular AE, VAE, and UMAP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data already has a latent embedding and only modality alignment is needed — use run_scTopoGAN directly on existing manifolds You need cell-type labels or supervised structure in the projection — topoAE is an unsupervised, per-modality embedding method Modalities are already low-dimensional in a shared space — computing a new topoAE embedding discards it

skills.description: Use when training or evaluating scTopoGAN: you need to quantify how well the topology of the source ATAC manifold is preserved after projection into the RNA target space, at training checkpoints (epochs 500–1000).
skills.name: topological-loss-computation
skills.search_text: topological-loss-computation Use when training or evaluating scTopoGAN: you need to quantify how well the topology of the source ATAC manifold is preserved after projection into the RNA target space, at training checkpoints (epochs 500–1000). When the two modalities share overlapping cells or features — the article notes current integration methods that rely on overlapping features or cells, and scTopoGAN/topological loss is designed for non-overlapping single-modality datasets When evaluating the quality of per-modality latent representations themselves (use TopoAE_benchmark.py comparing topoAE with Autoencoder, VAE, or UMAP, not the GAN alignment loss) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes the topological loss (Eq. 2 in scTopoGAN) between the source-modality topoAE manifold and its GAN-projected output in target space, serving both as the topology-preserving training objective and as an alignment-quality diagnostic. In scTopoGAN this loss was negatively correlated with label-matching performance (Pearson r ≈ −0.73 for Celltype, −0.67 for Subcelltype across 40 GAN initializations). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad171
skills.summary: Computes the topological loss (Eq. 2 in scTopoGAN) between the source-modality topoAE manifold and its GAN-projected output in target space, serving both as the topology-preserving training objective and as an alignment-quality diagnostic. In scTopoGAN this loss was negatively correlated with label-matching performance (Pearson r ≈ −0.73 for Celltype, −0.67 for Subcelltype across 40 GAN initializations).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the two modalities share overlapping cells or features — the article notes current integration methods that rely on overlapping features or cells, and scTopoGAN/topological loss is designed for non-overlapping single-modality datasets When evaluating the quality of per-modality latent representations themselves (use TopoAE_benchmark.py comparing topoAE with Autoencoder, VAE, or UMAP, not the GAN alignment loss)

skills.description: Use when a multi-sample bulk RNA-seq count matrix (e.g., 192-sample 5xFAD/C57BL/6J cortex and hippocampus data with age, genotype, tissue, sex traits) needs to be partitioned into co-expression modules tied to sample traits.
skills.name: topological-overlap-matrix-clustering
skills.search_text: topological-overlap-matrix-clustering Use when a multi-sample bulk RNA-seq count matrix (e.g., 192-sample 5xFAD/C57BL/6J cortex and hippocampus data with age, genotype, tissue, sex traits) needs to be partitioned into co-expression modules tied to sample traits. The goal is comparison against an external gene list or another WGCNA object rather than de novo module detection — use PyWGCNA's comparison tutorials instead The input is not a raw/well-expressed count matrix (e.g., already-aggregated module eigengenes), since preprocessing per the Data_format tutorial is a prerequisite step Only a handful of samples are available, so scale-free topology fitting and TOM-based module detection are not well supported http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies gene co-expression modules from bulk RNA-seq count matrices by building a soft-thresholded correlation adjacency, converting it to a topological overlap matrix (TOM), and cutting TOM dissimilarity with dynamic tree cut, as implemented in PyWGCNA. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad415
skills.summary: Identifies gene co-expression modules from bulk RNA-seq count matrices by building a soft-thresholded correlation adjacency, converting it to a topological overlap matrix (TOM), and cutting TOM dissimilarity with dynamic tree cut, as implemented in PyWGCNA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is comparison against an external gene list or another WGCNA object rather than de novo module detection — use PyWGCNA's comparison tutorials instead The input is not a raw/well-expressed count matrix (e.g., already-aggregated module eigengenes), since preprocessing per the Data_format tutorial is a prerequisite step Only a handful of samples are available, so scale-free topology fitting and TOM-based module detection are not well supported

skills.description: Use when two single-cell modalities must be aligned into a common latent space without overlapping cells or features, using topology-guided GAN training on separately computed topoAE manifolds.
skills.name: topology-guided-gan-training
skills.search_text: topology-guided-gan-training Use when two single-cell modalities must be aligned into a common latent space without overlapping cells or features, using topology-guided GAN training on separately computed topoAE manifolds. The modalities share overlapping cells or features — current integration methods that rely on overlap are applicable and this fully unsupervised alignment is unnecessary You need only a low-dimensional projection of a single dataset, not cross-modality alignment — use get_TopoAE_Embeddings / TopoAE_benchmark.py instead Input is raw counts rather than pre-processed data in the Data folder format, which the scTopoGAN scripts are not set up to consume directly http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Train scTopoGAN, a topology-guided Generative Adversarial Network that aligns a source single-cell manifold (e.g., ATAC topoAE embeddings) onto a target manifold (e.g., RNA topoAE embeddings) in a fully unsupervised setting with non-overlapping cells or features. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad171
skills.summary: Train scTopoGAN, a topology-guided Generative Adversarial Network that aligns a source single-cell manifold (e.g., ATAC topoAE embeddings) onto a target manifold (e.g., RNA topoAE embeddings) in a fully unsupervised setting with non-overlapping cells or features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The modalities share overlapping cells or features — current integration methods that rely on overlap are applicable and this fully unsupervised alignment is unnecessary You need only a low-dimensional projection of a single dataset, not cross-modality alignment — use get_TopoAE_Embeddings / TopoAE_benchmark.py instead Input is raw counts rather than pre-processed data in the Data folder format, which the scTopoGAN scripts are not set up to consume directly

skills.description: Use when a ranked differential-expression gene list (e.g., scTITANS SigGenes at fdr 0.01) needs functional interpretation via GO biological-process enrichment, especially for non-model organisms like Caenorhabditis elegans.
skills.name: toppgene-enrichment-querying
skills.search_text: toppgene-enrichment-querying Use when a ranked differential-expression gene list (e.g., scTITANS SigGenes at fdr 0.01) needs functional interpretation via GO biological-process enrichment, especially for non-model organisms like Caenorhabditis elegans. The input is not a gene list from differential expression analysis (e.g., raw expression matrices or cell metadata files) — enrichment requires a defined DEG set The organism of the DEG list is unknown or unsupported, since the ToppGene query requires an explicit organism selection (e.g., C. elegans for CEED) The upstream scTITANS run has not been performed at the paper's fdr level (0.01), since the skill validates DEGs at that significance threshold http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Submit a list of differential genes (e.g., top scTITANS DEGs at fdr 0.01 from the CEED/GSE126954 C. elegans dataset) to the ToppGene Suite web service to retrieve Gene Ontology biological-process enrichment with p-values and FDR-adjusted significance, then compile the results into a structured table for biological validation of the DEG list. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.07.016
skills.summary: Submit a list of differential genes (e.g., top scTITANS DEGs at fdr 0.01 from the CEED/GSE126954 C. elegans dataset) to the ToppGene Suite web service to retrieve Gene Ontology biological-process enrichment with p-values and FDR-adjusted significance, then compile the results into a structured table for biological validation of the DEG list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a gene list from differential expression analysis (e.g., raw expression matrices or cell metadata files) — enrichment requires a defined DEG set The organism of the DEG list is unknown or unsupported, since the ToppGene query requires an explicit organism selection (e.g., C. elegans for CEED) The upstream scTITANS run has not been performed at the paper's fdr level (0.01), since the skill validates DEGs at that significance threshold

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq imputation or representation-learning pipeline needs a cell-cell graph (nodes = cells, edges = k nearest neighbors) built from a normalized, HVG-filtered expression matrix before graph contrastive learning.
skills.name: torch-geometric-graph-data-preparation
skills.search_text: torch-geometric-graph-data-preparation Use when a scRNA-seq imputation or representation-learning pipeline needs a cell-cell graph (nodes = cells, edges = k nearest neighbors) built from a normalized, HVG-filtered expression matrix before graph contrastive learning. The input is already a graph/adjacency structure rather than a tabular expression matrix — no kNN construction is needed The expression matrix has not been normalized and HVG-filtered yet; building the kNN graph on raw counts distorts cosine neighborhoods The analysis does not need cell-cell topological structure (e.g. purely gene-level statistics with no graph-based model downstream) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Constructs a kNN cell graph over scRNA-seq cells from the pre-processed expression matrix, using cosine distance and k=15 neighbors, as done in scGCL before graph contrastive learning. This preserves cell-cell topological relationships that imputation methods ignoring structure cannot use. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad098
skills.summary: Constructs a kNN cell graph over scRNA-seq cells from the pre-processed expression matrix, using cosine distance and k=15 neighbors, as done in scGCL before graph contrastive learning. This preserves cell-cell topological relationships that imputation methods ignoring structure cannot use.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a graph/adjacency structure rather than a tabular expression matrix — no kNN construction is needed The expression matrix has not been normalized and HVG-filtered yet; building the kNN graph on raw counts distorts cosine neighborhoods The analysis does not need cell-cell topological structure (e.g. purely gene-level statistics with no graph-based model downstream)

skills.description: Use when resuming PRESCIENT workflows from the `prescient process_data` output or when a downstream task (fate simulation, TF perturbation screen, UMAP plotting) needs the bundled data_pt contents.
skills.name: torch-serialized-object-handling
skills.search_text: torch-serialized-object-handling Use when resuming PRESCIENT workflows from the `prescient process_data` output or when a downstream task (fate simulation, TF perturbation screen, UMAP plotting) needs the bundled data_pt contents. Raw, unnormalized scRNA-seq files that have not been pre-processed with Seurat or scanpy — process_data expects normalized inputs Analyses needing full per-gene resolution outside PCA space — the article notes information is lost about individual genes when transforming data into PCA space Datasets whose final time point is not at steady-state — the PRESCIENT model constraint would make downstream training from data_pt invalid http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Load and work with the PRESCIENT serialized PyTorch object (data_pt), a torch .pt dictionary containing normalized gene expression, gene features, cell type annotations, time-point labels, and fitted PCA/UMAP objects, to enable downstream training, simulation, and perturbation screens. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23518-w
skills.summary: Load and work with the PRESCIENT serialized PyTorch object (data_pt), a torch .pt dictionary containing normalized gene expression, gene features, cell type annotations, time-point labels, and fitted PCA/UMAP objects, to enable downstream training, simulation, and perturbation screens.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw, unnormalized scRNA-seq files that have not been pre-processed with Seurat or scanpy — process_data expects normalized inputs Analyses needing full per-gene resolution outside PCA space — the article notes information is lost about individual genes when transforming data into PCA space Datasets whose final time point is not at steady-state — the PRESCIENT model constraint would make downstream training from data_pt invalid

skills.description: Use when recursively forecasting single-cell expression over many time steps (e.g., 72 hourly steps with predictCellFutures) and you must verify the neural ODE's predictions have not exploded beyond biologically realistic expression levels.
skills.name: total-counts-per-cell-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: total-counts-per-cell-quality-assessment Use when recursively forecasting single-cell expression over many time steps (e.g., 72 hourly steps with predictCellFutures) and you must verify the neural ODE's predictions have not exploded beyond biologically realistic expression levels. Input is a single one-step prediction rather than recursive multi-step forecasting — extreme outputs are not compounded, so the total-counts stability check is less informative Data are not log-normalized single-cell expression from paired dynamic time points (e.g., standard scRNA-seq without metabolic labeling), which RNAForecaster's training scheme requires http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A quality-control check for RNAForecaster's recursive multi-step predictions: after capping expression forecasts at an allowed maximum, per-gene predictions are summed per cell and the median total counts per cell (e.g., after 72 h of cell-cycle forecasting on scEU-seq RPE data) is computed to confirm no runaway growth of predicted expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100793
skills.summary: A quality-control check for RNAForecaster's recursive multi-step predictions: after capping expression forecasts at an allowed maximum, per-gene predictions are summed per cell and the median total counts per cell (e.g., after 72 h of cell-cycle forecasting on scEU-seq RPE data) is computed to confirm no runaway growth of predicted expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single one-step prediction rather than recursive multi-step forecasting — extreme outputs are not compounded, so the total-counts stability check is less informative Data are not log-normalized single-cell expression from paired dynamic time points (e.g., standard scRNA-seq without metabolic labeling), which RNAForecaster's training scheme requires

skills.description: Use when a gene-by-cell relative expression matrix (baseline-subtracted scRNA-seq counts ordered by genomic position) must be denoised while preserving piecewise-constant breakpoints prior to copy number segmentation.
skills.name: total-variation-expression-profile-smoothing
skills.search_text: total-variation-expression-profile-smoothing Use when a gene-by-cell relative expression matrix (baseline-subtracted scRNA-seq counts ordered by genomic position) must be denoised while preserving piecewise-constant breakpoints prior to copy number segmentation. The matrix has not yet been baseline-corrected into a relative expression matrix (no normal-cell median subtraction or gaussian baseline removal) The goal is fine-grained denoising that preserves per-gene continuous variation rather than piecewise-constant segments (higher beta values coarsen the segmentation) The tumor type has minimal genomic alterations (e.g. leukemia, pediatric cancers, ependymomas) where aneuploidy-based regularization is unsuitable http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Edge-preserving nonlinear diffusion smoothing of the relative expression matrix (genes x cells, sorted by genomic coordinate) inside SCEVAN, minimizing a total variation functional with a phi(x)=logcosh(x) prior so noise is regularized while copy number breakpoints are retained before joint segmentation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36790-9
skills.summary: Edge-preserving nonlinear diffusion smoothing of the relative expression matrix (genes x cells, sorted by genomic coordinate) inside SCEVAN, minimizing a total variation functional with a phi(x)=logcosh(x) prior so noise is regularized while copy number breakpoints are retained before joint segmentation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The matrix has not yet been baseline-corrected into a relative expression matrix (no normal-cell median subtraction or gaussian baseline removal) The goal is fine-grained denoising that preserves per-gene continuous variation rather than piecewise-constant segments (higher beta values coarsen the segmentation) The tumor type has minimal genomic alterations (e.g. leukemia, pediatric cancers, ependymomas) where aneuploidy-based regularization is unsuitable

skills.description: Use when you have a short list of differentially expressed genes (e.g. ~27 DE genes from a toxicant-exposure microarray study like cobalt-exposed rat liver cell lines) and want to test whether environmental toxic-chemical gene modules are enriched.
skills.name: toxic-chemical-gene-module-annotation
skills.search_text: toxic-chemical-gene-module-annotation Use when you have a short list of differentially expressed genes (e.g. ~27 DE genes from a toxicant-exposure microarray study like cobalt-exposed rat liver cell lines) and want to test whether environmental toxic-chemical gene modules are enriched. The gene list comes from a non-environmental factor of interest outside the database's four environmental factors (cigarette smoking, diet, infections, toxic chemicals) — the database cannot cover other exposure types Input genetic data are SNPs, CNVs or DNA methylations rather than a gene list — these data types are not yet covered by the tool You need joint or interaction odds-ratio statistics — these statistical tests are not yet included http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3321 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Annotate a differentially-expressed gene list against the E.PAGE curated toxic-chemical gene modules using Fisher exact (hypergeometric) enrichment with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, to link toxic-exposure signatures to modules such as Genotoxicity and Carcinogen. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-21988-6
skills.summary: Annotate a differentially-expressed gene list against the E.PAGE curated toxic-chemical gene modules using Fisher exact (hypergeometric) enrichment with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, to link toxic-exposure signatures to modules such as Genotoxicity and Carcinogen.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene list comes from a non-environmental factor of interest outside the database's four environmental factors (cigarette smoking, diet, infections, toxic chemicals) — the database cannot cover other exposure types Input genetic data are SNPs, CNVs or DNA methylations rather than a gene list — these data types are not yet covered by the tool You need joint or interaction odds-ratio statistics — these statistical tests are not yet included

skills.description: Use when implementing or debugging a marker-selection optimization (e.g., scGeneFit's slack LP from Eq. 4) and you need a minimal labeled toy expression matrix plus a concrete expected marker output to verify solver correctness.
skills.name: toy-dataset-validation-of-optimization-solver
skills.search_text: toy-dataset-validation-of-optimization-solver Use when implementing or debugging a marker-selection optimization (e.g., scGeneFit's slack LP from Eq. 4) and you need a minimal labeled toy expression matrix plus a concrete expected marker output to verify solver correctness. The goal is validating scGeneFit on real scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., CBMC or mouse somatosensory cortex) rather than verifying the solver logic on a small controlled toy model Cell type classes are not linearly separable or the task requires nonlinear dimension reduction — the paper notes this linear separability assumption underlies the formulation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A validation harness that reconstructs scGeneFit's sparse linear-program (slack LP, Eq. 4) marker solver with scipy.optimize.linprog and tests it on the small labeled spectral toy dataset, where the two circle-coordinate features must be selected whenever the target marker set size is >=2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21453-4
skills.summary: A validation harness that reconstructs scGeneFit's sparse linear-program (slack LP, Eq. 4) marker solver with scipy.optimize.linprog and tests it on the small labeled spectral toy dataset, where the two circle-coordinate features must be selected whenever the target marker set size is >=2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is validating scGeneFit on real scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., CBMC or mouse somatosensory cortex) rather than verifying the solver logic on a small controlled toy model Cell type classes are not linearly separable or the task requires nonlinear dimension reduction — the paper notes this linear separability assumption underlies the formulation

skills.description: Use when a locus- or family-level TE quantification tool needs an accuracy benchmark against simulated ground-truth data, especially where multi-mapping of young TEs complicates read assignment.
skills.name: tp-fp-fn-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: tp-fp-fn-accuracy-evaluation Use when a locus- or family-level TE quantification tool needs an accuracy benchmark against simulated ground-truth data, especially where multi-mapping of young TEs complicates read assignment. Analyzing real (non-simulated) scRNA-Seq data where no ground-truth TE expression profile exists — TP/FP/FN labels cannot be assigned The tool's output is already aggregated at family level only and the question is locus-level accuracy, since FP/FN per locus cannot be resolved from metagene counts Input BAMs were aligned without multi-mapping-aware settings, so the multi-mapping conditions the benchmark is designed to stress are absent http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark a TE-expression quantification method (e.g., SoloTE vs scTE) by simulating scRNA-Seq reads with known ground-truth TE expression and classifying each predicted expressed TE locus as True Positive, False Positive, or False Negative, with separate assessment of old (>10% divergence) vs young (≤10% divergence) TEs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04020-5
skills.summary: Benchmark a TE-expression quantification method (e.g., SoloTE vs scTE) by simulating scRNA-Seq reads with known ground-truth TE expression and classifying each predicted expressed TE locus as True Positive, False Positive, or False Negative, with separate assessment of old (>10% divergence) vs young (≤10% divergence) TEs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analyzing real (non-simulated) scRNA-Seq data where no ground-truth TE expression profile exists — TP/FP/FN labels cannot be assigned The tool's output is already aggregated at family level only and the question is locus-level accuracy, since FP/FN per locus cannot be resolved from metagene counts Input BAMs were aligned without multi-mapping-aware settings, so the multi-mapping conditions the benchmark is designed to stress are absent

skills.description: Use when a single sample shows a SCISSOR-detected local shape change near a TP53 splice junction and you must test whether a junction-proximal insertion is associated with retained-intron reads versus exonic reads.
skills.name: tp53-intron-retention-interpretation
skills.search_text: tp53-intron-retention-interpretation Use when a single sample shows a SCISSOR-detected local shape change near a TP53 splice junction and you must test whether a junction-proximal insertion is associated with retained-intron reads versus exonic reads. When the goal is unsupervised cohort-level discovery of shape changes (GSC/LSC) rather than read-level validation of an already-called insertion in a single sample When there is no candidate insertion or splice-site mutation at the junction to test against intron retention When the gene's reads cannot be unambiguously split into intronic (retained-intron) and exonic classes at the junction http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Read-level validation that a candidate RNA insertion at a TP53 exon-intron junction functionally drives intron retention, by tabulating insertion presence among intronic vs exonic junction reads and testing the 2x2 contingency table with Fisher's exact test. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20593-3
skills.summary: Read-level validation that a candidate RNA insertion at a TP53 exon-intron junction functionally drives intron retention, by tabulating insertion presence among intronic vs exonic junction reads and testing the 2x2 contingency table with Fisher's exact test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is unsupervised cohort-level discovery of shape changes (GSC/LSC) rather than read-level validation of an already-called insertion in a single sample When there is no candidate insertion or splice-site mutation at the junction to test against intron retention When the gene's reads cannot be unambiguously split into intronic (retained-intron) and exonic classes at the junction

skills.description: Use when you have ranked protein interaction lists (e.g., from FAVA, scLink, hdWGCNA, PCC) on scRNA-seq datasets and need a comparable accuracy metric against curated references such as KEGG or BioGRID.
skills.name: tpfp-ratio-evaluation-of-network-predictions
skills.search_text: tpfp-ratio-evaluation-of-network-predictions Use when you have ranked protein interaction lists (e.g., from FAVA, scLink, hdWGCNA, PCC) on scRNA-seq datasets and need a comparable accuracy metric against curated references such as KEGG or BioGRID. When the compared ranked lists are truncated to different lengths or count protein pairs with different direction conventions, since TP/FP ratios would not be comparable When the goal is network inference itself (VAE latent-space compression, pair ranking) rather than post-hoc accuracy assessment of already-ranked predictions When input is bulk omics data without single-cell sparseness/redundancy, the scRNA-seq-specific benchmarking context of this skill does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Benchmark inferred functional association networks by truncating each method's ranked interaction list to the top 10,000 pairs and counting true positives and false positives against KEGG Release 95 and BioGRID Release 4.4.217, summarized as TP/FP ratios per method, dataset, and reference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae010
skills.summary: Benchmark inferred functional association networks by truncating each method's ranked interaction list to the top 10,000 pairs and counting true positives and false positives against KEGG Release 95 and BioGRID Release 4.4.217, summarized as TP/FP ratios per method, dataset, and reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the compared ranked lists are truncated to different lengths or count protein pairs with different direction conventions, since TP/FP ratios would not be comparable When the goal is network inference itself (VAE latent-space compression, pair ranking) rather than post-hoc accuracy assessment of already-ranked predictions When input is bulk omics data without single-cell sparseness/redundancy, the scRNA-seq-specific benchmarking context of this skill does not apply

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ files from the disease RNA-seq datasets (GSE203206, GSE128177, GSE205867, PRJNA433105) must be converted into transcript-level TPM values compatible with CanIsoNet's transcript isoform definitions.
skills.name: tpm-abundance-aggregation
skills.search_text: tpm-abundance-aggregation Use when raw paired-end FASTQ files from the disease RNA-seq datasets (GSE203206, GSE128177, GSE205867, PRJNA433105) must be converted into transcript-level TPM values compatible with CanIsoNet's transcript isoform definitions. Input is already a transcript-level TPM or expression matrix — aggregation has already been performed and re-running Kallisto would be redundant Analysis targets the 27 PCAWG cancer types, which were processed by the prior isoform-specific interaction network study rather than by RNA-seq quantification of these four disease datasets Gene-level abundance estimates are required — this workflow deliberately quantifies at the transcript/isoform level to preserve the isoform switching definitions used in CanIsoNet http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies transcript-level abundances for the four CanIsoNet disease RNA-seq datasets (OIH, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Behcet's) with Kallisto against Ensembl GRCh37.p13 human cDNA, then aggregates per-sample TPM values into a single transcripts-by-samples matrix used downstream by CanIsoNet. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad050
skills.summary: Quantifies transcript-level abundances for the four CanIsoNet disease RNA-seq datasets (OIH, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Behcet's) with Kallisto against Ensembl GRCh37.p13 human cDNA, then aggregates per-sample TPM values into a single transcripts-by-samples matrix used downstream by CanIsoNet.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a transcript-level TPM or expression matrix — aggregation has already been performed and re-running Kallisto would be redundant Analysis targets the 27 PCAWG cancer types, which were processed by the prior isoform-specific interaction network study rather than by RNA-seq quantification of these four disease datasets Gene-level abundance estimates are required — this workflow deliberately quantifies at the transcript/isoform level to preserve the isoform switching definitions used in CanIsoNet

skills.description: Use when a transcript-level TPM matrix from an RNA-seq disease dataset (e.g. GSE203206 Alzheimer's) must be reduced to per-sample dominant isoforms to call disease-specific dMDT isoform switching events.
skills.name: tpm-expression-data-handling
skills.search_text: tpm-expression-data-handling Use when a transcript-level TPM matrix from an RNA-seq disease dataset (e.g. GSE203206 Alzheimer's) must be reduced to per-sample dominant isoforms to call disease-specific dMDT isoform switching events. Input is raw FASTQ or unquantified reads — transcript-level TPM values must already exist before MDT calling Goal is splice-junction/PSI-based isoform switching detection rather than dominant-transcript switching derived from TPM maxima Analysis targets one of the 27 PCAWG cancer types rather than the non-cancer RNA-seq datasets (OIH, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Behçet's) covered by the dMDT workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Handles transcript-per-million (TPM) expression matrices to identify per-sample Most Dominant Transcripts (MDTs) and derive disease-specific dMDT isoform switching events, following the CanIsoNet dMDT calling procedure on datasets such as Alzheimer's disease RNA-seq (GSE203206). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad050
skills.summary: Handles transcript-per-million (TPM) expression matrices to identify per-sample Most Dominant Transcripts (MDTs) and derive disease-specific dMDT isoform switching events, following the CanIsoNet dMDT calling procedure on datasets such as Alzheimer's disease RNA-seq (GSE203206).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ or unquantified reads — transcript-level TPM values must already exist before MDT calling Goal is splice-junction/PSI-based isoform switching detection rather than dominant-transcript switching derived from TPM maxima Analysis targets one of the 27 PCAWG cancer types rather than the non-cancer RNA-seq datasets (OIH, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Behçet's) covered by the dMDT workflow

skills.description: Use when a de novo transcriptome assembly (e.g., Trinity FASTA plus RNA-Seq reads) contains lowly expressed contigs that should be removed prior to CD-HIT-EST redundancy filtering, following Bellerophon's default TPM cut-off of 1.
skills.name: tpm-expression-filtering-of-contigs
skills.search_text: tpm-expression-filtering-of-contigs Use when a de novo transcriptome assembly (e.g., Trinity FASTA plus RNA-Seq reads) contains lowly expressed contigs that should be removed prior to CD-HIT-EST redundancy filtering, following Bellerophon's default TPM cut-off of 1.
