skills.summary: Uses GTEx TPM expression values as a candidate proxy for RNA-seq suitability by testing whether relative gene expression predicts MRSD (minimum required sequencing depth) across four human biosamples, quantifying the strength and limits of that proxy via correlation and distribution-overlap statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input RNA-seq data were not generated with the GTEx-like Illumina 75 bp paired-end poly-A enrichment workflow, since pre-computed MRSD scores are most accurate only for similar workflows The goal is to assess suitability for detecting allele-specific expression biases or differential gene expression, which the MRSD model cannot directly predict MRSD scores are unavailable for the gene because median splice junction coverage was 0 reads ('-' entries) — these must be excluded rather than treated as TPM-comparable values

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression matrices are log-transformed — scID requires library-depth (TPM/CPM) normalized, not log-transformed data Neither the reference nor target dataset is well clustered or contains good gene signatures — the article states scID is not a recommended approach in that case Reference and target are identical or near-duplicate datasets with no batch effect, where the DPR-vs-weighted-scoring comparison has no discriminative contrast to measure

skills.search_text: tpr-fpr-benchmark-evaluation Use when benchmarking an SVG-detection method's false positive behavior — e.g. validating that simulated noise genes are not called significant and that coordinate-permuted null data yields FPR near nominal thresholds. skills.summary: Reproduces nnSVG's simulation-based sensitivity/specificity benchmark: parameterize 1000 simulated genes (100 SVGs, 900 noise genes) from MOBP statistics on Visium DLPFC coordinates, then compute true and false positive rates at adjusted p-value cutoffs 0.01/0.05/0.10 plus coordinate-shuffled null calibration.

skills.description: Use when analyzing a sparse single-cell expression matrix with PCA/RMT and you need to separate noise bulk, sparsity-induced artifacts, and true low-rank signal via eigenvalue deviations from MP/TW laws.

skills.search_text: tracy-widom-marchenko-pastur-universality-comparison Use when analyzing a sparse single-cell expression matrix with PCA/RMT and you need to separate noise bulk, sparsity-induced artifacts, and true low-rank signal via eigenvalue deviations from MP/TW laws. Input data has already been sparsity-filtered or genes causing localization in the randomized case have been removed, so upper-edge deviations can be interpreted directly without this comparison The matrix is dense or the cell-gene matrix is so small that MP/TW asymptotic universality assumptions do not plausibly hold http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Compares the bulk eigenvalue spectrum of a single-cell covariance matrix against Marchenko-Pastur (MP) and Tracy-Widom (TW) universality predictions so that large deviations can be interpreted as candidate biological signal while deviations attributable to sparsity are first discounted via randomization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100035
skills.summary: Compares the bulk eigenvalue spectrum of a single-cell covariance matrix against Marchenko-Pastur (MP) and Tracy-Widom (TW) universality predictions so that large deviations can be interpreted as candidate biological signal while deviations attributable to sparsity are first discounted via randomization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has already been sparsity-filtered or genes causing localization in the randomized case have been removed, so upper-edge deviations can be interpreted directly without this comparison The matrix is dense or the cell-gene matrix is so small that MP/TW asymptotic universality assumptions do not plausibly hold

skills.search_text: train-test-split-benchmarking-across-datasets Use when two or more feature representations must be compared for the same classification task across several scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., Chuang, Karaayvaz, PBMC3k, Lee), using held-out test partitions and metrics such as accuracy and weighted-F1. Input is already a scored comparison table or you only need a single classifier on a single feature set — a full cross-dataset benchmark is overkill The task is de novo feature construction (k-mer matrix generation, CKG generation, or cell matrix generation) rather than evaluating already-built feature matrices No held-out labels exist — train/test benchmarking requires ground-truth cell type labels to compute accuracy and weighted-F1 Benchmarks alternative feature representations (e.g., CKG vs. gene expression features) for cell type classification by running identical train/test splits across multiple scRNA-seq datasets and multiple classifiers, then aggregating accuracy and weighted-F1 into one comparison table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102855
skills.summary: Benchmarks alternative feature representations (e.g., CKG vs. gene expression features) for cell type classification by running identical train/test splits across multiple scRNA-seq datasets and multiple classifiers, then aggregating accuracy and weighted-F1 into one comparison table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a scored comparison table or you only need a single classifier on a single feature set — a full cross-dataset benchmark is overkill The task is de novo feature construction (k-mer matrix generation, CKG generation, or cell matrix generation) rather than evaluating already-built feature matrices No held-out labels exist — train/test benchmarking requires ground-truth cell type labels to compute accuracy and weighted-F1

skills.description: Use when evaluating a supervised cell-type classifier on annotated AnnData single-cell/nuclei data where you need quantified accuracy on held-out cells and cross-sample generalization bounds.
skills.name: train-test-split-evaluation
skills.search_text: train-test-split-evaluation Use when evaluating a supervised cell-type classifier on annotated AnnData single-cell/nuclei data where you need quantified accuracy on held-out cells and cross-sample generalization bounds. Trans-species label transfer: the authors limited validation to samples within the same species because neuronal subtypes diverge significantly between species Data lacking pre-existing annotations — SIMS is supervised and requires normalized, clustered, differentially-expressed and expert-annotated labels; annotation errors propagate to the classifier Cases requiring the fastest classifier — the authors note SIMS 'is not the fastest of the methods we benchmarked' http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Benchmark SIMS label-transfer accuracy by holding out a fraction of an annotated single-nuclei dataset (e.g., 20% of the human adult cerebral cortex dataset) and measuring held-out accuracy and Macro F1, plus trans-sample (donor-holdout) generalization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2024.100581
skills.summary: Benchmark SIMS label-transfer accuracy by holding out a fraction of an annotated single-nuclei dataset (e.g., 20% of the human adult cerebral cortex dataset) and measuring held-out accuracy and Macro F1, plus trans-sample (donor-holdout) generalization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Trans-species label transfer: the authors limited validation to samples within the same species because neuronal subtypes diverge significantly between species Data lacking pre-existing annotations — SIMS is supervised and requires normalized, clustered, differentially-expressed and expert-annotated labels; annotation errors propagate to the classifier Cases requiring the fastest classifier — the authors note SIMS 'is not the fastest of the methods we benchmarked'

skills.description: Use when benchmarking cell-annotation or classification methods under controlled sample-size conditions, especially to stress-test them on closely correlated classes versus easy low-correlation classes.
skills.name: train-test-split-simulation-design
skills.search_text: train-test-split-simulation-design Use when benchmarking cell-annotation or classification methods under controlled sample-size conditions, especially to stress-test them on closely correlated classes versus easy low-correlation classes. The data contain novel/unknown cell types absent from the reference training data — NeuCA assumes all cell types in the new sample exist in the reference, and the merged-class easy task presumes exhaustive labeling. The scientific question is clustering rather than supervised label assignment using known training labels — unsupervised tools (Seurat, SC3, TSCAN) are the alternative when no training data exist. The aim is a single one-off prediction rather than a controlled size/correlation sweep — a simple train/test split without the p/n grid suffices. http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Designs controlled train/test simulation benchmarks from real PBMC scRNA-seq data by varying training proportions (p = 10%, 20%, 50%, 80%) and test sizes (n = 800, 1600, 4000) under a difficult (five highly correlated T-cell types) and an easy (merged major cell types) prediction task, then scores accuracy, ARI, and unassigned-label fractions per method. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04473-4
skills.summary: Designs controlled train/test simulation benchmarks from real PBMC scRNA-seq data by varying training proportions (p = 10%, 20%, 50%, 80%) and test sizes (n = 800, 1600, 4000) under a difficult (five highly correlated T-cell types) and an easy (merged major cell types) prediction task, then scores accuracy, ARI, and unassigned-label fractions per method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data contain novel/unknown cell types absent from the reference training data — NeuCA assumes all cell types in the new sample exist in the reference, and the merged-class easy task presumes exhaustive labeling. The scientific question is clustering rather than supervised label assignment using known training labels — unsupervised tools (Seurat, SC3, TSCAN) are the alternative when no training data exist. The aim is a single one-off prediction rather than a controlled size/correlation sweep — a simple train/test split without the p/n grid suffices.

skills.description: Use when a classifier trained on pathway-module-derived features (e.g., GSVA scores of high-weight MOFA pathways) must be assessed for generalization on held-out samples and an independent bulk RNA cohort.
skills.name: train-test-split-stratification
skills.search_text: train-test-split-stratification Use when a classifier trained on pathway-module-derived features (e.g., GSVA scores of high-weight MOFA pathways) must be assessed for generalization on held-out samples and an independent bulk RNA cohort. The study cohort has fewer than 15 samples — scPAFA requires at least 15 samples (not cells) for MOFA-based multicellular pathway module identification, so no module features would exist to split and classify The input is already a fitted model or feature table and the goal is downstream interpretation of multicellular pathway modules rather than classifier validation Pathway selection is supervised — if pathway features are chosen using the full dataset before splitting, the held-out test AUROC is no longer an honest estimate of generalization http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Strategy for validating disease-status classifiers built from scPAFA/MOFA module features by splitting a labeled bulk RNA cohort (GSE39582) 70/30 into training/test partitions, selecting regularization via 4-fold CV, and confirming on an independent cohort (TCGA COAD-READ). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-07238-7
skills.summary: Strategy for validating disease-status classifiers built from scPAFA/MOFA module features by splitting a labeled bulk RNA cohort (GSE39582) 70/30 into training/test partitions, selecting regularization via 4-fold CV, and confirming on an independent cohort (TCGA COAD-READ).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The study cohort has fewer than 15 samples — scPAFA requires at least 15 samples (not cells) for MOFA-based multicellular pathway module identification, so no module features would exist to split and classify The input is already a fitted model or feature table and the goal is downstream interpretation of multicellular pathway modules rather than classifier validation Pathway selection is supervised — if pathway features are chosen using the full dataset before splitting, the held-out test AUROC is no longer an honest estimate of generalization

skills.description: Use when training a supervised malignancy or cell-type classifier on multi-sample scRNA-seq data and held-out performance must reflect generalization to unseen patients/samples rather than unseen cells from already-seen samples.
skills.name: train-validation-split-by-sample-source
skills.search_text: train-validation-split-by-sample-source Use when training a supervised malignancy or cell-type classifier on multi-sample scRNA-seq data and held-out performance must reflect generalization to unseen patients/samples rather than unseen cells from already-seen samples. The dataset contains cells from a single sample or lacks sample-source metadata, so a source-disjoint split is impossible and leakage-avoidance by sample cannot be implemented The goal is to annotate cells with an already-validated pretrained model (e.g. scCancer2's predCellType/runCellSubtypeClassify on new tumor data) rather than to benchmark classifier generalization The task is cross-dataset label similarity quantification (similarityCalculation between reference annotations), which does not involve a supervised malignant/nonMalignant training split Partitions a scRNA-seq malignancy reference dataset into training and validation sets by sample source (not by cell) before training classifiers such as XGBoost, ElasticNet, and Neural Networks, preventing cross-sample leakage when evaluating malignant vs nonMalignant prediction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae028
skills.summary: Partitions a scRNA-seq malignancy reference dataset into training and validation sets by sample source (not by cell) before training classifiers such as XGBoost, ElasticNet, and Neural Networks, preventing cross-sample leakage when evaluating malignant vs nonMalignant prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains cells from a single sample or lacks sample-source metadata, so a source-disjoint split is impossible and leakage-avoidance by sample cannot be implemented The goal is to annotate cells with an already-validated pretrained model (e.g. scCancer2's predCellType/runCellSubtypeClassify on new tumor data) rather than to benchmark classifier generalization The task is cross-dataset label similarity quantification (similarityCalculation between reference annotations), which does not involve a supervised malignant/nonMalignant training split

skills.description: Use when training a neural-network classifier on high-dimensional transcriptomic data (e.g., TCGA pan-cancer cancer-vs-normal labels) and you need a defensible train/validation split before sweeping the number of ranked features to find where accuracy plateaus.
skills.name: train-validation-split-stratification
skills.search_text: train-validation-split-stratification Use when training a neural-network classifier on high-dimensional transcriptomic data (e.g., TCGA pan-cancer cancer-vs-normal labels) and you need a defensible train/validation split before sweeping the number of ranked features to find where accuracy plateaus. The task is pure DEG analysis (e.g., edgeR adjusted p-value ranking) with no classifier-based evaluation, so no train/validation split is needed Evaluation is on independent external GEO datasets (GSE72056, GSE40419, GSE103322) where the paper already applies 5-fold cross validation instead of a single train/validation split Sample sizes are too small for a neural network — the paper notes a large number of samples are needed to achieve good classification performance http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Stratified random splitting of cancer/normal TCGA pan-cancer RNA-seq samples into training and validation partitions so that gene-count sweeps of Wx DI-ranked features (top 1–1,000) can be scored by average NN classification accuracy, revealing a plateau at ~top 100 genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-47016-8
skills.summary: Stratified random splitting of cancer/normal TCGA pan-cancer RNA-seq samples into training and validation partitions so that gene-count sweeps of Wx DI-ranked features (top 1–1,000) can be scored by average NN classification accuracy, revealing a plateau at ~top 100 genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is pure DEG analysis (e.g., edgeR adjusted p-value ranking) with no classifier-based evaluation, so no train/validation split is needed Evaluation is on independent external GEO datasets (GSE72056, GSE40419, GSE103322) where the paper already applies 5-fold cross validation instead of a single train/validation split Sample sizes are too small for a neural network — the paper notes a large number of samples are needed to achieve good classification performance

skills.description: Use when re-implementing a published neural architecture in Keras/TensorFlow and you need objective confirmation that layer configurations (filters, kernel sizes, dense units) reproduce the paper's reported model exactly.
skills.name: trainable-parameter-count-verification
skills.search_text: trainable-parameter-count-verification Use when re-implementing a published neural architecture in Keras/TensorFlow and you need objective confirmation that layer configurations (filters, kernel sizes, dense units) reproduce the paper's reported model exactly. You are training or fine-tuning an intentionally modified architecture (e.g., different dense width or added layers), where the paper's parameter count is no longer the correct invariant You only need to verify hyperparameters such as learning rate, dropout rates, or kernel regularizer weights — these do not affect the parameter count and require different checks The source paper reports no architecture details or parameter totals, leaving no reference value to verify against http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A structural sanity check that validates a reconstructed deep learning model (e.g., the MU-PseUDeep dual-branch 1D CNN) by confirming its total trainable parameter count matches the value reported in the source paper (661,118), catching silent architecture errors such as wrong filter sizes, kernel dimensions, or dense-layer widths. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2020.07.010
skills.summary: A structural sanity check that validates a reconstructed deep learning model (e.g., the MU-PseUDeep dual-branch 1D CNN) by confirming its total trainable parameter count matches the value reported in the source paper (661,118), catching silent architecture errors such as wrong filter sizes, kernel dimensions, or dense-layer widths.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are training or fine-tuning an intentionally modified architecture (e.g., different dense width or added layers), where the paper's parameter count is no longer the correct invariant You only need to verify hyperparameters such as learning rate, dropout rates, or kernel regularizer weights — these do not affect the parameter count and require different checks The source paper reports no architecture details or parameter totals, leaving no reference value to verify against

skills.description: Use when training uniPort's coupled-VAE (uniport.Run with default lambda_s=0.5, lambda_recon=1.0, lambda_kl=0.5, lambda_ot=1.0, iteration=30000) and you must confirm the composite VAE + Minibatch-UOT loss decreases rather than diverges.
skills.name: training-loss-convergence-monitoring
skills.search_text: training-loss-convergence-monitoring Use when training uniPort's coupled-VAE (uniport.Run with default lambda_s=0.5, lambda_recon=1.0, lambda_kl=0.5, lambda_ot=1.0, iteration=30000) and you must confirm the composite VAE + Minibatch-UOT loss decreases rather than diverges. Input data has not been preprocessed (normalize_total, log1p, MaxAbsScaler 0-1 scaling) — loss behavior is then uninterpretable and any divergence reflects bad scaling, not model failure A different integration framework (e.g. Seurat CCA, Harmony, LIGER NMF) is used — those have no coupled-VAE/UOT composite loss whose trajectory can be logged Only a single dataset with no cross-dataset alignment goal — the UOT term of the loss is then meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Monitors the total loss L = -L_ELBO* + gamma * L_UOT* of uniPort's coupled-VAE with Minibatch-UOT training to verify the objective is actually being minimized across the 30000 training iterations on datasets such as the PBMC AnnData matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-35094-8
skills.summary: Monitors the total loss L = -L_ELBO* + gamma * L_UOT* of uniPort's coupled-VAE with Minibatch-UOT training to verify the objective is actually being minimized across the 30000 training iterations on datasets such as the PBMC AnnData matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has not been preprocessed (normalize_total, log1p, MaxAbsScaler 0-1 scaling) — loss behavior is then uninterpretable and any divergence reflects bad scaling, not model failure A different integration framework (e.g. Seurat CCA, Harmony, LIGER NMF) is used — those have no coupled-VAE/UOT composite loss whose trajectory can be logged Only a single dataset with no cross-dataset alignment goal — the UOT term of the loss is then meaningless

skills.description: Use when you need to determine whether model performance scaling with training corpus size reflects added cells or added donor/batch diversity, by comparing subsampling regimes on a donor-stratified dataset.
skills.name: training-subset-scaling-curve-analysis
skills.search_text: training-subset-scaling-curve-analysis Use when you need to determine whether model performance scaling with training corpus size reflects added cells or added donor/batch diversity, by comparing subsampling regimes on a donor-stratified dataset. The dataset has no donor/batch identifier, so a donor-based split (the variable being tested) cannot be constructed The goal is overall benchmark comparison of annotation models rather than attribution of data-scaling effects — use a standard benchmarking protocol instead Only a single fixed training set is available and subsampling to 2.1M–15.2M cells is infeasible http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Trains a classifier (scTab's TabNet) on nested training-set subsamples under two regimes — donor/batch-based and cell-based subsampling — and fits macro F1-score and cross-entropy loss against training size to disentangle whether data scaling is driven by cell count or by donor/batch diversity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51059-5
skills.summary: Trains a classifier (scTab's TabNet) on nested training-set subsamples under two regimes — donor/batch-based and cell-based subsampling — and fits macro F1-score and cross-entropy loss against training size to disentangle whether data scaling is driven by cell count or by donor/batch diversity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no donor/batch identifier, so a donor-based split (the variable being tested) cannot be constructed The goal is overall benchmark comparison of annotation models rather than attribution of data-scaling effects — use a standard benchmarking protocol instead Only a single fixed training set is available and subsampling to 2.1M–15.2M cells is infeasible

skills.description: Use when you have preprocessed GWAS trait-associated gene lists (e.g., from 51 GWAS summary datasets) and want to map traits to associated human cell types via CTgene enrichment.
skills.name: trait-cell-type-association-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: trait-cell-type-association-matrix-construction Use when you have preprocessed GWAS trait-associated gene lists (e.g., from 51 GWAS summary datasets) and want to map traits to associated human cell types via CTgene enrichment. The query is a gene expression profile (scRNA-seq/bulk RNA-seq matrix) rather than a gene list — deCS.correlation() should be used instead of deCS.fisher(). The goal is annotating scRNA-seq clusters rather than linking traits to cell types via enrichment over CTgenes. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs a trait x cell type association table/heatmap by testing whether GWAS trait-associated gene sets are disproportionately overlapped in cell type-specific genes (CTgenes) using deCS's Fisher's exact test against a specificity-score reference panel such as BlueprintEncode_main. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.04.001
skills.summary: Constructs a trait x cell type association table/heatmap by testing whether GWAS trait-associated gene sets are disproportionately overlapped in cell type-specific genes (CTgenes) using deCS's Fisher's exact test against a specificity-score reference panel such as BlueprintEncode_main.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query is a gene expression profile (scRNA-seq/bulk RNA-seq matrix) rather than a gene list — deCS.correlation() should be used instead of deCS.fisher(). The goal is annotating scRNA-seq clusters rather than linking traits to cell types via enrichment over CTgenes.

skills.description: Use when per-cell scores for trait association are needed from scRNA-seq data given GWAS summary statistics, e.g., to identify trait-relevant cells against a scDesign2 ground truth or real disease data.
skills.name: trait-relevance-score-computation-single-cell
skills.search_text: trait-relevance-score-computation-single-cell Use when per-cell scores for trait association are needed from scRNA-seq data given GWAS summary statistics, e.g., to identify trait-relevant cells against a scDesign2 ground truth or real disease data. Input is already a per-cell score or significance table (no GWAS-to-gene prioritization step is needed). The goal is cell-type-level (bulk) enrichment rather than single-cell inference; methods like LDSC-SEG, RolyPoly, or EPIC target tissue/cell-type resolution and neglect within-cell-type heterogeneity. The scRNA-seq data lack normalized RNA assay and enough cells/genes after filtering (min_cells=50 genes, min_genes=200 cells), making TRS and background correction unstable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute per-cell trait-relevance scores (TRS) from scRNA-seq data using Seurat's AddModuleScore on scPagwas-prioritized trait-relevant genes, with Monte Carlo background correction (Get_CorrectBg_p, iters_singlecell=100) to call trait-relevant cells at p < 0.05. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100383
skills.summary: Compute per-cell trait-relevance scores (TRS) from scRNA-seq data using Seurat's AddModuleScore on scPagwas-prioritized trait-relevant genes, with Monte Carlo background correction (Get_CorrectBg_p, iters_singlecell=100) to call trait-relevant cells at p < 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-cell score or significance table (no GWAS-to-gene prioritization step is needed). The goal is cell-type-level (bulk) enrichment rather than single-cell inference; methods like LDSC-SEG, RolyPoly, or EPIC target tissue/cell-type resolution and neglect within-cell-type heterogeneity. The scRNA-seq data lack normalized RNA assay and enough cells/genes after filtering (min_cells=50 genes, min_genes=200 cells), making TRS and background correction unstable.

skills.description: Use when you must decide which 2D embedding (t-SNE/UMAP/MDS over 20/40/100% HVGs) to feed Slingshot or Monocle3, or when benchmarking inferred pseudotime against ground truth on simulated scRNA-seq data.
skills.name: trajectory-accuracy-benchmarking
skills.search_text: trajectory-accuracy-benchmarking Use when you must decide which 2D embedding (t-SNE/UMAP/MDS over 20/40/100% HVGs) to feed Slingshot or Monocle3, or when benchmarking inferred pseudotime against ground truth on simulated scRNA-seq data. The trajectory method does not use two-dimensional representations — Escort presently only considers trajectory inference approaches that use two-dimensional representations You rely on RNA velocity-derived dimension reduction — support for these is not yet implemented in Escort You need a guaranteed recommendation — Escort is not guaranteed to identify a recommended embedding among the choices being evaluated http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarks single-cell RNA-seq trajectory inference accuracy across embeddings built from varying highly variable gene (HVG) proportions and dimension reduction techniques, scoring each embedding with Escort and, when ground-truth pseudotime exists, Kendall rank correlation and mean squared error. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae216
skills.summary: Benchmarks single-cell RNA-seq trajectory inference accuracy across embeddings built from varying highly variable gene (HVG) proportions and dimension reduction techniques, scoring each embedding with Escort and, when ground-truth pseudotime exists, Kendall rank correlation and mean squared error.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trajectory method does not use two-dimensional representations — Escort presently only considers trajectory inference approaches that use two-dimensional representations You rely on RNA velocity-derived dimension reduction — support for these is not yet implemented in Escort You need a guaranteed recommendation — Escort is not guaranteed to identify a recommended embedding among the choices being evaluated

skills.description: Use when cells are assigned to more than one CellPath trajectory (cellpath_obj.pseudo_order) and you need to quantify whether inferred pseudotime is consistent across those paths per dataset.
skills.name: trajectory-assignment-deviation-analysis
skills.search_text: trajectory-assignment-deviation-analysis Use when cells are assigned to more than one CellPath trajectory (cellpath_obj.pseudo_order) and you need to quantify whether inferred pseudotime is consistent across those paths per dataset. Cells assigned to only a single trajectory path, since Diffpst cannot be computed without at least two path assignments Trajectory outputs from tools other than CellPath, whose pseudo_order structure differs (e.g. PAGA, Slingshot, CellRank outputs) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantifies pseudotime consistency for cells assigned to multiple CellPath trajectories by computing Diffpst, the mean absolute deviation of each cell's percentile-scaled pseudotime positions across its assigned paths, and tabulating per-dataset Diffpst category proportions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100095
skills.summary: Quantifies pseudotime consistency for cells assigned to multiple CellPath trajectories by computing Diffpst, the mean absolute deviation of each cell's percentile-scaled pseudotime positions across its assigned paths, and tabulating per-dataset Diffpst category proportions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells assigned to only a single trajectory path, since Diffpst cannot be computed without at least two path assignments Trajectory outputs from tools other than CellPath, whose pseudo_order structure differs (e.g. PAGA, Slingshot, CellRank outputs)

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq differentiation data (pre-processed adata with cluster annotations and optionally RNA velocity) plus a TF binding-site matrix must be converted into time- and lineage-specific TF activity estimates along cell-fate decision trajectories.
skills.name: trajectory-based-gene-regulatory-dynamics-analysis
skills.search_text: trajectory-based-gene-regulatory-dynamics-analysis Use when scRNA-seq differentiation data (pre-processed adata with cluster annotations and optionally RNA velocity) plus a TF binding-site matrix must be converted into time- and lineage-specific TF activity estimates along cell-fate decision trajectories. The goal is bulk RNA-seq motif-activity inference with no single-cell trajectory structure — ISMARA or DOROTHEA2 already cover that regime and FateCompass extends rather than replaces them Only a static feature/cluster table is available without differentiation potential, RNA velocity, or progenitor-to-fate structure from which transition probabilities can be estimated Regulatory interactions are known to be dominated by distal enhancers, since FateCompass considers only TF-promoter binding sites in the binding-site matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Estimates time- and fate-specific transcription factor activities along stochastic differentiation trajectories by modeling gene expression as a linear combination of regulatory sites and TF activities, then classifies lineage-specific TFs using Z-score, regulatory-activity-change, and dynamical-correlation criteria (FateCompass). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100512
skills.summary: Estimates time- and fate-specific transcription factor activities along stochastic differentiation trajectories by modeling gene expression as a linear combination of regulatory sites and TF activities, then classifies lineage-specific TFs using Z-score, regulatory-activity-change, and dynamical-correlation criteria (FateCompass).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is bulk RNA-seq motif-activity inference with no single-cell trajectory structure — ISMARA or DOROTHEA2 already cover that regime and FateCompass extends rather than replaces them Only a static feature/cluster table is available without differentiation potential, RNA velocity, or progenitor-to-fate structure from which transition probabilities can be estimated Regulatory interactions are known to be dominated by distal enhancers, since FateCompass considers only TF-promoter binding sites in the binding-site matrix

skills.description: Use when single-cell multiome (RNA+ATAC) data contain an ordered cell state transition (e.g. naive-to-memory CD4 T cells, SCARA5+ fibroblasts to myofibroblasts) and you need TF-gene regulatory relationships along that trajectory.
skills.name: trajectory-based-tf-gene-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: trajectory-based-tf-gene-correlation-analysis Use when single-cell multiome (RNA+ATAC) data contain an ordered cell state transition (e.g. naive-to-memory CD4 T cells, SCARA5+ fibroblasts to myofibroblasts) and you need TF-gene regulatory relationships along that trajectory. Data lack an ordered biological process (trajectory) — scMEGA's eGRN inference depends on correlating TF activity and expression along pseudotime, so static or unstructured cell populations cannot support it. Input is unimodal (RNA-only or ATAC-only) — the method needs motif accessibility plus gene expression from the same or paired cells. Goal is generic single-modal GRN inference without enhancer/peak-to-gene links; the enhancer-based design requires motif matching and peak accessibility evidence. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Infer enhancer-based gene regulatory networks (eGRNs) from single-cell multiome data by correlating TF activity (chromVAR deviation scores) with gene expression along a pseudotime trajectory, and anchor candidate TFs/genes to motif and peak-to-gene links. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad003
skills.summary: Infer enhancer-based gene regulatory networks (eGRNs) from single-cell multiome data by correlating TF activity (chromVAR deviation scores) with gene expression along a pseudotime trajectory, and anchor candidate TFs/genes to motif and peak-to-gene links.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lack an ordered biological process (trajectory) — scMEGA's eGRN inference depends on correlating TF activity and expression along pseudotime, so static or unstructured cell populations cannot support it. Input is unimodal (RNA-only or ATAC-only) — the method needs motif accessibility plus gene expression from the same or paired cells. Goal is generic single-modal GRN inference without enhancer/peak-to-gene links; the enhancer-based design requires motif matching and peak accessibility evidence.

skills.description: Use when a single-cell dataset with a low-dimensional embedding (e.g. Dim1/Dim2 coordinates) and binary condition labels needs a per-cell diagnostic of where condition imbalance concentrates along a trajectory, before formal differential topology or progression testing.
skills.name: trajectory-condition-imbalance-visualization
skills.search_text: trajectory-condition-imbalance-visualization Use when a single-cell dataset with a low-dimensional embedding (e.g. Dim1/Dim2 coordinates) and binary condition labels needs a per-cell diagnostic of where condition imbalance concentrates along a trajectory, before formal differential topology or progression testing. Data is not time-series single-cell RNA-seq or lacks a biological ordering along which pseudotime is meaningful (e.g., a static case-control bulk comparison such as the 'edge' baseline) You already have a validated trajectory and pseudotime from another tool and only need downstream testing — scTITANS_partial, or the article notes partial mode is 'much more suitable', is preferable to rerunning full trajectory inference Cell cluster information needed for the partial mode's cell_metadata is missing and you cannot run full mode's annotation (which requires sp = Human or Mouse and a tissue/organ name) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs single-cell trajectories and pseudotime using Monocle3 within the scTITANS pipeline, correcting cell asynchrony in time-series scRNA-seq data before DEG and subcluster identification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.07.016
skills.summary: Constructs single-cell trajectories and pseudotime using Monocle3 within the scTITANS pipeline, correcting cell asynchrony in time-series scRNA-seq data before DEG and subcluster identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is not time-series single-cell RNA-seq or lacks a biological ordering along which pseudotime is meaningful (e.g., a static case-control bulk comparison such as the 'edge' baseline) You already have a validated trajectory and pseudotime from another tool and only need downstream testing — scTITANS_partial, or the article notes partial mode is 'much more suitable', is preferable to rerunning full trajectory inference Cell cluster information needed for the partial mode's cell_metadata is missing and you cannot run full mode's annotation (which requires sp = Human or Mouse and a tissue/organ name)

skills.description: Use when a bifurcating or multi-fate single-cell trajectory (scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, integrated, or cytometry) must have its terminal fates and branch probabilities detected automatically without prior fate labels.
skills.name: trajectory-inference-terminal-state-detection
skills.search_text: trajectory-inference-terminal-state-detection Use when a bifurcating or multi-fate single-cell trajectory (scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, integrated, or cytometry) must have its terminal fates and branch probabilities detected automatically without prior fate labels. The goal is benchmarking TI methods on synthetic tree/loop topologies where a dedicated simulation framework (e.g., dyntoy/dyngen toy data) is the appropriate input rather than real annotated progenitor data Only a global low-resolution trajectory is needed and rare or less populous terminal fates are of no interest, so simpler methods like Slingshot may suffice The data modality lacks a meaningful low-dimensional embedding (10s-100s of PCs/features); VIA relies on adata.obsm['X_pca'] or equivalent reduced space http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Detect terminal cell fates and lineages in single-cell trajectories using VIA's lazy-teleporting random walks on a PARC cluster-graph, recovering less populous fates (e.g., Isl1+ cardiac progenitor cardiomyocyte and endothelial branches) that SlingShot, Palantir, STREAM, and Monocle3 merge or fragment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25773-3
skills.summary: Detect terminal cell fates and lineages in single-cell trajectories using VIA's lazy-teleporting random walks on a PARC cluster-graph, recovering less populous fates (e.g., Isl1+ cardiac progenitor cardiomyocyte and endothelial branches) that SlingShot, Palantir, STREAM, and Monocle3 merge or fragment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is benchmarking TI methods on synthetic tree/loop topologies where a dedicated simulation framework (e.g., dyntoy/dyngen toy data) is the appropriate input rather than real annotated progenitor data Only a global low-resolution trajectory is needed and rare or less populous terminal fates are of no interest, so simpler methods like Slingshot may suffice The data modality lacks a meaningful low-dimensional embedding (10s-100s of PCs/features); VIA relies on adata.obsm['X_pca'] or equivalent reduced space

skills.description: Use when paired lineage-barcode and scRNA-seq data need a cell-state tree (state_lineages) over k-means clusters of top-50 PCs, so a lineage-reconstruction method like LinRace can map mutations onto state transitions.
skills.name: trajectory-inference-with-slingshot
skills.search_text: trajectory-inference-with-slingshot Use when paired lineage-barcode and scRNA-seq data need a cell-state tree (state_lineages) over k-means clusters of top-50 PCs, so a lineage-reconstruction method like LinRace can map mutations onto state transitions. Input lacks paired scRNA-seq expression data (barcode-only data), since the state lineages must be derived from expression clusters on the UMAP layout Cell states are expected to be transient/absent from the final sample (fast-changing systems), so ancestral states reconstructed from current-day clusters would be incomplete Differentiation is largely reversible — LinRace assumes irreversible cell state transitions, so Slingshot-ordered lineages would misrepresent reversible state changes http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Derives cell-state lineages (pseudotime trajectories over clusters) from a UMAP embedding of the zebrafish scGESTALT expression data using R/Slingshot; these state lineages become the state-transition prior that LinRace's NJ_asym_Dif uses when reconstructing the cell division tree. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44173-3
skills.summary: Derives cell-state lineages (pseudotime trajectories over clusters) from a UMAP embedding of the zebrafish scGESTALT expression data using R/Slingshot; these state lineages become the state-transition prior that LinRace's NJ_asym_Dif uses when reconstructing the cell division tree.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks paired scRNA-seq expression data (barcode-only data), since the state lineages must be derived from expression clusters on the UMAP layout Cell states are expected to be transient/absent from the final sample (fast-changing systems), so ancestral states reconstructed from current-day clusters would be incomplete Differentiation is largely reversible — LinRace assumes irreversible cell state transitions, so Slingshot-ordered lineages would misrepresent reversible state changes

skills.description: Use when you have two lineage-specific single-cell trajectories (e.g. Seurat objects with EPI/PE identities and a monocle3 cds) and need to test whether LR pairs co-vary and causally precede master TFs along pseudotime.
skills.name: trajectory-interpolation-alignment-between-lineages
skills.search_text: trajectory-interpolation-alignment-between-lineages Use when you have two lineage-specific single-cell trajectories (e.g. Seurat objects with EPI/PE identities and a monocle3 cds) and need to test whether LR pairs co-vary and causally precede master TFs along pseudotime. The goal is communication between well-defined static cell types rather than dynamic lineages along pseudotime — CellPhoneDB or CellChat are designed for that setting and the article states they 'cannot meet the requirements of early embryo development research, where definitive cell types do not emerge until blastocyst formation' The study concerns maternal-embryo interactions, since the autocrine assumption in eLR screening 'precludes our study from exploring maternal-embryo interactions during early embryo development' The communication of interest is not ligand-receptor mediated (e.g. EV-mediated), as the current framework is 'designed for cell-cell communication mediated by ligand-receptor interactions' http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Aligns two developmental lineage trajectories (e.g. EPI and PE from blastoid and natural blastocyst scRNA-seq) by ordering cells with monocle3, interpolating each lineage onto a common axis with cellAlign, and computing Spearman cross-correlations (SCC ≥ 0.2) so ligand-receptor vs. TF temporal profiles can be causally compared via Granger tests (cutoff 1e-2). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05283-2
skills.summary: Aligns two developmental lineage trajectories (e.g. EPI and PE from blastoid and natural blastocyst scRNA-seq) by ordering cells with monocle3, interpolating each lineage onto a common axis with cellAlign, and computing Spearman cross-correlations (SCC ≥ 0.2) so ligand-receptor vs. TF temporal profiles can be causally compared via Granger tests (cutoff 1e-2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is communication between well-defined static cell types rather than dynamic lineages along pseudotime — CellPhoneDB or CellChat are designed for that setting and the article states they 'cannot meet the requirements of early embryo development research, where definitive cell types do not emerge until blastocyst formation' The study concerns maternal-embryo interactions, since the autocrine assumption in eLR screening 'precludes our study from exploring maternal-embryo interactions during early embryo development' The communication of interest is not ligand-receptor mediated (e.g. EV-mediated), as the current framework is 'designed for cell-cell communication mediated by ligand-receptor interactions'

skills.description: Use when comparing trajectory/pseudotime inference tools on scRNA-seq data with known cell type labels, to quantify which method recovers developmental ordering on neuronal or hematopoietic datasets.
skills.name: trajectory-method-benchmarking
skills.search_text: trajectory-method-benchmarking Use when comparing trajectory/pseudotime inference tools on scRNA-seq data with known cell type labels, to quantify which method recovers developmental ordering on neuronal or hematopoietic datasets. Input is already a filtered/normalized feature table that has not undergone the same GO-subsetting (get_GO_exp) and dispersion filtering (dispersion_threshold = 10) as the method being benchmarked — comparisons on differently preprocessed matrices are not valid Datasets with no known cell type labels, since CI, BI, KC, and POS are computed against known labels Non-developmental scRNA-seq analyses (e.g. differential expression or clustering-only goals) where pseudotime ordering is not the target output http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark pseudotime-inference methods (redPATH vs SCORPIUS, TSCAN, Monocle2, DPT) on developmental single-cell RNA-seq datasets using ordering-agreement metrics CI, BI, KC, and POS against known cell type labels. Grounded in the redPATH paper's Figure 2b comparison workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.06.014
skills.summary: Benchmark pseudotime-inference methods (redPATH vs SCORPIUS, TSCAN, Monocle2, DPT) on developmental single-cell RNA-seq datasets using ordering-agreement metrics CI, BI, KC, and POS against known cell type labels. Grounded in the redPATH paper's Figure 2b comparison workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered/normalized feature table that has not undergone the same GO-subsetting (get_GO_exp) and dispersion filtering (dispersion_threshold = 10) as the method being benchmarked — comparisons on differently preprocessed matrices are not valid Datasets with no known cell type labels, since CI, BI, KC, and POS are computed against known labels Non-developmental scRNA-seq analyses (e.g. differential expression or clustering-only goals) where pseudotime ordering is not the target output

skills.description: Use when benchmarking single-cell DEG prediction methods on simulated data where cluster structure and continuous trajectories between clusters are both required, and ground-truth DE labels are needed for accuracy evaluation.
skills.name: trajectory-path-simulation-between-clusters
skills.search_text: trajectory-path-simulation-between-clusters Use when benchmarking single-cell DEG prediction methods on simulated data where cluster structure and continuous trajectories between clusters are both required, and ground-truth DE labels are needed for accuracy evaluation. When the goal is to benchmark methods on realistic biological variation rather than Splatter's cluster-centric generative model, since its cluster-based structure can bias results toward cluster-based DEG approaches When a real transcriptome dataset with known DEG labels is already available (e.g. the Tabula Muris thymus dataset used in the paper) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Generates artificial scRNA-seq datasets in which clusters of cells are connected by simulated differentiation paths using Splatter's path mode (method='paths' with path.from), producing 200 benchmark count matrices with binary DEG ground-truth labels to test DEG prediction methods such as singleCellHaystack. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17900-3
skills.summary: Generates artificial scRNA-seq datasets in which clusters of cells are connected by simulated differentiation paths using Splatter's path mode (method='paths' with path.from), producing 200 benchmark count matrices with binary DEG ground-truth labels to test DEG prediction methods such as singleCellHaystack.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to benchmark methods on realistic biological variation rather than Splatter's cluster-centric generative model, since its cluster-based structure can bias results toward cluster-based DEG approaches When a real transcriptome dataset with known DEG labels is already available (e.g. the Tabula Muris thymus dataset used in the paper)

skills.description: Use when you need per-cell PPIN activity scores for 18 preloaded biological processes and want to embed cells in activity space (UMAP) and assign pseudotime along differentiation.
skills.name: trajectory-pseudotime-inference
skills.search_text: trajectory-pseudotime-inference Use when you need per-cell PPIN activity scores for 18 preloaded biological processes and want to embed cells in activity space (UMAP) and assign pseudotime along differentiation. You already have a cells x features embedding and only need annotation — use cell-annotation approaches instead of rebuilding the activity space You need cell-type counts or a predefined number of states — ORIGINS2 explicitly does not require a predefined number of cell types or states Expression matrix is raw/unaligned (ORIGINS2 expects a normalized expression matrix with genes as rows and cells as columns) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Maps scRNA-seq cells onto an ORIGINS2 per-cell biological-process activity space and performs trajectory inference (UMAP embedding + pseudotime scoring) to order cells along a differentiation path. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2023.102179
skills.summary: Maps scRNA-seq cells onto an ORIGINS2 per-cell biological-process activity space and performs trajectory inference (UMAP embedding + pseudotime scoring) to order cells along a differentiation path.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a cells x features embedding and only need annotation — use cell-annotation approaches instead of rebuilding the activity space You need cell-type counts or a predefined number of states — ORIGINS2 explicitly does not require a predefined number of cell types or states Expression matrix is raw/unaligned (ORIGINS2 expects a normalized expression matrix with genes as rows and cells as columns)

skills.description: Use when inferring developmental pseudotime on a plant scRNA-seq atlas with scPlant (RunMonocle2, RunMonocle3, RunSlingshot, RunCytoTRACE) and a biologically plausible origin — such as meristem cells — must be chosen or validated against a tool's automatic root prediction.
skills.name: trajectory-root-cell-selection-and-correction
skills.search_text: trajectory-root-cell-selection-and-correction Use when inferring developmental pseudotime on a plant scRNA-seq atlas with scPlant (RunMonocle2, RunMonocle3, RunSlingshot, RunCytoTRACE) and a biologically plausible origin — such as meristem cells — must be chosen or validated against a tool's automatic root prediction. The dataset has no identifiable progenitor/stem-cell population (e.g., meristem cells) to serve as a biologically justified trajectory root The goal is trajectory inference on non-plant single-cell data outside the scPlant framework Only one pseudotime tool will be run, so the cross-tool root consistency check (Figure 4E-4F) cannot be performed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Select a biologically justified root cell type (e.g., meristem root cells in the Arabidopsis thaliana root atlas of Zhang et al., 2019) when running pseudotime inference in scPlant, and sanity-check the resulting trajectory root — as demonstrated by CytoTRACE incorrectly rooting at xylem cells despite overall positive pseudotime correlation with Monocle2, Monocle3, and Slingshot. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xplc.2023.100631
skills.summary: Select a biologically justified root cell type (e.g., meristem root cells in the Arabidopsis thaliana root atlas of Zhang et al., 2019) when running pseudotime inference in scPlant, and sanity-check the resulting trajectory root — as demonstrated by CytoTRACE incorrectly rooting at xylem cells despite overall positive pseudotime correlation with Monocle2, Monocle3, and Slingshot.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no identifiable progenitor/stem-cell population (e.g., meristem cells) to serve as a biologically justified trajectory root The goal is trajectory inference on non-plant single-cell data outside the scPlant framework Only one pseudotime tool will be run, so the cross-tool root consistency check (Figure 4E-4F) cannot be performed

skills.description: Use when validating a trajectory-level differential test (e.g. progressionTest) against realistic trajectory-inference errors, or when reporting how much pseudotime noise and lineage misassignment a method tolerates.
skills.name: trajectory-simulation-perturbation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: trajectory-simulation-perturbation-benchmarking Use when validating a trajectory-level differential test (e.g. progressionTest) against realistic trajectory-inference errors, or when reporting how much pseudotime noise and lineage misassignment a method tolerates. The question is whether trajectory topology differs between conditions — use topologyTest, not perturbation-robustness benchmarking of progressionTest The input is real single-cell data without ground-truth pseudotimes; swapping lineage assignments would not be verifiable against a known reference Gene-level differential expression is the goal — conditionTest along lineages is the appropriate skill instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A simulation-based benchmarking skill that perturbs a ground-truth dyngen trajectory's pseudotimes and lineage assignments to stress-test the robustness of condiments::progressionTest, showing the test still rejects the null at the 5% level under substantial trajectory-inference error. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44823-0
skills.summary: A simulation-based benchmarking skill that perturbs a ground-truth dyngen trajectory's pseudotimes and lineage assignments to stress-test the robustness of condiments::progressionTest, showing the test still rejects the null at the 5% level under substantial trajectory-inference error.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is whether trajectory topology differs between conditions — use topologyTest, not perturbation-robustness benchmarking of progressionTest The input is real single-cell data without ground-truth pseudotimes; swapping lineage assignments would not be verifiable against a known reference Gene-level differential expression is the goal — conditionTest along lineages is the appropriate skill instead

skills.description: Use when an AnnData object with spliced/unspliced layers and scvelo-estimated RNA velocity has already been processed through Cytopath's Markov simulation and consensus-step construction, and you need cell-level scores against the inferred trajectories.
skills.name: trajectory-step-consensus-state-matching
skills.search_text: trajectory-step-consensus-state-matching Use when an AnnData object with spliced/unspliced layers and scvelo-estimated RNA velocity has already been processed through Cytopath's Markov simulation and consensus-step construction, and you need cell-level scores against the inferred trajectories. The underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty or unverifiable (e.g. time-dependent degradation rates), since Cytopath inference is not meaningful in that case Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable (e.g. fuzzy root probabilities with no discernible pattern, as in the hepatocyte zonation dataset) The input lacks spliced/unspliced layers, so no RNA velocity profile can be computed for the velocity-weighted alignment score http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assigns individual cells to the consensus trajectory steps of Cytopath by scoring each cell's static expression and RNA velocity profile against every consensus step, yielding per-cell trajectory assignments, pseudotime, fate probabilities, and differentiation-potential (entropy) scores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Assigns individual cells to the consensus trajectory steps of Cytopath by scoring each cell's static expression and RNA velocity profile against every consensus step, yielding per-cell trajectory assignments, pseudotime, fate probabilities, and differentiation-potential (entropy) scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty or unverifiable (e.g. time-dependent degradation rates), since Cytopath inference is not meaningful in that case Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable (e.g. fuzzy root probabilities with no discernible pattern, as in the hepatocyte zonation dataset) The input lacks spliced/unspliced layers, so no RNA velocity profile can be computed for the velocity-weighted alignment score

skills.description: Use when starting a scRNA-seq trajectory analysis and you need to decide whether fitting a trajectory is appropriate — e.g. datasets may be homogeneous or contain disconnected cell populations with no underlying dynamic.
skills.name: trajectory-suitability-assessment
skills.search_text: trajectory-suitability-assessment Use when starting a scRNA-seq trajectory analysis and you need to decide whether fitting a trajectory is appropriate — e.g. datasets may be homogeneous or contain disconnected cell populations with no underlying dynamic. The dataset already has a known continuous trajectory with ground truth pseudotime — proceed directly to embedding evaluation rather than re-testing suitability The trajectory inference method does not use two-dimensional representations; Escort only considers approaches based on two-dimensional embeddings Input is raw unprocessed counts — quality control, filtering of genes with fewer than three total counts, and LogNormalize normalization (Seurat NormalizeData()) should precede the suitability assessment http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Escort's Step 1 determines whether a scRNA-seq dataset is suitable for trajectory inference at all, by testing for disconnected cell clusters and homogeneous cells lacking trajectory signal before any embedding or pseudotime estimation is attempted. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae216
skills.summary: Escort's Step 1 determines whether a scRNA-seq dataset is suitable for trajectory inference at all, by testing for disconnected cell clusters and homogeneous cells lacking trajectory signal before any embedding or pseudotime estimation is attempted.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset already has a known continuous trajectory with ground truth pseudotime — proceed directly to embedding evaluation rather than re-testing suitability The trajectory inference method does not use two-dimensional representations; Escort only considers approaches based on two-dimensional embeddings Input is raw unprocessed counts — quality control, filtering of genes with fewer than three total counts, and LogNormalize normalization (Seurat NormalizeData()) should precede the suitability assessment

skills.description: Use when scRNA-Seq data from ≥2 conditions (e.g. control vs ILD) are projected onto a common slingshot trajectory and you must test whether conditions differ in topology, pseudotime progression, fate selection between lineages, or gene expression along lineages.
skills.name: trajectory-topology-testing
skills.search_text: trajectory-topology-testing Use when scRNA-Seq data from ≥2 conditions (e.g. control vs ILD) are projected onto a common slingshot trajectory and you must test whether conditions differ in topology, pseudotime progression, fate selection between lineages, or gene expression along lineages. Steady-state systems where cells are best clustered into identities and assessed per cluster for differential abundance rather than projected onto a trajectory Data from a single condition with no comparison to test, since topology, progression, and fate-selection tests require ≥2 conditions You need a probabilistic interpretation of the p-values — the authors only attach numerical-summary status to them http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 The condiments workflow for comparing single-cell trajectories across multiple conditions: it integrates conditions into a single slingshot trajectory, then hierarchically tests differential topology (topologyTest), differential progression and fate selection (progressionTest, fateSelectionTest), and gene-level differential expression (tradeSeq conditionTest). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44823-0
skills.summary: The condiments workflow for comparing single-cell trajectories across multiple conditions: it integrates conditions into a single slingshot trajectory, then hierarchically tests differential topology (topologyTest), differential progression and fate selection (progressionTest, fateSelectionTest), and gene-level differential expression (tradeSeq conditionTest).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Steady-state systems where cells are best clustered into identities and assessed per cluster for differential abundance rather than projected onto a trajectory Data from a single condition with no comparison to test, since topology, progression, and fate-selection tests require ≥2 conditions You need a probabilistic interpretation of the p-values — the authors only attach numerical-summary status to them

skills.description: Use when comparing pseudotime trajectories between related scRNA-seq datasets from different species (or conditions) whose trajectories contain branches, and you need to ask whether cell-type marker gene expression dynamics are conserved along aligned pseudotime.
skills.name: trajectory-tree-alignment-across-species
skills.search_text: trajectory-tree-alignment-across-species Use when comparing pseudotime trajectories between related scRNA-seq datasets from different species (or conditions) whose trajectories contain branches, and you need to ask whether cell-type marker gene expression dynamics are conserved along aligned pseudotime. Datasets have different global topological structure — CAPITAL's alignment accuracy degraded in the authors' benchmarking for such cases Trajectories form complex graphs with cycles or disconnected components — CAPITAL in its present form deals only with trajectory trees, not general graphs The trajectories are simple linear paths with no branches — DTW-based linear alignment methods suffice and selecting a single lineage pair manually is straightforward http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Globally aligns branched pseudotime trajectory trees from scRNA-seq datasets of different species (e.g., human Velten et al. and mouse Paul et al. bone marrow) using CAPITAL's dynamic-time-warping-extended-to-trees, then compares marker-gene expression kinetics along aligned pseudotime to identify conserved vs. divergent lineage dynamics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-33681-3
skills.summary: Globally aligns branched pseudotime trajectory trees from scRNA-seq datasets of different species (e.g., human Velten et al. and mouse Paul et al. bone marrow) using CAPITAL's dynamic-time-warping-extended-to-trees, then compares marker-gene expression kinetics along aligned pseudotime to identify conserved vs. divergent lineage dynamics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets have different global topological structure — CAPITAL's alignment accuracy degraded in the authors' benchmarking for such cases Trajectories form complex graphs with cycles or disconnected components — CAPITAL in its present form deals only with trajectory trees, not general graphs The trajectories are simple linear paths with no branches — DTW-based linear alignment methods suffice and selecting a single lineage pair manually is straightforward

skills.description: Use when building benchmark synthetic scRNA-seq data for branched trajectory alignment and only simulations whose cluster-derived MST has a specified topology (e.g., exactly four leaves) should enter the benchmark.
skills.name: trajectory-tree-topology-filtering
skills.search_text: trajectory-tree-topology-filtering Use when building benchmark synthetic scRNA-seq data for branched trajectory alignment and only simulations whose cluster-derived MST has a specified topology (e.g., exactly four leaves) should enter the benchmark. When aligning already-generated real scRNA-seq trajectory trees (e.g., bone marrow, human vs. mouse) — use CAPITAL's tl.trajectory_tree and tl.tree_alignment directly instead of simulating and filtering. When the trajectory structures of interest are cycles or disconnected graphs — CAPITAL 'can deal only with trajectory trees (including single lineages)' and not complex graphs. When the target analysis requires topologies other than four-leaf trees — the filter discards all other leaf counts and alignment accuracy degrades for datasets with different global topological structure. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates and then filters synthetic scRNA-seq datasets by trajectory-tree topology: run dyngen simulations on a binary-tree backbone, compute the minimum spanning tree (MST) over cell clusters for each simulation, and retain only those whose cluster-derived MST has the required leaf count (four leaves, yielding 68 of 120 datasets for CAPITAL benchmarking). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-33681-3
skills.summary: Generates and then filters synthetic scRNA-seq datasets by trajectory-tree topology: run dyngen simulations on a binary-tree backbone, compute the minimum spanning tree (MST) over cell clusters for each simulation, and retain only those whose cluster-derived MST has the required leaf count (four leaves, yielding 68 of 120 datasets for CAPITAL benchmarking).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When aligning already-generated real scRNA-seq trajectory trees (e.g., bone marrow, human vs. mouse) — use CAPITAL's tl.trajectory_tree and tl.tree_alignment directly instead of simulating and filtering. When the trajectory structures of interest are cycles or disconnected graphs — CAPITAL 'can deal only with trajectory trees (including single lineages)' and not complex graphs. When the target analysis requires topologies other than four-leaf trees — the filter discards all other leaf counts and alignment accuracy degrades for datasets with different global topological structure.

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq reads must be quantified against an augmented transcriptome that includes InPACT-reconstructed novel IPA isoforms, and per-site IPA usage (PAU) values are needed downstream.
skills.name: transcript-abundance-quantification
skills.search_text: transcript-abundance-quantification Use when RNA-seq reads must be quantified against an augmented transcriptome that includes InPACT-reconstructed novel IPA isoforms, and per-site IPA usage (PAU) values are needed downstream. Only annotated 3'UTR APA quantification is needed and no novel IPA isoform discovery is required — tools like QAPA or LABRAT suffice and InPACT transcript assembly/quantification is unnecessary. Input is single-cell UMI count data (e.g., SMART-seq2 or 10x scRNA-seq matrices) — Salmon quant of full transcriptomes from bulk FASTQ does not apply directly to scRNA-seq pipelines. Only 3'-end sequencing (3P-seq, polyA-seq, A-seq) data are available — this skill targets conventional RNA-seq alignments/reads, not dedicated 3'-end assays. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 Quantify transcript-level abundances of annotated and InPACT-assembled novel IPA isoforms by extracting transcript sequences with gffread, building a Salmon index (k-mer size 31), running salmon quant with --validateMappings, and computing per-site IPA usage (PAU) with InPACT_quantify. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46875-8
skills.summary: Quantify transcript-level abundances of annotated and InPACT-assembled novel IPA isoforms by extracting transcript sequences with gffread, building a Salmon index (k-mer size 31), running salmon quant with --validateMappings, and computing per-site IPA usage (PAU) with InPACT_quantify.
