skills.search_text: transcript-reference-sampling Use when benchmarking the query scalability of an indexed sequence-collection search structure (e.g. PAC) and you need realistic, size-graded query workloads drawn from a reference transcript database. The analysis goal is measuring index construction time or memory rather than query performance on sampled transcript batches The query workload must be a real user query set rather than a synthetically subsampled reference batch The index under test does not support batch querying of FASTA input (e.g. no multithreaded query mode comparable across batch sizes) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A benchmarking recipe that samples query batches of increasing size from a reference transcript set (human RefSeq) using seqkit, and measures a sequence-search index's query CPU time, wall-clock time, and peak RAM across batch sizes (100 to 500,000 transcripts). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad225
skills.summary: A benchmarking recipe that samples query batches of increasing size from a reference transcript set (human RefSeq) using seqkit, and measures a sequence-search index's query CPU time, wall-clock time, and peak RAM across batch sizes (100 to 500,000 transcripts).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is measuring index construction time or memory rather than query performance on sampled transcript batches The query workload must be a real user query set rather than a synthetically subsampled reference batch The index under test does not support batch querying of FASTA input (e.g. no multithreaded query mode comparable across batch sizes)

skills.description: Use when preparing a custom kallisto target transcriptome (GTF + FASTA + kdx + merge table) for 3' UTR isoform quantification from 10X Chromium 3'-tag scRNA-seq data, where reads are short and must be anchored near cleavage sites.
skills.name: transcript-sequence-deduplication
skills.search_text: transcript-sequence-deduplication Use when preparing a custom kallisto target transcriptome (GTF + FASTA + kdx + merge table) for 3' UTR isoform quantification from 10X Chromium 3'-tag scRNA-seq data, where reads are short and must be anchored near cleavage sites. Reads span the cleavage site or come from full-length/long-read protocols — the 500-nt 3'-anchored truncation is designed for short 3'-tag reads (e.g., 10X Chromium) that do not span cleavage sites You only need gene-level counts — the deduplicated UTRome and merge table are specific to resolving 3'UTR isoforms An equivalent txcutr-db reference index already exists for your annotation — prefer downloading the deposited index (e.g., Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.8118405 for GENCODE vM25) over regenerating http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Build a 3'-truncated, deduplicated UTRome target transcriptome for pseudoalignment of 3' end scRNA-seq data using txcutr: truncate GENCODE transcripts to a 500-nt 3'-anchored window, collapse identical truncated sequences to single features, and emit a merge table that maps collapsed sequences back to full-length transcripts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Build a 3'-truncated, deduplicated UTRome target transcriptome for pseudoalignment of 3' end scRNA-seq data using txcutr: truncate GENCODE transcripts to a 500-nt 3'-anchored window, collapse identical truncated sequences to single features, and emit a merge table that maps collapsed sequences back to full-length transcripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads span the cleavage site or come from full-length/long-read protocols — the 500-nt 3'-anchored truncation is designed for short 3'-tag reads (e.g., 10X Chromium) that do not span cleavage sites You only need gene-level counts — the deduplicated UTRome and merge table are specific to resolving 3'UTR isoforms An equivalent txcutr-db reference index already exists for your annotation — prefer downloading the deposited index (e.g., Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.8118405 for GENCODE vM25) over regenerating

skills.description: Use when lncRNA vs protein-coding transcript (PCT) FASTA sequences need to be converted into numeric feature vectors, or when verifying via dimensionality-reduction visualization that ORF-attention features separate the two classes.
skills.name: transcript-sequence-encoding
skills.search_text: transcript-sequence-encoding Use when lncRNA vs protein-coding transcript (PCT) FASTA sequences need to be converted into numeric feature vectors, or when verifying via dimensionality-reduction visualization that ORF-attention features separate the two classes. Input is already a numeric feature matrix or embedding — re-extracting sequence features would be redundant Transcripts are shorter than 200 nt or the study requires distinguishing RNAs without ORFs, since ncRNAs shorter than 200 nt are eliminated in this pipeline The goal is classifying full-length proteins or genomic DNA rather than transcript-level lncRNA/PCT discrimination http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Encode lncRNA/PCT transcript sequences into fused feature vectors (codon-related, GC-related, sequence-related, peptide-related, and ORF-attention features) as used by LncCat, then embed them in 2D with UMAP to verify that ORF-attention features discriminate lncRNAs from protein-coding transcripts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.02.012
skills.summary: Encode lncRNA/PCT transcript sequences into fused feature vectors (codon-related, GC-related, sequence-related, peptide-related, and ORF-attention features) as used by LncCat, then embed them in 2D with UMAP to verify that ORF-attention features discriminate lncRNAs from protein-coding transcripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a numeric feature matrix or embedding — re-extracting sequence features would be redundant Transcripts are shorter than 200 nt or the study requires distinguishing RNAs without ORFs, since ncRNAs shorter than 200 nt are eliminated in this pipeline The goal is classifying full-length proteins or genomic DNA rather than transcript-level lncRNA/PCT discrimination

skills.description: Reference for preparing a spliced+intronic (splici) reference and its 3-column transcript-to-gene mapping from a reference genome FASTA and GTF before single-cell quantification with alevin-fry/simpleaf.
skills.name: transcript-to-gene-map-preparation
skills.search_text: transcript-to-gene-map-preparation Reference for preparing a spliced+intronic (splici) reference and its 3-column transcript-to-gene mapping from a reference genome FASTA and GTF before single-cell quantification with alevin-fry/simpleaf. A piscem index and t2g mapping already exist for the reference (proceed directly to simpleaf quant instead of re-indexing) The task is bulk RNA-seq quantification against an unmodified transcriptome, where an expanded splici reference and gene-level t2g are not the target representation Inputs are raw sequencing reads rather than a reference genome FASTA plus GTF — this skill operates on reference/annotation files, not FASTQ http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Builds the expanded (splici/spliceu) reference and its transcript-to-gene (t2g) mapping from a genome FASTA plus GTF/GFF3 annotation, as implemented by simpleaf (via roers) in the alevin-fry single-cell pipeline. The t2g file is the artifact downstream mapping and quantification depend on, so its correct construction is a prerequisite for simpleaf quant. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad614
skills.summary: Builds the expanded (splici/spliceu) reference and its transcript-to-gene (t2g) mapping from a genome FASTA plus GTF/GFF3 annotation, as implemented by simpleaf (via roers) in the alevin-fry single-cell pipeline. The t2g file is the artifact downstream mapping and quantification depend on, so its correct construction is a prerequisite for simpleaf quant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A piscem index and t2g mapping already exist for the reference (proceed directly to simpleaf quant instead of re-indexing) The task is bulk RNA-seq quantification against an unmodified transcriptome, where an expanded splici reference and gene-level t2g are not the target representation Inputs are raw sequencing reads rather than a reference genome FASTA plus GTF — this skill operates on reference/annotation files, not FASTQ

skills.description: Use when you need to score TF activities from RNA perturbation compendia (e.g. Holland et al. 2020 transcriptomics data) using a prior-knowledge gene regulatory network like DoRothEA and rank inference methods by sensitivity.
skills.name: transcription-factor-activity-inference
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-activity-inference Use when you need to score TF activities from RNA perturbation compendia (e.g. Holland et al. 2020 transcriptomics data) using a prior-knowledge gene regulatory network like DoRothEA and rank inference methods by sensitivity. The goal is phospho-proteomic perturbation benchmarking of kinase activities rather than TF activity from RNA — run the phospho benchmark (run_php_bench.R) instead. You only need enrichment scores from single-cell or bulk omics data without a perturbation benchmark — the Python scverse/decoupler package (pip install decoupler) is the maintained implementation, not the decoupleRBench pipeline. Input data lacks a gene regulatory network covering the perturbed regulators — true positive classes are limited by regulators covered in the perturbation experiments, so uncovered TFs cannot be evaluated. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Infer transcription factor activities from transcriptomics perturbation data by running decoupleR's 11 statistical methods (AUCell, fast GSEA, GSVA, ORA, ULM, VIPER, mlm, consensus, etc.) against the DoRothEA gene regulatory network, then benchmark which methods best rank the experimentally perturbed TF among top regulators. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac016
skills.summary: Infer transcription factor activities from transcriptomics perturbation data by running decoupleR's 11 statistical methods (AUCell, fast GSEA, GSVA, ORA, ULM, VIPER, mlm, consensus, etc.) against the DoRothEA gene regulatory network, then benchmark which methods best rank the experimentally perturbed TF among top regulators.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is phospho-proteomic perturbation benchmarking of kinase activities rather than TF activity from RNA — run the phospho benchmark (run_php_bench.R) instead. You only need enrichment scores from single-cell or bulk omics data without a perturbation benchmark — the Python scverse/decoupler package (pip install decoupler) is the maintained implementation, not the decoupleRBench pipeline. Input data lacks a gene regulatory network covering the perturbed regulators — true positive classes are limited by regulators covered in the perturbation experiments, so uncovered TFs cannot be evaluated.

skills.description: Use when a counts table with pre-defined cell/spot clusters (e.g., SIMLR annotations over a Visium breast cancer section) must be linked to specific transcription factors via an autoencoder latent space.
skills.name: transcription-factor-activity-inference-from-autoencoder-latent-space
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-activity-inference-from-autoencoder-latent-space Use when a counts table with pre-defined cell/spot clusters (e.g., SIMLR annotations over a Visium breast cancer section) must be linked to specific transcription factors via an autoencoder latent space. The input is not a raw scRNAseq/spatial counts table with a pre-computed cluster assignment — clustering must be done first (e.g., with SIMLR) before SCA can query subpopulations The goal is de novo clustering rather than functional annotation of existing clusters; SCA reconstructs only specific clusters and is not a general clustering tool You need TF-miRNA circuit measurements: miRNAs cannot currently be quantified together with mRNAs at single-cell level, so such interactions cannot be directly assessed Infers cluster-specific transcription factor activity by encoding scRNAseq/spatial counts through the rCASC Sparsely-Connected Autoencoder (SCA) with TF-target-informed hidden layers, then ranking TFs in the latent space (e.g., with COMET). Applied on a Visium breast cancer section, it recovered SOX5 as the top TF for cluster 7 (COMETsc 2.88E-184, TP 0.623, TN 0.968). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-020-00162-6
skills.summary: Infers cluster-specific transcription factor activity by encoding scRNAseq/spatial counts through the rCASC Sparsely-Connected Autoencoder (SCA) with TF-target-informed hidden layers, then ranking TFs in the latent space (e.g., with COMET). Applied on a Visium breast cancer section, it recovered SOX5 as the top TF for cluster 7 (COMETsc 2.88E-184, TP 0.623, TN 0.968).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a raw scRNAseq/spatial counts table with a pre-computed cluster assignment — clustering must be done first (e.g., with SIMLR) before SCA can query subpopulations The goal is de novo clustering rather than functional annotation of existing clusters; SCA reconstructs only specific clusters and is not a general clustering tool You need TF-miRNA circuit measurements: miRNAs cannot currently be quantified together with mRNAs at single-cell level, so such interactions cannot be directly assessed

skills.description: Use when you have preprocessed single-cell RNA-seq (Scanpy/scVelo adata) plus a TF binding-site matrix and want to estimate time- and fate-specific TF activities along stochastic cell-fate differentiation trajectories.
skills.name: transcription-factor-activity-inference-linear-model
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-activity-inference-linear-model Use when you have preprocessed single-cell RNA-seq (Scanpy/scVelo adata) plus a TF binding-site matrix and want to estimate time- and fate-specific TF activities along stochastic cell-fate differentiation trajectories. The input is raw unprocessed scRNA-seq without basic Scanpy/scVelo preprocessing and cluster annotations You need distal regulatory interactions — FateCompass only considers binding sites in promoter regions, not long-range interactions Trajectories are already fixed or the analysis is bulk RNA-seq only, where the original ISMARA suffices without the single-cell trajectory machinery http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Infers dynamic transcription factor activities from single-cell RNA-seq by extending the ISMARA linear model of gene regulation (Balwierz et al. 2014) to single-cell transcriptomics with data-diffusion regularization, along the stochastic differentiation trajectories generated by FateCompass. It enables time- and lineage-specific TF activity estimation where TF activities cannot be measured directly, only gene expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100512
skills.summary: Infers dynamic transcription factor activities from single-cell RNA-seq by extending the ISMARA linear model of gene regulation (Balwierz et al. 2014) to single-cell transcriptomics with data-diffusion regularization, along the stochastic differentiation trajectories generated by FateCompass. It enables time- and lineage-specific TF activity estimation where TF activities cannot be measured directly, only gene expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw unprocessed scRNA-seq without basic Scanpy/scVelo preprocessing and cluster annotations You need distal regulatory interactions — FateCompass only considers binding sites in promoter regions, not long-range interactions Trajectories are already fixed or the analysis is bulk RNA-seq only, where the original ISMARA suffices without the single-cell trajectory machinery

skills.description: Use when you have a pre-processed single-cell count matrix (e.g. PBMC SingleCellExperiment) plus a TF-target prior such as DoRothEA, and want cell-level TF regulon activity scores and projections.
skills.name: transcription-factor-activity-projection
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-activity-projection Use when you have a pre-processed single-cell count matrix (e.g. PBMC SingleCellExperiment) plus a TF-target prior such as DoRothEA, and want cell-level TF regulon activity scores and projections. No TF-gene prior knowledge (e.g. DoRothEA) is available for the organism or tissue, since the skill depends on the C matrix to define regulons The data are not gene-level counts but a ratio-based modality (e.g. splicing inclusion/exclusion reads); use GEDI's ratio mode instead The goal is standard clustering or generic dimensionality reduction without an interpretable regulon-activity readout http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Uses GEDI with a DoRothEA-derived TF-gene prior matrix (C) to project transcription factor regulon activities onto single cells in the PBMC/COVID-19 data, yielding interpretable, cell-type-restricted activity embeddings validated against TF mRNA abundance (74 of 89 TFs significant). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50963-0
skills.summary: Uses GEDI with a DoRothEA-derived TF-gene prior matrix (C) to project transcription factor regulon activities onto single cells in the PBMC/COVID-19 data, yielding interpretable, cell-type-restricted activity embeddings validated against TF mRNA abundance (74 of 89 TFs significant).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No TF-gene prior knowledge (e.g. DoRothEA) is available for the organism or tissue, since the skill depends on the C matrix to define regulons The data are not gene-level counts but a ratio-based modality (e.g. splicing inclusion/exclusion reads); use GEDI's ratio mode instead The goal is standard clustering or generic dimensionality reduction without an interpretable regulon-activity readout

skills.description: Use when converting a co-expression network (GCN) to a directed GRN and candidate TF→TG edges (e.g. from GRNBoost2/GENIE3-style regression) must be filtered by cis-regulatory motif enrichment to keep only motif-supported regulators.
skills.name: transcription-factor-binding-motif-enrichment
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-binding-motif-enrichment Use when converting a co-expression network (GCN) to a directed GRN and candidate TF→TG edges (e.g. from GRNBoost2/GENIE3-style regression) must be filtered by cis-regulatory motif enrichment to keep only motif-supported regulators. The goal is co-expression structure or hub detection rather than directionality — the plain GCN (correlation-based, e.g. correlation ≥ 0.9 for M11) suffices and motif validation is unnecessary The input module contains no transcription factors to serve as candidate regulators Edges must be interpreted causally without motif support — RcisTarget validation removes edges, so false negatives may cause subtle true relationships between genes to be undetected http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Validates candidate transcription factor–target gene (TF, TG) edges in single-cell gene regulatory networks by testing whether the TF's regulatory binding motif is significantly enriched at the TG's cis-regulatory region, discarding edges that fail — as done in SCANet's GCN-to-GRN conversion following the pySCENIC/RcisTarget workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad644
skills.summary: Validates candidate transcription factor–target gene (TF, TG) edges in single-cell gene regulatory networks by testing whether the TF's regulatory binding motif is significantly enriched at the TG's cis-regulatory region, discarding edges that fail — as done in SCANet's GCN-to-GRN conversion following the pySCENIC/RcisTarget workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is co-expression structure or hub detection rather than directionality — the plain GCN (correlation-based, e.g. correlation ≥ 0.9 for M11) suffices and motif validation is unnecessary The input module contains no transcription factors to serve as candidate regulators Edges must be interpreted causally without motif support — RcisTarget validation removes edges, so false negatives may cause subtle true relationships between genes to be undetected

skills.description: Use when an initial MI-based GRN (e.g., from RNA-Seq time series) should be filtered or upgraded with motif evidence from upstream promoter sequences, or when reproducing Augusta's 'with refinement' benchmark.
skills.name: transcription-factor-binding-motif-refinement
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-binding-motif-refinement Use when an initial MI-based GRN (e.g., from RNA-Seq time series) should be filtered or upgraded with motif evidence from upstream promoter sequences, or when reproducing Augusta's 'with refinement' benchmark. The organism's genome is not available in annotated form (e.g., no GenBank file), since refining steps cannot be performed without additional knowledge of a genome A quick, low-cost network estimate is the goal and the initial unrefined MI-based GRN already has adequate sensitivity — refinement is computationally very demanding The target is Boolean logic rule assignment rather than GRN edge refinement (use the Cell Collective database search / GRN_to_BN path instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Refines an initially inferred gene regulatory network by de novo transcription factor binding motif (TFBM) discovery in the promoters of regulated genes, as implemented in the Augusta pipeline to boost network accuracy beyond mutual-information-only inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2024.01.013
skills.summary: Refines an initially inferred gene regulatory network by de novo transcription factor binding motif (TFBM) discovery in the promoters of regulated genes, as implemented in the Augusta pipeline to boost network accuracy beyond mutual-information-only inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism's genome is not available in annotated form (e.g., no GenBank file), since refining steps cannot be performed without additional knowledge of a genome A quick, low-cost network estimate is the goal and the initial unrefined MI-based GRN already has adequate sensitivity — refinement is computationally very demanding The target is Boolean logic rule assignment rather than GRN edge refinement (use the Cell Collective database search / GRN_to_BN path instead)

skills.description: Use when preparing FateCompass inputs from single-cell transcriptomics (e.g., a pre-processed AnnData from Dyngen simulation or pancreatic endocrine differentiation) and you must supply the TF/motif-vs-expressed-gene binding-site matrix needed for TF activity inference.
skills.name: transcription-factor-binding-site-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-binding-site-matrix-construction Use when preparing FateCompass inputs from single-cell transcriptomics (e.g., a pre-processed AnnData from Dyngen simulation or pancreatic endocrine differentiation) and you must supply the TF/motif-vs-expressed-gene binding-site matrix needed for TF activity inference. You lack a defined set of TFs/motifs and promoter-region annotations for the organism, so computationally predicted regulatory sites cannot be generated Your goal is to capture distal (long-range) enhancer regulation — FateCompass considers only TF-promoter interactions, not distal regulatory sites The analysis goal is method benchmarking of fate-probability tools alone, with no need to infer TF activities from a regulatory-site matrix Constructs the transcription-factor binding-site matrix that FateCompass requires as input: rows are expressed genes, columns are TFs or motifs, encoding computationally predicted regulatory sites used by the linear model of gene regulation to infer TF activities. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100512
skills.summary: Constructs the transcription-factor binding-site matrix that FateCompass requires as input: rows are expressed genes, columns are TFs or motifs, encoding computationally predicted regulatory sites used by the linear model of gene regulation to infer TF activities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You lack a defined set of TFs/motifs and promoter-region annotations for the organism, so computationally predicted regulatory sites cannot be generated Your goal is to capture distal (long-range) enhancer regulation — FateCompass considers only TF-promoter interactions, not distal regulatory sites The analysis goal is method benchmarking of fate-probability tools alone, with no need to infer TF activities from a regulatory-site matrix

skills.description: Use when a cell type has already been identified in a scRNA-Seq dataset (SINCERA S4 object) and you need to find its driving forces — key transcription factors — from differential expression and network centrality.
skills.name: transcription-factor-candidate-selection
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-candidate-selection Use when a cell type has already been identified in a scRNA-Seq dataset (SINCERA S4 object) and you need to find its driving forces — key transcription factors — from differential expression and network centrality. Cell types have not yet been identified — SINCERA's driving-force step presumes clustering and cell type identification have already been run, since candidates come from cell type-specific differential expression The goal is differential expression or gene signature prediction only, without regulatory-network interpretation — the preceding SINCERA stages cover that without needing TRN inference Expression data has not been normalized (e.g. per-sample z-score via normalization.zscore), so cross-cell-type comparisons and conditional-dependence inference would be invalid http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identifies driving forces (key regulatory nodes) of a given cell type in SINCERA by assembling candidate TFs, selecting candidate target genes, inferring a TF-TF/TF-TG transcriptional regulatory network, and ranking TFs by integrated node-importance metrics within its largest connected component. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/978-1-4939-7710-9_15
skills.summary: Identifies driving forces (key regulatory nodes) of a given cell type in SINCERA by assembling candidate TFs, selecting candidate target genes, inferring a TF-TF/TF-TG transcriptional regulatory network, and ranking TFs by integrated node-importance metrics within its largest connected component.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell types have not yet been identified — SINCERA's driving-force step presumes clustering and cell type identification have already been run, since candidates come from cell type-specific differential expression The goal is differential expression or gene signature prediction only, without regulatory-network interpretation — the preceding SINCERA stages cover that without needing TRN inference Expression data has not been normalized (e.g. per-sample z-score via normalization.zscore), so cross-cell-type comparisons and conditional-dependence inference would be invalid

skills.description: Use when a time-course single-cell dataset needs TF activity profiles aligned to ligand-receptor dynamics — e.g. to test whether co-varying LR pairs are causally linked to temporal TF clusters.
skills.name: transcription-factor-cluster-activity-analysis
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-cluster-activity-analysis Use when a time-course single-cell dataset needs TF activity profiles aligned to ligand-receptor dynamics — e.g. to test whether co-varying LR pairs are causally linked to temporal TF clusters. When the goal is paracrine communication between defined cell types rather than autocrine/temporal LR-to-TF linkage — CellPhoneDB/CellChat-style tools are the intended choice for given cell types When studying maternal-embryo interactions: TimeTalk's autocrine screening hypothesis precludes this analysis When high-confidence LR-TF regulatory confirmation is required — the article states these inferred relationships need wet-lab confirmation and Granger conclusions are winsz-sensitive http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identifies temporal transcription factors (tTFs) by master regulator analysis on cell-type-specific TRNs, clusters them by ward.D2 hierarchical clustering, and derives TF-cluster activity profiles (average expression per cluster over pseudotime) that feed TimeTalk's Granger causal testing of eLRs, yielding 430 eLRs and 229 tTFs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05283-2
skills.summary: Identifies temporal transcription factors (tTFs) by master regulator analysis on cell-type-specific TRNs, clusters them by ward.D2 hierarchical clustering, and derives TF-cluster activity profiles (average expression per cluster over pseudotime) that feed TimeTalk's Granger causal testing of eLRs, yielding 430 eLRs and 229 tTFs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is paracrine communication between defined cell types rather than autocrine/temporal LR-to-TF linkage — CellPhoneDB/CellChat-style tools are the intended choice for given cell types When studying maternal-embryo interactions: TimeTalk's autocrine screening hypothesis precludes this analysis When high-confidence LR-TF regulatory confirmation is required — the article states these inferred relationships need wet-lab confirmation and Granger conclusions are winsz-sensitive

skills.description: Use when DC3 has assigned scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq cells to subpopulations and you need to rank transcription factors driving each subpopulation by joint expression and motif enrichment evidence.
skills.name: transcription-factor-composite-ranking
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-composite-ranking Use when DC3 has assigned scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq cells to subpopulations and you need to rank transcription factors driving each subpopulation by joint expression and motif enrichment evidence. When only bulk RNA-seq or bulk ATAC-seq is available without single-cell data, since subpopulation-specific FPKM and subpopulation-specific peak calling require DC3 cell-to-subpopulation assignments When the goal is deconvolution or clustering itself rather than downstream regulator ranking — use the core DC3 workflow instead When candidate regulators are not transcription factors or lack motif models, since the importance score requires motif enrichment evidence http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Identifies and ranks subpopulation-specific key transcription factors by combining DC3-derived subpopulation gene expression (FPKM) with scATAC-seq motif enrichment, using a composite importance score to surface regulators specific to each subpopulation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-12547-1
skills.summary: Identifies and ranks subpopulation-specific key transcription factors by combining DC3-derived subpopulation gene expression (FPKM) with scATAC-seq motif enrichment, using a composite importance score to surface regulators specific to each subpopulation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only bulk RNA-seq or bulk ATAC-seq is available without single-cell data, since subpopulation-specific FPKM and subpopulation-specific peak calling require DC3 cell-to-subpopulation assignments When the goal is deconvolution or clustering itself rather than downstream regulator ranking — use the core DC3 workflow instead When candidate regulators are not transcription factors or lack motif models, since the importance score requires motif enrichment evidence

skills.description: Use when running TFvelo on scRNA-seq data and you need to restrict the TF pool per target gene — e.g., preparing the gene regulatory input before weight initialization and velocity inference.
skills.name: transcription-factor-database-selection
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-database-selection Use when running TFvelo on scRNA-seq data and you need to restrict the TF pool per target gene — e.g., preparing the gene regulatory input before weight initialization and velocity inference. You need splicing-based velocity from unspliced/spliced counts — use scVelo's dynamical model instead; TFvelo's TF selection targets datasets without splicing information. You intend to fit gene dynamics for targets with no TFs present in ENCODE/ChEA — TFvelo still cannot fit the dynamics of some genes well (Fig. S14 limitation). http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Selects candidate transcription factors (TFs) from curated TF-target databases (ENCODE and ChEA by default) to define which regulators TFvelo uses to model each target gene's RNA dynamics without splicing information. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45661-w
skills.summary: Selects candidate transcription factors (TFs) from curated TF-target databases (ENCODE and ChEA by default) to define which regulators TFvelo uses to model each target gene's RNA dynamics without splicing information.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need splicing-based velocity from unspliced/spliced counts — use scVelo's dynamical model instead; TFvelo's TF selection targets datasets without splicing information. You intend to fit gene dynamics for targets with no TFs present in ENCODE/ChEA — TFvelo still cannot fit the dynamics of some genes well (Fig. S14 limitation).

skills.description: Use when you have a fitted PRESCIENT model (data_pt) on time-series scRNA-seq and need to identify which transcription factors significantly bias differentiation toward a target fate before designing an in vitro perturbational screen.
skills.name: transcription-factor-hit-prioritization
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-hit-prioritization Use when you have a fitted PRESCIENT model (data_pt) on time-series scRNA-seq and need to identify which transcription factors significantly bias differentiation toward a target fate before designing an in vitro perturbational screen. skills.when_to_use_negative: When cell identities are not yet defined (pre-blastocyst stages without definitive cell types) — cell-type-specific TRN construction requires per-identity annotations When the goal is ligand-receptor pair discovery alone without downstream TF regulation — use plain LR co-varying screens instead When only bulk RNA-seq or low-cell-count data is available — MRA requires sufficient cells per cell type to build regulons

skills.description: Use when you have a time-course or trajectory-ordered scRNA-seq dataset with cell-type labels and need to identify upstream temporal transcription factors (e.g., as downstream targets of LR signaling) via TRN inference plus MRA.

skills.search_text: transcriptional-regulatory-network-inference-from-scrnaseq Use when you have a time-course or trajectory-ordered scRNA-seq dataset with cell-type labels and need to identify upstream temporal transcription factors (e.g., as downstream targets of LR signaling) via TRN inference plus MRA. The goal is inferring ligand-receptor communication itself (eLRs); tTF identification is a downstream by-product, so TRN/MRA should be run only after trajectory-variable gene inputs exist. skills.summary: Infers cell-type-specific transcriptional regulatory networks (TRNs) from scRNA-seq with RTN and identifies temporal TFs (tTFs) by master regulator analysis (tna.mra), yielding 229 tTFs in the TimeTalk pre-implantation embryo study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is inferring ligand-receptor communication itself (eLRs); tTF identification is a downstream by-product, so TRN/MRA should be run only after trajectory-variable gene inputs exist. skills.description: Use when a mutational signature call from fitting (mmsig, deconstructSigs, MutationalPatterns) needs independent confirmation — e.g., platinum signature SBS35 in therapy-related AML — and WGS data with strand annotations are available.
skills.name: transcriptional-strand-bias-testing
skills.search_text: transcriptional-strand-bias-testing Use when a mutational signature call from fitting (mmsig, deconstructSigs, MutationalPatterns) needs independent confirmation — e.g., platinum signature SBS35 in therapy-related AML — and WGS data with strand annotations are available. Targeted capture panels covering a few megabases — mutation burdens are too low for meaningful individual-patient signature fitting or strand-bias testing Catalogs with fewer than ~500 mutations — fitting accuracy, and hence the CI/strand-bias confirmation logic, is suboptimal Flat mutational signatures that mmsig may falsely remove because mutations can be re-classified to another signature at low cosine-similarity cost http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assess transcriptional strand bias of fitted mutational signatures (e.g., SBS35, SBS-MM1) as an orthogonal confirmation that a signature is truly present, complementing the non-zero bootstrap 95% CI criterion in mmsig. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-01938-0
skills.summary: Assess transcriptional strand bias of fitted mutational signatures (e.g., SBS35, SBS-MM1) as an orthogonal confirmation that a signature is truly present, complementing the non-zero bootstrap 95% CI criterion in mmsig.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Targeted capture panels covering a few megabases — mutation burdens are too low for meaningful individual-patient signature fitting or strand-bias testing Catalogs with fewer than ~500 mutations — fitting accuracy, and hence the CI/strand-bias confirmation logic, is suboptimal Flat mutational signatures that mmsig may falsely remove because mutations can be re-classified to another signature at low cosine-similarity cost

skills.description: Use when you have a time-series RNA-Seq count table (e.g., DREAM 4 100-gene/21-sample, C. beijerinckii 6 time points) and need to assign direction (TF→TG) and sign (activation/repression) to mutual-information-derived edges.
skills.name: transcriptional-time-lag-edge-orientation
skills.search_text: transcriptional-time-lag-edge-orientation Use when you have a time-series RNA-Seq count table (e.g., DREAM 4 100-gene/21-sample, C. beijerinckii 6 time points) and need to assign direction (TF→TG) and sign (activation/repression) to mutual-information-derived edges. Data are not a measured time series (no adjacent time points exist), so the most-significant-difference time-lag evaluation cannot be performed You only need an undirected, unsigned association network — MI inference alone (e.g., Augusta without refinement, which scored sensitivity 0.38, specificity 0.54 on DREAM 4) suffices without edge orientation Processing multiple RNA-Seq experiments measured under various environmental conditions, which Augusta does not yet support in a single computation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Orients and signs edges of an MI-inferred gene regulatory network by identifying the most significant difference (MSD) among adjacent pairs of time points in a time-series RNA-Seq count table, which evaluates the transcriptional time lag between each TF-TG pair. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2024.01.013
skills.summary: Orients and signs edges of an MI-inferred gene regulatory network by identifying the most significant difference (MSD) among adjacent pairs of time points in a time-series RNA-Seq count table, which evaluates the transcriptional time lag between each TF-TG pair.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not a measured time series (no adjacent time points exist), so the most-significant-difference time-lag evaluation cannot be performed You only need an undirected, unsigned association network — MI inference alone (e.g., Augusta without refinement, which scored sensitivity 0.38, specificity 0.54 on DREAM 4) suffices without edge orientation Processing multiple RNA-Seq experiments measured under various environmental conditions, which Augusta does not yet support in a single computation

skills.description: Use when building a custom pseudoalignment target for 3'-end tag scRNA-seq data (e.g., 10X Chromium) where reads do not span cleavage sites and full-length transcripts would collapse 3'UTR isoforms.
skills.name: transcriptome-3-prime-truncation
skills.search_text: transcriptome-3-prime-truncation Use when building a custom pseudoalignment target for 3'-end tag scRNA-seq data (e.g., 10X Chromium) where reads do not span cleavage sites and full-length transcripts would collapse 3'UTR isoforms. Reads come from a full-length or long-read protocol that spans cleavage sites — de novo 3' end mapping, not 3'-anchored truncation, is appropriate. You only need gene-level counts; a standard transcriptome/kallisto index without UTRome truncation suffices. A pre-built txcutr-db UTRome index already exists for your exact annotation release — reuse it rather than regenerating. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generate a 3'-truncated UTRome (e.g., via txcutr) from a GENCODE GTF/GFF annotation so that kallisto bus pseudoalignment of 3'-tagged scRNA-seq reads can distinguish 3'UTR isoforms; the 500-nt truncation is empirically justified for 10X Chromium 3' libraries. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Generate a 3'-truncated UTRome (e.g., via txcutr) from a GENCODE GTF/GFF annotation so that kallisto bus pseudoalignment of 3'-tagged scRNA-seq reads can distinguish 3'UTR isoforms; the 500-nt truncation is empirically justified for 10X Chromium 3' libraries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads come from a full-length or long-read protocol that spans cleavage sites — de novo 3' end mapping, not 3'-anchored truncation, is appropriate. You only need gene-level counts; a standard transcriptome/kallisto index without UTRome truncation suffices. A pre-built txcutr-db UTRome index already exists for your exact annotation release — reuse it rather than regenerating.

skills.summary: Benchmark genome-guided transcriptome assemblers (Tiglon, StringTie2, Scallop, StringTie2-Merge) under different alignment conditions (Hisat2, Star, merged) by evaluating assembled GTFs against a reference transcriptome (NCBI RefSeq hg38) with Cuffcompare, counting correct transcripts, precision, and F-score.

skills.description: Use when you have a de novo assembled transcriptome (e.g. Trinity output) plus the original RNA-Seq reads and need to remove low-expression, redundant, and chimeric contigs without a reference genome.
skills.name: transcriptome-assembly-filtering
skills.search_text: transcriptome-assembly-filtering Use when you have a de novo assembled transcriptome (e.g. Trinity output) plus the original RNA-Seq reads and need to remove low-expression, redundant, and chimeric contigs without a reference genome. When a custom order of filtering steps is required — the README states 'Custom order of filtering steps is disabled in this version' When you need a reference-based transcriptome assessment — the article notes 'When there is no reference genome available, the quality of a de novo assembled transcriptome is difficult to assess' only in the reference-free context; this skill is reference-free, so it is the wrong choice if a curated reference genome/transcriptome exists and reference-guided methods are preferred When transcripts from alternative splicing of one gene are present and must be preserved — Bellerophon may erroneously remove such contigs misclassified as chimeras http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Filter a de novo transcriptome assembly with the Bellerophon pipeline, which uses TransRate quality assessment, a TPM filter (cut-off 1), CD-HIT-EST (95% identity), and TransRate-C to remove lowly expressed, redundant, and chimeric contigs. It is specifically aimed at removing falsely assembled chimeras to reduce false-positive gene discovery and false-negative differential expression calls. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/ece3.5571
skills.summary: Filter a de novo transcriptome assembly with the Bellerophon pipeline, which uses TransRate quality assessment, a TPM filter (cut-off 1), CD-HIT-EST (95% identity), and TransRate-C to remove lowly expressed, redundant, and chimeric contigs. It is specifically aimed at removing falsely assembled chimeras to reduce false-positive gene discovery and false-negative differential expression calls.

skills.name: transcriptome-evolutionary-index-calculation
skills.search_text: transcriptome-evolutionary-index-calculation Use when single-cell RNA data (Scanpy AnnData) needs a gene age-weighted expression index per cell, stage, or cell type — e.g. to detect whether young gene age classes peak in early embryos — or when per-class partial TEI / relative expression profiles are required. Input lacks an orthomap or any per-gene category (gene age class or binned metric) — the TEI weighting cannot be computed without a gene-to-class mapping matched to the scRNA identifiers The goal is standard differential expression or clustering rather than evolutionary-age-weighted expression profiles — use standard Scanpy workflows instead Data is not a Scanpy-compatible scRNA object (oggmap's TEI calculation is implemented on Scanpy AnnData objects) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Computes the transcriptome evolutionary index (TEI) — a gene age-weighted expression index — per cell or per annotated stage/group from single-cell RNA data using oggmap's TEI module on Scanpy AnnData objects. skills.summary: Computes the transcriptome evolutionary index (TEI) — a gene age-weighted expression index — per cell or per annotated stage/group from single-cell RNA data using oggmap's TEI module on Scanpy AnnData objects.
