skills.search_text: transcriptome-reference-index-preparation Use when quantifying transcript abundances with Kallisto from RNA-Seq FASTQ files and an Ensembl transcript cDNA reference must first be converted into a Kallisto index that matches downstream isoform-switching analysis. When abundances must be gene-level or genome-alignment based (e.g. STAR/RSEM), since CanIsoNet's isoform-switching analysis depends on transcript-level TPM against Ensembl isoform definitions When the reference must be single-cell-compatible or alignment-free without paired-end FASTQ input; the described workflow is paired-end Kallisto quant only http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Prepare a transcript-level reference index for Kallisto from Ensembl cDNA sequences (human GRCh37.p13, mouse GRCm38.p6) so that transcript abundance quantification (TPM) for the four disease RNA-Seq datasets (OIH, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Behcet's) is compatible with the transcript isoform definitions used downstream in CanIsoNet. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad050
skills.summary: Prepare a transcript-level reference index for Kallisto from Ensembl cDNA sequences (human GRCh37.p13, mouse GRCm38.p6) so that transcript abundance quantification (TPM) for the four disease RNA-Seq datasets (OIH, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Behcet's) is compatible with the transcript isoform definitions used downstream in CanIsoNet.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When abundances must be gene-level or genome-alignment based (e.g. STAR/RSEM), since CanIsoNet's isoform-switching analysis depends on transcript-level TPM against Ensembl isoform definitions When the reference must be single-cell-compatible or alignment-free without paired-end FASTQ input; the described workflow is paired-end Kallisto quant only

skills.description: Use when counting overlaps between transcriptome region sets or between isoform-ambiguous genomic features and transcriptome regions of interest (ROI), and when RgnTX's overlapCountsTx / overlapCountsTxIA measures must be reproduced or verified.
skills.name: transcriptome-region-overlap-counting
skills.search_text: transcriptome-region-overlap-counting Use when counting overlaps between transcriptome region sets or between isoform-ambiguous genomic features and transcriptome regions of interest (ROI), and when RgnTX's overlapCountsTx / overlapCountsTxIA measures must be reproduced or verified. The features already have a known isoform association — use the non-IA path (overlapCountsTx with permTestTx / permTestTx_customPick) instead of the isoform-ambiguity averaging. The analysis is genome-based and transcriptome annotation/heterogeneity is irrelevant — genome-level tools like LOLA, GREAT or GenomeRunner are the intended comparison there. The goal is p-value/z-score estimation rather than the raw colocalization measure — the permutation machinery (permTestTx family, shiftedZScoreTx, Benjamini-Hochberg correction) is a separate skill built on top of these counts. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Reimplements and validates RgnTX's weighted overlapping-count evaluation for transcriptome colocalization, including the isoform-ambiguity variant (overlapCountsTxIA) where each ambiguous feature contributes a c(i)/n(i) ratio clamped to [0, 1]. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.08.021
skills.summary: Reimplements and validates RgnTX's weighted overlapping-count evaluation for transcriptome colocalization, including the isoform-ambiguity variant (overlapCountsTxIA) where each ambiguous feature contributes a c(i)/n(i) ratio clamped to [0, 1].
skills.when_to_use_negative: The features already have a known isoform association — use the non-IA path (overlapCountsTx with permTestTx / permTestTx_customPick) instead of the isoform-ambiguity averaging. The analysis is genome-based and transcriptome annotation/heterogeneity is irrelevant — genome-level tools like LOLA, GREAT or GenomeRunner are the intended comparison there. The goal is p-value/z-score estimation rather than the raw colocalization measure — the permutation machinery (permTestTx family, shiftedZScoreTx, Benjamini-Hochberg correction) is a separate skill built on top of these counts.

skills.description: Use when you need null/randomized region sets that respect transcriptome annotation (e.g., for permutation tests of RNA element colocalization) or want to benchmark shuffling runtime over region-count grids.
skills.name: transcriptome-region-randomization
skills.search_text: transcriptome-region-randomization Use when you need null/randomized region sets that respect transcriptome annotation (e.g., for permutation tests of RNA element colocalization) or want to benchmark shuffling runtime over region-count grids. The analysis target is purely genomic (e.g., ChIP-seq peaks on DNA space) with no transcriptome constraint — genome-based shufflers like regioneR are appropriate instead Features have known, unambiguous isoform association and a custom region-of-interest test is needed — permTestTx_customPick or permTestTx are the fitting entry points rather than raw randomization http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Randomizes region sets within a transcriptome background using RgnTX's randomizeTx and randomizeFeaturesTx, so null regions preserve transcriptome structure (mRNA space, alternative splicing) rather than being drawn from genome space. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.08.021
skills.summary: Randomizes region sets within a transcriptome background using RgnTX's randomizeTx and randomizeFeaturesTx, so null regions preserve transcriptome structure (mRNA space, alternative splicing) rather than being drawn from genome space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis target is purely genomic (e.g., ChIP-seq peaks on DNA space) with no transcriptome constraint — genome-based shufflers like regioneR are appropriate instead Features have known, unambiguous isoform association and a custom region-of-interest test is needed — permTestTx_customPick or permTestTx are the fitting entry points rather than raw randomization

skills.description: Use when benchmarking phasiRNA prediction tools' runtime on the same sRNA library (e.g., rice SRR5049781) across cDNA and gDNA references, or when deciding whether multithreading (e.g., -j 4) is needed to make genome-based prediction tractable.
skills.name: transcriptome-versus-genome-reference-prediction
skills.search_text: transcriptome-versus-genome-reference-prediction Use when benchmarking phasiRNA prediction tools' runtime on the same sRNA library (e.g., rice SRR5049781) across cDNA and gDNA references, or when deciding whether multithreading (e.g., -j 4) is needed to make genome-based prediction tractable. When Bowtie index building or sRNA mapping time is itself part of the benchmark — this skill explicitly excludes the shared preprocess/mapping step from all timings. When benchmarking 24-nt phasiRNA prediction, since the workflow fixes -pl 21. When the goal is comparing prediction accuracy (sensitivity/precision of PHAS loci) rather than runtime. http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Benchmarking skill for comparing 21-nt phasiRNA prediction runtime across tools (PhasiHunter, unitas, PhaseTank, PhasiRNAnalyzer) against both transcriptome (cDNA) and genome (gDNA) references, using precomputed Bowtie mapping files so index preparation is excluded from all timings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad676
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill for comparing 21-nt phasiRNA prediction runtime across tools (PhasiHunter, unitas, PhaseTank, PhasiRNAnalyzer) against both transcriptome (cDNA) and genome (gDNA) references, using precomputed Bowtie mapping files so index preparation is excluded from all timings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When Bowtie index building or sRNA mapping time is itself part of the benchmark — this skill explicitly excludes the shared preprocess/mapping step from all timings. When benchmarking 24-nt phasiRNA prediction, since the workflow fixes -pl 21. When the goal is comparing prediction accuracy (sensitivity/precision of PHAS loci) rather than runtime.

skills.description: Use when you need transcriptome-wide, base-resolution prediction of novel RNA pseudouridine sites in human protein-coding genes using a trained sequence-plus-secondary-structure deep learning model.
skills.name: transcriptome-wide-pseudouridine-prediction
skills.search_text: transcriptome-wide-pseudouridine-prediction Use when you need transcriptome-wide, base-resolution prediction of novel RNA pseudouridine sites in human protein-coding genes using a trained sequence-plus-secondary-structure deep learning model. The goal is to re-identify already experimentally validated RMBase Ψ sites — masking step removes them, so the scan targets novel sites only Input species or genome build is not supported by the trained model reference files (hg19 human; mm10 mouse and sacCer3 yeast were used separately in the paper) Only a small set of individual RNA fragments needs classification — direct MU-PseUDeep prediction is more appropriate than a full transcriptome scan http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Scans human protein-coding transcriptome sequences with the trained MU-PseUDeep deep learning model to identify pseudouridine (Ψ) sites at a >0.99 precision threshold, yielding per-gene Ψ site predictions with high confidence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2020.07.010
skills.summary: Scans human protein-coding transcriptome sequences with the trained MU-PseUDeep deep learning model to identify pseudouridine (Ψ) sites at a >0.99 precision threshold, yielding per-gene Ψ site predictions with high confidence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to re-identify already experimentally validated RMBase Ψ sites — masking step removes them, so the scan targets novel sites only Input species or genome build is not supported by the trained model reference files (hg19 human; mm10 mouse and sacCer3 yeast were used separately in the paper) Only a small set of individual RNA fragments needs classification — direct MU-PseUDeep prediction is more appropriate than a full transcriptome scan

skills.description: Use when you have a single-cell expression matrix for one study (e.g. H5AD-imported study in Cellenium) and want to find, for a query gene, all genes with correlated expression across cells.
skills.name: transcriptome-wide-similarity-search
skills.search_text: transcriptome-wide-similarity-search Use when you have a single-cell expression matrix for one study (e.g. H5AD-imported study in Cellenium) and want to find, for a query gene, all genes with correlated expression across cells. You need co-expression across multiple studies rather than a within-study analysis — Cellenium also offers cross-study comparison, which is a different view You only need expression of one or a few genes in UMAP or violin plots, not transcriptome-wide correlated genes You are looking for differentially expressed genes between annotated cell clusters, not genes correlated with a query gene http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies genes whose single-cell expression profiles are correlated with a query gene of interest within one study, as enabled by Cellenium's single-study co-expression view, and returns a transcriptome-wide ranked gene-by-correlation table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad349
skills.summary: Identifies genes whose single-cell expression profiles are correlated with a query gene of interest within one study, as enabled by Cellenium's single-study co-expression view, and returns a transcriptome-wide ranked gene-by-correlation table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need co-expression across multiple studies rather than a within-study analysis — Cellenium also offers cross-study comparison, which is a different view You only need expression of one or a few genes in UMAP or violin plots, not transcriptome-wide correlated genes You are looking for differentially expressed genes between annotated cell clusters, not genes correlated with a query gene

skills.description: Use when two or more gene/biomarker candidate lists from the same transcriptomic cohort (e.g., TCGA pan-cancer RNA-seq) need intersection analysis to quantify agreement between feature-selection algorithms.
skills.name: transcriptomic-biomarker-set-comparison
skills.search_text: transcriptomic-biomarker-set-comparison Use when two or more gene/biomarker candidate lists from the same transcriptomic cohort (e.g., TCGA pan-cancer RNA-seq) need intersection analysis to quantify agreement between feature-selection algorithms. The goal is to compare classification accuracy of gene sets (LOOCV or NN/SVM accuracy) rather than gene membership overlap Input is a single gene list with no reference set to compare against Gene lists come from different identifiers or genome annotations that have not been harmonized to common symbols http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantify overlap between an algorithm-selected gene set (e.g., Wx-14-UGCB ranked by average DI score over 10,000 iterations) and reference biomarker/DEG lists (Peng-14-UGCB, Martinez-7-UGCB, edgeR DEG-14-UGCB) using set operations, to assess whether alternative feature-selection methods converge on the same genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-47016-8
skills.summary: Quantify overlap between an algorithm-selected gene set (e.g., Wx-14-UGCB ranked by average DI score over 10,000 iterations) and reference biomarker/DEG lists (Peng-14-UGCB, Martinez-7-UGCB, edgeR DEG-14-UGCB) using set operations, to assess whether alternative feature-selection methods converge on the same genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to compare classification accuracy of gene sets (LOOCV or NN/SVM accuracy) rather than gene membership overlap Input is a single gene list with no reference set to compare against Gene lists come from different identifiers or genome annotations that have not been harmonized to common symbols

skills.description: Use when loading raw RNA-seq/microarray expression .csv files (sample names in first column, labels in last column) that contain missing gene values and must be imputed and quantile-normalized before cross-platform training in Ciclops.
skills.name: transcriptomic-csv-matrix-handling
skills.search_text: transcriptomic-csv-matrix-handling Use when loading raw RNA-seq/microarray expression .csv files (sample names in first column, labels in last column) that contain missing gene values and must be imputed and quantile-normalized before cross-platform training in Ciclops. The --no_quantile flag is specified, meaning quantile normalization should be skipped Input already contains complete, normalized expression values shared between train and test sets — re-imputing or re-normalizing could distort the data Training and validation sets share no common genes — the silent-failure mode makes downstream preprocessing meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Preprocess cross-platform transcriptomic .csv matrices (e.g., GSE151189 training and GSE59098 validation) for Ciclops by performing gene-wise imputation of missing values followed by joint quantile normalization, so training and validation empirical distributions are aligned before model construction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101583
skills.summary: Preprocess cross-platform transcriptomic .csv matrices (e.g., GSE151189 training and GSE59098 validation) for Ciclops by performing gene-wise imputation of missing values followed by joint quantile normalization, so training and validation empirical distributions are aligned before model construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The --no_quantile flag is specified, meaning quantile normalization should be skipped Input already contains complete, normalized expression values shared between train and test sets — re-imputing or re-normalizing could distort the data Training and validation sets share no common genes — the silent-failure mode makes downstream preprocessing meaningless

skills.description: Use when reproducing a published nested-CV glmnet model on RNA-Seq data and you need to verify which genes the automatically refitted final model retains and that their ranked coefficients match the published output.
skills.name: transcriptomic-feature-selection-verification
skills.search_text: transcriptomic-feature-selection-verification Use when reproducing a published nested-CV glmnet model on RNA-Seq data and you need to verify which genes the automatically refitted final model retains and that their ranked coefficients match the published output. The dataset is not high-dimensional (P >> n) transcriptomic data with limited samples — conventional train/test splits may suffice You need unbiased accuracy estimation only; nested CV outer-loop performance is the target, not refitting a final model to the whole dataset Predictors are mixed continuous/categorical factors requiring one_hot() encoding beyond a simple gene-expression matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Reproduce and verify the final fitted glmnet model from nested cross-validation on high-dimensional transcriptomic data (e.g. the R4RA rituximab subset of E-MTAB-11611), extracting and ranking the retained nonzero coefficients against the published vignette output. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad048
skills.summary: Reproduce and verify the final fitted glmnet model from nested cross-validation on high-dimensional transcriptomic data (e.g. the R4RA rituximab subset of E-MTAB-11611), extracting and ranking the retained nonzero coefficients against the published vignette output.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is not high-dimensional (P >> n) transcriptomic data with limited samples — conventional train/test splits may suffice You need unbiased accuracy estimation only; nested CV outer-loop performance is the target, not refitting a final model to the whole dataset Predictors are mixed continuous/categorical factors requiring one_hot() encoding beyond a simple gene-expression matrix

skills.description: Use when a fitted suffPCR model on transcriptomic data yields feature-sparse loadings and the nonzero feature list must be mapped to genes and grouped into functional families for interpretation.
skills.name: transcriptomic-gene-list-annotation
skills.search_text: transcriptomic-gene-list-annotation Use when a fitted suffPCR model on transcriptomic data yields feature-sparse loadings and the nonzero feature list must be mapped to genes and grouped into functional families for interpretation. The feature list is already annotated gene identifiers and only needs counting — no sparse-loadings extraction is needed. The fitted model has dense (non-sparse) loadings, so there is no natural small subset of genes to annotate. The analysis goal is univariate differential-expression testing rather than interpreting a row-sparse PCA + regression subspace. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Annotate the nonzero, feature-sparse loadings extracted from a fitted SuffPCR model with gene identifiers, tally unique genes vs ESTs, and group them into functional categories (e.g. ribosomal-protein genes, MHCII genes) for biological interpretation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac033
skills.summary: Annotate the nonzero, feature-sparse loadings extracted from a fitted SuffPCR model with gene identifiers, tally unique genes vs ESTs, and group them into functional categories (e.g. ribosomal-protein genes, MHCII genes) for biological interpretation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature list is already annotated gene identifiers and only needs counting — no sparse-loadings extraction is needed. The fitted model has dense (non-sparse) loadings, so there is no natural small subset of genes to annotate. The analysis goal is univariate differential-expression testing rather than interpreting a row-sparse PCA + regression subspace.

skills.description: Use when you have a fitted GEDI model over a multi-sample, multi-condition single-cell dataset (e.g., healthy vs severe COVID-19) and need a cluster-free, per-cell-type direction/magnitude field of the condition effect plus TF activity gradients.
skills.name: transcriptomic-vector-field-computation
skills.search_text: transcriptomic-vector-field-computation Use when you have a fitted GEDI model over a multi-sample, multi-condition single-cell dataset (e.g., healthy vs severe COVID-19) and need a cluster-free, per-cell-type direction/magnitude field of the condition effect plus TF activity gradients. You need perturbation-response prediction in cell types not observed in the data — counterfactual prediction via GEDI's vector field is currently untested You only need standard pseudo-bulk per-cluster differential expression; a sequential workflow (normalize, integrate, cluster, DGE per cell type) may suffice and is simpler Your modality is not linear-embeddable — GEDI currently only supports linear manifold learning (with optional hyperellipsoid restriction) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Compute and visualize the severe-vs-healthy transcriptomic vector field of COVID-19 cohort 1 with GEDI's svd.vectorField.gedi/plot_vectorField in the Harmony-integrated embedding, then rank cell types by mean vector magnitude and test TF activity-gradient concordance (e.g., SPI1 in HLA-DRlo S100Ahi monocytes). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50963-0
skills.summary: Compute and visualize the severe-vs-healthy transcriptomic vector field of COVID-19 cohort 1 with GEDI's svd.vectorField.gedi/plot_vectorField in the Harmony-integrated embedding, then rank cell types by mean vector magnitude and test TF activity-gradient concordance (e.g., SPI1 in HLA-DRlo S100Ahi monocytes).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need perturbation-response prediction in cell types not observed in the data — counterfactual prediction via GEDI's vector field is currently untested You only need standard pseudo-bulk per-cluster differential expression; a sequential workflow (normalize, integrate, cluster, DGE per cell type) may suffice and is simpler Your modality is not linear-embeddable — GEDI currently only supports linear manifold learning (with optional hyperellipsoid restriction)

skills.description: Use when integrating scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq-derived gene activity data with an ST reference (Visium, Slide-seq, STARmap) whose platforms and batch effects prevent direct joint analysis for pseudo-space reconstruction.
skills.name: transfer-component-analysis-batch-correction
skills.search_text: transfer-component-analysis-batch-correction Use when integrating scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq-derived gene activity data with an ST reference (Visium, Slide-seq, STARmap) whose platforms and batch effects prevent direct joint analysis for pseudo-space reconstruction. The input data is already from the same platform and batch (no cross-modality/intersample batch effect to remove between scRNA-seq and ST) The target tissue has low spatial coherence (e.g., Patients 5 and 9 of SCC in the paper), where scSpace reconstruction including TCA alignment should be applied cautiously The available spatial reference is anatomically mismatched to the target tissue (e.g., dACC, which lacks cortical layer 4, for a DLPFC target) without appropriateness assessment or pre-processing http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Apply transfer component analysis (TCA), as implemented in scSpace, to eliminate the batch effect between scRNA-seq (or gene-activity-matrix) data and a spatial transcriptomics reference and extract their shared characteristic matrices, which are then used to train an MLP projector into pseudo-space. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38121-4
skills.summary: Apply transfer component analysis (TCA), as implemented in scSpace, to eliminate the batch effect between scRNA-seq (or gene-activity-matrix) data and a spatial transcriptomics reference and extract their shared characteristic matrices, which are then used to train an MLP projector into pseudo-space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data is already from the same platform and batch (no cross-modality/intersample batch effect to remove between scRNA-seq and ST) The target tissue has low spatial coherence (e.g., Patients 5 and 9 of SCC in the paper), where scSpace reconstruction including TCA alignment should be applied cautiously The available spatial reference is anatomically mismatched to the target tissue (e.g., dACC, which lacks cortical layer 4, for a DLPFC target) without appropriateness assessment or pre-processing

skills.description: Use when a consensus clustering must be derived from many base partitions of a single-cell latent embedding (the SDDA output Z), combining sample and cluster nodes in a bipartite graph and solving via transfer cut. Triggers: K-means ensemble inputs, ARI/NMI consensus evaluation.
skills.name: transfer-cut-graph-partitioning
skills.search_text: transfer-cut-graph-partitioning Use when a consensus clustering must be derived from many base partitions of a single-cell latent embedding (the SDDA output Z), combining sample and cluster nodes in a bipartite graph and solving via transfer cut. Triggers: K-means ensemble inputs, ARI/NMI consensus evaluation. The input is raw scRNA-seq count data or a preprocessed expression matrix — this module requires the latent embedding Z from the dual denoising autoencoder (SDDA.py) first Only a single clustering is available and no ensemble of basic clusterings can be generated — the consensus function needs K=100 base partitions MATLAB is unavailable and BC.m/BGEC.m cannot be executed — the transfer cut implementation is MATLAB-based http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 scBGEDA's third module: bipartite graph ensemble clustering that generates K=100 K-means basic clusterings on the latent embedding Z and merges them into one consensus partition via a graph-based consensus function solved with a transfer cut. It turns a deep autoencoder's representation into a robust cell-type clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad075
skills.summary: scBGEDA's third module: bipartite graph ensemble clustering that generates K=100 K-means basic clusterings on the latent embedding Z and merges them into one consensus partition via a graph-based consensus function solved with a transfer cut. It turns a deep autoencoder's representation into a robust cell-type clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw scRNA-seq count data or a preprocessed expression matrix — this module requires the latent embedding Z from the dual denoising autoencoder (SDDA.py) first Only a single clustering is available and no ensemble of basic clusterings can be generated — the consensus function needs K=100 base partitions MATLAB is unavailable and BC.m/BGEC.m cannot be executed — the transfer cut implementation is MATLAB-based

skills.description: Use when training data and validation data come from different transcriptomic platforms (e.g., RNA-seq vs. microarray) and you need clinical outcome models that generalize across platforms.
skills.name: transfer-learning-across-transcriptomic-platforms
skills.search_text: transfer-learning-across-transcriptomic-platforms Use when training data and validation data come from different transcriptomic platforms (e.g., RNA-seq vs. microarray) and you need clinical outcome models that generalize across platforms. Training and validation sets share no common genes — the program fails silently and the ./training csv splits contain only sample names and labels, missing gene expression columns. SHAP biomarker interpretation is required with the regression models — SHAP analysis is not implemented for Gaussian Process Regression (gpr) or Linear Regression (lr). Quantile normalization between platforms is inappropriate for the data — pass --no_quantile rather than using the default cross-platform pipeline. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train clinical outcome prediction models on one transcriptomic platform (e.g., RNA-seq GSE151189) with Ciclops and transfer them to another platform (e.g., microarray GSE59098) using quantile normalization and five model types, evaluating via 10-fold cross-validation and transfer test. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101583
skills.summary: Train clinical outcome prediction models on one transcriptomic platform (e.g., RNA-seq GSE151189) with Ciclops and transfer them to another platform (e.g., microarray GSE59098) using quantile normalization and five model types, evaluating via 10-fold cross-validation and transfer test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Training and validation sets share no common genes — the program fails silently and the ./training csv splits contain only sample names and labels, missing gene expression columns. SHAP biomarker interpretation is required with the regression models — SHAP analysis is not implemented for Gaussian Process Regression (gpr) or Linear Regression (lr). Quantile normalization between platforms is inappropriate for the data — pass --no_quantile rather than using the default cross-platform pipeline.

skills.description: Use when matching/aligning cell types across species from scRNA-seq data: you have two scRNA-seq datasets (e.g. human/mouse/marmoset motor cortex) and want to train a within-species classifier then propagate labels cross-species.
skills.name: transfer-learning-classifier-training
skills.search_text: transfer-learning-classifier-training Use when matching/aligning cell types across species from scRNA-seq data: you have two scRNA-seq datasets (e.g. human/mouse/marmoset motor cortex) and want to train a within-species classifier then propagate labels cross-species. Gene matching only, without cell type label transfer — use BLAST or the protein-embedding gene-matching step alone instead of the full classifier/transfer-learning pipeline When you need to compare against a state-of-the-art baseline at matched dataset sizes, run SAMap on the same subsets rather than relying on TACTiCS training alone Input data is not scRNA-seq cell x gene count data (TACTiCS requires two scRNA-seq datasets plus a gene distance matrix) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Train a neural network classifier on cell types within one species (TACTiCS) and use transfer learning to propagate those labels to a second species, with gene similarity between species derived from ProtBERT-style protein-sequence embeddings rather than BLAST. The resulting trained model and cell embeddings can be saved with TACTiCS.save. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad248
skills.summary: Train a neural network classifier on cell types within one species (TACTiCS) and use transfer learning to propagate those labels to a second species, with gene similarity between species derived from ProtBERT-style protein-sequence embeddings rather than BLAST. The resulting trained model and cell embeddings can be saved with TACTiCS.save.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Gene matching only, without cell type label transfer — use BLAST or the protein-embedding gene-matching step alone instead of the full classifier/transfer-learning pipeline When you need to compare against a state-of-the-art baseline at matched dataset sizes, run SAMap on the same subsets rather than relying on TACTiCS training alone Input data is not scRNA-seq cell x gene count data (TACTiCS requires two scRNA-seq datasets plus a gene distance matrix)

skills.description: Use when aligning cell types across two species from scRNA-seq data (e.g. human vs mouse primary motor cortex) where one-to-one orthologous subclasses must be matched and label-transfer recall quantified.
skills.name: transfer-learning-label-propagation
skills.search_text: transfer-learning-label-propagation Use when aligning cell types across two species from scRNA-seq data (e.g. human vs mouse primary motor cortex) where one-to-one orthologous subclasses must be matched and label-transfer recall quantified. Input is a single-species dataset with no cross-species comparison goal — within-species classification alone does not need label propagation Cell types lack comparable protein-coding ortholog information across species, so the ProtBERT-based gene similarity matrix cannot be computed reliably The comparison requires benchmarking against Seurat or SAMap rather than reproducing TACTiCS's own matching scores http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Cross-species cell type matching by propagating cell-type labels between species via transfer learning, as implemented in TACTiCS: genes are matched by protein-sequence embeddings, cell types are classified within species by a neural network, and labels are transferred between species to score subclass correspondences (e.g. all 23 shared human-mouse cortical subclasses matched correctly). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad248
skills.summary: Cross-species cell type matching by propagating cell-type labels between species via transfer learning, as implemented in TACTiCS: genes are matched by protein-sequence embeddings, cell types are classified within species by a neural network, and labels are transferred between species to score subclass correspondences (e.g. all 23 shared human-mouse cortical subclasses matched correctly).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-species dataset with no cross-species comparison goal — within-species classification alone does not need label propagation Cell types lack comparable protein-coding ortholog information across species, so the ProtBERT-based gene similarity matrix cannot be computed reliably The comparison requires benchmarking against Seurat or SAMap rather than reproducing TACTiCS's own matching scores

skills.description: Use when you have two cross-species scRNA-seq datasets (e.g. human, mouse, marmoset motor cortex), a gene similarity distance matrix, and trained TACTiCS models, and need to quantify cell type matching performance via ADS and recall.
skills.name: transfer-learning-model-evaluation
skills.search_text: transfer-learning-model-evaluation Use when you have two cross-species scRNA-seq datasets (e.g. human, mouse, marmoset motor cortex), a gene similarity distance matrix, and trained TACTiCS models, and need to quantify cell type matching performance via ADS and recall. Input is a single-species dataset with no cross-species comparison goal — TACTiCS transfer learning propagates labels between species and is not a within-species annotation tool You lack a gene similarity distance matrix (or protein sequences/embeddings to build one with embed_proteins and calc_dist), since TACTiCS requires it as mandatory input http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluating the TACTiCS transfer-learning cell type matching model by running the TACTiCS class (tactics.py) under PyTorch on cross-species scRNA-seq datasets and scoring predictions with average dimensional score (ADS) and recall, including benchmarking against SAMap and Seurat and gene-matching ablations (ProtBERT vs BLAST). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad248
skills.summary: Evaluating the TACTiCS transfer-learning cell type matching model by running the TACTiCS class (tactics.py) under PyTorch on cross-species scRNA-seq datasets and scoring predictions with average dimensional score (ADS) and recall, including benchmarking against SAMap and Seurat and gene-matching ablations (ProtBERT vs BLAST).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-species dataset with no cross-species comparison goal — TACTiCS transfer learning propagates labels between species and is not a within-species annotation tool You lack a gene similarity distance matrix (or protein sequences/embeddings to build one with embed_proteins and calc_dist), since TACTiCS requires it as mandatory input

skills.description: Use when a reference scRNA-seq AnnData with known cell labels must annotate an unlabeled query dataset, when rare/unseen cell types should be flagged as 'Unknown', or when batch-insensitive integration with interpretable attention is needed.

skills.search_text: transformer-based-cell-type-annotation Use when a reference scRNA-seq AnnData with known cell labels must annotate an unlabeled query dataset, when rare/unseen cell types should be flagged as 'Unknown', or when batch-insensitive integration with interpretable attention is needed. The reference and query AnnData have different or unordered var_names (genes) — the README warns they must be consistent and in the same order; run the subsetting step first You need unsupervised de novo clustering without a labeled reference — TOSICA is a label-transfer tool between a reference and a query dataset Seurat-based comparator methods are required for very large numbers of batches (they were inapplicable for >85 batches in the pan-cancer scIB benchmark) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 TOSICA is a multi-head self-attention Transformer model for one-stop interpretable cell type annotation and label transfer from a reference scRNA-seq dataset to a query dataset, using pathway/regulon-masked tokens so attention layers remain traceable to input genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-35923-4
skills.summary: TOSICA is a multi-head self-attention Transformer model for one-stop interpretable cell type annotation and label transfer from a reference scRNA-seq dataset to a query dataset, using pathway/regulon-masked tokens so attention layers remain traceable to input genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference and query AnnData have different or unordered var_names (genes) — the README warns they must be consistent and in the same order; run the subsetting step first You need unsupervised de novo clustering without a labeled reference — TOSICA is a label-transfer tool between a reference and a query dataset Seurat-based comparator methods are required for very large numbers of batches (they were inapplicable for >85 batches in the pan-cancer scIB benchmark)

skills.summary: Reconstruct the tGPT autoregressive GPT-2-style decoder architecture (8 transformer decoder blocks, 1024 hidden units, 16 attention heads) in PyTorch/Hugging Face, configured per the reported training hyperparameters, to model gene-expression rankings over the 20,706-gene vocabulary.

The input is an unlabeled query dataset with no reference training labels — use TOSICA.pre for prediction instead of training You need a general-purpose cell clustering or deconvolution tool rather than supervised label transfer from a reference dataset The query and reference var_names (genes) differ or are not in the same order and cannot be reconciled — predictions will be invalid http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains TOSICA, a Transformer-based multi-head self-attention model for interpretable cell type annotation on scRNA-seq reference data, using gene-set-masked attention tokens, and supports controlled ablations such as knowledge-based versus random masks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-35923-4

skills.description: Use when implementing or reproducing a masked self-attention cell-type annotation model that maps n input genes to k pathway tokens and returns per-cell attention matrices and cell-type probability vectors.
skills.name: transformer-multi-head-self-attention-implementation
skills.search_text: transformer-multi-head-self-attention-implementation Use when implementing or reproducing a masked self-attention cell-type annotation model that maps n input genes to k pathway tokens and returns per-cell attention matrices and cell-type probability vectors. When the task requires latent-space embedding or dimensionality reduction of scRNA-seq data — the Transformer framework deliberately does not involve dimensionality reduction, so attention layers are kept traceable to original input features instead When reference and query gene spaces differ — the var_names (genes) of ref_adata and query_adata must be consistent and in the same order before prediction When no pathway/regulon gene-set knowledge (gmt file or pre-prepared mask) is available for the species or gene nomenclature http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Implements TOSICA's masked Transformer pipeline in torch: gene expression is embedded into pathway tokens via a masked linear embedding (W' = W*M) from a gmt-derived mask, a learnable CLS token is prepended, and multi-head self-attention followed by a softmax fully connected layer yields interpretable cell-type probabilities. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-35923-4
skills.summary: Implements TOSICA's masked Transformer pipeline in torch: gene expression is embedded into pathway tokens via a masked linear embedding (W' = W*M) from a gmt-derived mask, a learnable CLS token is prepended, and multi-head self-attention followed by a softmax fully connected layer yields interpretable cell-type probabilities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the task requires latent-space embedding or dimensionality reduction of scRNA-seq data — the Transformer framework deliberately does not involve dimensionality reduction, so attention layers are kept traceable to original input features instead When reference and query gene spaces differ — the var_names (genes) of ref_adata and query_adata must be consistent and in the same order before prediction When no pathway/regulon gene-set knowledge (gmt file or pre-prepared mask) is available for the species or gene nomenclature

skills.search_text: transformer-sequence-tokenization Use when raw single-cell count matrices (e.g., HCL, GSE134355) must be converted into autoregressive transformer input sequences, and gene expression rankings — not raw expression values — are the desired model input. skills.description: Use when MuTrans DynamicalAnalysis has returned attractor basins and optimized membership functions rho*(x) for a dataset, and you need to order cells along a specific state transition i->j, distinguish stable (attractor) cells from transition-layer cells, or feed per-cell TCS into downstream.
skills.name: transition-cell-score-computation
skills.search_text: transition-cell-score-computation Use when MuTrans DynamicalAnalysis has returned attractor basins and optimized membership functions rho*(x) for a dataset, and you need to order cells along a specific state transition i->j, distinguish stable (attractor) cells from transition-layer cells, or feed per-cell TCS into downstream. The dataset has few cells (e.g., the myelopoiesis Fluidigm C1 dataset), where high-resolution identification of transition cells requires special care and confirmation. You only have raw expression data and have not yet run MuTrans DynamicalAnalysis — TCS depends on the optimized membership function rho*(x) and attractor basins. Non-stationary effects such as cell cycle or cell proliferation dynamics dominate, which the current MuTrans method does not model. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Computation of the transition cell score (TCS) tau_ij(x) = rho_i*(x)/(rho_i*(x)+rho_j*(x)) in MuTrans's Transcendental procedure, which quantifies each cell's relative position between a starting attractor basin Si* and a targeting basin Sj* to separate stable cells from transition cells. It relies on the optimized soft membership function rho*(x) from MuTrans's multi-scale analysis of the rwTPM. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25548-w
skills.summary: Computation of the transition cell score (TCS) tau_ij(x) = rho_i*(x)/(rho_i*(x)+rho_j*(x)) in MuTrans's Transcendental procedure, which quantifies each cell's relative position between a starting attractor basin Si* and a targeting basin Sj* to separate stable cells from transition cells. It relies on the optimized soft membership function rho*(x) from MuTrans's multi-scale analysis of the rwTPM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has few cells (e.g., the myelopoiesis Fluidigm C1 dataset), where high-resolution identification of transition cells requires special care and confirmation. You only have raw expression data and have not yet run MuTrans DynamicalAnalysis — TCS depends on the optimized membership function rho*(x) and attractor basins. Non-stationary effects such as cell cycle or cell proliferation dynamics dominate, which the current MuTrans method does not model.

skills.description: Use when single-cell cluster labels have already been assigned (e.g., via FFC.fit()) and the goal is to detect cells with ambiguous labels — candidate novel transition cell types — along a developmental pseudo-time manifold.
skills.name: transition-cell-type-identification-along-pseudotime
skills.search_text: transition-cell-type-identification-along-pseudotime Use when single-cell cluster labels have already been assigned (e.g., via FFC.fit()) and the goal is to detect cells with ambiguous labels — candidate novel transition cell types — along a developmental pseudo-time manifold. When the data contain only one cluster: every data point can only receive one type of label, so the Monte Carlo validation cannot accurately estimate uncertainty When clustering itself has not yet been performed — this skill validates existing FFC labels, not raw expression matrices When applied to very high-dimensional representations: FFC should be performed with nonlinear dimensionality reduction (e.g., UMAP, t-SNE, PHATE), and the curse of dimensionality degrades clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identifies candidate transition cells along developmental pseudo-time by computing point-wise label entropies from Monte Carlo internal validation of Forest Fire Clustering, where high-entropy cells flag boundary/transition states. Posterior exclusion probabilities (p-values) are computed alongside to quantify per-cell label confidence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31107-8
skills.summary: Identifies candidate transition cells along developmental pseudo-time by computing point-wise label entropies from Monte Carlo internal validation of Forest Fire Clustering, where high-entropy cells flag boundary/transition states. Posterior exclusion probabilities (p-values) are computed alongside to quantify per-cell label confidence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the data contain only one cluster: every data point can only receive one type of label, so the Monte Carlo validation cannot accurately estimate uncertainty When clustering itself has not yet been performed — this skill validates existing FFC labels, not raw expression matrices When applied to very high-dimensional representations: FFC should be performed with nonlinear dimensionality reduction (e.g., UMAP, t-SNE, PHATE), and the curse of dimensionality degrades clustering

skills.search_text: transition-driver-gene-classification Use when you have MuTrans DynamicalAnalysis output (attractor basins, coarse-grained transition matrix, optimized membership function ρ*(x)) for a specific attractor-to-attractor transition and need the genes marking or driving that transition. skills.search_text: transition-entropy-cell-state-bifurcation-analysis Use when a single-cell trajectory dataset (e.g. time-course iPSC induction data) is suspected to contain a cell-fate bifurcation and you need to localize the critical transition point via attractor-basin membership entropy. Datasets with relatively few cells (e.g. the myelopoiesis Fluidigm C1 dataset), where the article notes special care is needed and high-resolution identification of transition cells requires a sufficiently large number of cells When the goal is stable-state clustering rather than transient/bifurcation dynamics — high-accuracy methods like SC3 or SIMLR tend to enforce distinct cell states and will not capture transition entropy Systems where non-stationary cell-cycle or cell-proliferation dynamics dominate, since these effects were not considered in the current method http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Quantifies per-cell transition entropy H(x) = -sum_k rho_k*(x) log rho_k*(x) from the MuTrans-optimized attractor membership function to detect bifurcation points in cell-fate dynamics, e.g. peaking near the critical transition during iPSC induction around day 2.5 before fates commit at day 3. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25548-w
skills.summary: Quantifies per-cell transition entropy H(x) = -sum_k rho_k*(x) log rho_k*(x) from the MuTrans-optimized attractor membership function to detect bifurcation points in cell-fate dynamics, e.g. peaking near the critical transition during iPSC induction around day 2.5 before fates commit at day 3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with relatively few cells (e.g. the myelopoiesis Fluidigm C1 dataset), where the article notes special care is needed and high-resolution identification of transition cells requires a sufficiently large number of cells When the goal is stable-state clustering rather than transient/bifurcation dynamics — high-accuracy methods like SC3 or SIMLR tend to enforce distinct cell states and will not capture transition entropy Systems where non-stationary cell-cycle or cell-proliferation dynamics dominate, since these effects were not considered in the current method

skills.description: Use when a MuTrans DynamicalAnalysis output (attractor basins Sk* and optimized membership ρ*(x)) is available and you need to score each cell's transition propensity, e.g. to locate saddle points between attractors in a cell-fate dynamical manifold.
skills.name: transition-entropy-quantification-from-membership
skills.search_text: transition-entropy-quantification-from-membership Use when a MuTrans DynamicalAnalysis output (attractor basins Sk* and optimized membership ρ*(x)) is available and you need to score each cell's transition propensity, e.g. to locate saddle points between attractors in a cell-fate dynamical manifold. You only need static clustering labels (e.g. Louvain/Leiden) without any notion of transition dynamics or transient cells The dataset has too few cells to resolve transition cells at high resolution (e.g. small myelopoiesis datasets, which the authors flag as needing special care) No membership/attractor-basin decomposition has been inferred yet — run DynamicalAnalysis first; the entropy cannot be computed directly from raw expression Computes MuTrans's per-cell transition entropy H(x) = −Σ_k ρk*(x) log ρk*(x) from the optimized cell-cluster membership function ρ*(x) returned by DynamicalAnalysis, to distinguish transition cells (high entropy, near saddle/maximum points between attractor basins) from meta-stable cells (entropy near zero). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25548-w
skills.summary: Computes MuTrans's per-cell transition entropy H(x) = −Σ_k ρk*(x) log ρk*(x) from the optimized cell-cluster membership function ρ*(x) returned by DynamicalAnalysis, to distinguish transition cells (high entropy, near saddle/maximum points between attractor basins) from meta-stable cells (entropy near zero).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need static clustering labels (e.g. Louvain/Leiden) without any notion of transition dynamics or transient cells The dataset has too few cells to resolve transition cells at high resolution (e.g. small myelopoiesis datasets, which the authors flag as needing special care) No membership/attractor-basin decomposition has been inferred yet — run DynamicalAnalysis first; the entropy cannot be computed directly from raw expression
