skills.name: transition-gene-classification-td-ih-ms
skills.search_text: transition-gene-classification-td-ih-ms Use when a stable-attractor-to-attractor transition has been defined (e.g., states i and j from MuTrans dynamical analysis) and you need to identify which genes drive the transition, mark transient/hybrid cells, or label meta-stable cells. When attractor basins and the soft membership matrix have not yet been established (no prior dynamical_analysis on the dataset) When the analysis goal is pseudo-time ordering or clustering rather than gene classification along a specific two-state transition When the dataset is too small for high-resolution transition-cell identification (the article notes special care is needed for small datasets like myelopoiesis) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Classifies genes along a cell-fate transition (e.g., Pro-B to Pre-B) into transition-driver (TD), intermediate/hybrid-state (IH), and meta-stable (MS) categories using MuTrans' Transcendental/GeneAnalysis procedure, which couples transition cell scores (TCS) with gene expression dynamics across the reconstructed dynamical manifold. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25548-w
skills.summary: Classifies genes along a cell-fate transition (e.g., Pro-B to Pre-B) into transition-driver (TD), intermediate/hybrid-state (IH), and meta-stable (MS) categories using MuTrans' Transcendental/GeneAnalysis procedure, which couples transition cell scores (TCS) with gene expression dynamics across the reconstructed dynamical manifold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When attractor basins and the soft membership matrix have not yet been established (no prior dynamical_analysis on the dataset) When the analysis goal is pseudo-time ordering or clustering rather than gene classification along a specific two-state transition When the dataset is too small for high-resolution transition-cell identification (the article notes special care is needed for small datasets like myelopoiesis)

skills.description: Use when a large single-cell dataset makes full MuTrans dynamical_analysis slow, and you must verify that DECLARE-aggregated micro-states reproduce coarse-grained transition probabilities and transition path likelihoods computed on all cells, plus measure the speedup.
skills.name: transition-path-likelihood-comparison
skills.search_text: transition-path-likelihood-comparison Use when a large single-cell dataset makes full MuTrans dynamical_analysis slow, and you must verify that DECLARE-aggregated micro-states reproduce coarse-grained transition probabilities and transition path likelihoods computed on all cells, plus measure the speedup. Dataset is small (e.g., the Fluidigm C1 myelopoiesis data), where the article notes special care is needed and full-data analysis without aggregation is feasible Goal is de novo clustering or pseudotime ordering (SC3/SIMLR, DPT/Slingshot/Monocle) rather than validating dynamics-preserving aggregation of a MuTrans stochastic dynamical analysis The analysis does not involve transition probabilities or transition path likelihoods, so there is nothing to compare against a DECLARE-accelerated run http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compares the cell-fate transition path likelihoods and dynamical manifold structure produced by full MuTrans runs versus runs accelerated with the DECLARE dynamics-preserving aggregation module, and quantifies the wall-clock speedup on large-scale datasets such as the human bone-marrow hematopoiesis data (10X Chromium). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25548-w
skills.summary: Compares the cell-fate transition path likelihoods and dynamical manifold structure produced by full MuTrans runs versus runs accelerated with the DECLARE dynamics-preserving aggregation module, and quantifies the wall-clock speedup on large-scale datasets such as the human bone-marrow hematopoiesis data (10X Chromium).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Dataset is small (e.g., the Fluidigm C1 myelopoiesis data), where the article notes special care is needed and full-data analysis without aggregation is feasible Goal is de novo clustering or pseudotime ordering (SC3/SIMLR, DPT/Slingshot/Monocle) rather than validating dynamics-preserving aggregation of a MuTrans stochastic dynamical analysis The analysis does not involve transition probabilities or transition path likelihoods, so there is nothing to compare against a DECLARE-accelerated run

skills.description: Use when single-cell transcriptome data has been reduced to attractor basins via MuTrans multi-scale rwTPM analysis and you need to reconstruct transition trajectories/lineage between a defined starting and target attractor state, e.g. bifurcating lineages.
skills.name: transition-path-theory-lineage-inference
skills.search_text: transition-path-theory-lineage-inference Use when single-cell transcriptome data has been reduced to attractor basins via MuTrans multi-scale rwTPM analysis and you need to reconstruct transition trajectories/lineage between a defined starting and target attractor state, e.g. bifurcating lineages. When attractor basins and the coarse-grained rwTPM have not yet been computed — lineage inference requires the multi-scale analysis output When the number of cells is too small for high-resolution identification of transition cells (e.g. the myelopoiesis dataset), where transition-cell calls need special confirmation When cell-cycle or proliferation-driven non-stationary dynamics dominate, which the current method does not model http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Infer cell-fate lineages by applying coarse-grained transition path theory on the MuTrans dynamical manifold, using Most Probable Path Tree (MPPT) or Maximum Probability Flow Tree (MPFT) to recover bifurcating trajectories between attractor basins. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25548-w
skills.summary: Infer cell-fate lineages by applying coarse-grained transition path theory on the MuTrans dynamical manifold, using Most Probable Path Tree (MPPT) or Maximum Probability Flow Tree (MPFT) to recover bifurcating trajectories between attractor basins.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When attractor basins and the coarse-grained rwTPM have not yet been computed — lineage inference requires the multi-scale analysis output When the number of cells is too small for high-resolution identification of transition cells (e.g. the myelopoiesis dataset), where transition-cell calls need special confirmation When cell-cycle or proliferation-driven non-stationary dynamics dominate, which the current method does not model

skills.description: Use when single-cell transcriptome data has been multi-scale analyzed (attractor basins and coarse-grained transition probabilities from MuTrans dynamical_analysis) and you must infer lineage/transition path likelihoods between states, e.g. routing E->M flux through intermediate cell states.
skills.name: transition-path-theory-trajectory-likelihood-quantification
skills.search_text: transition-path-theory-trajectory-likelihood-quantification Use when single-cell transcriptome data has been multi-scale analyzed (attractor basins and coarse-grained transition probabilities from MuTrans dynamical_analysis) and you must infer lineage/transition path likelihoods between states, e.g. routing E->M flux through intermediate cell states. Dataset is small (e.g. the Olsson myelopoiesis dataset), where transition-cell analysis needs special care and confirmation The goal is static clustering only (SC3/SIMLR-style distinct states) rather than transition paths and trajectory likelihoods Non-stationary effects from cell cycle or proliferation dynamics dominate the system, which the current method does not model http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantify the likelihood of all possible transition trajectories between cell states by applying coarse-grained transition path theory (Most Probable Path Tree, MPPT, or Maximum Probability Flow Tree, MPFT) on the MuTrans multiscale stochastic dynamics output, as done for the E->ICS->M routes in the SCC Smart-Seq2 EMT dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25548-w
skills.summary: Quantify the likelihood of all possible transition trajectories between cell states by applying coarse-grained transition path theory (Most Probable Path Tree, MPPT, or Maximum Probability Flow Tree, MPFT) on the MuTrans multiscale stochastic dynamics output, as done for the E->ICS->M routes in the SCC Smart-Seq2 EMT dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Dataset is small (e.g. the Olsson myelopoiesis dataset), where transition-cell analysis needs special care and confirmation The goal is static clustering only (SC3/SIMLR-style distinct states) rather than transition paths and trajectory likelihoods Non-stationary effects from cell cycle or proliferation dynamics dominate the system, which the current method does not model

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data capture a differentiation process and you need quantitative fate probabilities from progenitor clusters to terminal states, using RNA velocity or a biologically defined differentiation potential as the biasing force.
skills.name: transition-probability-estimation-single-cell
skills.search_text: transition-probability-estimation-single-cell Use when scRNA-seq data capture a differentiation process and you need quantitative fate probabilities from progenitor clusters to terminal states, using RNA velocity or a biologically defined differentiation potential as the biasing force. Robust RNA velocity profiles are unavailable AND prior biological knowledge to define the differentiation potential cannot be supplied (e.g. cancer studies) Dimensionality reduction of the input space relies on methods like UMAP whose lack of biological interpretability undermines nearest-neighbor graph construction The goal is TF activity estimation rather than fate transition probabilities (use the downstream linear-model-of-gene-regulation step instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Estimates cell-fate transition probabilities in single-cell differentiation data using FateCompass's discrete Markov process, biased by RNA velocity or a differentiation-potential gradient, then propagates stochastic trajectories to quantify fate probabilities per progenitor cluster. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100512
skills.summary: Estimates cell-fate transition probabilities in single-cell differentiation data using FateCompass's discrete Markov process, biased by RNA velocity or a differentiation-potential gradient, then propagates stochastic trajectories to quantify fate probabilities per progenitor cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Robust RNA velocity profiles are unavailable AND prior biological knowledge to define the differentiation potential cannot be supplied (e.g. cancer studies) Dimensionality reduction of the input space relies on methods like UMAP whose lack of biological interpretability undermines nearest-neighbor graph construction The goal is TF activity estimation rather than fate transition probabilities (use the downstream linear-model-of-gene-regulation step instead)

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data contain annotated subpopulations and you need transition-specific ranked lists of overexpression or knockdown candidates for a defined start-to-target cell-state transition, such as reprogramming B-cells or monocytes/DCs to HSPCs.
skills.name: transition-specific-gene-expression-scoring
skills.search_text: transition-specific-gene-expression-scoring Use when single-cell RNA-seq data contain annotated subpopulations and you need transition-specific ranked lists of overexpression or knockdown candidates for a defined start-to-target cell-state transition, such as reprogramming B-cells or monocytes/DCs to HSPCs. When you only need a single linear pseudotemporal ordering without transition-specific regulator ranking — simpler tools (Waterfall, Monocle 1) or diffusion pseudotime may suffice When the input is not single-cell data with identifiable subpopulations (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or an already-aggregated feature table) When the goal is functional validation of engraftable HSC-like cells — the article explicitly defers thorough characterization of each identified gene's potential to future work http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Score genes and transcriptional regulators along CellRouter-reconstructed trajectories between defined subpopulations (e.g., B-cells subpop 10 and mono/DC subpop 17 toward HSPCs subpop 12 in GSE75478) to rank overexpression and knockdown candidates for cellular reprogramming. Rationale: transition-specific scoring integrates multi-state flow-network trajectories with gene regulatory networks to capture regulators driving or mediating specific cell-fate transitions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03214-y
skills.summary: Score genes and transcriptional regulators along CellRouter-reconstructed trajectories between defined subpopulations (e.g., B-cells subpop 10 and mono/DC subpop 17 toward HSPCs subpop 12 in GSE75478) to rank overexpression and knockdown candidates for cellular reprogramming. Rationale: transition-specific scoring integrates multi-state flow-network trajectories with gene regulatory networks to capture regulators driving or mediating specific cell-fate transitions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you only need a single linear pseudotemporal ordering without transition-specific regulator ranking — simpler tools (Waterfall, Monocle 1) or diffusion pseudotime may suffice When the input is not single-cell data with identifiable subpopulations (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or an already-aggregated feature table) When the goal is functional validation of engraftable HSC-like cells — the article explicitly defers thorough characterization of each identified gene's potential to future work

skills.description: Use when building a ground-truth bulk multi-omics simulation over a time-series or two-group design, where DEGs must carry labeled temporal profiles (scaled fold change, transitory, or flat) and regulator layers must reflect activator/repressor coupling.
skills.name: transitory-and-flat-temporal-profile-simulation
skills.search_text: transitory-and-flat-temporal-profile-simulation Use when building a ground-truth bulk multi-omics simulation over a time-series or two-group design, where DEGs must carry labeled temporal profiles (scaled fold change, transitory, or flat) and regulator layers must reflect activator/repressor coupling. Input is single-cell data — this skill covers the bulk mosim workflow only; single-cell simulation goes through sc_mosim, which relies on SPARSim functionality The goal is a spatially resolved GRN simulation — MOSim is not prepared to simulate GRNs with spatial resolution The target omics layers are proteomics or metabolomics, which are outside MOSim's simulated regulatory omics (RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, miRNA-seq, ChIP-seq, Methyl-seq, TFs) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generates bulk RNA-seq count data under the MOSim (mosim) workflow by fitting per-gene negative-binomial mean/dispersion parameters from a seed sample and assigning differentially expressed genes one of five temporal profiles (continuous induction/repression, transitory induction/repression, flat), then coupling each regulator's profile to its target genes as same-pattern (activator) or mirrored/opposite-pattern (repressor). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf110
skills.summary: Generates bulk RNA-seq count data under the MOSim (mosim) workflow by fitting per-gene negative-binomial mean/dispersion parameters from a seed sample and assigning differentially expressed genes one of five temporal profiles (continuous induction/repression, transitory induction/repression, flat), then coupling each regulator's profile to its target genes as same-pattern (activator) or mirrored/opposite-pattern (repressor).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell data — this skill covers the bulk mosim workflow only; single-cell simulation goes through sc_mosim, which relies on SPARSim functionality The goal is a spatially resolved GRN simulation — MOSim is not prepared to simulate GRNs with spatial resolution The target omics layers are proteomics or metabolomics, which are outside MOSim's simulated regulatory omics (RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, miRNA-seq, ChIP-seq, Methyl-seq, TFs)

skills.description: Use when raw RNA-seq FASTQ files come from a species without a reference transcriptome, and the goal is KO-level read quantification and functional profiling instead of de novo assembly plus annotation transfer.
skills.name: translated-read-alignment-to-kegg-ortholog-database
skills.search_text: translated-read-alignment-to-kegg-ortholog-database Use when raw RNA-seq FASTQ files come from a species without a reference transcriptome, and the goal is KO-level read quantification and functional profiling instead of de novo assembly plus annotation transfer. When the gene of interest is not in the KO system — KO-based annotation covers only 76.16% of human and 61.40% of zebrafish protein-coding genes, and vitellogenin is absent from the KO system entirely When the EcoOmicsDB sub-group database does not match the sample's taxonomy (e.g., reads from a protist sample mapped to the 'fishes' database) — key functional groups will be missed When a well-annotated reference transcriptome exists and conventional genome-based quantification (e.g., Kallisto with minimum quality score 25) is preferable http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Maps RNA-seq FASTQ reads from any eukaryotic species directly to a high-resolution KEGG ortholog (KO) protein database via translated search (Seq2Fun), replacing transcript assembly and BLAST-based annotation transfer. Produces KO-level count tables for non-model species without a reference transcriptome. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38785-y
skills.summary: Maps RNA-seq FASTQ reads from any eukaryotic species directly to a high-resolution KEGG ortholog (KO) protein database via translated search (Seq2Fun), replacing transcript assembly and BLAST-based annotation transfer. Produces KO-level count tables for non-model species without a reference transcriptome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the gene of interest is not in the KO system — KO-based annotation covers only 76.16% of human and 61.40% of zebrafish protein-coding genes, and vitellogenin is absent from the KO system entirely When the EcoOmicsDB sub-group database does not match the sample's taxonomy (e.g., reads from a protist sample mapped to the 'fishes' database) — key functional groups will be missed When a well-annotated reference transcriptome exists and conventional genome-based quantification (e.g., Kallisto with minimum quality score 25) is preferable

skills.description: Use when raw RNA-seq FASTQ reads from any eukaryotic (especially non-model) species must be quantified and functionally annotated without a reference transcriptome, by mapping translated reads directly to KO orthologs.
skills.name: translated-read-to-ortholog-mapping
skills.search_text: translated-read-to-ortholog-mapping Use when raw RNA-seq FASTQ reads from any eukaryotic (especially non-model) species must be quantified and functionally annotated without a reference transcriptome, by mapping translated reads directly to KO orthologs. The organism has a well-annotated reference transcriptome and the analysis requires full gene/transcript-level IDs (KO coverage is limited: only 76.16% of human and 61.40% of zebrafish protein-coding genes carry KOs; e.g., vitellogenin is absent from the KO system) A count table or gene list already exists — downstream analysis should use ExpressAnalystR's matrix/gene-list modules instead of re-quantifying reads The protein sub-group database is mismatched to the sample (e.g., mapping protist reads against the 'Fishes' database), which can miss key functional groups http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Directly maps raw RNA-seq FASTQ reads to protein ortholog (KEGG KO) databases by translating each cleaned read in all reading frames and performing a BLOSUM62-scored peptide search, replacing transcript assembly and annotation in non-model eukaryotes (implemented as Seq2Fun/ExpressAnalyst). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38785-y
skills.summary: Directly maps raw RNA-seq FASTQ reads to protein ortholog (KEGG KO) databases by translating each cleaned read in all reading frames and performing a BLOSUM62-scored peptide search, replacing transcript assembly and annotation in non-model eukaryotes (implemented as Seq2Fun/ExpressAnalyst).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism has a well-annotated reference transcriptome and the analysis requires full gene/transcript-level IDs (KO coverage is limited: only 76.16% of human and 61.40% of zebrafish protein-coding genes carry KOs; e.g., vitellogenin is absent from the KO system) A count table or gene list already exists — downstream analysis should use ExpressAnalystR's matrix/gene-list modules instead of re-quantifying reads The protein sub-group database is mismatched to the sample (e.g., mapping protist reads against the 'Fishes' database), which can miss key functional groups

skills.description: Use when scRNA-Seq BAM files (CellRanger or STAR output) need TE expression quantified per genomic locus, or when comparing locus-specific vs family-metagene TE quantification for cell-type marker discovery.
skills.name: transposable-element-expression-matrix-analysis
skills.search_text: transposable-element-expression-matrix-analysis Use when scRNA-Seq BAM files (CellRanger or STAR output) need TE expression quantified per genomic locus, or when comparing locus-specific vs family-metagene TE quantification for cell-type marker discovery. The input is already a gene/TE feature-count matrix — quantification is done; proceed directly to Seurat marker analysis The goal is to detect TEs acting as alternative transcription start sites — 3'-end 10X data cannot detect these due to 3' bias A non-TE repeat analysis (e.g. Satellites) is needed — note scTE indexes do not filter non-TE repeats, so family-metagene matrices may contain non-TE repeat rows that must be excluded http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Generate gene + transposable element (TE) expression matrices from single-cell RNA-Seq data at locus-specific resolution using SoloTE, and benchmark family-level summarization (scTE) against locus-level quantification for marker recovery and log2(FC) accuracy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04020-5
skills.summary: Generate gene + transposable element (TE) expression matrices from single-cell RNA-Seq data at locus-specific resolution using SoloTE, and benchmark family-level summarization (scTE) against locus-level quantification for marker recovery and log2(FC) accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a gene/TE feature-count matrix — quantification is done; proceed directly to Seurat marker analysis The goal is to detect TEs acting as alternative transcription start sites — 3'-end 10X data cannot detect these due to 3' bias A non-TE repeat analysis (e.g. Satellites) is needed — note scTE indexes do not filter non-TE repeats, so family-metagene matrices may contain non-TE repeat rows that must be excluded

skills.description: Use when you have single-cell RNA-seq (or ATAC-seq) BAM/SAM alignments from Cell Ranger or STARsolo and need per-cell TE expression counts alongside gene counts, e.g. to detect cell-type-specific or branch-restricted TE expression.
skills.name: transposable-element-expression-quantification
skills.search_text: transposable-element-expression-quantification Use when you have single-cell RNA-seq (or ATAC-seq) BAM/SAM alignments from Cell Ranger or STARsolo and need per-cell TE expression counts alongside gene counts, e.g. to detect cell-type-specific or branch-restricted TE expression. The input is already a gene/TE count matrix or feature table — scTE requires raw aligned BAM/SAM reads The analysis targets bulk RNA-seq read-to-TE counting with a different tool (e.g. te_counter for paired-end bulk BAMs), not single-cell barcode/UMI demultiplexing Only filtered Cell Ranger BAMs are available and per-cell barcode/UMI tags are absent, since unfiltered alignment files are highly recommended http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Quantify transposable element (TE) expression per cell from single-cell sequencing data using the scTE pipeline, which assigns reads first to gene exons and then to TE metagenes, producing a cell-by-gene/TE count matrix from BAM/SAM alignments. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21808-x
skills.summary: Quantify transposable element (TE) expression per cell from single-cell sequencing data using the scTE pipeline, which assigns reads first to gene exons and then to TE metagenes, producing a cell-by-gene/TE count matrix from BAM/SAM alignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a gene/TE count matrix or feature table — scTE requires raw aligned BAM/SAM reads The analysis targets bulk RNA-seq read-to-TE counting with a different tool (e.g. te_counter for paired-end bulk BAMs), not single-cell barcode/UMI demultiplexing Only filtered Cell Ranger BAMs are available and per-cell barcode/UMI tags are absent, since unfiltered alignment files are highly recommended

skills.description: Use when you need locus-specific TE expression quantification from scRNA-Seq BAM files (STAR or CellRanger) to identify TE markers of cell populations, especially repetitive-element activity in subpopulations like 2C-like cells or cancer clusters.
skills.name: transposable-element-locus-expression-quantification
skills.search_text: transposable-element-locus-expression-quantification Use when you need locus-specific TE expression quantification from scRNA-Seq BAM files (STAR or CellRanger) to identify TE markers of cell populations, especially repetitive-element activity in subpopulations like 2C-like cells or cancer clusters. The analysis already provides a combined gene+TE feature matrix and only downstream clustering/markers are needed — do not re-quantify The biology requires detecting TEs acting as alternative transcription start sites in 3'-end 10X data — the 3' bias prevents detection of such events The genome has a large proportion of transpositionally-active, genetically intact TE copies — most reads will multi-map and locus-level resolution will collapse to family-level summaries http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Quantifies transposable element (TE) expression at individual genomic locus resolution in scRNA-Seq data using the SoloTE pipeline, producing a combined gene+TE expression matrix compatible with Seurat for downstream cell-type marker analysis. Retains genomic location that family-level tools like scTE discard. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04020-5
skills.summary: Quantifies transposable element (TE) expression at individual genomic locus resolution in scRNA-Seq data using the SoloTE pipeline, producing a combined gene+TE expression matrix compatible with Seurat for downstream cell-type marker analysis. Retains genomic location that family-level tools like scTE discard.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis already provides a combined gene+TE feature matrix and only downstream clustering/markers are needed — do not re-quantify The biology requires detecting TEs acting as alternative transcription start sites in 3'-end 10X data — the 3' bias prevents detection of such events The genome has a large proportion of transpositionally-active, genetically intact TE copies — most reads will multi-map and locus-level resolution will collapse to family-level summaries

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how accurately a TE quantification method recovers locus-specific abundances by comparing against simulated reads with known ground-truth locus expression, e.g., simulated ~300 bp Alu repeats.
skills.name: transposable-element-read-simulation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: transposable-element-read-simulation-benchmarking Use when you need to quantify how accurately a TE quantification method recovers locus-specific abundances by comparing against simulated reads with known ground-truth locus expression, e.g., simulated ~300 bp Alu repeats. The question is TE quantification on real data where no ground-truth locus abundances exist — use downstream biological validation (e.g., long-read scNanoRNA-seq or PacBio) instead of simulation The target TE is a long autonomously expressed element such as L1HS spanning several thousand bases, which the MATES 2001-bp coverage vector design cannot fully capture The goal is subfamily-level-only TE quantification where multi-mapping read allocation is irrelevant http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark locus-specific TE quantification accuracy by generating synthetic single-cell read datasets with known ground truth (Polyester) and scoring MATES against baselines (scTE, SoloTE) on locus-level R2, read recapture rate, and isoform counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-53114-7
skills.summary: Benchmark locus-specific TE quantification accuracy by generating synthetic single-cell read datasets with known ground truth (Polyester) and scoring MATES against baselines (scTE, SoloTE) on locus-level R2, read recapture rate, and isoform counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is TE quantification on real data where no ground-truth locus abundances exist — use downstream biological validation (e.g., long-read scNanoRNA-seq or PacBio) instead of simulation The target TE is a long autonomously expressed element such as L1HS spanning several thousand bases, which the MATES 2001-bp coverage vector design cannot fully capture The goal is subfamily-level-only TE quantification where multi-mapping read allocation is irrelevant

skills.description: Use when analyzing pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns from bacterial transposon insertion sequencing or RNA-seq datasets with multiple antibiotic treatments, and you need a data-driven, quadrant-based summary of extreme gene changes.
skills.name: transposon-insertion-sequencing-differential-expression-interpretation
skills.search_text: transposon-insertion-sequencing-differential-expression-interpretation Use when analyzing pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns from bacterial transposon insertion sequencing or RNA-seq datasets with multiple antibiotic treatments, and you need a data-driven, quadrant-based summary of extreme gene changes. Input is raw sequencing data or differential analysis has not yet been performed — the scorecard requires pre-computed fold-change and adjusted p-value columns in the CSV You need standard four-way plots without statistical-significance filtering or cross-comparison merging (set 'multiplication factor' to 1 produces a four-way plot, defeating the scorecard's purpose) The dataset has fewer than two pairwise treatment-vs-control comparisons, since the scorecard's aggregation functions (multiple_view, count_frequencies, common_entries) assume a main folder of multiple comparison subfolders http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Interpret differential abundance/expression from Staphylococcus aureus USA300 (SAUSA300) transposon insertion sequencing data (Dataset 1, VAN/LZD/CPT/DEL) using the Python Scorecard library, which groups genes by fold-change magnitude and statistical significance across pairwise comparisons instead of preselecting genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00284-025-04435-3
skills.summary: Interpret differential abundance/expression from Staphylococcus aureus USA300 (SAUSA300) transposon insertion sequencing data (Dataset 1, VAN/LZD/CPT/DEL) using the Python Scorecard library, which groups genes by fold-change magnitude and statistical significance across pairwise comparisons instead of preselecting genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data or differential analysis has not yet been performed — the scorecard requires pre-computed fold-change and adjusted p-value columns in the CSV You need standard four-way plots without statistical-significance filtering or cross-comparison merging (set 'multiplication factor' to 1 produces a four-way plot, defeating the scorecard's purpose) The dataset has fewer than two pairwise treatment-vs-control comparisons, since the scorecard's aggregation functions (multiple_view, count_frequencies, common_entries) assume a main folder of multiple comparison subfolders

skills.description: Use when you have Cyclum-fitted pseudo-time for matched treated and control single-cell datasets and want to nominate target genes by differential circular expression patterns.
skills.name: treated-vs-control-gene-ranking
skills.search_text: treated-vs-control-gene-ranking Use when you have Cyclum-fitted pseudo-time for matched treated and control single-cell datasets and want to nominate target genes by differential circular expression patterns. Data are not single-cell expression matrices with an expected periodic (cell-cycle-like) process — Cyclum relies on circular manifolds rather than marker genes Only one condition is available; the skill requires fitting separate treated and control models to compute a per-gene difference The goal is cell-cycle effect removal or pseudotime refinement rather than differential circular-pattern gene nomination http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Ranks genes by the treated-minus-control difference in circular-pattern magnitude inferred by Cyclum, to nominate genes (e.g., LDHA, ENO1) whose periodic expression kinetics change between drug-treated and control scRNA-seq samples. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Ranks genes by the treated-minus-control difference in circular-pattern magnitude inferred by Cyclum, to nominate genes (e.g., LDHA, ENO1) whose periodic expression kinetics change between drug-treated and control scRNA-seq samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not single-cell expression matrices with an expected periodic (cell-cycle-like) process — Cyclum relies on circular manifolds rather than marker genes Only one condition is available; the skill requires fitting separate treated and control models to compute a per-gene difference The goal is cell-cycle effect removal or pseudotime refinement rather than differential circular-pattern gene nomination

skills.name: treatment-arm-subsetting-of-clinical-rnaseq
skills.search_text: treatment-arm-subsetting-of-clinical-rnaseq Use when you need the >16,000-gene rituximab-arm RNA-seq subset (n=68) from E-MTAB-11611 as a binary-classification input matrix for nested CV or feature-selection benchmarks. Input is already a feature-reduced or pre-filtered expression matrix for a single arm — the median-expression cut-off and arm subsetting would be applied twice Analysis targets multi-class or regression outcomes — this skill produces a binary rituximab-arm classification setup Sample size permits a conventional 2/3-1/3 train/test split — nested CV on the full subset is designed for the P >> n regime where such splits are unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Prepares the R4RA rheumatoid arthritis RNA-seq benchmark by downloading raw data for E-MTAB-11611 from ArrayExpress, applying a median-expression gene cut-off, and subsetting samples to the rituximab treatment arm (n=68) with an outcome vector and predictor matrix for nested CV modelling. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad048
skills.summary: Prepares the R4RA rheumatoid arthritis RNA-seq benchmark by downloading raw data for E-MTAB-11611 from ArrayExpress, applying a median-expression gene cut-off, and subsetting samples to the rituximab treatment arm (n=68) with an outcome vector and predictor matrix for nested CV modelling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature-reduced or pre-filtered expression matrix for a single arm — the median-expression cut-off and arm subsetting would be applied twice Analysis targets multi-class or regression outcomes — this skill produces a binary rituximab-arm classification setup Sample size permits a conventional 2/3-1/3 train/test split — nested CV on the full subset is designed for the P >> n regime where such splits are unreliable

skills.description: Use when a randomized or observational dataset has a treatment assignment variable, a response outcome, and covariates, and the goal is to identify subgroups with differential treatment effects (precision medicine setting).

skills.search_text: treatment-effect-subgroup-verification Use when a randomized or observational dataset has a treatment assignment variable, a response outcome, and covariates, and the goal is to identify subgroups with differential treatment effects (precision medicine setting). The goal is single-population treatment effect estimation without subgroup identification — DIPM is specifically a classification tree for identifying subgroups relevant to the precision medicine setting Predictors are continuous-only with no treatment assignment variable, so no treatment-contrast comparisons within subgroups can be formed A survival-type outcome is the target — use the package's spmtree function rather than the tree-based dipm workflow for subgroup search http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Fits a DIPM classification tree with the dipm R package to identify subgroups where subjects perform especially well or poorly under a particular treatment assignment, then verifies which treatment is optimal in each terminal-node subgroup. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac041
skills.summary: Fits a DIPM classification tree with the dipm R package to identify subgroups where subjects perform especially well or poorly under a particular treatment assignment, then verifies which treatment is optimal in each terminal-node subgroup.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is single-population treatment effect estimation without subgroup identification — DIPM is specifically a classification tree for identifying subgroups relevant to the precision medicine setting Predictors are continuous-only with no treatment assignment variable, so no treatment-contrast comparisons within subgroups can be formed A survival-type outcome is the target — use the package's spmtree function rather than the tree-based dipm workflow for subgroup search

skills.search_text: treatment-outcome-association-visualization Use when bulk tumor transcriptomes have been converted to tGPT attention features and you need to test and visualize whether per-head entropy/importance differs across immunotherapy response groups (CR/PR/SD/PD). Input is single-cell data for clustering or trajectory tasks — the paper's single-cell workflow uses embedding features with Leiden clustering, not attention-entropy response association The cohort lacks clinical response annotations (e.g. RECIST categories), so no responder/non-responder grouping can be formed Only actual expression levels are available without gene rankings — tGPT requires descending expression rankings of top-expressing genes as input http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Links tGPT-derived attention head entropy/importance features from bulk tumor transcriptomes to patient response to immune checkpoint blockade, and renders group-level summary panels (Figure 5G-5N style) showing entropy distributions stratified by RECIST response. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.106536
skills.summary: Links tGPT-derived attention head entropy/importance features from bulk tumor transcriptomes to patient response to immune checkpoint blockade, and renders group-level summary panels (Figure 5G-5N style) showing entropy distributions stratified by RECIST response.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell data for clustering or trajectory tasks — the paper's single-cell workflow uses embedding features with Leiden clustering, not attention-entropy response association The cohort lacks clinical response annotations (e.g. RECIST categories), so no responder/non-responder grouping can be formed Only actual expression levels are available without gene rankings — tGPT requires descending expression rankings of top-expressing genes as input

skills.description: Use when a cell-type perturbation signature discovered in single-cell immunotherapy cohorts (e.g., scDist FCER1G+ NK cells) must be tested against survival and radiologic response in independent bulk RNA-seq cohorts with clinical metadata.
skills.name: treatment-response-association-analysis
skills.search_text: treatment-response-association-analysis Use when a cell-type perturbation signature discovered in single-cell immunotherapy cohorts (e.g., scDist FCER1G+ NK cells) must be tested against survival and radiologic response in independent bulk RNA-seq cohorts with clinical metadata. The goal is detecting perturbed cell types in single-cell data itself — use scDist differential-state analysis instead of bulk signature validation No matched survival or radiologic response metadata exists for the bulk cohorts, so neither the KM/log-rank nor responder contrast can be computed Differential abundance (cell-proportion differences) is the question of interest — tools like DA-seq, Milo, or Meld address that, not transcriptomic signature-score association testing http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Validates single-cell-derived treatment-response signatures in independent bulk transcriptomes: compute a per-patient signature score (e.g., the NK-2/FCER1G+ NK-cell signature from scDist), dichotomize at the cohort median, and test association with overall survival via Kaplan-Meier/log-rank and with radiologic response via responder-vs-non-responder contrasts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51649-3
skills.summary: Validates single-cell-derived treatment-response signatures in independent bulk transcriptomes: compute a per-patient signature score (e.g., the NK-2/FCER1G+ NK-cell signature from scDist), dichotomize at the cohort median, and test association with overall survival via Kaplan-Meier/log-rank and with radiologic response via responder-vs-non-responder contrasts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is detecting perturbed cell types in single-cell data itself — use scDist differential-state analysis instead of bulk signature validation No matched survival or radiologic response metadata exists for the bulk cohorts, so neither the KM/log-rank nor responder contrast can be computed Differential abundance (cell-proportion differences) is the question of interest — tools like DA-seq, Milo, or Meld address that, not transcriptomic signature-score association testing

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq time-series has treated vs untreated conditions across timepoints (e.g., cisplatin X1–X4 in TNBC PDX) and GeneVector metagenes must be classified as treatment-specific using regression coefficients on module scores.
skills.name: treatment-response-linear-regression-coefficient-testing
skills.search_text: treatment-response-linear-regression-coefficient-testing Use when a scRNA-seq time-series has treated vs untreated conditions across timepoints (e.g., cisplatin X1–X4 in TNBC PDX) and GeneVector metagenes must be classified as treatment-specific using regression coefficients on module scores. The input lacks a treatment/condition contrast (e.g., a single-sample dataset or the PBMC interferon-stimulation cell-annotation workflow) — metagene module scores cannot be regressed on treatment status. Metagenes have not yet been extracted from the GeneVector embedding — this skill assumes GeneEmbedding.get_adata(resolution=40) and get_metagenes have already been run. The question is cell type annotation or batch correction rather than identifying treatment-dependent transcriptional programs — use CellEmbedding phenotype_probability or batch_correct instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Statistical skill for calling treatment-dependent metagenes: per-metagene module scores are regressed on treatment status across timepoints, and coefficients/p-values are thresholded (beta_treated > 0.1, Bonferroni-corrected p = 0.001, beta_treated > beta_untreated) to nominate drug-resistance programs such as the TGF-beta-signaling metagene 24 in cisplatin-treated TNBC PDXs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39985-2
skills.summary: Statistical skill for calling treatment-dependent metagenes: per-metagene module scores are regressed on treatment status across timepoints, and coefficients/p-values are thresholded (beta_treated > 0.1, Bonferroni-corrected p = 0.001, beta_treated > beta_untreated) to nominate drug-resistance programs such as the TGF-beta-signaling metagene 24 in cisplatin-treated TNBC PDXs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input lacks a treatment/condition contrast (e.g., a single-sample dataset or the PBMC interferon-stimulation cell-annotation workflow) — metagene module scores cannot be regressed on treatment status. Metagenes have not yet been extracted from the GeneVector embedding — this skill assumes GeneEmbedding.get_adata(resolution=40) and get_metagenes have already been run. The question is cell type annotation or batch correction rather than identifying treatment-dependent transcriptional programs — use CellEmbedding phenotype_probability or batch_correct instead.

skills.description: Use when a fitted subgroup tree (e.g. dipm on anorexia with a continuous outcome, or spmtree on GBSG2 with a survival outcome) needs terminal-node plots showing how treatment groups differ within each node.
skills.name: treatment-subgroup-boxplot-visualization
skills.search_text: treatment-subgroup-boxplot-visualization Use when a fitted subgroup tree (e.g. dipm on anorexia with a continuous outcome, or spmtree on GBSG2 with a survival outcome) needs terminal-node plots showing how treatment groups differ within each node. The goal is fitting or pruning a subgroup tree rather than visualizing an already-fitted one — use the dipm(), spmtree(), or pmprune() functions instead. The tree is not a partykit-compatible object, since node_dipm is designed as a panel function for partykit's plot method. The outcome is neither continuous nor survival, as node_dipm handles only boxplots for continuous outcomes and survival plots for survival outcomes. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Visualizes stratified treatment-effect subgroups from fitted DIPM/spmtree trees by attaching the dipm package's node_dipm panel function to partykit's plot method, rendering per-node treatment-group boxplots (continuous outcomes) or survival curves (survival outcomes). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac041
skills.summary: Visualizes stratified treatment-effect subgroups from fitted DIPM/spmtree trees by attaching the dipm package's node_dipm panel function to partykit's plot method, rendering per-node treatment-group boxplots (continuous outcomes) or survival curves (survival outcomes).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is fitting or pruning a subgroup tree rather than visualizing an already-fitted one — use the dipm(), spmtree(), or pmprune() functions instead. The tree is not a partykit-compatible object, since node_dipm is designed as a panel function for partykit's plot method. The outcome is neither continuous nor survival, as node_dipm handles only boxplots for continuous outcomes and survival plots for survival outcomes.

skills.description: Use when two single-cell datasets each have pseudotime trajectories with multiple branches (trajectory trees) and a global node-to-node correspondence between the trees is needed, e.g. comparing differentiation dynamics across species or conditions.
skills.name: tree-alignment-dynamic-programming
skills.search_text: tree-alignment-dynamic-programming Use when two single-cell datasets each have pseudotime trajectories with multiple branches (trajectory trees) and a global node-to-node correspondence between the trees is needed, e.g. comparing differentiation dynamics across species or conditions. The trajectories are single linear lineages and only a pairwise path comparison is needed — DTW-based alignment (tl.dtw) suffices and is simpler. The inferred structures are complex graphs such as cycles or disconnected graphs — CAPITAL in its present form can deal only with trajectory trees. The two datasets have very different global topological structure — alignment accuracy degraded in the authors' benchmarking test. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 A dynamic-programming tree-alignment method (related to tree edit distance) used by CAPITAL to compute an optimal alignment between two branched pseudotime trajectory trees from different but related scRNA-seq datasets, avoiding manual selection of linear paths. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-33681-3
skills.summary: A dynamic-programming tree-alignment method (related to tree edit distance) used by CAPITAL to compute an optimal alignment between two branched pseudotime trajectory trees from different but related scRNA-seq datasets, avoiding manual selection of linear paths.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trajectories are single linear lineages and only a pairwise path comparison is needed — DTW-based alignment (tl.dtw) suffices and is simpler. The inferred structures are complex graphs such as cycles or disconnected graphs — CAPITAL in its present form can deal only with trajectory trees. The two datasets have very different global topological structure — alignment accuracy degraded in the authors' benchmarking test.

skills.description: Use when you need to rank features from two alternative feature representations (e.g. CKG cell matrices and gene expression matrices) with tree-based models and quantify overlap between their top-ranked features.
skills.name: tree-based-feature-importance-ranking
skills.search_text: tree-based-feature-importance-ranking Use when you need to rank features from two alternative feature representations (e.g. CKG cell matrices and gene expression matrices) with tree-based models and quantify overlap between their top-ranked features. When the goal is classification accuracy itself rather than interpretability of top features — the article's classification module already provides four classification methods for that purpose When features are not comparable via gene annotations (e.g. k-mer groups cannot be resolved to genes through the CKG look-up table), since the shared-gene overlap step depends on that mapping When you only have raw reads and no gene expression matrix — the overlap analysis requires both feature representations http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Rank feature importance with scikit-learn tree ensembles (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting) applied to both CKG (compressed k-mer group) cell matrices and gene expression matrices, then compare top-ranked features by intersecting their gene annotations. Used to show that reference-free CKG features capture biologically meaningful signals comparable to gene expression features. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102855
skills.summary: Rank feature importance with scikit-learn tree ensembles (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting) applied to both CKG (compressed k-mer group) cell matrices and gene expression matrices, then compare top-ranked features by intersecting their gene annotations. Used to show that reference-free CKG features capture biologically meaningful signals comparable to gene expression features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is classification accuracy itself rather than interpretability of top features — the article's classification module already provides four classification methods for that purpose When features are not comparable via gene annotations (e.g. k-mer groups cannot be resolved to genes through the CKG look-up table), since the shared-gene overlap step depends on that mapping When you only have raw reads and no gene expression matrix — the overlap analysis requires both feature representations

skills.description: Use when multiple annotated, aligned datasets (e.g. simulated batches or PBMC-FACS) are combined with scHPL and you need to quantify how batch presentation order or missing populations affect the learned tree, or to compare linear SVM vs one-class SVM node classifiers.
skills.name: tree-stability-assessment-across-batch-orders
skills.search_text: tree-stability-assessment-across-batch-orders Use when multiple annotated, aligned datasets (e.g. simulated batches or PBMC-FACS) are combined with scHPL and you need to quantify how batch presentation order or missing populations affect the learned tree, or to compare linear SVM vs one-class SVM node classifiers. Datasets have not been aligned/integrated first — scHPL is not a batch correction tool, so population matching across unaligned batches is out of scope The goal is annotating a new unlabeled dataset with an already-trained tree (use scHPL predict) rather than assessing tree construction stability Only a single annotated dataset with a fixed known hierarchy is available and no cross-batch progressive learning is involved — there is no batch-order variation to assess http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assess the stability and correctness of hierarchical classification trees learned by scHPL by running progressive learning over multiple batch orders and folds, then comparing each learned tree against the expected reference hierarchy — including stress tests where a cell population (e.g. 'Group5') is withheld from a training batch. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23196-8
skills.summary: Assess the stability and correctness of hierarchical classification trees learned by scHPL by running progressive learning over multiple batch orders and folds, then comparing each learned tree against the expected reference hierarchy — including stress tests where a cell population (e.g. 'Group5') is withheld from a training batch.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets have not been aligned/integrated first — scHPL is not a batch correction tool, so population matching across unaligned batches is out of scope The goal is annotating a new unlabeled dataset with an already-trained tree (use scHPL predict) rather than assessing tree construction stability Only a single annotated dataset with a fixed known hierarchy is available and no cross-batch progressive learning is involved — there is no batch-order variation to assess

skills.description: Use when comparing trajectory inference methods for tree-shaped (linear, bifurcation, multifurcation) single-cell topologies on a common benchmark set, requiring standardized scoring with dynverse metrics and topology-stratified statistical testing.
skills.name: tree-topology-comparison-across-methods
skills.search_text: tree-topology-comparison-across-methods Use when comparing trajectory inference methods for tree-shaped (linear, bifurcation, multifurcation) single-cell topologies on a common benchmark set, requiring standardized scoring with dynverse metrics and topology-stratified statistical testing. The trajectories of interest are disconnected or contain cycles — Totem cannot generate disconnected trajectories or trajectories that have cycles, so tree-only benchmarking methods are the wrong scope Trajectories have multiple roots (converging topologies) — dynplot will not generate the correct pseudotime for multi-root trajectories, corrupting the comparison The embedding is a high-dimensional PCA (e.g. 30 principal components) — k-medoids may perform poorly, so Totem-based benchmark results would be confounded by the embedding choice http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks multiple tree-shaped trajectory inference methods (Totem, dynverse Slingshot, TinGa) on the same standardized single-cell datasets, scoring each against gold standards with the four dynverse metrics and comparing methods statistically by topology type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad515
skills.summary: Benchmarks multiple tree-shaped trajectory inference methods (Totem, dynverse Slingshot, TinGa) on the same standardized single-cell datasets, scoring each against gold standards with the four dynverse metrics and comparing methods statistically by topology type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trajectories of interest are disconnected or contain cycles — Totem cannot generate disconnected trajectories or trajectories that have cycles, so tree-only benchmarking methods are the wrong scope Trajectories have multiple roots (converging topologies) — dynplot will not generate the correct pseudotime for multi-root trajectories, corrupting the comparison The embedding is a high-dimensional PCA (e.g. 30 principal components) — k-medoids may perform poorly, so Totem-based benchmark results would be confounded by the embedding choice

skills.description: Use when you have a set of clusterings from Totem's CLARA k-medoids step, each converted to an MST via Slingshot, and need per-cell connectivity values to rank clusterings or identify trajectory leaves and branch points.
skills.name: tree-topology-vertex-degree-analysis
skills.search_text: tree-topology-vertex-degree-analysis Use when you have a set of clusterings from Totem's CLARA k-medoids step, each converted to an MST via Slingshot, and need per-cell connectivity values to rank clusterings or identify trajectory leaves and branch points. The data or goal involves trajectories with cycles or disconnected trajectory components — Totem cannot generate disconnected trajectories or trajectories that have cycles The goal is correct pseudotime for multi-root (converging) trajectories — dynplot will not generate the correct pseudotime for multi-root trajectories and a manual work-around is required You only have a single clustering and need trajectory construction, not connectivity estimation across multiple clusterings http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Quantifies cell connectivity from a set of Minimum Spanning Trees (MSTs), one per clustering, as implemented in the Totem R package: per-vertex connectivity is derived from inverse edge weights and vertex degrees, scaled per graph to a maximum of 1, and averaged over all L' clusterings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad515
skills.summary: Quantifies cell connectivity from a set of Minimum Spanning Trees (MSTs), one per clustering, as implemented in the Totem R package: per-vertex connectivity is derived from inverse edge weights and vertex degrees, scaled per graph to a maximum of 1, and averaged over all L' clusterings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data or goal involves trajectories with cycles or disconnected trajectory components — Totem cannot generate disconnected trajectories or trajectories that have cycles The goal is correct pseudotime for multi-root (converging) trajectories — dynplot will not generate the correct pseudotime for multi-root trajectories and a manual work-around is required You only have a single clustering and need trajectory construction, not connectivity estimation across multiple clusterings

skills.description: Use when the input is a continuous gene expression or synthetic numeric matrix and the goal is to detect trend-preserving biclusters whose rows maintain relative order of values across a subset of columns.
skills.name: trend-preserving-bicluster-discovery
skills.search_text: trend-preserving-bicluster-discovery Use when the input is a continuous gene expression or synthetic numeric matrix and the goal is to detect trend-preserving biclusters whose rows maintain relative order of values across a subset of columns. When the target biclusters are narrow — the article reports BicSPAM outperformed UniBic specifically on narrow biclusters When a constant-value (not trend/order-preserving) biclustering criterion is required — UniBic is designed for trend-preserving patterns When the identification of general (non-trend-preserving) biclusters is required — the paper notes this remains a challenging unsolved problem http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Discovery of trend-preserving (order-preserving) biclusters in noisy gene expression matrices by applying the longest common subsequence (LCS) framework to pairs of rows of an index matrix derived from the input data, as implemented in UniBic and its parallel R port runibic. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep23466
skills.summary: Discovery of trend-preserving (order-preserving) biclusters in noisy gene expression matrices by applying the longest common subsequence (LCS) framework to pairs of rows of an index matrix derived from the input data, as implemented in UniBic and its parallel R port runibic.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the target biclusters are narrow — the article reports BicSPAM outperformed UniBic specifically on narrow biclusters When a constant-value (not trend/order-preserving) biclustering criterion is required — UniBic is designed for trend-preserving patterns When the identification of general (non-trend-preserving) biclusters is required — the paper notes this remains a challenging unsolved problem

skills.description: Use when a gene-by-cell expression matrix with pre-defined cell-group labels (e.g., cortical subclasses from Yao 2021 cortex_data) must be reduced to robust per-group expression values before ligand/target abundance or communication-strength scoring.
skills.name: trimean-ensemble-expression-aggregation
skills.search_text: trimean-ensemble-expression-aggregation Use when a gene-by-cell expression matrix with pre-defined cell-group labels (e.g., cortical subclasses from Yao 2021 cortex_data) must be reduced to robust per-group expression values before ligand/target abundance or communication-strength scoring. The analysis targets spatial proximity or physical-contact signaling rather than neurotransmitter-based neural communication; CellChat/CellPhoneDB-style paracrine workflows without functional gene grouping will dramatically underestimate small-molecule neurotransmitter ligand abundance Protein or metabolite abundance data are available and preferred, since transcriptomics-based ligand/target estimates may be inconsistent with protein or metabolite levels Input is a bulk expression matrix without cell-group labels, since trimean aggregation requires per-cell-group quartiles http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Collapse a gene-by-cell normalized scRNA-seq matrix into robust per-gene, per-cell-group ensemble averages using Tukey's trimean, (Q1 + 2*median + Q3)/4, after filtering genes expressed in fewer than 25% of cells. This aggregated expression feeds NeuronChat's ligand/target abundance (AND/OR logic) and communication-strength computations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36800-w
skills.summary: Collapse a gene-by-cell normalized scRNA-seq matrix into robust per-gene, per-cell-group ensemble averages using Tukey's trimean, (Q1 + 2*median + Q3)/4, after filtering genes expressed in fewer than 25% of cells. This aggregated expression feeds NeuronChat's ligand/target abundance (AND/OR logic) and communication-strength computations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets spatial proximity or physical-contact signaling rather than neurotransmitter-based neural communication; CellChat/CellPhoneDB-style paracrine workflows without functional gene grouping will dramatically underestimate small-molecule neurotransmitter ligand abundance Protein or metabolite abundance data are available and preferred, since transcriptomics-based ligand/target estimates may be inconsistent with protein or metabolite levels Input is a bulk expression matrix without cell-group labels, since trimean aggregation requires per-cell-group quartiles

skills.description: Use when per-cell gene body coverage profiles (e.g. .geneBodyCoverage outputs from geneBodyCoverage.pl) are available and cells must be classified into typical vs skewed groups with a robust, trimming-based clustering.
skills.name: trimmed-clustering-of-coverage-profiles
skills.search_text: trimmed-clustering-of-coverage-profiles Use when per-cell gene body coverage profiles (e.g. .geneBodyCoverage outputs from geneBodyCoverage.pl) are available and cells must be classified into typical vs skewed groups with a robust, trimming-based clustering. Per-cell gene body coverage has not yet been computed (coverage.r / .geneBodyCoverage outputs are missing); run 0_split10XbyBarcode.sh and 1_geneBodyCoverage.sh first The goal is to pre-filter unwanted cells before coverage computation rather than classify cells after coverage — use the SkewC batch command 3_filter.sh instead The BAM files are already split per cell and downstream analysis only needs the coverage plots, not typical/skewed classification http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 SkewC's tclust-based trim clustering partitions single cells into typical and skewed groups based on their gene body coverage profiles, using a user-specified trimming level (alpha) to robustly down-weight outlier cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.102038

skills.when_to_use_negative: Per-cell gene body coverage has not yet been computed (coverage.r / .geneBodyCoverage outputs are missing); run 0_split10XbyBarcode.sh and 1_geneBodyCoverage.sh first The goal is to pre-filter unwanted cells before coverage computation rather than classify cells after coverage — use the SkewC batch command 3_filter.sh instead The BAM files are already split per cell and downstream analysis only needs the coverage plots, not typical/skewed classification

skills.description: Use when converting 41-bp RNA sequence segments (e.g., m5C candidate sites from A. thaliana or M. musculus) into PseEIIP numerical features for machine learning input.
skills.name: trinucleotide-electron-ion-pseudopotential-encoding
skills.search_text: trinucleotide-electron-ion-pseudopotential-encoding Use when converting 41-bp RNA sequence segments (e.g., m5C candidate sites from A. thaliana or M. musculus) into PseEIIP numerical features for machine learning input. Input sequences are not RNA/DNA sequence segments (e.g., a numeric feature table is already provided — no re-encoding is needed) The target task requires species-agnostic cross-species m5C prediction; the article notes it could be difficult to develop a general model for cross-species prediction and species-specific models are necessary Computes PseEIIP (electron-ion interaction pseudo potentials of trinucleotide) features for RNA sequence segments, as one of the four encoding schemes (PSP, k-mer k=1–3, PCPseDNC, PseEIIP) fused into the Staem5 m5C-site prediction input matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2021.10.012
skills.summary: Computes PseEIIP (electron-ion interaction pseudo potentials of trinucleotide) features for RNA sequence segments, as one of the four encoding schemes (PSP, k-mer k=1–3, PCPseDNC, PseEIIP) fused into the Staem5 m5C-site prediction input matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences are not RNA/DNA sequence segments (e.g., a numeric feature table is already provided — no re-encoding is needed) The target task requires species-agnostic cross-species m5C prediction; the article notes it could be difficult to develop a general model for cross-species prediction and species-specific models are necessary

skills.description: Use when implementing or reproducing ivis-style triplet-loss dimensionality reduction: a siamese network must be built, triplets must be sampled from KNN structure (positives from the KNN vector, negatives from outside it), and pn-loss must be minimised.
skills.name: triplet-loss-implementation
skills.search_text: triplet-loss-implementation Use when implementing or reproducing ivis-style triplet-loss dimensionality reduction: a siamese network must be built, triplets must be sampled from KNN structure (positives from the KNN vector, negatives from outside it), and pn-loss must be minimised. Data has not been scaled to the [0, 1] range and no MinMaxScaler step is planned — ivis expects preprocessed values in [0, 1] The goal is only to compare off-the-shelf dimensionality-reduction methods (t-SNE, LargeVis, SIMLR, scvis) rather than implement ivis's architecture and loss Supervised label information is the primary signal and a purely supervised model is desired — although ivis supports supervised mode, this skill targets the unsupervised triplet-based setup http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Implements ivis's siamese neural network trained with a triplet loss, where approximate nearest-neighbour identification (Annoy random projection trees) supplies the KNN vectors used to sample positive and negative triplets. This is the core training mechanism behind ivis's structure-preserving dimensionality reduction of high-dimensional single-cell datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-45301-0
skills.summary: Implements ivis's siamese neural network trained with a triplet loss, where approximate nearest-neighbour identification (Annoy random projection trees) supplies the KNN vectors used to sample positive and negative triplets. This is the core training mechanism behind ivis's structure-preserving dimensionality reduction of high-dimensional single-cell datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data has not been scaled to the [0, 1] range and no MinMaxScaler step is planned — ivis expects preprocessed values in [0, 1] The goal is only to compare off-the-shelf dimensionality-reduction methods (t-SNE, LargeVis, SIMLR, scvis) rather than implement ivis's architecture and loss Supervised label information is the primary signal and a purely supervised model is desired — although ivis supports supervised mode, this skill targets the unsupervised triplet-based setup

skills.description: Use when you need to embed high-dimensional single-cell expression data (e.g. CyTOF BMMC marker panels or scRNA-seq) into 2D while preserving local and global structure, and when new cells must be added to an existing embedding without rerunning the algorithm.
skills.name: triplet-loss-siamese-network-training
skills.search_text: triplet-loss-siamese-network-training Use when you need to embed high-dimensional single-cell expression data (e.g. CyTOF BMMC marker panels or scRNA-seq) into 2D while preserving local and global structure, and when new cells must be added to an existing embedding without rerunning the algorithm. When only local cluster separation matters and a well-established t-SNE workflow is already validated — though note t-SNE yields spurious clusters under uniform random noise When the input is a small low-dimensional dataset where simpler embeddings suffice (ivis still performs well on toy data like iris, but adds deep-learning overhead) When no feature matrix is available (e.g. raw FCS files must first be converted/transformed, e.g. arcsinh-transformed, before ivis can be applied) http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3306 Train a siamese neural network with a triplet loss function to reduce dimensionality of high-dimensional single-cell datasets, using ivis's novel triplet loss that samples positives from the KNN vector and negatives from outside it. This is the core mechanism by which ivis captures both local and global structure while learning a parametric mapping for out-of-sample embedding. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-45301-0
skills.summary: Train a siamese neural network with a triplet loss function to reduce dimensionality of high-dimensional single-cell datasets, using ivis's novel triplet loss that samples positives from the KNN vector and negatives from outside it. This is the core mechanism by which ivis captures both local and global structure while learning a parametric mapping for out-of-sample embedding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only local cluster separation matters and a well-established t-SNE workflow is already validated — though note t-SNE yields spurious clusters under uniform random noise When the input is a small low-dimensional dataset where simpler embeddings suffice (ivis still performs well on toy data like iris, but adds deep-learning overhead) When no feature matrix is available (e.g. raw FCS files must first be converted/transformed, e.g. arcsinh-transformed, before ivis can be applied)
