skills.description: Use when single-end sRNA-seq FASTQ reads must be assigned to tRF-5/tRF-3/tRF-1/tRNA-half classes against progenitor mature tRNA loci, or when testing whether tRNA cleavage is non-random and codon/anticodon-dependent.
skills.name: trna-fragment-classification-interpretation
skills.search_text: trna-fragment-classification-interpretation Use when single-end sRNA-seq FASTQ reads must be assigned to tRF-5/tRF-3/tRF-1/tRNA-half classes against progenitor mature tRNA loci, or when testing whether tRNA cleavage is non-random and codon/anticodon-dependent. The reads are not small RNA-seq (14-50 nt) or derive from organisms lacking curated tRNA predictions — the pipeline and its human-trained alternatives (tDRmapper, MINTmap, tRF2Cancer) do not generalize. The goal is general small-RNA annotation (miRNA, piRNA, rRNA) rather than tRNA-derived fragments; a pipeline like SPORTS1.0 is better suited. Input is already a classified tncRNA count matrix and the task is downstream expression or pathway analysis, not cleavage-position classification. http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Classifies small RNA-seq reads into tRNA-derived non-coding RNA (tncRNA) subtypes (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, 5'tRH, 3'tRH) and interprets their generation as codon-dependent, precise endoribonucleolytic cleavage rather than random tRNA degradation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Classifies small RNA-seq reads into tRNA-derived non-coding RNA (tncRNA) subtypes (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, 5'tRH, 3'tRH) and interprets their generation as codon-dependent, precise endoribonucleolytic cleavage rather than random tRNA degradation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reads are not small RNA-seq (14-50 nt) or derive from organisms lacking curated tRNA predictions — the pipeline and its human-trained alternatives (tDRmapper, MINTmap, tRF2Cancer) do not generalize. The goal is general small-RNA annotation (miRNA, piRNA, rRNA) rather than tRNA-derived fragments; a pipeline like SPORTS1.0 is better suited. Input is already a classified tncRNA count matrix and the task is downstream expression or pathway analysis, not cleavage-position classification.

skills.description: Use when sorted BAM alignments of tncRNA-derived small RNA reads to an artificial tRNA-plus-flank genome are available and per-tncRNA nucleoside modification calls and modification types are needed.
skills.name: trna-modification-signature-annotation
skills.search_text: trna-modification-signature-annotation Use when sorted BAM alignments of tncRNA-derived small RNA reads to an artificial tRNA-plus-flank genome are available and per-tncRNA nucleoside modification calls and modification types are needed. Input reads have not been quality-filtered and adapter-trimmed and aligned to the artificial tRNA genome — HAMR needs mismatch-aware alignments of tncRNA reads, not raw FASTQ The goal is de novo tncRNA discovery or subtype classification (tRF-5s, tRF-3s, tRF-1, tRNA halves) rather than modification site annotation Sequencing depth at candidate sites is below the HAMR minimum read depth of 30, since modification calls will not be reliable http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Annotates modified nucleoside sites (e.g., m3C, pseudouridine, dihydrouridine, m2G) on tRNA-derived non-coding RNAs using HAMR (v1.2) with a eukaryotic tRNA modification model, as done in the tncRNA Toolkit pipeline for six angiosperms. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Annotates modified nucleoside sites (e.g., m3C, pseudouridine, dihydrouridine, m2G) on tRNA-derived non-coding RNAs using HAMR (v1.2) with a eukaryotic tRNA modification model, as done in the tncRNA Toolkit pipeline for six angiosperms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not been quality-filtered and adapter-trimmed and aligned to the artificial tRNA genome — HAMR needs mismatch-aware alignments of tncRNA reads, not raw FASTQ The goal is de novo tncRNA discovery or subtype classification (tRF-5s, tRF-3s, tRF-1, tRNA halves) rather than modification site annotation Sequencing depth at candidate sites is below the HAMR minimum read depth of 30, since modification calls will not be reliable

skills.description: Use when scPagwas has produced a gPAS/TRS per cell from GWAS summary statistics plus scRNA-seq data and you need per-cell p-values corrected against a background of control TRSs to call trait-relevant individual cells.
skills.name: trs-background-correction-pvalue-computation
skills.search_text: trs-background-correction-pvalue-computation Use when scPagwas has produced a gPAS/TRS per cell from GWAS summary statistics plus scRNA-seq data and you need per-cell p-values corrected against a background of control TRSs to call trait-relevant individual cells. When the goal is cell-type-level (not single-cell-level) association — use the block bootstrap cell-type inference (Boot_evaluate, 200 iterations) instead of per-cell p-values When no GWAS summary statistics are available to derive the trait-relevant gene set, since control TRSs and background correction require a genetically informed TRS When the scRNA-seq object is raw counts without normalization/VST pathway activation transformation, as AddModuleScore-based TRS computation requires normalized data http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes per-cell significance of trait-relevant scores (TRS) in scPagwas by Monte Carlo comparison of each cell's Seurat AddModuleScore-based TRS against control TRSs matched by expression bins, then background-corrects the p-values (Get_CorrectBg_p with iters_singlecell = 100, n_topgenes = 1000) to identify individual trait-associated cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100383
skills.summary: Computes per-cell significance of trait-relevant scores (TRS) in scPagwas by Monte Carlo comparison of each cell's Seurat AddModuleScore-based TRS against control TRSs matched by expression bins, then background-corrects the p-values (Get_CorrectBg_p with iters_singlecell = 100, n_topgenes = 1000) to identify individual trait-associated cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is cell-type-level (not single-cell-level) association — use the block bootstrap cell-type inference (Boot_evaluate, 200 iterations) instead of per-cell p-values When no GWAS summary statistics are available to derive the trait-relevant gene set, since control TRSs and background correction require a genetically informed TRS When the scRNA-seq object is raw counts without normalization/VST pathway activation transformation, as AddModuleScore-based TRS computation requires normalized data

skills.description: Use when you have simulated or spike-in single-cell count data with a known ground-truth differentially expressed gene set, and need to compare TDR of competing DE methods across a threshold grid.
skills.name: true-discovery-rate-curve-evaluation
skills.search_text: true-discovery-rate-curve-evaluation Use when you have simulated or spike-in single-cell count data with a known ground-truth differentially expressed gene set, and need to compare TDR of competing DE methods across a threshold grid. No ground-truth tDEG set exists (e.g., real single-timepoint data with unknown true DE status) — true and false discovery counts cannot be computed The data are cross-sectional with no temporal dimension — CASi's FindTemporalDEGs and its GLM-based time-effect test do not apply The expected time effect is nonlinear — CASi's GLM framework only detects linear change of gene expression by time or time-by-condition interaction http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark evaluation of temporal differential expression detection by comparing per-method true-discovery and false-discovery counts against a known planted tDEG set, then averaging over repetitions to produce true discovery rate (TDR) curves across p-value thresholds. Used in the CASi paper to show CASi's negative-binomial-GLM FindTemporalDEGs outperforms DESeq2, MAST, and Seurat Wilcoxon under weak, medium, and strong time effects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-58566-x
skills.summary: Benchmark evaluation of temporal differential expression detection by comparing per-method true-discovery and false-discovery counts against a known planted tDEG set, then averaging over repetitions to produce true discovery rate (TDR) curves across p-value thresholds. Used in the CASi paper to show CASi's negative-binomial-GLM FindTemporalDEGs outperforms DESeq2, MAST, and Seurat Wilcoxon under weak, medium, and strong time effects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth tDEG set exists (e.g., real single-timepoint data with unknown true DE status) — true and false discovery counts cannot be computed The data are cross-sectional with no temporal dimension — CASi's FindTemporalDEGs and its GLM-based time-effect test do not apply The expected time effect is nonlinear — CASi's GLM framework only detects linear change of gene expression by time or time-by-condition interaction

skills.name: true-zero-fraction-quantification
skills.search_text: true-zero-fraction-quantification Use when matched bulk and single-cell RNA-seq data are available and you must test whether an imputation method preserves biologically silenced (true-zero) genes while still correcting dropout events. No matched bulk RNA-seq data exist to define which single-cell zeros are biological true zeros versus dropouts The goal is overall expression-recovery or clustering accuracy rather than true-zero preservation behavior of an imputer The single-cell matrix has not been imputed yet (the analysis evaluates zeros in imputed output, not the raw matrix) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantify how an imputation method treats biologically silent true zeros versus dropout zeros by binning genes according to matched bulk RNA-seq expression and computing per-bin zero fractions in the imputed single-cell data. skills.description: Use when a per-cell segment-level smoothed expression matrix (e.g. CNAmtx from SCEVAN's joint segmentation) must be discretized into the five CNV states via an EM-fitted truncated-normal mixture rather than ad hoc thresholding.
skills.name: truncated-normal-mixture-model-fitting
skills.search_text: truncated-normal-mixture-model-fitting Use when a per-cell segment-level smoothed expression matrix (e.g. CNAmtx from SCEVAN's joint segmentation) must be discretized into the five CNV states via an EM-fitted truncated-normal mixture rather than ad hoc thresholding. The tumor has minimal genomic alterations (e.g. leukemia, pediatric cancers, Ependymomas), where the aneuploidy-based mixture assumption does not hold Input is still a raw scRNA-seq count matrix without prior baseline correction and joint segmentation — the mixture must be fit to smoothed segment means, not raw counts Only malignant/non-malignant classification is needed with no segment-level CNV state assignment (run pipelineCNA without SUBCLONES instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fits a mixture of five truncated normal distributions to per-cell segment mean expression profiles and assigns each genomic segment to one of five copy number states (deletion, loss, neutral, gain, amplification), as done inside SCEVAN's CNV-calling workflow, with a final consensus call by majority vote across cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36790-9
skills.summary: Fits a mixture of five truncated normal distributions to per-cell segment mean expression profiles and assigns each genomic segment to one of five copy number states (deletion, loss, neutral, gain, amplification), as done inside SCEVAN's CNV-calling workflow, with a final consensus call by majority vote across cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tumor has minimal genomic alterations (e.g. leukemia, pediatric cancers, Ependymomas), where the aneuploidy-based mixture assumption does not hold Input is still a raw scRNA-seq count matrix without prior baseline correction and joint segmentation — the mixture must be fit to smoothed segment means, not raw counts Only malignant/non-malignant classification is needed with no segment-level CNV state assignment (run pipelineCNA without SUBCLONES instead)

skills.description: Use when you have a strand-split BAM of aligned reads (e.g. from 10x Chromium) and need per-position counts of polyA/soft-clip-driven read endpoints to locate precise UTR termination sites.
skills.name: truncation-point-pileup-aggregation
skills.search_text: truncation-point-pileup-aggregation Use when you have a strand-split BAM of aligned reads (e.g. from 10x Chromium) and need per-position counts of polyA/soft-clip-driven read endpoints to locate precise UTR termination sites. Input reads lack soft-clipped bases or polyA/polyT tails (e.g. fully aligned reads without 3' enrichment) — no truncation points will be detectable BAM files whose signal is not concentrated at UTR distal ends (the method favours 10x Chromium-style runs) You only need broad coverage peaks rather than precise UTR end bases — use MACS peak calling instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstructs the SPAT stage of peaks2utr: detect aligned reads carrying soft-clipped bases and a polyA-tail of a given length, then tally each read's final aligned end base as a 'truncation point' so piled-up co-occurring truncation points can pinpoint the precise 3' UTR end. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad112
skills.summary: Reconstructs the SPAT stage of peaks2utr: detect aligned reads carrying soft-clipped bases and a polyA-tail of a given length, then tally each read's final aligned end base as a 'truncation point' so piled-up co-occurring truncation points can pinpoint the precise 3' UTR end.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads lack soft-clipped bases or polyA/polyT tails (e.g. fully aligned reads without 3' enrichment) — no truncation points will be detectable BAM files whose signal is not concentrated at UTR distal ends (the method favours 10x Chromium-style runs) You only need broad coverage peaks rather than precise UTR end bases — use MACS peak calling instead

skills.description: Use when you have BAMM-SC posterior cluster probabilities per cell and need to quantify and spatially validate clustering uncertainty, e.g. confirming ambiguous cells sit at cluster boundaries on a t-SNE plot.
skills.name: tsne-cluster-boundary-visualization
skills.search_text: tsne-cluster-boundary-visualization Use when you have BAMM-SC posterior cluster probabilities per cell and need to quantify and spatially validate clustering uncertainty, e.g. confirming ambiguous cells sit at cluster boundaries on a t-SNE plot. You need posterior probabilities to represent continuous biological states (e.g. cell cycle or developmental stage) — BAMM-SC assumes each cell belongs to one distinct cluster and the posterior measures only clustering uncertainty. The data come from a single individual with no multi-individual batch heterogeneity, where the posterior-uncertainty workflow of BAMMSC (rather than DIMMSC) is not the intended mode. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Localizes uncertain cell-type assignments by flagging 'vague' cells (maximum BAMM-SC posterior cluster probability <0.95) and overlaying them on a t-SNE projection to verify they fall at cluster boundaries rather than cluster cores, as done in the human PBMC analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-09639-3
skills.summary: Localizes uncertain cell-type assignments by flagging 'vague' cells (maximum BAMM-SC posterior cluster probability <0.95) and overlaying them on a t-SNE projection to verify they fall at cluster boundaries rather than cluster cores, as done in the human PBMC analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need posterior probabilities to represent continuous biological states (e.g. cell cycle or developmental stage) — BAMM-SC assumes each cell belongs to one distinct cluster and the posterior measures only clustering uncertainty. The data come from a single individual with no multi-individual batch heterogeneity, where the posterior-uncertainty workflow of BAMMSC (rather than DIMMSC) is not the intended mode.

skills.summary: Visualize DESC soft-clustering results of single-cell RNA-seq data as t-SNE scatter plots colored by cluster assignment, per-cell maximum cluster probability (max.prob), cell type, and condition, enabling assessment of high-confidence cluster assignments and batch-effect removal.

skills.name: tsne-clustering-visualization-of-recovered-barcodes
skills.search_text: tsne-clustering-visualization-of-recovered-barcodes Use when you have EmptyNN-retained barcodes (e.g., 885 recovered barcodes below a Cell Ranger v.2 cutoff of 200 total counts) and need to visualize and identify their cell-type clusters via t-SNE. The count matrix is already filtered (e.g., Cell Ranger v.3 output) so low-count recovered barcodes are absent — EmptyNN recovery and this downstream visualization require the raw unfiltered matrix Barcodes with total counts <= 10 dominate the matrix, since EmptyNN excludes them from analysis before recovery The goal is ambient RNA correction rather than cell-calling visualization — EmptyNN does not correct gene expression estimates (use SoupX separately) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Seurat-based downstream processing (mitochondrial-fraction filtering, normalization, HVG detection, PCA, clustering at resolution 0.2, t-SNE) of barcodes recovered by EmptyNN below the original Cell Ranger v.2 threshold, used to resolve and annotate cell-type structure among low-total-count barcodes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2021.100311
skills.summary: Seurat-based downstream processing (mitochondrial-fraction filtering, normalization, HVG detection, PCA, clustering at resolution 0.2, t-SNE) of barcodes recovered by EmptyNN below the original Cell Ranger v.2 threshold, used to resolve and annotate cell-type structure among low-total-count barcodes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The count matrix is already filtered (e.g., Cell Ranger v.3 output) so low-count recovered barcodes are absent — EmptyNN recovery and this downstream visualization require the raw unfiltered matrix Barcodes with total counts <= 10 dominate the matrix, since EmptyNN excludes them from analysis before recovery The goal is ambient RNA correction rather than cell-calling visualization — EmptyNN does not correct gene expression estimates (use SoupX separately)

skills.description: Use when a raw (dropout-containing), noisy, or imputed scRNA-Seq matrix needs a 2-D visualization of cell-type clusters, or when computing average silhouette width (ASW) on the t-SNE embedding to compare imputation methods.
skills.name: tsne-dimensionality-reduction
skills.search_text: tsne-dimensionality-reduction Use when a raw (dropout-containing), noisy, or imputed scRNA-Seq matrix needs a 2-D visualization of cell-type clusters, or when computing average silhouette width (ASW) on the t-SNE embedding to compare imputation methods. Data are already an embedded feature representation (e.g. prior PCA-50 coordinates); re-applying the full take_norm -> PCA chain would be redundant The goal is gene-level interpretation or marker discovery rather than 2-D visualization or cluster-structure scoring of cells Cluster metrics are needed on the full-dimensional expression space rather than on a 2-D visualization embedding http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A two-stage embedding routine from the AutoClass paper: normalize the scRNA-Seq count matrix with take_norm, compress to 50 PCA components, then embed with scikit-learn TSNE(n_components=2) to visualize and score cell-type structure on raw, noisy, or imputed data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29576-y
skills.summary: A two-stage embedding routine from the AutoClass paper: normalize the scRNA-Seq count matrix with take_norm, compress to 50 PCA components, then embed with scikit-learn TSNE(n_components=2) to visualize and score cell-type structure on raw, noisy, or imputed data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already an embedded feature representation (e.g. prior PCA-50 coordinates); re-applying the full take_norm -> PCA chain would be redundant The goal is gene-level interpretation or marker discovery rather than 2-D visualization or cluster-structure scoring of cells Cluster metrics are needed on the full-dimensional expression space rather than on a 2-D visualization embedding

skills.description: Use when sample-wise small-RNA profiles (e.g. tncRNA sequence presence per tissue sample) need non-linear 2D embedding to test whether samples cluster by tissue of origin.
skills.name: tsne-dimensionality-reduction
skills.search_text: tsne-dimensionality-reduction Use when sample-wise small-RNA profiles (e.g. tncRNA sequence presence per tissue sample) need non-linear 2D embedding to test whether samples cluster by tissue of origin. Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or a continuous expression matrix where linear methods suffice Tissues have fewer than 10 samples — the paper only utilized tissues with at least 10 samples for t-SNE matrix generation Goal is tncRNA detection or classification rather than sample-level clustering/visualization http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Applies t-SNE non-linear dimensionality reduction to binary presence/absence matrices of unique tncRNA sequences (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, 5'tRH, 3'tRH) per tissue sample, to reveal tissue-specific clustering of plant tncRNAs under normal physiological conditions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Applies t-SNE non-linear dimensionality reduction to binary presence/absence matrices of unique tncRNA sequences (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, 5'tRH, 3'tRH) per tissue sample, to reveal tissue-specific clustering of plant tncRNAs under normal physiological conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or a continuous expression matrix where linear methods suffice Tissues have fewer than 10 samples — the paper only utilized tissues with at least 10 samples for t-SNE matrix generation Goal is tncRNA detection or classification rather than sample-level clustering/visualization

skills.description: Use when you have cells projected onto a small selected marker-gene panel (e.g. scGeneFit's 15 CBMC markers) plus cell type labels, and need a 2-D visualization to check that cell populations remain separated.
skills.name: tsne-dimensionality-reduction
skills.search_text: tsne-dimensionality-reduction Use when you have cells projected onto a small selected marker-gene panel (e.g. scGeneFit's 15 CBMC markers) plus cell type labels, and need a 2-D visualization to check that cell populations remain separated. The task is to select the marker genes themselves rather than visualize an existing panel — use scGeneFit marker selection, not t-SNE plotting. The cells lack cell type labels, so the scatter plot cannot be colored or evaluated for separation of the intended populations. A quantitative clustering or label-recovery metric is required — t-SNE 2-D distances are qualitative and should not be used as the sole accuracy measure. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Visualize single-cell RNA-seq cells in a reduced scGeneFit-selected marker space by running t-SNE on the 15-marker CBMC projection and rendering a scatter plot colored by cell type, to show that 13 cell populations remain distinguishable with few markers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21453-4
skills.summary: Visualize single-cell RNA-seq cells in a reduced scGeneFit-selected marker space by running t-SNE on the 15-marker CBMC projection and rendering a scatter plot colored by cell type, to show that 13 cell populations remain distinguishable with few markers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is to select the marker genes themselves rather than visualize an existing panel — use scGeneFit marker selection, not t-SNE plotting. The cells lack cell type labels, so the scatter plot cannot be colored or evaluated for separation of the intended populations. A quantitative clustering or label-recovery metric is required — t-SNE 2-D distances are qualitative and should not be used as the sole accuracy measure.

skills.description: Use when single-cell shape features are already encoded as autoencoder latent vectors (e.g., MIRIAM pipeline output) and you need a 2D t-SNE embedding to test whether similar geometries cluster and whether marker-positive cells form discrete populations.
skills.name: tsne-dimensionality-reduction-of-cell-shape-latents
skills.search_text: tsne-dimensionality-reduction-of-cell-shape-latents Use when single-cell shape features are already encoded as autoencoder latent vectors (e.g., MIRIAM pipeline output) and you need a 2D t-SNE embedding to test whether similar geometries cluster and whether marker-positive cells form discrete populations. Input is already a per-cell marker intensity table — the article's Figure 3A covers t-SNE on marker intensities directly, which is a distinct analysis from shape-latent t-SNE Shape features have not yet been encoded by the MIRIAM autoencoder (raw cell shape masks/outlines are the wrong input for this skill) The latent vectors being embedded were used to train the autoencoder — the article explicitly excludes autoencoder training cells from this analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Run t-SNE (Rtsne package) on held-out autoencoder-encoded latent vectors for cell shape from the MIRIAM pipeline to produce a 2D embedding in which cells of similar geometry lie near each other; then color by per-cell marker intensities (e.g., p-ERK) to test whether shape alone reveals cellular populations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/cyto.a.24541
skills.summary: Run t-SNE (Rtsne package) on held-out autoencoder-encoded latent vectors for cell shape from the MIRIAM pipeline to produce a 2D embedding in which cells of similar geometry lie near each other; then color by per-cell marker intensities (e.g., p-ERK) to test whether shape alone reveals cellular populations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-cell marker intensity table — the article's Figure 3A covers t-SNE on marker intensities directly, which is a distinct analysis from shape-latent t-SNE Shape features have not yet been encoded by the MIRIAM autoencoder (raw cell shape masks/outlines are the wrong input for this skill) The latent vectors being embedded were used to train the autoencoder — the article explicitly excludes autoencoder training cells from this analysis

skills.description: Use when you have normalized scRNA-seq count data (e.g. 10x Genomics PBMC, 4500 cells, 9 immune cell types) and need a 2D embedding to assess whether imputation or preprocessing improves subpopulation separation.
skills.name: tsne-dimensionality-reduction-of-scrna-seq
skills.search_text: tsne-dimensionality-reduction-of-scrna-seq Use when you have normalized scRNA-seq count data (e.g. 10x Genomics PBMC, 4500 cells, 9 immune cell types) and need a 2D embedding to assess whether imputation or preprocessing improves subpopulation separation. Input is not normalized scRNA-seq count data or lacks cell-type labels needed to color and assess cluster separation The analysis goal is a numeric clustering metric or differential expression testing rather than qualitative 2D visualization of subpopulation separation The dataset requires quantitative, threshold-based validation — this paper reports only qualitative t-SNE agreement with no numeric threshold http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Apply t-SNE dimension reduction to raw and scImpute-imputed scRNA-seq count matrices to visualize separation of immune cell subpopulations, e.g. resolving cytotoxic vs naive cytotoxic and naive vs memory T cells in the 10x Genomics PBMC dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03405-7
skills.summary: Apply t-SNE dimension reduction to raw and scImpute-imputed scRNA-seq count matrices to visualize separation of immune cell subpopulations, e.g. resolving cytotoxic vs naive cytotoxic and naive vs memory T cells in the 10x Genomics PBMC dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not normalized scRNA-seq count data or lacks cell-type labels needed to color and assess cluster separation The analysis goal is a numeric clustering metric or differential expression testing rather than qualitative 2D visualization of subpopulation separation The dataset requires quantitative, threshold-based validation — this paper reports only qualitative t-SNE agreement with no numeric threshold

skills.description: Use when you need to visually compare separability of predicted cancer/non-cancer driver gene classes across alternative graph-network embedding representations, especially for genes ranked by neighborhood discrete entropy.
skills.name: tsne-dimensionality-reduction-visualization
skills.search_text: tsne-dimensionality-reduction-visualization Use when you need to visually compare separability of predicted cancer/non-cancer driver gene classes across alternative graph-network embedding representations, especially for genes ranked by neighborhood discrete entropy. The goal is a quantitative performance metric (e.g., accuracy/AUC) rather than a qualitative visual class-separation check — use 5-fold cross-validation instead. Genes of interest have low neighborhood discrete entropy (neighbors similar to the gene), since DGCN alone already separates them well and the MLP-offset effect will not be visible. The trained model outputs in './code/result/' are unavailable — t-SNE requires the stored embedding vectors ZF, Zin, Zout, ZMLP, which cannot be reconstructed from 'logits' alone. http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies t-SNE to project high-dimensional gene embeddings (DGCN-only ZF/Zin/Zout vs concatenated DGCN+MLP ZMLP) into 2D scatter panels to visually assess whether MLP concatenation improves class separation of predicted cancer vs non-cancer driver genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.11.004
skills.summary: Applies t-SNE to project high-dimensional gene embeddings (DGCN-only ZF/Zin/Zout vs concatenated DGCN+MLP ZMLP) into 2D scatter panels to visually assess whether MLP concatenation improves class separation of predicted cancer vs non-cancer driver genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a quantitative performance metric (e.g., accuracy/AUC) rather than a qualitative visual class-separation check — use 5-fold cross-validation instead. Genes of interest have low neighborhood discrete entropy (neighbors similar to the gene), since DGCN alone already separates them well and the MLP-offset effect will not be visible. The trained model outputs in './code/result/' are unavailable — t-SNE requires the stored embedding vectors ZF, Zin, Zout, ZMLP, which cannot be reconstructed from 'logits' alone.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking dimensionality-reduction scalability on a large scRNA-seq or CyTOF matrix (e.g. the 1.3M-cell 10X Genomics mouse brain dataset), or when a t-SNE baseline embedding is required for comparison against ivis.
skills.name: tsne-embedding-computation
skills.search_text: tsne-embedding-computation Use when benchmarking dimensionality-reduction scalability on a large scRNA-seq or CyTOF matrix (e.g. the 1.3M-cell 10X Genomics mouse brain dataset), or when a t-SNE baseline embedding is required for comparison against ivis. When the goal is to embed millions of observations within practical time — the paper shows Barnes-Hut t-SNE did not finish within 24 hours on 1.3M cells; use ivis instead When embedding quality under random noise matters — t-SNE was shown to yield spurious clusters with clean boundaries in the presence of random noise When the downstream task requires adding new data points to an existing embedding — t-SNE lacks a transform method, unlike ivis's parametric mapping http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compute a Barnes-Hut t-SNE embedding of a high-dimensional single-cell (or general) matrix with scikit-learn, primarily as the runtime/scale baseline against which the ivis algorithm's scalability is measured. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-45301-0
skills.summary: Compute a Barnes-Hut t-SNE embedding of a high-dimensional single-cell (or general) matrix with scikit-learn, primarily as the runtime/scale baseline against which the ivis algorithm's scalability is measured.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to embed millions of observations within practical time — the paper shows Barnes-Hut t-SNE did not finish within 24 hours on 1.3M cells; use ivis instead When embedding quality under random noise matters — t-SNE was shown to yield spurious clusters with clean boundaries in the presence of random noise When the downstream task requires adding new data points to an existing embedding — t-SNE lacks a transform method, unlike ivis's parametric mapping

skills.description: Use when you have cell-to-cell similarity matrices from scRNA-seq methods (e.g. SSRE vs Corr, SIMLR, MPSSC, SSR, native t-SNE) and need 2D embeddings to visually compare how well each separates known cell types/stages.
skills.name: tsne-embedding-of-cell-similarity-matrices
skills.search_text: tsne-embedding-of-cell-similarity-matrices Use when you have cell-to-cell similarity matrices from scRNA-seq methods (e.g. SSRE vs Corr, SIMLR, MPSSC, SSR, native t-SNE) and need 2D embeddings to visually compare how well each separates known cell types/stages. The goal is clustering accuracy metrics (NMI, Purity, ARI) rather than visual comparison of similarity structure — use spectral clustering on the learned similarities instead The dataset is large-scale, where SSRE similarity learning is relatively time-consuming and parallel computing would be needed Input is raw gene expression without first computing a cell-to-cell similarity matrix via one of the six methods http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Embeds cell-to-cell similarity matrices learned by competing scRNA-seq methods (native t-SNE, Corr, SIMLR, MPSSC, SSR, SSRE) into 2D via a modified t-SNE, so that cell-type/stage separation on the Goolam and Yan datasets can be compared visually. This demonstrates SSRE's extension from clustering to visualization of single-cell data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.09.004
skills.summary: Embeds cell-to-cell similarity matrices learned by competing scRNA-seq methods (native t-SNE, Corr, SIMLR, MPSSC, SSR, SSRE) into 2D via a modified t-SNE, so that cell-type/stage separation on the Goolam and Yan datasets can be compared visually. This demonstrates SSRE's extension from clustering to visualization of single-cell data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is clustering accuracy metrics (NMI, Purity, ARI) rather than visual comparison of similarity structure — use spectral clustering on the learned similarities instead The dataset is large-scale, where SSRE similarity learning is relatively time-consuming and parallel computing would be needed Input is raw gene expression without first computing a cell-to-cell similarity matrix via one of the six methods

skills.description: Use when validating scGAN or cscGAN generated single-cell RNA-seq data: embeddings must show generated cells overlapping real validation clusters and recapitulating cluster/marker-gene structure.
skills.name: tsne-embedding-of-real-and-generated-cells
skills.search_text: tsne-embedding-of-real-and-generated-cells Use when validating scGAN or cscGAN generated single-cell RNA-seq data: embeddings must show generated cells overlapping real validation clusters and recapitulating cluster/marker-gene structure. No held-out validation set exists because the test set size was set to 0 and no validation split was retained — there are no real cells to co-embed The goal is quantitative realism assessment (e.g. Random Forest AUC 0.62/0.55 or MMD 0.286/0.238 for PBMC clusters 2 and 6) rather than visual cluster/marker-gene validation The input is a dataset format not yet converted to .h5/.h5ad (e.g. raw mtx/tsv), which must first be converted with the provided Jupyter notebook Produces t-SNE validation plots in the scGAN/cscGAN pipeline by jointly embedding the whole validation set together with an equal number of GAN-generated scRNA-seq cells, to visually confirm that generated cells overlap real clusters and reproduce marker-gene structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-14018-z
skills.summary: Produces t-SNE validation plots in the scGAN/cscGAN pipeline by jointly embedding the whole validation set together with an equal number of GAN-generated scRNA-seq cells, to visually confirm that generated cells overlap real clusters and reproduce marker-gene structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No held-out validation set exists because the test set size was set to 0 and no validation split was retained — there are no real cells to co-embed The goal is quantitative realism assessment (e.g. Random Forest AUC 0.62/0.55 or MMD 0.286/0.238 for PBMC clusters 2 and 6) rather than visual cluster/marker-gene validation The input is a dataset format not yet converted to .h5/.h5ad (e.g. raw mtx/tsv), which must first be converted with the provided Jupyter notebook

skills.description: Use when you have a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., Tabula Muris FACS counts CSV) and need a 2D t-SNE embedding whose per-cell quality can be statistically assessed against a signal-less null.
skills.name: tsne-embedding-of-scrna-seq-counts
skills.search_text: tsne-embedding-of-scrna-seq-counts Use when you have a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., Tabula Muris FACS counts CSV) and need a 2D t-SNE embedding whose per-cell quality can be statistically assessed against a signal-less null. You only need a static t-SNE visualization without per-sample statistical quality assessment — a plain openTSNE/FIt-SNE run without null embeddings suffices and is far cheaper. Your dataset is not normalized counts (e.g., raw non-normalized pipelines): the article notes EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets. You require p values with resolution finer than what the number of null embeddings supports, since empirical null distributions bound the lower limit of attainable p values. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Embed scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., ~4,800 FACS-sorted Tabula Muris bone marrow cells, GEO GSE109774) into 2D using an openTSNE-backed t-SNE implementation, as packaged in the EMBEDR Python library, so that per-sample embedding quality can be visualized by coloring cells with EMBEDR p values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100443
skills.summary: Embed scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., ~4,800 FACS-sorted Tabula Muris bone marrow cells, GEO GSE109774) into 2D using an openTSNE-backed t-SNE implementation, as packaged in the EMBEDR Python library, so that per-sample embedding quality can be visualized by coloring cells with EMBEDR p values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a static t-SNE visualization without per-sample statistical quality assessment — a plain openTSNE/FIt-SNE run without null embeddings suffices and is far cheaper. Your dataset is not normalized counts (e.g., raw non-normalized pipelines): the article notes EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets. You require p values with resolution finer than what the number of null embeddings supports, since empirical null distributions bound the lower limit of attainable p values.

skills.description: Use when a high-dimensional single-cell feature matrix (e.g., latent representations from Miscell, Seurat, Scanpy, or scVI) needs a fast 2D embedding for visualization and downstream clustering on datasets up to ~55,656 cells.
skills.name: tsne-embedding-of-single-cell-data
skills.search_text: tsne-embedding-of-single-cell-data Use when a high-dimensional single-cell feature matrix (e.g., latent representations from Miscell, Seurat, Scanpy, or scVI) needs a fast 2D embedding for visualization and downstream clustering on datasets up to ~55,656 cells. The input is already a 2D embedding or cluster labels are already available — embedding again adds no information. Subtle small-cluster detail is required and the multi-scale Annoy-based near-neighbor approximation is insufficient; the FIt-SNE README notes vantage-point trees should be used when 'subtle detail is required (e.g. in identifying small clusters)'. Batch effects are present and uncorrected — Miscell leaves batch correction as a preprocessing step, so embedding uncorrected features can confound clusters. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Compute 2D t-SNE embeddings of single-cell latent feature matrices using FIt-SNE (FFT-accelerated, interpolation-based t-SNE) with multi-scale perplexities, then cluster and visualize the embedding for benchmarking single-cell clustering methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103200
skills.summary: Compute 2D t-SNE embeddings of single-cell latent feature matrices using FIt-SNE (FFT-accelerated, interpolation-based t-SNE) with multi-scale perplexities, then cluster and visualize the embedding for benchmarking single-cell clustering methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a 2D embedding or cluster labels are already available — embedding again adds no information. Subtle small-cluster detail is required and the multi-scale Annoy-based near-neighbor approximation is insufficient; the FIt-SNE README notes vantage-point trees should be used when 'subtle detail is required (e.g. in identifying small clusters)'. Batch effects are present and uncorrected — Miscell leaves batch correction as a preprocessing step, so embedding uncorrected features can confound clusters.

skills.name: tsne-embedding-of-single-cell-data
skills.search_text: tsne-embedding-of-single-cell-data Use when single-cell expression matrices (e.g., Villani PBMC, Baron pancreatic islet) need a 2-D visualization of cell-type separation or batch mixing, or a t-SNE embedding is required before KMeans clustering for ASW/ARI/NMI/purity evaluation. Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or 2-D coordinates — re-embedding would discard signal The analysis goal is a quantitative reconstruction-accuracy check against true counts rather than visual/batch-effect assessment, where metric computation on highly variable genes is preferred http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generate 2-D t-SNE embeddings of scRNA-Seq matrices (raw or imputed) by first reducing library-normalized counts to 50 PCA components, then embedding to 2-D with TSNE, for visual assessment of cell-type separation and batch mixing and as input to KMeans-based clustering metrics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29576-y
skills.summary: Generate 2-D t-SNE embeddings of scRNA-Seq matrices (raw or imputed) by first reducing library-normalized counts to 50 PCA components, then embedding to 2-D with TSNE, for visual assessment of cell-type separation and batch mixing and as input to KMeans-based clustering metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or 2-D coordinates — re-embedding would discard signal The analysis goal is a quantitative reconstruction-accuracy check against true counts rather than visual/batch-effect assessment, where metric computation on highly variable genes is preferred

skills.description: Use when a cell-to-cell similarity matrix (e.g. learned by SIMLR from scRNA-seq expression data) must be turned into low-dimensional coordinates for visualizing and interpreting subpopulations.
skills.name: tsne-embedding-on-similarity-matrix
skills.search_text: tsne-embedding-on-similarity-matrix Use when a cell-to-cell similarity matrix (e.g. learned by SIMLR from scRNA-seq expression data) must be turned into low-dimensional coordinates for visualizing and interpreting subpopulations. The goal is clustering or de novo discovery rather than visualization — SIMLR's similarity learning itself (multi-kernel + graph diffusion) is the appropriate stage, not the downstream t-SNE embedding The input is raw high-throughput data at a scale beyond the standard implementation — use SIMLR_Large_Scale (with Rcpp, pracma, RcppAnnoy, RSpectra) instead of the standard pipeline Example datasets are needed as authoritative data — the README states the provided Test_*.RData files are preprocessed examples 'and should not be used in place of the ones provided in the respective publications' http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Converts a learned cell-to-cell similarity matrix — such as the one produced by SIMLR's multi-kernel optimization — into 2-D (or 3-D) coordinates via stochastic neighbor embedding, enabling visualization and interpretation of single-cell populations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/pmic.201700232
skills.summary: Converts a learned cell-to-cell similarity matrix — such as the one produced by SIMLR's multi-kernel optimization — into 2-D (or 3-D) coordinates via stochastic neighbor embedding, enabling visualization and interpretation of single-cell populations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is clustering or de novo discovery rather than visualization — SIMLR's similarity learning itself (multi-kernel + graph diffusion) is the appropriate stage, not the downstream t-SNE embedding The input is raw high-throughput data at a scale beyond the standard implementation — use SIMLR_Large_Scale (with Rcpp, pracma, RcppAnnoy, RSpectra) instead of the standard pipeline Example datasets are needed as authoritative data — the README states the provided Test_*.RData files are preprocessed examples 'and should not be used in place of the ones provided in the respective publications'

skills.description: Use when a t-SNE (or UMAP) embedding's quality depends on an unknown scale hyperparameter and you need to pick perplexity/kEff or detect characteristic neighborhood scales using per-sample p values rather than visual inspection.
skills.name: tsne-perplexity-hyperparameter-sweep
skills.search_text: tsne-perplexity-hyperparameter-sweep Use when a t-SNE (or UMAP) embedding's quality depends on an unknown scale hyperparameter and you need to pick perplexity/kEff or detect characteristic neighborhood scales using per-sample p values rather than visual inspection. You only need a single t-SNE embedding for visualization and do not intend to compare scales or optimize perplexity — plain EMBEDR (single fit) suffices. Your question is about cluster identity or annotation of an existing embedding rather than whether the embedding's structure exceeds what a marginally-resampled null would produce. You cannot afford multiple embeddings per scale — with only 1 data and 1 null embedding the empirical p values have coarse resolution and sweep conclusions weaken. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Sweep the t-SNE perplexity (kEff) hyperparameter with EMBEDR_sweep, embedding data and marginally-resampled null data at each scale to obtain per-sample EMBEDR p values, so the characteristic neighborhood scales and the optimal perplexity for a dataset can be identified statistically rather than by eye. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100443
skills.summary: Sweep the t-SNE perplexity (kEff) hyperparameter with EMBEDR_sweep, embedding data and marginally-resampled null data at each scale to obtain per-sample EMBEDR p values, so the characteristic neighborhood scales and the optimal perplexity for a dataset can be identified statistically rather than by eye.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a single t-SNE embedding for visualization and do not intend to compare scales or optimize perplexity — plain EMBEDR (single fit) suffices. Your question is about cluster identity or annotation of an existing embedding rather than whether the embedding's structure exceeds what a marginally-resampled null would produce. You cannot afford multiple embeddings per scale — with only 1 data and 1 null embedding the empirical p values have coarse resolution and sweep conclusions weaken.
