skills.name: tsne-visualization-of-simulated-counts
skills.search_text: tsne-visualization-of-simulated-counts Use when you have run SymSim's SimulateTrueCounts for discrete or continuous populations on a phyla tree (e.g. Phyla5()) and need to verify the simulated cell organization reflects the tree, or to inspect how Sigma changes population heterogeneity. Input is observed counts from a real single-cell dataset rather than SymSim true counts — PlotTsne as used here operates on simulated log2(true_counts+1) with known population labels The analysis requires trajectory inference on real data — use dynverse tools (dynwrap/dynmethods) instead of simulated-tree validation Only one homogeneous population with no tree structure or population labels exists, so there is nothing to compare against tree leaves http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 Visualize SymSim-simulated true counts with t-SNE (via PlotTsne on log2-transformed counts) to check that discrete and continuous cell populations from an input tree structure separate or connect as expected. This validates that the simulator's EVF-based variability parameter Sigma produces heterogeneity patterns consistent with the generative tree. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10500-w
skills.summary: Visualize SymSim-simulated true counts with t-SNE (via PlotTsne on log2-transformed counts) to check that discrete and continuous cell populations from an input tree structure separate or connect as expected. This validates that the simulator's EVF-based variability parameter Sigma produces heterogeneity patterns consistent with the generative tree.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is observed counts from a real single-cell dataset rather than SymSim true counts — PlotTsne as used here operates on simulated log2(true_counts+1) with known population labels The analysis requires trajectory inference on real data — use dynverse tools (dynwrap/dynmethods) instead of simulated-tree validation Only one homogeneous population with no tree structure or population labels exists, so there is nothing to compare against tree leaves

skills.description: Use when you have translated or measured single-cell profiles (e.g., predicted ADT from consecutive epigenome→transcriptome→proteome translation) and need a 2-D embedding to visually assess cell-type separation.
skills.name: tsne-visualization-of-single-cell-profiles
skills.search_text: tsne-visualization-of-single-cell-profiles Use when you have translated or measured single-cell profiles (e.g., predicted ADT from consecutive epigenome→transcriptome→proteome translation) and need a 2-D embedding to visually assess cell-type separation. Input is raw count matrices that have not yet been translated or preprocessed (RNA_data_preprocessing, ATAC_data_preprocessing, CLR_transform should run first) You need quantitative clustering scores rather than visual embeddings — use calculate_cluster.calculate_cluster_index (AMI, ARI, HOM, NMI) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Render t-SNE embeddings of single-cell profiles (e.g., scButterfly-predicted ADT values) using scButterfly's draw_cluster.draw_tsne to visually inspect whether translated profiles recapitulate nuanced differences among cells and cell-type structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47418-x
skills.summary: Render t-SNE embeddings of single-cell profiles (e.g., scButterfly-predicted ADT values) using scButterfly's draw_cluster.draw_tsne to visually inspect whether translated profiles recapitulate nuanced differences among cells and cell-type structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw count matrices that have not yet been translated or preprocessed (RNA_data_preprocessing, ATAC_data_preprocessing, CLR_transform should run first) You need quantitative clustering scores rather than visual embeddings — use calculate_cluster.calculate_cluster_index (AMI, ARI, HOM, NMI) instead

skills.description: Use when a normalized c-CSN-derived CNDM (m genes x n cells, e.g. >20,000 Tabula Muris droplet cells) needs dimension reduction and 2D visualization to confirm that cells segregate by known origin or cluster structure.
skills.name: tsne-visualization-single-cell
skills.search_text: tsne-visualization-single-cell Use when a normalized c-CSN-derived CNDM (m genes x n cells, e.g. >20,000 Tabula Muris droplet cells) needs dimension reduction and 2D visualization to confirm that cells segregate by known origin or cluster structure. Input is a raw gene expression matrix (GEM) rather than a c-CSN-transformed CNDM; use standard scRNA-seq visualization workflows instead Goal is to construct the conditional cell-specific network itself rather than visualize an already-computed CNDM Goal is trajectory directionality or differentiation potency estimation, which requires NFE computation rather than plain t-SNE embedding http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Apply t-SNE (optionally after PCA) to a c-CSN-derived conditional network degree matrix (CNDM) to visualize single-cell structure, enabling assessment of tissue- or cell-type separation compatible with standard scRNA-seq pipelines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.05.005
skills.summary: Apply t-SNE (optionally after PCA) to a c-CSN-derived conditional network degree matrix (CNDM) to visualize single-cell structure, enabling assessment of tissue- or cell-type separation compatible with standard scRNA-seq pipelines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw gene expression matrix (GEM) rather than a c-CSN-transformed CNDM; use standard scRNA-seq visualization workflows instead Goal is to construct the conditional cell-specific network itself rather than visualize an already-computed CNDM Goal is trajectory directionality or differentiation potency estimation, which requires NFE computation rather than plain t-SNE embedding

skills.description: Use when you have predicted core promoter elements anchored to annotated TSSs across multiple species and need to compare element position/score distributions to assess conservation or motif positioning quality.
skills.name: tss-anchored-motif-coordinate-analysis
skills.search_text: tss-anchored-motif-coordinate-analysis Use when you have predicted core promoter elements anchored to annotated TSSs across multiple species and need to compare element position/score distributions to assess conservation or motif positioning quality. Your goal is de novo motif discovery or scanning arbitrary user-supplied sequences for motifs rather than analyzing already-predicted elements anchored to annotated TSSs. Your TSS annotations are not CAGE-based/EPDnew-style, so element positions cannot be meaningfully expressed relative to a high-confidence TSS. The species or element types of interest are outside the CORE database's 10 metazoan species (worm to human). http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Workflow for computing per-species frequency distributions of predicted core promoter element positions (TATA, dInr, PB) relative to CAGE-annotated TSSs from EPDnew, using ElemeNT 2023's expanded 10-species CORE database to test cross-species conservation of element positioning. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae110
skills.summary: Workflow for computing per-species frequency distributions of predicted core promoter element positions (TATA, dInr, PB) relative to CAGE-annotated TSSs from EPDnew, using ElemeNT 2023's expanded 10-species CORE database to test cross-species conservation of element positioning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is de novo motif discovery or scanning arbitrary user-supplied sequences for motifs rather than analyzing already-predicted elements anchored to annotated TSSs. Your TSS annotations are not CAGE-based/EPDnew-style, so element positions cannot be meaningfully expressed relative to a high-confidence TSS. The species or element types of interest are outside the CORE database's 10 metazoan species (worm to human).

skills.description: Use when you have a set of TSS coordinates (e.g. EPDnew, GSE221852 csRNA-seq, GSE89299 RAMPAGE) and need promoter windows around each TSS as FASTA for motif-position analysis.
skills.name: tss-coordinate-sequence-extraction
skills.search_text: tss-coordinate-sequence-extraction Use when you have a set of TSS coordinates (e.g. EPDnew, GSE221852 csRNA-seq, GSE89299 RAMPAGE) and need promoter windows around each TSS as FASTA for motif-position analysis. Input sequences are already provided as FASTA windows aligned on the TSS — re-extraction adds no value The goal is de novo motif discovery in arbitrary sequences not tied to TSS coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Extracts promoter sequence windows centered on each annotated TSS coordinate and formats them as FASTA input for ElemeNT core promoter element detection, enabling cross-dataset TSS source comparisons such as EPDnew/CAGE vs csRNA-seq vs RAMPAGE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae110
skills.summary: Extracts promoter sequence windows centered on each annotated TSS coordinate and formats them as FASTA input for ElemeNT core promoter element detection, enabling cross-dataset TSS source comparisons such as EPDnew/CAGE vs csRNA-seq vs RAMPAGE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences are already provided as FASTA windows aligned on the TSS — re-extraction adds no value The goal is de novo motif discovery in arbitrary sequences not tied to TSS coordinates

skills.description: Use when you have a set of TSS annotations (e.g. from EPDnew/CAGE, csRNA-seq GSE221852, or RAMPAGE GSE89299) and want to judge dataset quality or compare TSS sources by the stringency of core promoter element positioning.
skills.name: tss-dataset-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: tss-dataset-quality-assessment Use when you have a set of TSS annotations (e.g. from EPDnew/CAGE, csRNA-seq GSE221852, or RAMPAGE GSE89299) and want to judge dataset quality or compare TSS sources by the stringency of core promoter element positioning. Input is a raw sequencing dataset (FASTQ/BAM) without called TSS peaks — TSS peaks must first be called (e.g. with HOMER) before element positioning can be evaluated Sequences are not centered on a TSS (arbitrary genomic regions) — preferential-position-based quality assessment is only meaningful relative to an annotated TSS Searching a user-defined, non-core-promoter motif — ElemeNT 2023 supports this, but the positional-quality logic here applies to core promoter elements http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Assess the quality of high-throughput TSS datasets (CAGE, csRNA-seq, RAMPAGE) by running ElemeNT 2023 on promoter sequences centered on each TSS and checking whether core promoter elements (dInr, DPE, PB, TATA, Motif 1, dTCT) appear at their preferential positions relative to the TSS; strict positional preference indicates high-quality TSS input data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae110
skills.summary: Assess the quality of high-throughput TSS datasets (CAGE, csRNA-seq, RAMPAGE) by running ElemeNT 2023 on promoter sequences centered on each TSS and checking whether core promoter elements (dInr, DPE, PB, TATA, Motif 1, dTCT) appear at their preferential positions relative to the TSS; strict positional preference indicates high-quality TSS input data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw sequencing dataset (FASTQ/BAM) without called TSS peaks — TSS peaks must first be called (e.g. with HOMER) before element positioning can be evaluated Sequences are not centered on a TSS (arbitrary genomic regions) — preferential-position-based quality assessment is only meaningful relative to an annotated TSS Searching a user-defined, non-core-promoter motif — ElemeNT 2023 supports this, but the positional-quality logic here applies to core promoter elements

skills.description: Use when starting a scATAC-seq analysis from a fragments file (e.g. BMMC data) and you must exclude low-quality cells — low transcription start site (TSS) enrichment or too few unique nuclear fragments — before building the peak-count matrix and running LSI.
skills.name: tss-enrichment-cell-filtering
skills.search_text: tss-enrichment-cell-filtering Use when starting a scATAC-seq analysis from a fragments file (e.g. BMMC data) and you must exclude low-quality cells — low transcription start site (TSS) enrichment or too few unique nuclear fragments — before building the peak-count matrix and running LSI. Input is scRNA-seq data — SCALA's RNA modality uses Seurat-based QC rather than TSS enrichment metrics. Cells have already been filtered and an ArchR Arrow project exists — reapplying minTSS/minFrags would duplicate QC. Analysis targets organisms other than human or mouse — SCALA supports only hg19/hg38/mm9/mm10 genome builds. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Quality-control filter for scATAC-seq cells based on TSS enrichment and fragment-count thresholds, as implemented in SCALA/ArchR. It removes low-quality cells before dimensionality reduction so that downstream LSI, clustering, and UMAP reflect accessible chromatin rather than technical noise. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.10.032
skills.summary: Quality-control filter for scATAC-seq cells based on TSS enrichment and fragment-count thresholds, as implemented in SCALA/ArchR. It removes low-quality cells before dimensionality reduction so that downstream LSI, clustering, and UMAP reflect accessible chromatin rather than technical noise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is scRNA-seq data — SCALA's RNA modality uses Seurat-based QC rather than TSS enrichment metrics. Cells have already been filtered and an ArchR Arrow project exists — reapplying minTSS/minFrags would duplicate QC. Analysis targets organisms other than human or mouse — SCALA supports only hg19/hg38/mm9/mm10 genome builds.

skills.description: Use when a mosaic dataset contains scATAC-seq batches but lacks scRNA-seq matrices for some batches (None placeholders in the counts dictionary), so that gene activity scores can substitute for missing gene expression.
skills.name: tss-proximal-peak-aggregation
skills.search_text: tss-proximal-peak-aggregation Use when a mosaic dataset contains scATAC-seq batches but lacks scRNA-seq matrices for some batches (None placeholders in the counts dictionary), so that gene activity scores can substitute for missing gene expression. The batch already has a measured scRNA-seq count matrix — use the real counts rather than gene activity scores Feature entities (regions and genes) are already connected across all batches by the available input matrices, so no pseudo-count imputation is needed You need chromatin-region-level (peak) features in the output; aggregation to gene bodies discards per-peak resolution http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Aggregates scATAC-seq per-cell peak counts into per-gene accessibility scores by summing peaks within 2000 bp upstream of each gene's TSS plus the gene body, then binarizes the result to form a pseudo-scRNA-seq matrix that fills missing gene-expression modalities in scMoMaT mosaic layouts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36066-2
skills.summary: Aggregates scATAC-seq per-cell peak counts into per-gene accessibility scores by summing peaks within 2000 bp upstream of each gene's TSS plus the gene body, then binarizes the result to form a pseudo-scRNA-seq matrix that fills missing gene-expression modalities in scMoMaT mosaic layouts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The batch already has a measured scRNA-seq count matrix — use the real counts rather than gene activity scores Feature entities (regions and genes) are already connected across all batches by the available input matrices, so no pseudo-count imputation is needed You need chromatin-region-level (peak) features in the output; aggregation to gene bodies discards per-peak resolution

skills.description: Use when profiling how far UMI-collapsed transcript coverage extends from transcript ends in 10x Chromium scRNA-seq data (e.g., to justify detecting SNVs up to ~10 kbp from the capture site).
skills.name: tss-tts-distance-normalization
skills.search_text: tss-tts-distance-normalization Use when profiling how far UMI-collapsed transcript coverage extends from transcript ends in 10x Chromium scRNA-seq data (e.g., to justify detecting SNVs up to ~10 kbp from the capture site). Genes with multiple isoforms — the distance normalization is restricted to the 20,090 single-isoform genes, so applying it to multi-isoform genes confounds TSS/TTS assignment The goal is genotyping individual cells (e.g., assigning variants to barcodes with cb_sniffer or VarTrix) rather than characterizing transcript coverage distribution Input is bulk RNA-seq or full-length cDNA data (e.g., Fluidigm C1/SMART-seq) where end-biased coverage decay is not the limiting factor http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies single-cell transcript coverage as a function of signed distance from the transcription start site (TSS) or transcription termination site (TTS) for 10x Chromium 5' (v1) and 3' (v2) libraries, to assess whether end-biased capture retains enough coverage distal to transcript ends for variant detection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-11591-1
skills.summary: Quantifies single-cell transcript coverage as a function of signed distance from the transcription start site (TSS) or transcription termination site (TTS) for 10x Chromium 5' (v1) and 3' (v2) libraries, to assess whether end-biased capture retains enough coverage distal to transcript ends for variant detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genes with multiple isoforms — the distance normalization is restricted to the 20,090 single-isoform genes, so applying it to multi-isoform genes confounds TSS/TTS assignment The goal is genotyping individual cells (e.g., assigning variants to barcodes with cb_sniffer or VarTrix) rather than characterizing transcript coverage distribution Input is bulk RNA-seq or full-length cDNA data (e.g., Fluidigm C1/SMART-seq) where end-biased coverage decay is not the limiting factor

skills.description: Use when high-dimensional transcriptomic data (P >> n, e.g. RNA-seq expression matrices) must be filtered to a small top-variable set before fitting glmnet/elastic-net models, and you need an unbiased performance estimate rather than the optimistically biased inner-CV metric.
skills.name: ttest-feature-filtering-within-cv-loop
skills.search_text: ttest-feature-filtering-within-cv-loop Use when high-dimensional transcriptomic data (P >> n, e.g. RNA-seq expression matrices) must be filtered to a small top-variable set before fitting glmnet/elastic-net models, and you need an unbiased performance estimate rather than the optimistically biased inner-CV metric. When the predictor set is already a small curated feature table — univariate t-test filtering (nfilter = 300) is meant for P >> n high-dimensional data When you intend to filter features once on the full dataset before CV — this creates the performance-estimation bias the skill exists to avoid When the outcome is not a two-class response compatible with a t-test filter (e.g. multinomial or regression targets need other filters like anova_filter or correl_filter) http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Applies the nestedcv R package's ttest_filter (univariate t-test ranking, e.g. nfilter = 300) strictly inside the outer loop of nested cross-validation so feature selection is re-run on each outer training fold and the outer-fold AUC is an unbiased estimate, unlike filtering on the whole dataset which inflates performance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad048
skills.summary: Applies the nestedcv R package's ttest_filter (univariate t-test ranking, e.g. nfilter = 300) strictly inside the outer loop of nested cross-validation so feature selection is re-run on each outer training fold and the outer-fold AUC is an unbiased estimate, unlike filtering on the whole dataset which inflates performance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the predictor set is already a small curated feature table — univariate t-test filtering (nfilter = 300) is meant for P >> n high-dimensional data When you intend to filter features once on the full dataset before CV — this creates the performance-estimation bias the skill exists to avoid When the outcome is not a two-class response compatible with a t-test filter (e.g. multinomial or regression targets need other filters like anova_filter or correl_filter)

skills.description: Use when a GapClust (or similar) rare-cluster detection run on scRNA-seq data yields candidate minor clusters whose identity must be confirmed by enrichment of known marker genes (e.g. Dclk1/Trpm5 for tuft cells).
skills.name: tuft-cell-marker-gene-enrichment
skills.search_text: tuft-cell-marker-gene-enrichment Use when a GapClust (or similar) rare-cluster detection run on scRNA-seq data yields candidate minor clusters whose identity must be confirmed by enrichment of known marker genes (e.g. Dclk1/Trpm5 for tuft cells). Input is not a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. already-normalized, aggregated, or bulk expression data), since GapClust operates on cell-level expression profiles The goal is to detect rare clusters de novo without any known marker genes available for identity validation Rare cell types of interest have already been identified and removed — per the article, GapClust should be rerun to discover additional hidden clusters rather than revalidating known ones http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates rare-cell clusters detected by GapClust — such as the 29-cell R2 tuft-cell cluster in the 4491-cell non-irradiated intestinal crypt dataset from Arshad et al. — by checking enrichment of established marker genes (Dclk1, Trpm5) via Seurat-style differential expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24489-8
skills.summary: Validates rare-cell clusters detected by GapClust — such as the 29-cell R2 tuft-cell cluster in the 4491-cell non-irradiated intestinal crypt dataset from Arshad et al. — by checking enrichment of established marker genes (Dclk1, Trpm5) via Seurat-style differential expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. already-normalized, aggregated, or bulk expression data), since GapClust operates on cell-level expression profiles The goal is to detect rare clusters de novo without any known marker genes available for identity validation Rare cell types of interest have already been identified and removed — per the article, GapClust should be rerun to discover additional hidden clusters rather than revalidating known ones

skills.description: Use when you have per-method, per-condition activity-inference scores (e.g. Spearman correlations to unperturbed activities across normal, edge-addition and edge-deletion networks) and need an omnibus ANOVA plus pairwise Tukey HSD comparison of group means.
skills.name: tukey-hsd-posthoc-testing
skills.search_text: tukey-hsd-posthoc-testing Use when you have per-method, per-condition activity-inference scores (e.g. Spearman correlations to unperturbed activities across normal, edge-addition and edge-deletion networks) and need an omnibus ANOVA plus pairwise Tukey HSD comparison of group means. The data are simple paired observations with only two groups (e.g. one perturbed vs one unperturbed condition) — a paired test suffices; ANOVA+Tukey adds no information The analysis compares method ranking performance (AUROC/AUPRC from decoupleRBench) rather than predictability across noise conditions — use the benchmark evaluation pipeline instead Only a single network perturbation condition exists (no normal/addition/deletion grouping), so the three-level ANOVA design cannot be formed http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Apply a one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's HSD posthoc test to compare method predictability across prior-knowledge perturbation conditions (normal, edge addition, edge deletion) in the decoupleR noise-robustness benchmark, yielding adjusted P-values and F statistics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac016
skills.summary: Apply a one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's HSD posthoc test to compare method predictability across prior-knowledge perturbation conditions (normal, edge addition, edge deletion) in the decoupleR noise-robustness benchmark, yielding adjusted P-values and F statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are simple paired observations with only two groups (e.g. one perturbed vs one unperturbed condition) — a paired test suffices; ANOVA+Tukey adds no information The analysis compares method ranking performance (AUROC/AUPRC from decoupleRBench) rather than predictability across noise conditions — use the benchmark evaluation pipeline instead Only a single network perturbation condition exists (no normal/addition/deletion grouping), so the three-level ANOVA design cannot be formed

skills.description: Use when multiplexed single-cell data with x/y coordinates (e.g., MCMICRO-processed CyCIF output) needs region-based analysis requiring tumor/stromal region boundaries and per-cell region labels.
skills.name: tumor-boundary-delineation
skills.search_text: tumor-boundary-delineation Use when multiplexed single-cell data with x/y coordinates (e.g., MCMICRO-processed CyCIF output) needs region-based analysis requiring tumor/stromal region boundaries and per-cell region labels. Input lacks spatial coordinates (no x/y per cell) or is already a per-cell region/feature table — boundary construction from point coordinates is meaningless The goal is cell-phenotyping or neighborhood-graph analysis rather than region-based delineation (e.g., Squidpy specializes in neighborhood graph construction and analysis) No user-specified marker-defined cell population is available to anchor the boundary (e.g., no SOX10+ tumor cell gate set via setGates) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Delineates tumor regional boundaries from marker-defined cell populations (e.g., SOX10+ melanoma cells) using SpatialCells' getBoundary/getShrunkenBoundary/getExtendedBoundary, then assigns every cell to exactly one named region via assignPointsToRegions for region-based TME analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae189
skills.summary: Delineates tumor regional boundaries from marker-defined cell populations (e.g., SOX10+ melanoma cells) using SpatialCells' getBoundary/getShrunkenBoundary/getExtendedBoundary, then assigns every cell to exactly one named region via assignPointsToRegions for region-based TME analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks spatial coordinates (no x/y per cell) or is already a per-cell region/feature table — boundary construction from point coordinates is meaningless The goal is cell-phenotyping or neighborhood-graph analysis rather than region-based delineation (e.g., Squidpy specializes in neighborhood graph construction and analysis) No user-specified marker-defined cell population is available to anchor the boundary (e.g., no SOX10+ tumor cell gate set via setGates)

skills.description: Use when you have raw scRNA-seq count matrices (Smart-seq2 or 10X Chromium) from tumor biopsies and need a fully unsupervised malignant/non-malignant cell classification without manually identified reference cell clusters.
skills.name: tumor-cell-classification-scrna
skills.search_text: tumor-cell-classification-scrna Use when you have raw scRNA-seq count matrices (Smart-seq2 or 10X Chromium) from tumor biopsies and need a fully unsupervised malignant/non-malignant cell classification without manually identified reference cell clusters. Tumors with minimal genomic alterations where the aneuploidy assumption fails (e.g. leukemia, pediatric cancers, Ependymomas) You already have manual reference clusters and prefer inferCNV-style guided analysis, or the goal is clonal phylogeny across multiple samples rather than single-sample classification (use multiSampleComparisonClonalCN instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Automatically classify malignant versus non-malignant cells in tumor scRNA-seq count matrices using SCEVAN, a variational aneuploidy-analysis approach that detects confident normal cells and segments copy number profiles, benchmarked against CopyKAT. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36790-9
skills.summary: Automatically classify malignant versus non-malignant cells in tumor scRNA-seq count matrices using SCEVAN, a variational aneuploidy-analysis approach that detects confident normal cells and segments copy number profiles, benchmarked against CopyKAT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Tumors with minimal genomic alterations where the aneuploidy assumption fails (e.g. leukemia, pediatric cancers, Ependymomas) You already have manual reference clusters and prefer inferCNV-style guided analysis, or the goal is clonal phylogeny across multiple samples rather than single-sample classification (use multiSampleComparisonClonalCN instead)

skills.description: Use when annotating normal cells within a tumor scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. TNBC GSE176078) and malignant clusters must be excluded first so cluster markers and cell-type calls reflect non-malignant biology only.
skills.name: tumor-cell-filtering-in-scrna-seq-clusters
skills.search_text: tumor-cell-filtering-in-scrna-seq-clusters Use when annotating normal cells within a tumor scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. TNBC GSE176078) and malignant clusters must be excluded first so cluster markers and cell-type calls reflect non-malignant biology only. The dataset contains no malignant cells (e.g. PBMC 3k) — there is nothing to filter and QC-based subsetting alone suffices The goal is to annotate or characterize the tumor cells themselves; this skill removes them from the annotation scope Tumor clusters have not yet been identified — cluster-level exclusion requires prior malignant-cell labels, not just per-cell QC metrics Removes previously annotated malignant tumor-cell clusters from a tumor scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. the Wu et al. 2021a TNBC dataset, GSE176078) so that downstream marker-based annotation with EasyCellType/SingleR/scCATCH operates only on non-malignant populations (CAFs, T cells, PVL, epithelial, endothelial). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad029
skills.summary: Removes previously annotated malignant tumor-cell clusters from a tumor scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. the Wu et al. 2021a TNBC dataset, GSE176078) so that downstream marker-based annotation with EasyCellType/SingleR/scCATCH operates only on non-malignant populations (CAFs, T cells, PVL, epithelial, endothelial).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains no malignant cells (e.g. PBMC 3k) — there is nothing to filter and QC-based subsetting alone suffices The goal is to annotate or characterize the tumor cells themselves; this skill removes them from the annotation scope Tumor clusters have not yet been identified — cluster-level exclusion requires prior malignant-cell labels, not just per-cell QC metrics

skills.description: Use when a marker-intensity single-cell table from multiplexed imaging (e.g. MCMICRO output of a CyCIF slide) must be scored per-cell for proliferation status (MPI in {-1, 0, 1}) and the fraction of a tumor-cell type such as SOX10+ cells with MPI = 1 quantified.
skills.name: tumor-cell-fraction-quantification
skills.search_text: tumor-cell-fraction-quantification Use when a marker-intensity single-cell table from multiplexed imaging (e.g. MCMICRO output of a CyCIF slide) must be scored per-cell for proliferation status (MPI in {-1, 0, 1}) and the fraction of a tumor-cell type such as SOX10+ cells with MPI = 1 quantified. Input is raw multi-channel whole-slide images rather than MCMICRO-derived single-cell marker-intensity data — SpatialCells expects the output of MCMICRO as its input Input is spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. the Visium lymph node sample deconvoluted with Cell2location) rather than multiplexed single-cell imaging marker intensities, where region-based rather than marker-gated MPI analysis applies Gates for the proliferation and arrest markers have not been defined — getMPI requires setGate/setGates thresholds to run http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Quantifies the fraction of a marker-defined tumor-cell population (e.g. SOX10+ melanoma cells) in a proliferating state by assigning per-cell multivariate proliferation index (MPI) labels with spatialcells.msmt.getMPI from SpatialCells. MPI integrates mitosis/proliferation markers against cell cycle arrest markers so a single per-cell label in {-1, 0, 1} can be aggregated into population-level proliferation fractions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae189
skills.summary: Quantifies the fraction of a marker-defined tumor-cell population (e.g. SOX10+ melanoma cells) in a proliferating state by assigning per-cell multivariate proliferation index (MPI) labels with spatialcells.msmt.getMPI from SpatialCells. MPI integrates mitosis/proliferation markers against cell cycle arrest markers so a single per-cell label in {-1, 0, 1} can be aggregated into population-level proliferation fractions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw multi-channel whole-slide images rather than MCMICRO-derived single-cell marker-intensity data — SpatialCells expects the output of MCMICRO as its input Input is spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. the Visium lymph node sample deconvoluted with Cell2location) rather than multiplexed single-cell imaging marker intensities, where region-based rather than marker-gated MPI analysis applies Gates for the proliferation and arrest markers have not been defined — getMPI requires setGate/setGates thresholds to run

skills.description: Use when you have normal-tissue scRNA-seq reference data with cell-type labels and tumor scRNA-seq test data, and need to identify malignant cells as those left unassigned by cell-type classifiers.
skills.name: tumor-cell-malignancy-classification
skills.search_text: tumor-cell-malignancy-classification Use when you have normal-tissue scRNA-seq reference data with cell-type labels and tumor scRNA-seq test data, and need to identify malignant cells as those left unassigned by cell-type classifiers. The goal is ordinary cell-type assignment between matched tissues, not new (malignant) cell-type detection — in that setting unassigned cells are not positives but errors. There is no labeled normal-tissue reference available for the tumor's tissue of origin, so classifier training is impossible. The dataset is the self-projection cross-validation benchmark (e.g. Tabula Muris or PBMC SCP424), where labels exist in both train and test and malignant-cell detection is not defined. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Detects malignant tumor cells in late-stage lung cancer scRNA-seq data by applying automatic cell-type identification methods trained on matched normal lung reference data, treating 'unknown'/'unassigned' predictions as malignant. Validated by sensitivity/specificity per method, with clustifyr achieving nearly 100% of both. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.10.027
skills.summary: Detects malignant tumor cells in late-stage lung cancer scRNA-seq data by applying automatic cell-type identification methods trained on matched normal lung reference data, treating 'unknown'/'unassigned' predictions as malignant. Validated by sensitivity/specificity per method, with clustifyr achieving nearly 100% of both.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is ordinary cell-type assignment between matched tissues, not new (malignant) cell-type detection — in that setting unassigned cells are not positives but errors. There is no labeled normal-tissue reference available for the tumor's tissue of origin, so classifier training is impossible. The dataset is the self-projection cross-validation benchmark (e.g. Tabula Muris or PBMC SCP424), where labels exist in both train and test and malignant-cell detection is not defined.

skills.description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq or microarray data with matched overall survival (or immunotherapy response) information and cell-type marker lists, and you need to infer which immune cell-cell interactions drive favorable/unfavorable prognosis.
skills.name: tumor-immune-microenvironment-cell-interaction-inference
skills.search_text: tumor-immune-microenvironment-cell-interaction-inference Use when you have bulk RNA-seq or microarray data with matched overall survival (or immunotherapy response) information and cell-type marker lists, and you need to infer which immune cell-cell interactions drive favorable/unfavorable prognosis. The cohort lacks matched survival information or has too few samples/events — TimiGP requires a large gene expression dataset with matched survival information to identify prognostic gene pairs The goal is deconvolving absolute cell-type proportions from bulk data (deconvolution tools like CIBERSORTx or xCell are the appropriate class) The analysis requires experimentally validated interactions — the paper notes no wet-lab validation was performed, so inferred interactions carry uncertainty http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A workflow, implemented in the TimiGP R package, that infers directed cell-cell interactions and prognostic associations in the tumor immune microenvironment from bulk transcriptomics plus survival data using marker gene pairs, Cox regression, and enrichment analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2023.101121
skills.summary: A workflow, implemented in the TimiGP R package, that infers directed cell-cell interactions and prognostic associations in the tumor immune microenvironment from bulk transcriptomics plus survival data using marker gene pairs, Cox regression, and enrichment analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cohort lacks matched survival information or has too few samples/events — TimiGP requires a large gene expression dataset with matched survival information to identify prognostic gene pairs The goal is deconvolving absolute cell-type proportions from bulk data (deconvolution tools like CIBERSORTx or xCell are the appropriate class) The analysis requires experimentally validated interactions — the paper notes no wet-lab validation was performed, so inferred interactions carry uncertainty

skills.search_text: tumor-immune-regulator-prioritization Use when you have pretrained MetaTiME MeC gene-weight tables (86 MeCs) and want to identify and rank putative TF regulators of a cell-state or signaling component using ChIP-seq binding evidence. skills.search_text: tumor-microenvironment-cell-identification Use when annotating human scRNA-seq cells whose exact types may be missing from the classifier's training set (e.g. endothelial, fibroblast, plasmacytoid dendritic cells in LX675/LX679/LX682 lung tumor samples), and hierarchical Cell Ontology-consistent labels are wanted. skills.description: Use when you have matched bulk DNA WES and scRNA-seq SNV read counts (Rs, Xs, Rb, Xb) for the same tumor and need to infer subclone number, mutational profiles, cell-of-origin, and cell-to-clone assignments jointly.
skills.name: tumor-phylogeny-inference-from-bulk-and-single-cell-snv
skills.search_text: tumor-phylogeny-inference-from-bulk-and-single-cell-snv Use when you have matched bulk DNA WES and scRNA-seq SNV read counts (Rs, Xs, Rb, Xb) for the same tumor and need to infer subclone number, mutational profiles, cell-of-origin, and cell-to-clone assignments jointly. You have only scRNA-seq SNVs without matched bulk DNA-seq data — Cardelino with a guide clonal tree is the alternative that takes scRNA-seq input indirectly informed by a first-step Canopy run. The read count matrices have not passed the stringent QC / pre-processing pipeline (somatic and germline variant calling; Zenodo scripts) needed to produce the finalized SNV callset. Mutations lack estimable bursting kinetics — subset alternative and total read counts to only mutations for which gene burstiness (alpha, beta) can be estimated before calling get_trees(). http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Joint Bayesian inference of tumor phylogeny from SNVs derived from bulk DNA WES and scRNA-seq using the Canopy2 R package, which samples the clonal configuration Z, single-cell assignment P^s, and bulk composition P^b via Markov chain Monte Carlo from a mixture of binomial (bulk) and beta-binomial (single-cell) likelihoods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s12561-024-09466-1
skills.summary: Joint Bayesian inference of tumor phylogeny from SNVs derived from bulk DNA WES and scRNA-seq using the Canopy2 R package, which samples the clonal configuration Z, single-cell assignment P^s, and bulk composition P^b via Markov chain Monte Carlo from a mixture of binomial (bulk) and beta-binomial (single-cell) likelihoods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only scRNA-seq SNVs without matched bulk DNA-seq data — Cardelino with a guide clonal tree is the alternative that takes scRNA-seq input indirectly informed by a first-step Canopy run. The read count matrices have not passed the stringent QC / pre-processing pipeline (somatic and germline variant calling; Zenodo scripts) needed to produce the finalized SNV callset. Mutations lack estimable bursting kinetics — subset alternative and total read counts to only mutations for which gene burstiness (alpha, beta) can be estimated before calling get_trees().

skills.summary: Benchmark Canopy2 against Canopy and Cardelino (with/without a guide clonal tree) on simulated bulk DNA-seq plus scRNA-seq read counts, quantifying reconstruction error of the mutation-to-clone matrix Z and the cell-to-clone matrix Ps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is inference on real patient data rather than simulation-based benchmarking against a known ground-truth Z and Ps Input lacks paired bulk DNA WES and single-cell RNA-seq SNV read counts, which Canopy2 requires as Rs/Xs/Rb/Xb Only a single method is to be run; the skill's value comes from the head-to-head error comparison with Canopy and Cardelino

skills.description: Use when you need to verify that simulated TWAS Z-scores or p-values are consistent with the null (KS p > 0.05 vs Uniform(0,1)), with FWER ~0.05 and genomic inflation lambda ~1.
skills.name: twas-null-calibration-analysis
skills.search_text: twas-null-calibration-analysis Use when you need to verify that simulated TWAS Z-scores or p-values are consistent with the null (KS p > 0.05 vs Uniform(0,1)), with FWER ~0.05 and genomic inflation lambda ~1. Estimating TWAS power under alternative models (h2ge > 0) — use power-analysis rather than null calibration, where p-value uniformity is expected to break by design. Assessing calibration under LD misspecification (mismatched GWAS/eQTL/TWAS panels via --eqtl-prefix/--test-prefix) — that requires the matched-LD null as the correctly specified baseline comparison instead. Calibrating statistics from real observed GWAS data rather than twas_sim-simulated summary statistics, since the null expectation here derives from simulated loci with alpha = 0. http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Evaluates whether TWAS test statistics produced by the twas_sim simulator are unbiased and well-calibrated under null simulations (alpha = 0), using Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests on TWAS Z-scores/p-values, family-wise error rate (FWER), and genomic inflation factors across linear prediction models. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad288
skills.summary: Evaluates whether TWAS test statistics produced by the twas_sim simulator are unbiased and well-calibrated under null simulations (alpha = 0), using Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests on TWAS Z-scores/p-values, family-wise error rate (FWER), and genomic inflation factors across linear prediction models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Estimating TWAS power under alternative models (h2ge > 0) — use power-analysis rather than null calibration, where p-value uniformity is expected to break by design. Assessing calibration under LD misspecification (mismatched GWAS/eQTL/TWAS panels via --eqtl-prefix/--test-prefix) — that requires the matched-LD null as the correctly specified baseline comparison instead. Calibrating statistics from real observed GWAS data rather than twas_sim-simulated summary statistics, since the null expectation here derives from simulated loci with alpha = 0.

Input is real (not simulated) GWAS/eQTL summary data — the benchmarking logic requires known ground-truth causal architecture to estimate power No individual-level reference data are available to train the FUSION baseline for comparison The goal is cross-population or trans-eQTL TWAS, which OTTERS explicitly does not support http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Benchmark GReX imputation accuracy (out-of-sample test R2) and TWAS power of PRS-based training methods (P+T, lassosum, SDPR, PRS-CS) and the OTTERS omnibus test against FUSION, using simulated eQTL/GWAS summary statistics under multiple genetic architectures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36862-w
skills.summary: Benchmark GReX imputation accuracy (out-of-sample test R2) and TWAS power of PRS-based training methods (P+T, lassosum, SDPR, PRS-CS) and the OTTERS omnibus test against FUSION, using simulated eQTL/GWAS summary statistics under multiple genetic architectures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real (not simulated) GWAS/eQTL summary data — the benchmarking logic requires known ground-truth causal architecture to estimate power No individual-level reference data are available to train the FUSION baseline for comparison The goal is cross-population or trans-eQTL TWAS, which OTTERS explicitly does not support

skills.search_text: twas-power-estimation-across-ld-panels Use when evaluating how TWAS power or type-I error changes when eQTL weight-training LD and TWAS testing LD come from a different reference panel than the GWAS LD, or when planning TWAS power analyses. The goal is gene fine-mapping of real TWAS summary statistics rather than simulation-based power/calibration analysis — use FOCUS/MA-FOCUS instead. GWAS, eQTL, and TWAS testing necessarily share a single LD panel and the question is not sensitivity to LD reference choice. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Estimate TWAS power and calibration under matched vs. mismatched LD reference panels by simulating GWAS summary statistics and TWAS test statistics with twas_sim's sim.py, sweeping h2ge over null and alternative values across many seeded replicates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad288
skills.summary: Estimate TWAS power and calibration under matched vs. mismatched LD reference panels by simulating GWAS summary statistics and TWAS test statistics with twas_sim's sim.py, sweeping h2ge over null and alternative values across many seeded replicates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is gene fine-mapping of real TWAS summary statistics rather than simulation-based power/calibration analysis — use FOCUS/MA-FOCUS instead. Individual-level GWAS genotype and phenotype data are available and standard GWAS simulation is desired rather than the fast multivariate-normal shortcut. GWAS, eQTL, and TWAS testing necessarily share a single LD panel and the question is not sensitivity to LD reference choice.

skills.description: Use when you need to compare TWAS power across prediction models or quantify how power scales with GWAS/eQTL sample size, eqtl-h2, h2ge, and number of causal eQTLs before choosing weights for a real TWAS.
skills.name: twas-power-estimation-across-parameter-grid
skills.search_text: twas-power-estimation-across-parameter-grid Use when you need to compare TWAS power across prediction models or quantify how power scales with GWAS/eQTL sample size, eqtl-h2, h2ge, and number of causal eQTLs before choosing weights for a real TWAS. You need fine-mapped credible sets of causal genes from existing TWAS statistics — use FOCUS/MA-FOCUS instead of simulation-based power analysis. You have real GWAS and eQTL weights and only want to compute a single TWAS statistic on observed data rather than estimate power under simulated causal models. h2ge = 0 null behavior is the only interest and you cannot afford replicate-level simulation; empirical power estimation requires many replicates per setting. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 A simulation-based TWAS power analysis workflow using twas_sim's sim.py to estimate how statistical power varies across expression prediction models (LASSO, Elastic Net, GBLUP, SuSiE) and simulation parameters (h2ge, GWAS/eQTL sample sizes, eQTL sparsity) under a causal eQTL-trait model. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad288
skills.summary: A simulation-based TWAS power analysis workflow using twas_sim's sim.py to estimate how statistical power varies across expression prediction models (LASSO, Elastic Net, GBLUP, SuSiE) and simulation parameters (h2ge, GWAS/eQTL sample sizes, eQTL sparsity) under a causal eQTL-trait model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need fine-mapped credible sets of causal genes from existing TWAS statistics — use FOCUS/MA-FOCUS instead of simulation-based power analysis. You have real GWAS and eQTL weights and only want to compute a single TWAS statistic on observed data rather than estimate power under simulated causal models. h2ge = 0 null behavior is the only interest and you cannot afford replicate-level simulation; empirical power estimation requires many replicates per setting.

skills.description: Use when the task requires simulating a complex trait from real 1000G Phase 3 PLINK genotypes and producing GWAS/TWAS statistics for evaluating TWAS method performance or power at settings like --ngwas 100000 and --nqtl 500.
skills.name: twas-simulation-execution
skills.search_text: twas-simulation-execution Use when the task requires simulating a complex trait from real 1000G Phase 3 PLINK genotypes and producing GWAS/TWAS statistics for evaluating TWAS method performance or power at settings like --ngwas 100000 and --nqtl 500. The goal is fine-mapping of real GWAS summary statistics into causal gene sets rather than simulation — use FOCUS/MA-FOCUS instead The task only needs weight construction or fine-mapping on real molecular data (e.g., SuSiE/susieR or SuShiE workflows) without a simulated trait GWAS sample size is extremely large and wall-clock/memory budget is tight while fast-mode approximations are unacceptable — standard individual-level GWAS simulation will be prohibitively slow (41x more CPU time at N=500K) http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Execute end-to-end TWAS simulations with twas_sim's sim.py: sample a 1000G genomic region, filter genotypes (HapMap3, MAF>=1%, HWE>=1e-5), simulate eQTL/GWAS data, fit prediction weights, and compute TWAS statistics and power. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad288
skills.summary: Execute end-to-end TWAS simulations with twas_sim's sim.py: sample a 1000G genomic region, filter genotypes (HapMap3, MAF>=1%, HWE>=1e-5), simulate eQTL/GWAS data, fit prediction weights, and compute TWAS statistics and power.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is fine-mapping of real GWAS summary statistics into causal gene sets rather than simulation — use FOCUS/MA-FOCUS instead The task only needs weight construction or fine-mapping on real molecular data (e.g., SuSiE/susieR or SuShiE workflows) without a simulated trait GWAS sample size is extremely large and wall-clock/memory budget is tight while fast-mode approximations are unacceptable — standard individual-level GWAS simulation will be prohibitively slow (41x more CPU time at N=500K)

skills.description: Use when performing differential expression on scRNA-seq UMI or non-UMI count matrices (or other omics counts) between two conditions, especially when data are sparse, zero-inflated, or heavy-tailed and standard NB-based methods underperform.
skills.name: tweedie-model-gene-level-fitting
skills.search_text: tweedie-model-gene-level-fitting Use when performing differential expression on scRNA-seq UMI or non-UMI count matrices (or other omics counts) between two conditions, especially when data are sparse, zero-inflated, or heavy-tailed and standard NB-based methods underperform. Zero-inflation is a property specific to only a subset of genes — the paper states Tweedieverse 'is not architected for the situation when zero-inflation is a property specific only to a subset of the genes' Multi-subject experimental designs, individual-level differential expression, or differential subpopulation analysis — extension and validation of Tweedieverse to these settings had not been done Continuous measurements where the analysis goal requires shrinkage/borrowed-information gene ranking — the article notes no shrinkage estimates for improved DE gene ranking are implemented http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fit per-gene generalized linear models with a Tweedie-distributed response (CPLM for UMI counts, ZICP for zero-inflated read counts) using the Tweedieverse R/Bioconductor package, then call differentially expressed genes via Wald tests with FDR correction. The three-parameter Tweedie family captures heavy tails and zero-inflation of scRNA-seq data in a single zero-adjusted model, bypassing ad hoc normalization or transformation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/sim.9430
skills.summary: Fit per-gene generalized linear models with a Tweedie-distributed response (CPLM for UMI counts, ZICP for zero-inflated read counts) using the Tweedieverse R/Bioconductor package, then call differentially expressed genes via Wald tests with FDR correction. The three-parameter Tweedie family captures heavy tails and zero-inflation of scRNA-seq data in a single zero-adjusted model, bypassing ad hoc normalization or transformation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Zero-inflation is a property specific to only a subset of genes — the paper states Tweedieverse 'is not architected for the situation when zero-inflation is a property specific only to a subset of the genes' Multi-subject experimental designs, individual-level differential expression, or differential subpopulation analysis — extension and validation of Tweedieverse to these settings had not been done Continuous measurements where the analysis goal requires shrinkage/borrowed-information gene ranking — the article notes no shrinkage estimates for improved DE gene ranking are implemented

skills.description: Use when fitting per-gene (or per-feature) GLMs to sparse, semi-continuous count or abundance data where the optimal Tweedie index parameter p is unknown and must be estimated automatically within the constrained interval (1, 2).
skills.name: tweedie-profile-likelihood-estimation
skills.search_text: tweedie-profile-likelihood-estimation Use when fitting per-gene (or per-feature) GLMs to sparse, semi-continuous count or abundance data where the optimal Tweedie index parameter p is unknown and must be estimated automatically within the constrained interval (1, 2). Zero-inflation is a property specific only to a subset of the genes — the article states Tweedieverse 'is not architected for the situation when zero-inflation is a property specific only to a subset of the genes' Multi-subject experimental designs, individual-level differential expression, or differential subpopulation analysis — extension of Tweedieverse to these designs is explicitly listed as not yet done The goal requires borrowing information across genes (shrinkage estimates for DE ranking) — the article notes this is not implemented and left to further research http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fits per-feature Compound Poisson Linear Models (CPLM/ZICP) from the Tweedie family by jointly estimating the dispersion ϕ and index parameter p ∈ (1, 2) via profile likelihood, enabling self-adaptive semi-continuous modeling of scRNA-seq and other omics data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/sim.9430
skills.summary: Fits per-feature Compound Poisson Linear Models (CPLM/ZICP) from the Tweedie family by jointly estimating the dispersion ϕ and index parameter p ∈ (1, 2) via profile likelihood, enabling self-adaptive semi-continuous modeling of scRNA-seq and other omics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Zero-inflation is a property specific only to a subset of the genes — the article states Tweedieverse 'is not architected for the situation when zero-inflation is a property specific only to a subset of the genes' Multi-subject experimental designs, individual-level differential expression, or differential subpopulation analysis — extension of Tweedieverse to these designs is explicitly listed as not yet done The goal requires borrowing information across genes (shrinkage estimates for DE ranking) — the article notes this is not implemented and left to further research

skills.description: Use when the input is a sparse, semi-continuous omics feature-by-sample matrix (counts or relative abundances) with point mass at zero and heavy tails, and you need per-feature differential testing between conditions.

skills.search_text: tweedie-semicontinuous-count-modeling Use when the input is a sparse, semi-continuous omics feature-by-sample matrix (counts or relative abundances) with point mass at zero and heavy tails, and you need per-feature differential testing between conditions. When zero-inflation is a property specific to only a subset of genes/features — Tweedieverse is not architected for that situation When the analysis requires multi-subject designs, individual-level differential expression, or differential subpopulation analysis — these extensions are not yet validated When the input is already a normalized/transformed expression matrix with no zero point mass, since the method relies on a semi-continuous response with log(S) as an offset rather than ad hoc normalization or transformation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Fits Compound Poisson Linear Models (CPLM/ZICP) with a Tweedie-distributed response (1 < p < 2) to semi-continuous, zero-inflated omics data — including scRNA-seq UMI/non-UMI counts, microbiome counts or relative abundances, and metabolomics peak intensities — for feature-level differential expression testing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/sim.9430
skills.summary: Fits Compound Poisson Linear Models (CPLM/ZICP) with a Tweedie-distributed response (1 < p < 2) to semi-continuous, zero-inflated omics data — including scRNA-seq UMI/non-UMI counts, microbiome counts or relative abundances, and metabolomics peak intensities — for feature-level differential expression testing.
