skills.description: Use when analyzing a simulated two-cluster perturbation/control parameter grid varying cluster distance d and ratio change r, to verify that infected proportion bias on PCs scales linearly with d and r as derived in Equations 14-15.
skills.name: two-cluster-gaussian-simulation-analysis
skills.search_text: two-cluster-gaussian-simulation-analysis Use when analyzing a simulated two-cluster perturbation/control parameter grid varying cluster distance d and ratio change r, to verify that infected proportion bias on PCs scales linearly with d and r as derived in Equations 14-15. Real scCRISPR-seq data with more than two clusters or unknown cluster structure — the exact linear factorization (Equations 14-15) only holds in the two-cluster synthetic scenario; use the full scDecouple GMM/EM decoupling pipeline instead Systems where the Gaussian mixture assumption may not hold, such as intricate systems or disease tissues like tumors, or when rare cell types are completely absent from infection Analysis of genuine biological perturbation responses rather than validating the mathematical bias model — downstream gene ranking and pathway enrichment (scDecouple step 4) is the appropriate skill http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Validates the linear factorization of infected proportion bias in the paper's synthetic two-cluster scCRISPR-seq scenario, where the bias on any PC equals (lambda_1 - delta_1)(mu_1 - mu_2) — the product of the cluster-proportion ratio change r and the mean-expression cluster distance d (Equations 14-15). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae011
skills.summary: Validates the linear factorization of infected proportion bias in the paper's synthetic two-cluster scCRISPR-seq scenario, where the bias on any PC equals (lambda_1 - delta_1)(mu_1 - mu_2) — the product of the cluster-proportion ratio change r and the mean-expression cluster distance d (Equations 14-15).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real scCRISPR-seq data with more than two clusters or unknown cluster structure — the exact linear factorization (Equations 14-15) only holds in the two-cluster synthetic scenario; use the full scDecouple GMM/EM decoupling pipeline instead Systems where the Gaussian mixture assumption may not hold, such as intricate systems or disease tissues like tumors, or when rare cell types are completely absent from infection Analysis of genuine biological perturbation responses rather than validating the mathematical bias model — downstream gene ranking and pathway enrichment (scDecouple step 4) is the appropriate skill

skills.description: Use when comparing cell-cycle-corrected vs. original scRNA-Seq matrices and you need DE genes plus a signature-gene enrichment statistic (odds ratio, hypergeometric p, 95% CI) to judge whether recovered substructure is biologically meaningful.
skills.name: two-means-differential-expression-clustering
skills.search_text: two-means-differential-expression-clustering Use when comparing cell-cycle-corrected vs. original scRNA-Seq matrices and you need DE genes plus a signature-gene enrichment statistic (odds ratio, hypergeometric p, 95% CI) to judge whether recovered substructure is biologically meaningful. The goal is to detect more than two subpopulations — the paper instead uses hierarchical clustering with 5 clusters for the glioblastoma data and 4-means clustering for lung adenocarcinoma replicate separation The task is removing the cell-cycle effect itself rather than evaluating corrected data downstream — use ccRemover (cutoff=3, max_it=4, nboot=200, ntop=10) as a pre-processing step first The expression data has not been corrected or centered gene-by-gene on the log scale — clustering raw uncorrected data on the T-helper data yields a signature odds ratio below 1 and is not physiologically meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A downstream evaluation procedure from Barron & Li (2016): split corrected (or original) single-cell expression matrices into two cell clusters via 2-means clustering, identify differentially expressed genes with a t-test at FDR 0.01, and quantify biological meaningfulness by hypergeometric enrichment of curated signature genes (e.g. the 122 TH2 signature genes). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep33892
skills.summary: A downstream evaluation procedure from Barron & Li (2016): split corrected (or original) single-cell expression matrices into two cell clusters via 2-means clustering, identify differentially expressed genes with a t-test at FDR 0.01, and quantify biological meaningfulness by hypergeometric enrichment of curated signature genes (e.g. the 122 TH2 signature genes).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to detect more than two subpopulations — the paper instead uses hierarchical clustering with 5 clusters for the glioblastoma data and 4-means clustering for lung adenocarcinoma replicate separation The task is removing the cell-cycle effect itself rather than evaluating corrected data downstream — use ccRemover (cutoff=3, max_it=4, nboot=200, ntop=10) as a pre-processing step first The expression data has not been corrected or centered gene-by-gene on the log scale — clustering raw uncorrected data on the T-helper data yields a signature odds ratio below 1 and is not physiologically meaningful

skills.description: Use when cells from two conditions share a single slingshot trajectory and you must test whether lineage-membership weight distributions differ, i.e., whether conditions allocate cells to lineages in different proportions.
skills.name: two-sample-distribution-testing-between-conditions
skills.search_text: two-sample-distribution-testing-between-conditions Use when cells from two conditions share a single slingshot trajectory and you must test whether lineage-membership weight distributions differ, i.e., whether conditions allocate cells to lineages in different proportions. The research question is whether the trajectory topology itself differs between conditions (Step 1) — use topologyTest instead. The question is differential progression along a common lineage (pseudotime distributions) — use progressionTest, not fateSelectionTest. The goal is gene-level differential expression along lineages (Step 3) — use conditionTest / fitGAM instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A two-sample distributional test (as instantiated by condiments' fateSelectionTest) that assesses whether two multivariate or scalar distributions differ, here applied to slingshot lineage-membership weights to detect differential fate selection between biological conditions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44823-0
skills.summary: A two-sample distributional test (as instantiated by condiments' fateSelectionTest) that assesses whether two multivariate or scalar distributions differ, here applied to slingshot lineage-membership weights to detect differential fate selection between biological conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The research question is whether the trajectory topology itself differs between conditions (Step 1) — use topologyTest instead. The question is differential progression along a common lineage (pseudotime distributions) — use progressionTest, not fateSelectionTest. The goal is gene-level differential expression along lineages (Step 3) — use conditionTest / fitGAM instead.

skills.description: Use when annotating t1 scRNA-seq cells against a t0 label set (via CASi's neural network) and you need to flag cells that may belong to newly emerged cell types rather than forcing known labels.
skills.name: two-sample-t-test-cell-correlation-testing
skills.search_text: two-sample-t-test-cell-correlation-testing Use when annotating t1 scRNA-seq cells against a t0 label set (via CASi's neural network) and you need to flag cells that may belong to newly emerged cell types rather than forcing known labels. The novel cell type is transcriptomically similar to a known cell type — the paper states the framework may not work well in this case. You only have a single timepoint with no annotated t0 reference to correlate against — the t-test operates on correlations to known-type mean UMAP vectors. You need unsupervised discovery of all cell types rather than screening for novel cells among already-annotated t1 labels — use unsupervised clustering pipelines (e.g. Seurat, scran) instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 CASi's novel-cell detection procedure: within each annotated cell type at a later timepoint, cells are Pearson-correlated to the mean UMAP vector of their assigned known type, iteratively bisected by Louvain clustering, and a two-sample t-test plus cutoffs (corr.cutoff = 0.4, p.cutoff = 0.01) flags the low-correlation cluster as potentially novel cell type members. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-58566-x
skills.summary: CASi's novel-cell detection procedure: within each annotated cell type at a later timepoint, cells are Pearson-correlated to the mean UMAP vector of their assigned known type, iteratively bisected by Louvain clustering, and a two-sample t-test plus cutoffs (corr.cutoff = 0.4, p.cutoff = 0.01) flags the low-correlation cluster as potentially novel cell type members.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The novel cell type is transcriptomically similar to a known cell type — the paper states the framework may not work well in this case. You only have a single timepoint with no annotated t0 reference to correlate against — the t-test operates on correlations to known-type mean UMAP vectors. You need unsupervised discovery of all cell types rather than screening for novel cells among already-annotated t1 labels — use unsupervised clustering pipelines (e.g. Seurat, scran) instead.

skills.description: Use when transforming a filtered, non-negative single-cell representation (e.g., from the non-negative kernel autoencoder) into a low-dimensional compressed latent embedding for downstream clustering, visualization, classification, or pseudo-time inference.
skills.name: two-stage-adamw-warmup-training
skills.search_text: two-stage-adamw-warmup-training Use when transforming a filtered, non-negative single-cell representation (e.g., from the non-negative kernel autoencoder) into a low-dimensional compressed latent embedding for downstream clustering, visualization, classification, or pseudo-time inference. Input is raw scRNA-seq counts that have not been filtered and converted to a non-negative, part-based representation by the first scDHA module The goal is only clustering or visualization from an existing reduced representation — call the higher-level scDHA, scDHA.vis, or scDHA.pt functions instead of re-training the second module http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Trains the Stacked Bayesian Self-learning Network (the second scDHA module) with a two-stage AdamW schedule: a warm-up phase emphasizing reconstruction loss, followed by a phase adding the KL-divergence loss, while repeatedly perturbing the 15-dimensional latent space to reduce overfitting. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21312-2
skills.summary: Trains the Stacked Bayesian Self-learning Network (the second scDHA module) with a two-stage AdamW schedule: a warm-up phase emphasizing reconstruction loss, followed by a phase adding the KL-divergence loss, while repeatedly perturbing the 15-dimensional latent space to reduce overfitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw scRNA-seq counts that have not been filtered and converted to a non-negative, part-based representation by the first scDHA module The goal is only clustering or visualization from an existing reduced representation — call the higher-level scDHA, scDHA.vis, or scDHA.pt functions instead of re-training the second module

skills.description: Use when building or retraining a CausalGAN-style simulator for scRNA-seq where a masked causal controller must first be pretrained as a non-conditional WGAN-GP generator before the GRN-structured model is trained end-to-end.
skills.name: two-stage-gan-pretraining-procedure
skills.search_text: two-stage-gan-pretraining-procedure Use when building or retraining a CausalGAN-style simulator for scRNA-seq where a masked causal controller must first be pretrained as a non-conditional WGAN-GP generator before the GRN-structured model is trained end-to-end. You need a predictive model for an existing trained checkpoint on a new dataset - GRouNdGAN is generative, not predictive, and must be retrained for a new dataset Your GRN is multi-layer or includes TF-gene-phenotype edges - the current version only supports imposing a bipartite GRN You need unnormalized count output - the model only generates library-size normalized expression values http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A two-stage training scheme in which GRouNdGAN first pretrains a causal controller as a non-conditional scRNA-seq GAN (WGAN-GP generator), then trains the full causal GAN (target generators, critic, labeler/anti-labeler) so that a user-defined causal GRN governs TF-gene relationships in simulated scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48516-6
skills.summary: A two-stage training scheme in which GRouNdGAN first pretrains a causal controller as a non-conditional scRNA-seq GAN (WGAN-GP generator), then trains the full causal GAN (target generators, critic, labeler/anti-labeler) so that a user-defined causal GRN governs TF-gene relationships in simulated scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a predictive model for an existing trained checkpoint on a new dataset - GRouNdGAN is generative, not predictive, and must be retrained for a new dataset Your GRN is multi-layer or includes TF-gene-phenotype edges - the current version only supports imposing a bipartite GRN You need unnormalized count output - the model only generates library-size normalized expression values

skills.description: Use when deconvolving bulk RNA-seq from tissues containing closely related cell types whose expression collinearity breaks single-stage NNLS deconvolution, and a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference is available.
skills.name: two-stage-recursive-cell-type-estimation
skills.search_text: two-stage-recursive-cell-type-estimation Use when deconvolving bulk RNA-seq from tissues containing closely related cell types whose expression collinearity breaks single-stage NNLS deconvolution, and a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference is available. Single-cell proportions themselves are the target — scRNA-seq data do not reflect true cell type proportions in intact tissues due to biased cell dissociation Input bulk data are TPM-normalized — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input; use read counts (RPKM only with cell type-specific total RNA abundance estimates) Bulk samples come from multiple clinical conditions mismatched to the reference — use MuSiC2's iterative algorithm instead of the two-stage recursive procedure http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 MuSiC's tree-guided recursive procedure for estimating proportions of closely related cell types: hierarchical clustering groups similar cell types, cluster proportions are estimated in stage 1, and within-cluster cell type proportions are recovered in stage 2 via constrained W-NNLS. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-08023-x
skills.summary: MuSiC's tree-guided recursive procedure for estimating proportions of closely related cell types: hierarchical clustering groups similar cell types, cluster proportions are estimated in stage 1, and within-cluster cell type proportions are recovered in stage 2 via constrained W-NNLS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-cell proportions themselves are the target — scRNA-seq data do not reflect true cell type proportions in intact tissues due to biased cell dissociation Input bulk data are TPM-normalized — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input; use read counts (RPKM only with cell type-specific total RNA abundance estimates) Bulk samples come from multiple clinical conditions mismatched to the reference — use MuSiC2's iterative algorithm instead of the two-stage recursive procedure

skills.description: Use when validating a differential topology/proportion test on multi-sample scRNA-seq data: simulated perturbations (e.g., removing myeloid cells from 0–80% of samples' cells) must show controlled type I error at 0% and monotonically increasing power.
skills.name: type-i-error-and-power-assessment
skills.search_text: type-i-error-and-power-assessment Use when validating a differential topology/proportion test on multi-sample scRNA-seq data: simulated perturbations (e.g., removing myeloid cells from 0–80% of samples' cells) must show controlled type I error at 0% and monotonically increasing power. When the goal is testing for differential gene expression (TDE) or cell density (TCD/XCD) changes rather than trajectory topology/branch proportion changes — the topology simulations use branchPropTest specifically When samples are not replicated (e.g., one sample per condition), since Lamian's type I error control relies on accounting for cross-sample variability, which single-sample designs cannot support When the input data has not been quality-filtered (e.g., HCA-BM cells with <5000 reads, <1000 expressed genes, or >10% mitochondrial reads), since low-quality cells distort branch proportions and bootstrap detection rates http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A simulation-based validation skill that assesses whether Lamian's differential topology tests control the type I error rate under no difference (0% cell removal) and gain statistical power as the true difference (myeloid cell removal percentage) increases, using the 8-sample HCA-BM scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-42841-y
skills.summary: A simulation-based validation skill that assesses whether Lamian's differential topology tests control the type I error rate under no difference (0% cell removal) and gain statistical power as the true difference (myeloid cell removal percentage) increases, using the 8-sample HCA-BM scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is testing for differential gene expression (TDE) or cell density (TCD/XCD) changes rather than trajectory topology/branch proportion changes — the topology simulations use branchPropTest specifically When samples are not replicated (e.g., one sample per condition), since Lamian's type I error control relies on accounting for cross-sample variability, which single-sample designs cannot support When the input data has not been quality-filtered (e.g., HCA-BM cells with <5000 reads, <1000 expressed genes, or >10% mitochondrial reads), since low-quality cells distort branch proportions and bootstrap detection rates

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a statistical method on null/permuted data and you need to verify that its p-values are Uniform(0,1)-calibrated rather than inflated (false positives) or deflated (lost power).
skills.name: type-i-error-qq-plot-calibration-assessment
skills.search_text: type-i-error-qq-plot-calibration-assessment Use when benchmarking a statistical method on null/permuted data and you need to verify that its p-values are Uniform(0,1)-calibrated rather than inflated (false positives) or deflated (lost power). The data are real (non-null) biological samples with genuine co-expression — type-I error at a nominal threshold cannot be judged without a known null You need to assess estimation bias of co-expression values rather than p-value calibration — use the mean-expression binning bias curves of Fig. 1a instead The method outputs only correlation/co-expression estimates without p-values or a test of independence — there is nothing to Q-Q against the uniform null http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Assesses whether a co-expression inference method's p-values are well-calibrated on permuted null scRNA-seq data by aggregating p-values, applying Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and drawing Q-Q plots against Uniform(0,1) to quantify type-I error at the 0.05 threshold. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40503-7
skills.summary: Assesses whether a co-expression inference method's p-values are well-calibrated on permuted null scRNA-seq data by aggregating p-values, applying Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and drawing Q-Q plots against Uniform(0,1) to quantify type-I error at the 0.05 threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are real (non-null) biological samples with genuine co-expression — type-I error at a nominal threshold cannot be judged without a known null You need to assess estimation bias of co-expression values rather than p-value calibration — use the mean-expression binning bias curves of Fig. 1a instead The method outputs only correlation/co-expression estimates without p-values or a test of independence — there is nothing to Q-Q against the uniform null

skills.description: Use when whole-blood transcript levels (e.g. MCEMP1, HLA-DRA, ETS1) must be correlated sample-wise with clinical severity predictors — CRP, lymphocyte counts or the 28-gene type I IFN score — in the Ong et al. COVID-19 cohort.
skills.name: type-i-ifn-score-interpretation
skills.search_text: type-i-ifn-score-interpretation Use when whole-blood transcript levels (e.g. MCEMP1, HLA-DRA, ETS1) must be correlated sample-wise with clinical severity predictors — CRP, lymphocyte counts or the 28-gene type I IFN score — in the Ong et al. COVID-19 cohort. The goal is differential expression between severe and mild patients across the 7 cross-sectional datasets (Fong, Bibert, McClain, Overmyer, Arunachalam, Carapito, Zhang) — use the repository's counts/anova box-and-strip workflow instead of this correlation analysis No matched CRP, lymphocyte-count or type I IFN-score measurements are available for the transcript samples, so sample-wise Pearson correlation cannot be computed The analysis requires non-linear or partial (confounder-adjusted) associations rather than two-sided Pearson correlation of raw values http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Interprets whole-blood expression of the COVID-19 severity genes MCEMP1, HLA-DRA and ETS1 by quantifying their Pearson correlations with the 28-gene type I IFN score, CRP levels and lymphocyte counts in the longitudinal Ong et al. 2021 cohort, reproducing the association directions reported in Fig. 2 of Chan et al. 2023. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ebiom.2023.104472
skills.summary: Interprets whole-blood expression of the COVID-19 severity genes MCEMP1, HLA-DRA and ETS1 by quantifying their Pearson correlations with the 28-gene type I IFN score, CRP levels and lymphocyte counts in the longitudinal Ong et al. 2021 cohort, reproducing the association directions reported in Fig. 2 of Chan et al. 2023.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is differential expression between severe and mild patients across the 7 cross-sectional datasets (Fong, Bibert, McClain, Overmyer, Arunachalam, Carapito, Zhang) — use the repository's counts/anova box-and-strip workflow instead of this correlation analysis No matched CRP, lymphocyte-count or type I IFN-score measurements are available for the transcript samples, so sample-wise Pearson correlation cannot be computed The analysis requires non-linear or partial (confounder-adjusted) associations rather than two-sided Pearson correlation of raw values

Input tissue labels are already standardized Uberon terms and no cross-source integration is needed The task is cell-type annotation of a count matrix with the built-in accordion() database rather than building or re-mapping the database itself The organism/tissue of interest is not covered by the Uberon release used by the Cell Marker Accordion (212 human tissues) http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Standardizes heterogeneous tissue labels from marker gene sources onto Uberon anatomy ontology terms (release 2024-09-03) so that markers from different databases can be integrated consistently by tissue in the Cell Marker Accordion database. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60900-4
skills.summary: Standardizes heterogeneous tissue labels from marker gene sources onto Uberon anatomy ontology terms (release 2024-09-03) so that markers from different databases can be integrated consistently by tissue in the Cell Marker Accordion database.

When no interpretable gene modules/factor gene sets exist (e.g., using purely embedding-based integration like Harmony or scVI without factor gene sets) When the goal is batch integration or clustering itself rather than interpretation — JOINTLY clustering with FindNeighbors/FindClusters (dims 1:15, res = 0.05) or ARI/NMI evaluation via aricode is the appropriate step http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Score every JOINTLY-derived interpretable gene module per single cell using AddModuleScore_UCell from the UCell package, enabling visualization of factor activity (e.g., factor_1_UCell) on UMAP embeddings and downstream cell-type specificity analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44279-8

skills.search_text: umap-2d-embedding-visualization Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has been reduced to a high-dimensional embedding (e.g. 40 PCA dimensions) and a 2D visualization is needed to inspect or display Leiden cluster structure, as done for the HuBMAP HBMP3-spleen-CC2 dataset. When the goal is the clustering itself — Cellar constructs the neighbors graph for Leiden clustering on the PCA embedding, not on the 2D UMAP projection When analyzing non-expression modalities that Cellar handles with other reductions, e.g. lymph node CODEX data which was 'reduced via UMAP with 10 dimensions' When the input data has not been filtered, CPM-normalized (total count 1e5), log1p-transformed, and scaled — the embedding is defined downstream of those preprocessing steps http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reduce high-dimensional single-cell embeddings (e.g. 40-dimension PCA of scRNA-seq data) to 2D with UMAP within the Cellar pipeline, producing a low-dimensional visualization that accompanies Leiden clustering of the cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29744-0

skills.search_text: umap-activity-colormap-visualization Use when scRNA-seq cells already have a UMAP embedding and per-cell activity scores from a PPIN (with or without negative-regulator edges) need to be visualized as a color scale and compared across cell-type populations. The input is raw (not normalized) single-cell expression data — the activity() call expects a normalized expression matrix No precomputed UMAP embedding exists for the cells and the goal is dimensionality reduction rather than activity visualization The biological process of interest has no corresponding PPIN edge list (neither bundled in ORIGINS2 nor buildable from a gene ID list via build_ppin with full_human_ppin) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Overlay per-cell PPIN activity scores (e.g., cell differentiation GO:0030154 computed with the ORIGINS2 activity() function) as color scales on a precomputed UMAP embedding of scRNA-seq cells, and compare probability densities of activity per cell type to assess how network composition changes the visualization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2023.102179

skills.description: Use when single-cell data (mass cytometry, scRNA-seq, or spatially reconstructed transcriptomics) have a priori class labels and you need to decide whether supervised LD axes separate labeled structure better than unsupervised UMAP/PCA/PHATE embeddings.
skills.name: umap-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: umap-benchmark-comparison Use when single-cell data (mass cytometry, scRNA-seq, or spatially reconstructed transcriptomics) have a priori class labels and you need to decide whether supervised LD axes separate labeled structure better than unsupervised UMAP/PCA/PHATE embeddings. Class labels are unknown, or an unbiased view of the data is preferable — the article explicitly states the supervised approach is inappropriate in these situations. No labeled classes exist to supervise LDA, so only UMAP/PCA/PHATE can be computed and no benchmark of supervised vs. unsupervised separation is possible. The biology of interest is non-linear or requires preserving local neighborhood structure — LDA maximizes class separability at the expense of local data structure. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Benchmark HSS-LDA (supervised linear discriminant axes) against unsupervised embeddings such as UMAP, PCA, and PHATE on the same single-cell data to assess whether a priori class labels (e.g., differentiation time points, spatial zones) are more coherently organized under supervised dimensionality reduction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100536
skills.summary: Benchmark HSS-LDA (supervised linear discriminant axes) against unsupervised embeddings such as UMAP, PCA, and PHATE on the same single-cell data to assess whether a priori class labels (e.g., differentiation time points, spatial zones) are more coherently organized under supervised dimensionality reduction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Class labels are unknown, or an unbiased view of the data is preferable — the article explicitly states the supervised approach is inappropriate in these situations. No labeled classes exist to supervise LDA, so only UMAP/PCA/PHATE can be computed and no benchmark of supervised vs. unsupervised separation is possible. The biology of interest is non-linear or requires preserving local neighborhood structure — LDA maximizes class separability at the expense of local data structure.

skills.search_text: umap-cell-embedding-visualization Use when a scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq dataset has already been quality-controlled and dimension-reduced (PCA or iterative LSI) and a 2D visualization of cells colored by Louvain/Seurat cluster identity is needed. skills.name: umap-cluster-label-propagation
skills.search_text: umap-cluster-label-propagation Use when a Seurat object has root-node hierarchical predictions from a pretrained Census model (or analogous classifier) and per-cell labels need smoothing/denoising before proceeding to the next node in the cell-type hierarchy. Input lacks a UMAP dimensionality reduction — the Seurat object must be processed through the standard Seurat pipeline (NormalizeData, ScaleData, FindVariableFeatures, RunPCA, RunUMAP) first Cell-type labels are already stable terminal classifications with no overlapping prediction contours — no further stabilization is needed Seurat version is not v4 — Census requires Seurat version 4 to run http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Census's label-stabilizing algorithm that refines per-cell cell-type predictions by propagating average labels within UMAP SNN clusters and resolving overlapping MASS-based prediction contours, iterating until convergence to counteract dataset noise and prediction error. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad714
skills.summary: Census's label-stabilizing algorithm that refines per-cell cell-type predictions by propagating average labels within UMAP SNN clusters and resolving overlapping MASS-based prediction contours, iterating until convergence to counteract dataset noise and prediction error.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks a UMAP dimensionality reduction — the Seurat object must be processed through the standard Seurat pipeline (NormalizeData, ScaleData, FindVariableFeatures, RunPCA, RunUMAP) first Cell-type labels are already stable terminal classifications with no overlapping prediction contours — no further stabilization is needed Seurat version is not v4 — Census requires Seurat version 4 to run

skills.name: umap-coordinate-mapping

skills.summary: Incorporates clonal barcode information into the dimensionality-reduction step prior to UMAP visualization via the Warp Factor parameter s (0–10), which warps each cell's principal component values toward the mean PC value of its clone cluster before running UMAP on the modified matrix.

skills.description: Use when running SCASL on single-cell SMART-seq junction/AS matrices and you need a 2D visualization of spectral-clustering results on the imputed AS probability matrix (dimension_reduction_method='umap' in configs/srr.yaml).
skills.name: umap-dimensionality-reduction-visualization
skills.search_text: umap-dimensionality-reduction-visualization Use when running SCASL on single-cell SMART-seq junction/AS matrices and you need a 2D visualization of spectral-clustering results on the imputed AS probability matrix (dimension_reduction_method='umap' in configs/srr.yaml). You only have a gene-expression matrix without junction reads — SCASL's AS-based UMAP requires junction-derived AS probability data, and gene-expression clustering will not resolve the same fine clusters. You need a deterministic, reproducible embedding — imputation, dimensionality reduction, and unsupervised clustering are stochastic, so run-to-run results differ. You need cell identities from splicing without any visualization — UMAP here is purely a 2D visualization layer; the clustering itself is spectral and does not depend on the UMAP output. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 Use UMAP (via the umap-learn package) inside the SCASL pipeline to embed and visualize single-cell alternative splicing clusters computed on the imputed AS probability matrix, producing cluster-colored 2D plots (cluster.png) that expose fine subpopulations such as the C3 vs C4 tumor-infiltrating Treg split. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46480-9
skills.summary: Use UMAP (via the umap-learn package) inside the SCASL pipeline to embed and visualize single-cell alternative splicing clusters computed on the imputed AS probability matrix, producing cluster-colored 2D plots (cluster.png) that expose fine subpopulations such as the C3 vs C4 tumor-infiltrating Treg split.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a gene-expression matrix without junction reads — SCASL's AS-based UMAP requires junction-derived AS probability data, and gene-expression clustering will not resolve the same fine clusters. You need a deterministic, reproducible embedding — imputation, dimensionality reduction, and unsupervised clustering are stochastic, so run-to-run results differ. You need cell identities from splicing without any visualization — UMAP here is purely a 2D visualization layer; the clustering itself is spectral and does not depend on the UMAP output.

skills.search_text: umap-embedding-evaluation Use when benchmarking how well cell-cell communication features (UMAP embeddings or tensor factor loadings) separate phenotypic contexts such as COVID-19 status and severity, using a supervised classifier's cross-validated AUC. Only a single sample/context is available — the benchmark's premise is separating information across multiple contexts, so embeddings from one context cannot be evaluated this way. Cell types are not shared across all samples — the COVID-19 and ASD tensors included only cell types shared across all samples, so classification features would be incomparable. skills.summary: Evaluates whether low-dimensional embeddings (e.g., CellChat's joint-manifold UMAP embeddings or Tensor-cell2cell factor loadings) capture biologically meaningful, context-specific information by training a Random-forest classifier to predict phenotype labels and comparing accuracy, runtime, and memory against competing representations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single sample/context is available — the benchmark's premise is separating information across multiple contexts, so embeddings from one context cannot be evaluated this way. skills.search_text: umap-embedding-overlay-visualization Use when per-cell scores (DA-seq differential abundance scores, cluster or severity annotations) need to be visualized in low-dimensional space on a UMAP built from scMerge2-adjusted single-cell expression data. The expression data have not been integrated across samples/conditions (batch variability will dominate the UMAP), so first apply scMerge2 integration Only embedding outputs (no adjusted expression matrix) are available and interpretable per-gene features are needed downstream — the article notes 'a low-dimensional representation does not naturally lend itself to the development of interpretable features' Overlays per-cell quantitative scores (e.g., DA-seq differential abundance scores) onto a UMAP embedding computed from the scMerge2-adjusted single-cell expression matrix, enabling visual localization of severity-associated cell states in the COVID-19 atlas. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39923-2
skills.summary: Overlays per-cell quantitative scores (e.g., DA-seq differential abundance scores) onto a UMAP embedding computed from the scMerge2-adjusted single-cell expression matrix, enabling visual localization of severity-associated cell states in the COVID-19 atlas.

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether cell-type annotations from an embedding-dependent annotation method (e.g. Census, whose label-stabilizing step uses UMAP clusters and prediction contours) remain stable across UMAP hyperparameter variations like n.neighbors and min.dist.
skills.name: umap-embedding-parameter-sensitivity-analysis
skills.search_text: umap-embedding-parameter-sensitivity-analysis Use when evaluating whether cell-type annotations from an embedding-dependent annotation method (e.g. Census, whose label-stabilizing step uses UMAP clusters and prediction contours) remain stable across UMAP hyperparameter variations like n.neighbors and min.dist. The cell-type annotation method under test is not embedding-dependent (e.g. purely transcriptome-based classifiers), so UMAP hyperparameters cannot plausibly affect its output. The dataset lacks reference cell-type labels, making per-cell-type F1 score computation against ground truth impossible. The goal is to tune UMAP parameters for optimal visualization rather than to assess annotation robustness across parameters. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Tests whether Census cell-type annotations are robust to UMAP embedding choices by re-annotating a scRNA-seq dataset across a grid of n.neighbors and min.dist settings and statistically comparing per-cell-type F1 scores with Kruskal-Wallis tests. This directly probes the sensitivity of Census's label-stabilizing algorithm, which depends on UMAP-space clusters and prediction contours. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad714
skills.summary: Tests whether Census cell-type annotations are robust to UMAP embedding choices by re-annotating a scRNA-seq dataset across a grid of n.neighbors and min.dist settings and statistically comparing per-cell-type F1 scores with Kruskal-Wallis tests. This directly probes the sensitivity of Census's label-stabilizing algorithm, which depends on UMAP-space clusters and prediction contours.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cell-type annotation method under test is not embedding-dependent (e.g. purely transcriptome-based classifiers), so UMAP hyperparameters cannot plausibly affect its output. The dataset lacks reference cell-type labels, making per-cell-type F1 score computation against ground truth impossible. The goal is to tune UMAP parameters for optimal visualization rather than to assess annotation robustness across parameters.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking UMI deduplication or read-level count-recovery tools against a ground-truth gene-by-cell UMI matrix and you need a cell-position-level accuracy metric (mean Euclidean UMAP distance per tool) rather than only correlation statistics.
skills.name: umap-embedding-projection-and-distance-computation
skills.search_text: umap-embedding-projection-and-distance-computation Use when benchmarking UMI deduplication or read-level count-recovery tools against a ground-truth gene-by-cell UMI matrix and you need a cell-position-level accuracy metric (mean Euclidean UMAP distance per tool) rather than only correlation statistics. The input is raw synthetic or real sequencing reads rather than already-deduplicated gene-by-cell count matrices — deduplication (UMI-tools/STARsolo/cellranger) must happen first The tool under test studies isoforms or alternative splicing — the scReadSim authors do not recommend their ground truths for that purpose (gene-level UMI ground truths only) You need an embedding metric where cells unseen by all tools can be compared — comparisons are restricted to the common cells shared across all tools A benchmark-accuracy skill from the scReadSim UMI-deduplication study (Fig. 4d): fit a UMAP embedding on the ground-truth UMI count matrix (after log-transformation and top-30-PC PCA), project each tool's deduplicated matrix onto that fixed embedding via the R umap package's predict() function, and score each tool by mean Euclidean distance between projected and ground-truth cell positions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43162-w
skills.summary: A benchmark-accuracy skill from the scReadSim UMI-deduplication study (Fig. 4d): fit a UMAP embedding on the ground-truth UMI count matrix (after log-transformation and top-30-PC PCA), project each tool's deduplicated matrix onto that fixed embedding via the R umap package's predict() function, and score each tool by mean Euclidean distance between projected and ground-truth cell positions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw synthetic or real sequencing reads rather than already-deduplicated gene-by-cell count matrices — deduplication (UMI-tools/STARsolo/cellranger) must happen first The tool under test studies isoforms or alternative splicing — the scReadSim authors do not recommend their ground truths for that purpose (gene-level UMI ground truths only) You need an embedding metric where cells unseen by all tools can be compared — comparisons are restricted to the common cells shared across all tools

skills.search_text: umap-embedding-visualization Use when a trained autoBioSeqpy/Keras model (tmpMod., tmpWeight.bin, parameters.txt) must be validated or diagnosed by visualizing its hidden-layer activations as a 2D UMAP scatter plot colored by class labels. Input is bulk RNA-seq or a processed differential-expression table (e.g., the counts/anova files from the COVID19-severity repo) rather than per-cell single-cell data Data have not been batch-corrected (Harmony) and PCA-embedded, since UMAP on uncorrected counts will mix severe/mild batch effects into the layout The goal is only to query gene expression statistics between severe and mild patients via the Streamlit box/strip plots, not to localize expression to cell subsets http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Embeds Harmony-integrated single-cell PBMC data in 2D with UMAP so cell-type clusters (e.g., CD14+ monocytes) can be annotated from canonical marker expression and gene-level dysregulation (MCEMP1, HLA-DRA, ETS1) can be visualized as violin plots per cluster. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ebiom.2023.104472

skills.search_text: umap-embedding-visualization Use when you have a learned low-dimensional joint embedding (e.g. scConfluence latent space in MuData obsm) and need a 2D visualization to inspect cell-type organization, subclusters, or modality alignment. When the embedding is derived from paired data with ground-truth correspondences where quantitative alignment metrics like FOSCTTM are more appropriate than qualitative UMAP inspection When the input is raw high-dimensional counts rather than a reduced latent representation — dimensionality reduction (e.g. scConfluence's uncoupled autoencoders with latent dimension 16) must precede the neighbor graph http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compute a neighbor graph on inferred shared latent embeddings (e.g. scConfluence's mdata.obsm['latent']) and embed with UMAP to visualize joint cell structure across modalities, coloring by cell type, cluster, modality, or gene expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51382-x
skills.summary: Compute a neighbor graph on inferred shared latent embeddings (e.g. scConfluence's mdata.obsm['latent']) and embed with UMAP to visualize joint cell structure across modalities, coloring by cell type, cluster, modality, or gene expression.

skills.description: Use when a fitted GEDI model's integrated cell space or sample-specific manifold parameters need a 2D UMAP visualization annotated by donor, technology, sample, or cell type.
skills.name: umap-embedding-visualization
skills.search_text: umap-embedding-visualization Use when a fitted GEDI model's integrated cell space or sample-specific manifold parameters need a 2D UMAP visualization annotated by donor, technology, sample, or cell type. The input is raw counts or a SingleCellExperiment without a fitted GEDI model — GEDI must be fit first and the integrated/manifold space recovered (svd.gedi or Qi) before UMAP is meaningful. The goal is producing the integration_benchmark_scores.csv quantitative ranking (Luecken-style batch-removal and cell-type-conservation metrics) — UMAP here is a qualitative visualization step, not the scored output. Embeds GEDI-derived latent spaces — either the recovered integrated cell embedding (svd_res$v %*% diag(svd_res$d)) or the top-20 most variable sample-specific manifold parameters (Qi) after PCA rotation — into 2D with uwot::umap (min_dist = 0.01, euclidean metric) and visualizes them with GEDI::plot_embedding colored by donor, technology, sample, or cell type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50963-0
skills.summary: Embeds GEDI-derived latent spaces — either the recovered integrated cell embedding (svd_res$v %*% diag(svd_res$d)) or the top-20 most variable sample-specific manifold parameters (Qi) after PCA rotation — into 2D with uwot::umap (min_dist = 0.01, euclidean metric) and visualizes them with GEDI::plot_embedding colored by donor, technology, sample, or cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw counts or a SingleCellExperiment without a fitted GEDI model — GEDI must be fit first and the integrated/manifold space recovered (svd.gedi or Qi) before UMAP is meaningful. skills.description: Use when you have an integrated or batch-adjusted single-cell expression matrix (scRNA-seq or CyTOF) and need to visually verify that datasets are mixed within shared cell types and that cell-type-specific populations are preserved.
skills.name: umap-embedding-visualization-of-integrated-data
skills.search_text: umap-embedding-visualization-of-integrated-data Use when you have an integrated or batch-adjusted single-cell expression matrix (scRNA-seq or CyTOF) and need to visually verify that datasets are mixed within shared cell types and that cell-type-specific populations are preserved. The expression data are raw/unintegrated — the UMAP is used here specifically to evaluate post-integration dataset mixing, though a raw-data UMAP can serve as the pre-integration comparison. Only an embedding output is available and you need interpretable downstream features such as cell–cell interactions or pathway information — the article notes a low-dimensional representation 'does not naturally lend itself to the development of interpretable features'. The goal is quantitative batch-removal benchmarking against other methods rather than qualitative visual inspection of one integration. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Compute a joint UMAP embedding on scMerge2-adjusted single-cell expression matrices (e.g. the 11M+ cell COMBAT and Geanon CyTOF datasets) and render it colored by dataset and unified cell type to visually confirm batch/dataset-effect removal while retaining biologically distinct populations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39923-2
skills.summary: Compute a joint UMAP embedding on scMerge2-adjusted single-cell expression matrices (e.g. the 11M+ cell COMBAT and Geanon CyTOF datasets) and render it colored by dataset and unified cell type to visually confirm batch/dataset-effect removal while retaining biologically distinct populations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression data are raw/unintegrated — the UMAP is used here specifically to evaluate post-integration dataset mixing, though a raw-data UMAP can serve as the pre-integration comparison. Only an embedding output is available and you need interpretable downstream features such as cell–cell interactions or pathway information — the article notes a low-dimensional representation 'does not naturally lend itself to the development of interpretable features'. The goal is quantitative batch-removal benchmarking against other methods rather than qualitative visual inspection of one integration.

skills.description: Use when 2D UMAP visualizations of deep-learning (e.g. RFCN) hidden-layer representations of scRNA-seq cells look unstable or poorly separated and you need to determine whether n_neighbors or min_dist drives the clustering before trusting the embedding.
skills.name: umap-hyperparameter-grid-search
skills.search_text: umap-hyperparameter-grid-search Use when 2D UMAP visualizations of deep-learning (e.g. RFCN) hidden-layer representations of scRNA-seq cells look unstable or poorly separated and you need to determine whether n_neighbors or min_dist drives the clustering before trusting the embedding. The model's hidden outputs live in a branch of the built network — layerUMAP cannot capture branched-layer outputs automatically; capture them manually via Jupyter Notebook instead. You need quantitative clustering metrics rather than visual separation assessment — the skill's validation criterion is the visual, min_dist-dependent change in cell-population separation, not a numeric score. The input is raw sequence/expression data rather than extracted hidden-layer representations — run autoBioSeqpy training/feature extraction first (running.py) before any UMAP visualization. http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 A sensitivity-analysis skill that exhaustively sweeps UMAP embedding parameters (n_neighbors and min_dist) over 126 combinations using the layerUMAP grid-search command to assess how each parameter changes the visual separation of cell populations in learned RFCN representations, as demonstrated on the Zheng sorted scRNA-seq dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105530
skills.summary: A sensitivity-analysis skill that exhaustively sweeps UMAP embedding parameters (n_neighbors and min_dist) over 126 combinations using the layerUMAP grid-search command to assess how each parameter changes the visual separation of cell populations in learned RFCN representations, as demonstrated on the Zheng sorted scRNA-seq dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model's hidden outputs live in a branch of the built network — layerUMAP cannot capture branched-layer outputs automatically; capture them manually via Jupyter Notebook instead. You need quantitative clustering metrics rather than visual separation assessment — the skill's validation criterion is the visual, min_dist-dependent change in cell-population separation, not a numeric score. The input is raw sequence/expression data rather than extracted hidden-layer representations — run autoBioSeqpy training/feature extraction first (running.py) before any UMAP visualization.

skills.description: Use when a Seurat scRNA-seq or CyTOF object needs UMAP visualization and the analyst must choose min.dist and n.neighbors objectively rather than by default, e.g. when 2D cluster layout trustworthiness is in question.
skills.name: umap-hyperparameter-grid-search
skills.search_text: umap-hyperparameter-grid-search Use when a Seurat scRNA-seq or CyTOF object needs UMAP visualization and the analyst must choose min.dist and n.neighbors objectively rather than by default, e.g. when 2D cluster layout trustworthiness is in question. When you need a clustering or trajectory result rather than a 2D visualization — scDEED optimizes the 2D embedding only and cannot guarantee that embeddings preserve inter-cluster distances When the number of dubious embeddings shows a complex non-monotonic trend as a hyperparameter increases — the authors advise caution, as cells may have complex topology and another embedding method may be preferable When the input is not a Seurat object or the desired dimension reduction is not t-SNE/UMAP without additional adaptation work http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Grid-search UMAP hyperparameters (min.dist, n.neighbors) using the scDEED R package, which classifies each cell embedding as dubious, trustworthy, or intermediate by comparing 2D-embedding neighbors with pre-embedding (PCA) neighbors, and selects the settings that minimize the number of dubious cell embeddings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45891-y
skills.summary: Grid-search UMAP hyperparameters (min.dist, n.neighbors) using the scDEED R package, which classifies each cell embedding as dubious, trustworthy, or intermediate by comparing 2D-embedding neighbors with pre-embedding (PCA) neighbors, and selects the settings that minimize the number of dubious cell embeddings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need a clustering or trajectory result rather than a 2D visualization — scDEED optimizes the 2D embedding only and cannot guarantee that embeddings preserve inter-cluster distances When the number of dubious embeddings shows a complex non-monotonic trend as a hyperparameter increases — the authors advise caution, as cells may have complex topology and another embedding method may be preferable When the input is not a Seurat object or the desired dimension reduction is not t-SNE/UMAP without additional adaptation work

skills.description: Use when you have raw and scMerge2-adjusted expression matrices from a multi-sample, multi-condition single-cell atlas (e.g. 20 COVID-19 studies, 1298 samples, 963 donors) and must demonstrate integration quality via UMAP embedding plots and technical-label PCA metrics.
skills.name: umap-integration-visualization
skills.search_text: umap-integration-visualization Use when you have raw and scMerge2-adjusted expression matrices from a multi-sample, multi-condition single-cell atlas (e.g. 20 COVID-19 studies, 1298 samples, 963 donors) and must demonstrate integration quality via UMAP embedding plots and technical-label PCA metrics. Data has not been integrated (no adjusted expression matrix) — UMAP on raw data will show technical separation and cannot serve as integration evidence Analysis goal is joint multi-modal integration — the paper notes integration was only performed within each modality and multi-modal incorporation is deferred to future work The embedding alone is the deliverable for interpretable downstream features — the article warns an embedding output by itself increases interpretability challenges for features like cell–cell interactions or pathway information http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Visualize atlas-scale scMerge2-integrated single-cell data by computing PCA scores on technical labels (dataset, protocol, technology) and generating UMAP integration plots, as done for the ~5M-cell COVID-19 PBMC collection in Fig. 3a-b, to confirm reduced technical variation with preserved biological cell-state separation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39923-2
skills.summary: Visualize atlas-scale scMerge2-integrated single-cell data by computing PCA scores on technical labels (dataset, protocol, technology) and generating UMAP integration plots, as done for the ~5M-cell COVID-19 PBMC collection in Fig. 3a-b, to confirm reduced technical variation with preserved biological cell-state separation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data has not been integrated (no adjusted expression matrix) — UMAP on raw data will show technical separation and cannot serve as integration evidence Analysis goal is joint multi-modal integration — the paper notes integration was only performed within each modality and multi-modal incorporation is deferred to future work The embedding alone is the deliverable for interpretable downstream features — the article warns an embedding output by itself increases interpretability challenges for features like cell–cell interactions or pathway information

skills.search_text: umap-visualization-of-da-scores Use when two processed single-cell datasets (e.g. early fetal liver eFL and fetal liver FL HSPC objects) have been integrated and annotated, and you need to identify and visualize which cell subpopulations are differentially abundant between them via DAseq scores on UMAP. When only a single dataset is available — DAseq comparison requires a pairwise objectA/objectB comparison of cell sets When the SingCellaR objects lack an integrated UMAP embedding or cell-type annotations, since DA scores must be projected onto the existing UMAP and interpreted per annotated subpopulation When the goal is differential gene expression rather than differential abundance of cell populations — use identifyDifferentialGenes directly instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Projects per-cell differential abundance (DAseq) log-fold-change scores onto a pre-computed UMAP embedding of integrated SingCellaR single-cell RNA-seq objects, and draws the DA UMAP with cell-type annotation labels so enriched subpopulations (e.g. erythroid in FL vs megakaryocytic in eFL HSPCs) are visually resolved. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101266
skills.summary: Projects per-cell differential abundance (DAseq) log-fold-change scores onto a pre-computed UMAP embedding of integrated SingCellaR single-cell RNA-seq objects, and draws the DA UMAP with cell-type annotation labels so enriched subpopulations (e.g. erythroid in FL vs megakaryocytic in eFL HSPCs) are visually resolved.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single dataset is available — DAseq comparison requires a pairwise objectA/objectB comparison of cell sets When the SingCellaR objects lack an integrated UMAP embedding or cell-type annotations, since DA scores must be projected onto the existing UMAP and interpreted per annotated subpopulation When the goal is differential gene expression rather than differential abundance of cell populations — use identifyDifferentialGenes directly instead

skills.search_text: umap-visualization-of-imputed-protein-abundance Use when scRNA-seq cells (e.g. van Galen AML or normal bone marrow) have had surface proteins imputed by cTP-net and you need a 2D embedding to order cells along a differentiation trajectory or annotate immunophenotype clusters. Expression input is not UMI-based counts (e.g. TPM or RPKM metrics) — prediction accuracy is unknown and cTP-net only applies to count-based UMI input Cells are outside the hematopoietic lineage — generalization of the immune-marker imputation to non-hematopoietic cells was not tested A CITE-seq/REAP-seq run already provides directly measured protein abundances, making imputation unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Builds a Seurat UMAP embedding from cTP-net-imputed surface protein levels (e.g. the 24-protein immunophenotype panel) so malignant AML cells can be placed along the myeloid differentiation trajectory (CD34+ -> CD38+CD123+ -> CD11c+/CD14+) and aberrant clusters such as the hyper-CD38 immunophenotype in AML707B can be annotated. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14391-0
