skills.description: Use when Nanopore long reads aligned with minimap2 yield spurious isoforms from wrongly mapped small internal exons (e.g., VPS28-201) or truncated ends, and read-level counts must be corrected within UMI clusters before isoform quantification.
skills.name: umi-based-misalignment-correction
skills.search_text: umi-based-misalignment-correction Use when Nanopore long reads aligned with minimap2 yield spurious isoforms from wrongly mapped small internal exons (e.g., VPS28-201) or truncated ends, and read-level counts must be corrected within UMI clusters before isoform quantification. Data are short reads or full-length Illumina-based single-cell data where UMI error rates do not require long-read consensus correction UMIs have not been recovered or are unreliable, since the correction depends on grouping PCR duplicates sharing the same UMI The goal is de novo isoform discovery where wrongly mapped small internal exons should be flagged rather than reassigned to annotated isoforms http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Longcell's UMI-cluster-based correction step that detects isoforms frequently co-occurring within the same UMI cluster, designates the lower-bulk-proportion isoform as misalignment (A_ii / sum_{i≠j} A_ij < 2), and reassigns or consensus-corrects those reads to fix mapping and truncation errors in Nanopore single-cell isoform quantification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60902-2
skills.summary: Longcell's UMI-cluster-based correction step that detects isoforms frequently co-occurring within the same UMI cluster, designates the lower-bulk-proportion isoform as misalignment (A_ii / sum_{i≠j} A_ij < 2), and reassigns or consensus-corrects those reads to fix mapping and truncation errors in Nanopore single-cell isoform quantification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are short reads or full-length Illumina-based single-cell data where UMI error rates do not require long-read consensus correction UMIs have not been recovered or are unreliable, since the correction depends on grouping PCR duplicates sharing the same UMI The goal is de novo isoform discovery where wrongly mapped small internal exons should be flagged rather than reassigned to annotated isoforms

skills.description: Use when calling SNVs from UMI-based scRNA-seq data (e.g. Cell Ranger-aligned 10x droplet data) to classify individual cells by genotype, quantify chimerism or multiplets, or need variant quality criteria tied to UMI/cell-barcode support rather than read depth alone.
skills.name: umi-based-variant-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: umi-based-variant-quality-filtering Use when calling SNVs from UMI-based scRNA-seq data (e.g. Cell Ranger-aligned 10x droplet data) to classify individual cells by genotype, quantify chimerism or multiplets, or need variant quality criteria tied to UMI/cell-barcode support rather than read depth alone. Input is already a variant VCF scored at read depth without UMI counts — UMI-level support filters cannot be applied retroactively. The goal is germline variant discovery from bulk exome/genome data; these thresholds are tuned for sparse single-cell 3' transcriptome coverage. Genotypes of the two cell populations are known and can be distinguished by expressed markers alone; SNV-based assignment adds value mainly for de novo chimerism without prior genotypes. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A filtering scheme for single nucleotide variants (SNVs) called from single-cell 3' UMI transcriptome data, in which variants called with Freebayes on the Cell Ranger/STAR genome BAM are retained only when backed by sufficient UMI counts and cell barcodes, then used for single-cell genotype/chimerism assignment. It enables de novo determination of cell origin from sequence variation without prior genotype knowledge. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: A filtering scheme for single nucleotide variants (SNVs) called from single-cell 3' UMI transcriptome data, in which variants called with Freebayes on the Cell Ranger/STAR genome BAM are retained only when backed by sufficient UMI counts and cell barcodes, then used for single-cell genotype/chimerism assignment. It enables de novo determination of cell origin from sequence variation without prior genotype knowledge.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a variant VCF scored at read depth without UMI counts — UMI-level support filters cannot be applied retroactively. The goal is germline variant discovery from bulk exome/genome data; these thresholds are tuned for sparse single-cell 3' transcriptome coverage. Genotypes of the two cell populations are known and can be distinguished by expressed markers alone; SNV-based assignment adds value mainly for de novo chimerism without prior genotypes.

skills.description: Use when single-cell CRISPR screen gRNA library BAM alignments must be deduplicated into per-UMI per-cell consensus gRNA sequences before variant calling, e.g. to reproduce the 28.4% mutant molecule fraction.
skills.name: umi-cell-barcode-consensus-generation
skills.search_text: umi-cell-barcode-consensus-generation Use when single-cell CRISPR screen gRNA library BAM alignments must be deduplicated into per-UMI per-cell consensus gRNA sequences before variant calling, e.g. to reproduce the 28.4% mutant molecule fraction. Input BAM has not been through utils.gRNA_bam_filter (secondary alignments and off-cassette reads still present) — run the filtration step first The goal is assigning gRNAs to cells (assign_gRNA.assign_gRNA_to_cell with min_umi=3) or detecting Cas9 editing effects — these are separate GiRAFR steps/modes Data are bulk or UMI-less; grouping by UMI + cell barcode combination requires droplet-based single-cell gRNA library reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 GiRAFR's Step-2 module that collapses the filtered gRNA BAM (gRNA.sorted.mapped.removedSecondaryAlignment.onlyMappedToGrnaChrom.bam) into one most-read-supported consensus sequence per UMI-cell barcode combination, discarding UMIs below min_reads so sequencing errors never enter downstream mutation calling. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05351-7
skills.summary: GiRAFR's Step-2 module that collapses the filtered gRNA BAM (gRNA.sorted.mapped.removedSecondaryAlignment.onlyMappedToGrnaChrom.bam) into one most-read-supported consensus sequence per UMI-cell barcode combination, discarding UMIs below min_reads so sequencing errors never enter downstream mutation calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input BAM has not been through utils.gRNA_bam_filter (secondary alignments and off-cassette reads still present) — run the filtration step first The goal is assigning gRNAs to cells (assign_gRNA.assign_gRNA_to_cell with min_umi=3) or detecting Cas9 editing effects — these are separate GiRAFR steps/modes Data are bulk or UMI-less; grouping by UMI + cell barcode combination requires droplet-based single-cell gRNA library reads

skills.description: Use when droplet-based 10x Genomics libraries from multiple samples were sequenced together on patterned flow-cell instruments (HiSeq 4000, HiSeq X, NovaSeq) and swapped molecules sharing UMI, cell barcode, and gene across samples must be removed.
skills.name: umi-cell-barcode-gene-combination-deduplication
skills.search_text: umi-cell-barcode-gene-combination-deduplication Use when droplet-based 10x Genomics libraries from multiple samples were sequenced together on patterned flow-cell instruments (HiSeq 4000, HiSeq X, NovaSeq) and swapped molecules sharing UMI, cell barcode, and gene across samples must be removed. Non-multiplexed samples sequenced on non-patterned instruments such as the HiSeq 2500, where the control expectation is a negligible removed fraction (below 0.0005%) Plate-based scRNA-seq data, where the article instead applies cell exclusion by removing all barcodes shared between samples rather than molecule-level exclusion Data lacking per-molecule UMI/cell-barcode/gene assignments (e.g. only aggregated count matrices without molecule information) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Excludes molecules that share the same combination of UMI, cell barcode, and aligned gene across multiplexed 10x Genomics samples, as implemented in DropletUtils, to remove artefactual barcode-swapped molecules from patterned flow-cell (HiSeq 4000) droplet scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05083-x
skills.summary: Excludes molecules that share the same combination of UMI, cell barcode, and aligned gene across multiplexed 10x Genomics samples, as implemented in DropletUtils, to remove artefactual barcode-swapped molecules from patterned flow-cell (HiSeq 4000) droplet scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Non-multiplexed samples sequenced on non-patterned instruments such as the HiSeq 2500, where the control expectation is a negligible removed fraction (below 0.0005%) Plate-based scRNA-seq data, where the article instead applies cell exclusion by removing all barcodes shared between samples rather than molecule-level exclusion Data lacking per-molecule UMI/cell-barcode/gene assignments (e.g. only aggregated count matrices without molecule information)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq UMI deduplication or read-level tools on 10X-style data and you need synthetic reads whose true UMI counts and cell barcodes are known (e.g. from a 10X BAM with CB/UMI structure).
skills.name: umi-cell-barcode-synthesis
skills.search_text: umi-cell-barcode-synthesis Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq UMI deduplication or read-level tools on 10X-style data and you need synthetic reads whose true UMI counts and cell barcodes are known (e.g. from a 10X BAM with CB/UMI structure). Benchmarking tools that need isoform-level ground truths (isoform abundance or alternative splicing events) — scReadSim provides gene-level UMI counts only Multi-sample or multi-condition studies requiring automatic simulation across samples — one BAM file per sample/condition must be supplied manually Data whose cells follow continuous trajectories or spatial locations, unless substituting scDesign3 as the count simulator http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generates synthetic read 1 sequences (a concatenated UMI and 10X-style cell barcode) plus a synthetic UMI-by-cell count matrix, using scDesign2 trained on real gene/inter-gene UMI count matrices so downstream UMI deduplication tools can be benchmarked against known ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43162-w
skills.summary: Generates synthetic read 1 sequences (a concatenated UMI and 10X-style cell barcode) plus a synthetic UMI-by-cell count matrix, using scDesign2 trained on real gene/inter-gene UMI count matrices so downstream UMI deduplication tools can be benchmarked against known ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Benchmarking tools that need isoform-level ground truths (isoform abundance or alternative splicing events) — scReadSim provides gene-level UMI counts only Multi-sample or multi-condition studies requiring automatic simulation across samples — one BAM file per sample/condition must be supplied manually Data whose cells follow continuous trajectories or spatial locations, unless substituting scDesign3 as the count simulator

skills.description: Use when processing molecule information files from multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet libraries sequenced on patterned flow-cell instruments (HiSeq 4000, HiSeq X, NovaSeq) where ~2.5% of reads may be mislabelled between samples via barcode swapping.
skills.name: umi-cellbarcode-gene-collision-resolution
skills.search_text: umi-cellbarcode-gene-collision-resolution Use when processing molecule information files from multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet libraries sequenced on patterned flow-cell instruments (HiSeq 4000, HiSeq X, NovaSeq) where ~2.5% of reads may be mislabelled between samples via barcode swapping. Libraries were sequenced on non-patterned-flowcell instruments such as the HiSeq 2500, where swapping is not elevated — the paper used HiSeq 2500 sequencing precisely as a negative control The goal is plate-based (Smart-seq2) scRNA-seq swapping quantification, which the paper handles with regression-based estimation rather than molecule exclusion A coarse cell-exclusion strategy is acceptable and discarding entire cell libraries sharing barcodes between samples is tolerable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A molecule-level collision resolution procedure (implemented as swappedDrops in DropletUtils) that detects barcode-swapped molecules in multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq data by grouping molecules sharing the same UMI, cell barcode, and aligned gene across samples, then reassigning or removing them based on a minimum read-fraction threshold. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05083-x
skills.summary: A molecule-level collision resolution procedure (implemented as swappedDrops in DropletUtils) that detects barcode-swapped molecules in multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq data by grouping molecules sharing the same UMI, cell barcode, and aligned gene across samples, then reassigning or removing them based on a minimum read-fraction threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Libraries were sequenced on non-patterned-flowcell instruments such as the HiSeq 2500, where swapping is not elevated — the paper used HiSeq 2500 sequencing precisely as a negative control The goal is plate-based (Smart-seq2) scRNA-seq swapping quantification, which the paper handles with regression-based estimation rather than molecule exclusion A coarse cell-exclusion strategy is acceptable and discarding entire cell libraries sharing barcodes between samples is tolerable

skills.description: Use when quantifying isoforms from single-cell or spatially barcoded Nanopore long reads with high per-base error (85-99%), where UMI scattering inflates UMI counts and fixed-edit-distance collapsing would overestimate expression.
skills.name: umi-cluster-size-scatter-reduction
skills.search_text: umi-cluster-size-scatter-reduction Use when quantifying isoforms from single-cell or spatially barcoded Nanopore long reads with high per-base error (85-99%), where UMI scattering inflates UMI counts and fixed-edit-distance collapsing would overestimate expression. Data with low sequencing error (e.g., short-read Illumina UMI data), where fixed-edit-distance UMI collapsing suffices and adaptive pruning could remove true small clusters Reads lacking recoverable cell barcodes/UMIs, since the pruning operates on per-isoform UMI cluster sizes within cells Already-deduplicated UMI count matrices, where no cluster-size distribution is available to prune http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Longcell's adaptive UMI-cluster pruning step: within each isoform in each cell, UMI clusters are ranked by size and the smallest clusters (e.g., singletons) are iteratively removed as error-driven scatter, because sequencing errors inflate UMI counts in Nanopore long-read quantification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60902-2
skills.summary: Longcell's adaptive UMI-cluster pruning step: within each isoform in each cell, UMI clusters are ranked by size and the smallest clusters (e.g., singletons) are iteratively removed as error-driven scatter, because sequencing errors inflate UMI counts in Nanopore long-read quantification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data with low sequencing error (e.g., short-read Illumina UMI data), where fixed-edit-distance UMI collapsing suffices and adaptive pruning could remove true small clusters Reads lacking recoverable cell barcodes/UMIs, since the pruning operates on per-isoform UMI cluster sizes within cells Already-deduplicated UMI count matrices, where no cluster-size distribution is available to prune

skills.description: Use when processing a single-cell CRISPR screen gRNA library BAM (mapped to the designed gRNA cassette reference) whose reads carry cell barcodes and UMIs, and you need per-UMI consensus sequences before calling mutations or assigning gRNAs to cells.
skills.name: umi-consensus-sequence-construction
skills.search_text: umi-consensus-sequence-construction Use when processing a single-cell CRISPR screen gRNA library BAM (mapped to the designed gRNA cassette reference) whose reads carry cell barcodes and UMIs, and you need per-UMI consensus sequences before calling mutations or assigning gRNAs to cells. The gRNA-to-cell annotation is already available from Cell Ranger feature barcoding and you only want intact-gRNA calls — this skill exists precisely because Cell Ranger misses mutant gRNAs. You are running GiRAFR's separate CRISPR-Cas9 editing-effect mode on transcriptome data, which does not use UMI consensus construction of the gRNA library. The input is raw unfiltered FASTQ or a BAM that still contains secondary alignments and reads not mapped to the designed gRNA cassette — run utils.gRNA_bam_filter first. GiRAFR pipeline step 2: build one consensus gRNA sequence per UMI–cell barcode combination from the filtered gRNA-library BAM, retaining only UMIs supported by at least min_reads reads, so that subsequent mutation calling operates on collapsed rather than raw reads. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05351-7
skills.summary: GiRAFR pipeline step 2: build one consensus gRNA sequence per UMI–cell barcode combination from the filtered gRNA-library BAM, retaining only UMIs supported by at least min_reads reads, so that subsequent mutation calling operates on collapsed rather than raw reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gRNA-to-cell annotation is already available from Cell Ranger feature barcoding and you only want intact-gRNA calls — this skill exists precisely because Cell Ranger misses mutant gRNAs. You are running GiRAFR's separate CRISPR-Cas9 editing-effect mode on transcriptome data, which does not use UMI consensus construction of the gRNA library. The input is raw unfiltered FASTQ or a BAM that still contains secondary alignments and reads not mapped to the designed gRNA cassette — run utils.gRNA_bam_filter first.

skills.description: Use when phase-annotated h5ad data (adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta'] from a DeepCycle run) is available and you need to verify that UMI counts per cell increase roughly 2-fold along the cell cycle prior to the mitotic drop.
skills.name: umi-count-aggregation-per-phase
skills.search_text: umi-count-aggregation-per-phase Use when phase-annotated h5ad data (adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta'] from a DeepCycle run) is available and you need to verify that UMI counts per cell increase roughly 2-fold along the cell cycle prior to the mitotic drop. The h5ad lacks a DeepCycle cell_cycle_theta annotation — the circular binning requires a continuous transcriptional phase; rerun DeepCycle first (e.g., with pp.moments from scVelo preprocessing). No cycling genes were found in the dataset — DeepCycle warns the results will not be reliable in this case, so UMI-vs-phase aggregation would be meaningless. The question is about gene-level cycling expression dynamics rather than bulk RNA content per cell; use the DeepCycle gene fitting workflow instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Quantifies total RNA content (UMI counts) per cell binned circularly by DeepCycle's cell_cycle_theta to test whether RNAs per cell approximately double (~2.0–2.1 fold change) across the transcriptional phase before mitosis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8
skills.summary: Quantifies total RNA content (UMI counts) per cell binned circularly by DeepCycle's cell_cycle_theta to test whether RNAs per cell approximately double (~2.0–2.1 fold change) across the transcriptional phase before mitosis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The h5ad lacks a DeepCycle cell_cycle_theta annotation — the circular binning requires a continuous transcriptional phase; rerun DeepCycle first (e.g., with pp.moments from scVelo preprocessing). No cycling genes were found in the dataset — DeepCycle warns the results will not be reliable in this case, so UMI-vs-phase aggregation would be meaningless. The question is about gene-level cycling expression dynamics rather than bulk RNA content per cell; use the DeepCycle gene fitting workflow instead.

skills.description: Use when recovering true UMIs from error-prone Nanopore single-cell long reads, or when testing whether a UMI collapsing strategy (e.g. DBSCAN at eps=2) inflates UMI counts at high PCR amplification.
skills.name: umi-count-inflation-benchmark-analysis
skills.search_text: umi-count-inflation-benchmark-analysis Use when recovering true UMIs from error-prone Nanopore single-cell long reads, or when testing whether a UMI collapsing strategy (e.g. DBSCAN at eps=2) inflates UMI counts at high PCR amplification. UMIs come from a short-read platform with per-base accuracy high enough that fixed-edit-distance collapsing (e.g. Sicelore2 or FLAMES style) does not inflate counts Ground truth is unknown and the goal is downstream isoform analysis (use Longcell's quantification pipeline functions like HighExprsGene or getIsoform instead of the benchmark) Input is already a cell-by-isoform expression matrix — this skill operates upstream at the UMI-recovery step http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark of Longcell's iterative UMI clustering within meta-isoform groups against fixed-edit-distance collapsing (DBSCAN, eps=2), quantifying how UMI-count estimates inflate under Nanopore sequencing error as PCR amplification increases from 2x to 50x. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60902-2
skills.summary: Benchmark of Longcell's iterative UMI clustering within meta-isoform groups against fixed-edit-distance collapsing (DBSCAN, eps=2), quantifying how UMI-count estimates inflate under Nanopore sequencing error as PCR amplification increases from 2x to 50x.
skills.when_to_use_negative: UMIs come from a short-read platform with per-base accuracy high enough that fixed-edit-distance collapsing (e.g. Sicelore2 or FLAMES style) does not inflate counts Ground truth is unknown and the goal is downstream isoform analysis (use Longcell's quantification pipeline functions like HighExprsGene or getIsoform instead of the benchmark) Input is already a cell-by-isoform expression matrix — this skill operates upstream at the UMI-recovery step

skills.description: Use when you have an scRNA-seq BAM file aligned to mm10, a gene annotation GTF (e.g., gencode.vM10.annotation.gtf), and a chromosome size file, and you need gene- and inter-gene-by-cell UMI count matrices as ground truth for simulation or benchmarking.
skills.name: umi-count-matrix-construction-from-bam
skills.search_text: umi-count-matrix-construction-from-bam Use when you have an scRNA-seq BAM file aligned to mm10, a gene annotation GTF (e.g., gencode.vM10.annotation.gtf), and a chromosome size file, and you need gene- and inter-gene-by-cell UMI count matrices as ground truth for simulation or benchmarking. Your goal is scATAC-seq feature/count construction — use Utility.scATAC_CreateFeatureSets and Utility.scATAC_bam2countmat instead, which work on peak/foreground regions rather than gene annotations. You only need synthetic reads without ground-truth counts — but note count matrices are the required intermediate for scDesign2 training, so they must be built anyway when simulating. The data are isoform-level or alternative-splicing studies — scReadSim provides gene-level UMI ground truths only. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Segment an scRNA-seq reference genome into genes (foreground) and inter-genes (background) from a BAM file plus GTF annotation, then summarize reads into gene-by-cell and inter-gene-by-cell UMI count matrices with scReadSim. These matrices are the ground-truth inputs for scDesign2-based synthetic count generation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43162-w
skills.summary: Segment an scRNA-seq reference genome into genes (foreground) and inter-genes (background) from a BAM file plus GTF annotation, then summarize reads into gene-by-cell and inter-gene-by-cell UMI count matrices with scReadSim. These matrices are the ground-truth inputs for scDesign2-based synthetic count generation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is scATAC-seq feature/count construction — use Utility.scATAC_CreateFeatureSets and Utility.scATAC_bam2countmat instead, which work on peak/foreground regions rather than gene annotations. You only need synthetic reads without ground-truth counts — but note count matrices are the required intermediate for scDesign2 training, so they must be built anyway when simulating. The data are isoform-level or alternative-splicing studies — scReadSim provides gene-level UMI ground truths only.

skills.description: Use when you have a cellranger count output folder for a 10x scRNAseq sample (e.g. HIV donor or SARS-CoV-2 airway data) and need pathogen UMI counts merged into features.tsv.gz/matrix.mtx.gz so Seurat or standard single-cell pipelines can analyze infected cells downstream.
skills.name: umi-count-matrix-integration-10x
skills.search_text: umi-count-matrix-integration-10x Use when you have a cellranger count output folder for a 10x scRNAseq sample (e.g. HIV donor or SARS-CoV-2 airway data) and need pathogen UMI counts merged into features.tsv.gz/matrix.mtx.gz so Seurat or standard single-cell pipelines can analyze infected cells downstream. skills.description: Use when a read-level analysis requires two or more sequential operations (e.g. selecting reads containing a variant, then demultiplexing cell barcodes) and the tools involved can read from stdin and write to stdout, so intermediate FASTQ files can be avoided.
skills.name: unix-pipe-chaining-of-bioinformatics-tools
skills.search_text: unix-pipe-chaining-of-bioinformatics-tools Use when a read-level analysis requires two or more sequential operations (e.g. selecting reads containing a variant, then demultiplexing cell barcodes) and the tools involved can read from stdin and write to stdout, so intermediate FASTQ files can be avoided. skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a label-transfer annotator handles truly unseen cell types: a cell type is deleted from the training reference and held-out query cells of that type should be reported as 'Unknown' instead of receiving a wrong label.
skills.name: unknown-label-abstention-benchmarking
skills.search_text: unknown-label-abstention-benchmarking Use when evaluating whether a label-transfer annotator handles truly unseen cell types: a cell type is deleted from the training reference and held-out query cells of that type should be reported as 'Unknown' instead of receiving a wrong label. All query cell types are represented in the training reference — abstention benchmarking is only meaningful for a deliberately deleted/unseen cell type. The query AnnData gene space or gene order differs from ref_adata.var_names and cannot be aligned — TOSICA requires identical, same-order var_names. The goal is absolute annotation accuracy on known labels rather than open-set recognition / 'Unknown' detection behavior. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark whether a supervised cell-type annotator can abstain with an 'Unknown' label when a high-abundance reference cell type (e.g., alpha cells in hPancreas) is deleted from training, rather than force-mislabeling held-out cells. In the TOSICA paper, removing alpha cells from the reference leads TOSICA to flag ~76% of held-out alpha cells as 'Unknown' while SingleR, SciBet, and ACTINN incorrectly assign 'PP', 'delta', or 'beta'. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-35923-4
skills.summary: Benchmark whether a supervised cell-type annotator can abstain with an 'Unknown' label when a high-abundance reference cell type (e.g., alpha cells in hPancreas) is deleted from training, rather than force-mislabeling held-out cells. skills.search_text: unmapped-read-extraction-from-aligned-rnaseq Use when you have TCGA (or similar) paired-end RNA-seq FASTQs that have been aligned to hg19, and you need the unaligned fraction as FASTQ input for alignment-free viral read detection. When the analysis target is the human (host) transcriptome itself — this step deliberately discards all reads aligned to hg19, so it is unsuitable for host expression or variant work When reads from non-human/non-viral organisms are expected — the viRNAtrap 48 bp model's predictions for such sequences are undefined per the article's stated scope When you need to keep paired mates in separate R1/R2 files — viRNAtrap would treat each mate file as a distinct sample, splitting the sample's downstream viral contig calls http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Prepares viRNAtrap input by extracting RNA-seq reads that fail to align to the human genome (hg19) and the phiX phage contaminant, writing them as *_unmapped.fastq files with paired-end mates concatenated per sample so each sample is a single input file. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36336-z
