skills.name: unshared-feature-augmentation-for-integration
skills.search_text: unshared-feature-augmentation-for-integration Use when integrating scRNA-seq count matrices from multiple species via BENGAL/LIGER UINMF and genes lacking annotated ENSEMBL homology should be retained as unshared features instead of being dropped. If the downstream integration method does not accept unshared features (e.g. standard LIGER iNMF, fastMNN, Harmony, SeuratV4, scVI/scANVI which rely only on shared homologous features) If the goal is strict orthology-based matching only — cross-species integration in this benchmark relies on curated sequence-based gene orthology, so sequence-similarity heuristics like SAMap are a different strategy If cell-type (rather than gene) correspondence is one-to-many or flat mappings are insufficient — the benchmark is limited to one-to-one cell type mappings http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Augments cross-species single-cell integration by appending each species' non-homologous (unshared) genes to the concatenated homologous feature matrix, enabling the LIGER UINMF integrative non-negative matrix factorization to use dataset-specific signals that one-to-one/one-to-many/many-to-many orthology mapping alone would discard. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41855-w
skills.summary: Augments cross-species single-cell integration by appending each species' non-homologous (unshared) genes to the concatenated homologous feature matrix, enabling the LIGER UINMF integrative non-negative matrix factorization to use dataset-specific signals that one-to-one/one-to-many/many-to-many orthology mapping alone would discard.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the downstream integration method does not accept unshared features (e.g. standard LIGER iNMF, fastMNN, Harmony, SeuratV4, scVI/scANVI which rely only on shared homologous features) If the goal is strict orthology-based matching only — cross-species integration in this benchmark relies on curated sequence-based gene orthology, so sequence-similarity heuristics like SAMap are a different strategy If cell-type (rather than gene) correspondence is one-to-many or flat mappings are insufficient — the benchmark is limited to one-to-one cell type mappings

skills.description: Use when loading a new scRNA-seq h5ad into TFvelo_run_demo.py and you need to measure zero-fraction in unspliced counts to justify applying a regulation-based (TF) velocity model instead of a splicing-based one.
skills.name: unspliced-count-sparsity-quantification
skills.search_text: unspliced-count-sparsity-quantification Use when loading a new scRNA-seq h5ad into TFvelo_run_demo.py and you need to measure zero-fraction in unspliced counts to justify applying a regulation-based (TF) velocity model instead of a splicing-based one. The dataset already has dense, well-populated unspliced counts where a splicing-based method like ScVelo's dynamical EM model will fit well The input lacks any unspliced/spliced layers and the goal is pure TF-weight analysis rather than quantifying splicing-count coverage You only need trajectory visualization (pseudotime/streamplot) from an already-fitted TFvelo.h5ad via TFvelo_analysis_demo.py http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies how sparse the unspliced count layer of a raw single-cell h5ad dataset is, as a pre-check during TFvelo's preprocess() step to determine whether splicing-based velocity (e.g., ScVelo dynamical modeling) is viable or a TF-regulation-based fit is needed. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45661-w
skills.summary: Quantifies how sparse the unspliced count layer of a raw single-cell h5ad dataset is, as a pre-check during TFvelo's preprocess() step to determine whether splicing-based velocity (e.g., ScVelo dynamical modeling) is viable or a TF-regulation-based fit is needed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset already has dense, well-populated unspliced counts where a splicing-based method like ScVelo's dynamical EM model will fit well The input lacks any unspliced/spliced layers and the goal is pure TF-weight analysis rather than quantifying splicing-count coverage You only need trajectory visualization (pseudotime/streamplot) from an already-fitted TFvelo.h5ad via TFvelo_analysis_demo.py

skills.description: Use when a velocyto/scVelo-processed scRNA-seq dataset (h5ad with Mu/Ms layers) shows cycling patterns in the unspliced-spliced space of GOterm cell_cycle genes and you need a continuous, circular cell cycle trajectory per cell.
skills.name: unspliced-spliced-dynamics-fitting
skills.search_text: unspliced-spliced-dynamics-fitting Use when a velocyto/scVelo-processed scRNA-seq dataset (h5ad with Mu/Ms layers) shows cycling patterns in the unspliced-spliced space of GOterm cell_cycle genes and you need a continuous, circular cell cycle trajectory per cell. scRNA-seq data lacking spliced/unspliced quantification (no velocyto/scVelo moments), since DeepCycle requires imputed Mu and Ms layers Datasets where no cycling genes are detected after the hotelling filter — README warns the results will not be reliable and deeper sequencing may be needed Assigning cell cycle phases based solely on gene markers in heterogeneous models, which the paper notes lacks generalizability across cellular models http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit circular unspliced-spliced (Mu/Ms) dynamics of cell cycle genes in scRNA-seq data using DeepCycle, a deep-learning method based on RNA velocity, to assign each cell a continuous transcriptional phase (cell_cycle_theta). Motivated by scVelo's dynamical model failing to fit single-gene cycling patterns. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8
skills.summary: Fit circular unspliced-spliced (Mu/Ms) dynamics of cell cycle genes in scRNA-seq data using DeepCycle, a deep-learning method based on RNA velocity, to assign each cell a continuous transcriptional phase (cell_cycle_theta). Motivated by scVelo's dynamical model failing to fit single-gene cycling patterns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: scRNA-seq data lacking spliced/unspliced quantification (no velocyto/scVelo moments), since DeepCycle requires imputed Mu and Ms layers Datasets where no cycling genes are detected after the hotelling filter — README warns the results will not be reliable and deeper sequencing may be needed Assigning cell cycle phases based solely on gene markers in heterogeneous models, which the paper notes lacks generalizability across cellular models

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data with spliced/unspliced layers (velocyto + scvelo.pp.moments) shows cycling patterns in unspliced-spliced space of cell-cycle genes and you need a high-resolution continuous cell cycle phase per cell.
skills.name: unspliced-spliced-gene-pattern-fitting
skills.search_text: unspliced-spliced-gene-pattern-fitting Use when scRNA-seq data with spliced/unspliced layers (velocyto + scvelo.pp.moments) shows cycling patterns in unspliced-spliced space of cell-cycle genes and you need a high-resolution continuous cell cycle phase per cell. When no cycling genes are found after running DeepCycle — the results will not be reliable, likely because sequencing depth (RNAs per cell) is insufficient When the input Anndata lacks spliced/unspliced layers or has not been preprocessed with scvelo.pp.moments When the goal is cell-cycle phase labeling based purely on gene marker expression — the paper notes marker-based phase definitions lack generalizability, whereas this skill relies on dynamical unspliced-spliced features http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Fits circular unspliced-spliced (Mu/Ms) expression patterns of cycling genes with DeepCycle, a TensorFlow autoencoder built on RNA velocity, to assign each cell a continuous cell-cycle angle (cell_cycle_theta) and build a high-resolution map of the cell cycle transcriptome. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8
skills.summary: Fits circular unspliced-spliced (Mu/Ms) expression patterns of cycling genes with DeepCycle, a TensorFlow autoencoder built on RNA velocity, to assign each cell a continuous cell-cycle angle (cell_cycle_theta) and build a high-resolution map of the cell cycle transcriptome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no cycling genes are found after running DeepCycle — the results will not be reliable, likely because sequencing depth (RNAs per cell) is insufficient When the input Anndata lacks spliced/unspliced layers or has not been preprocessed with scvelo.pp.moments When the goal is cell-cycle phase labeling based purely on gene marker expression — the paper notes marker-based phase definitions lack generalizability, whereas this skill relies on dynamical unspliced-spliced features

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data preprocessed with scvelo.pp.moments (Ms/Mu layers) should be assigned a continuous high-resolution cell-cycle phase per cell, and a cycling base gene (e.g. Nusap1 or MELK) is available for phase initialization.
skills.name: unspliced-spliced-phase-seeding
skills.search_text: unspliced-spliced-phase-seeding Use when scRNA-seq data preprocessed with scvelo.pp.moments (Ms/Mu layers) should be assigned a continuous high-resolution cell-cycle phase per cell, and a cycling base gene (e.g. Nusap1 or MELK) is available for phase initialization. When no cycling genes can be found (e.g. shallow sequencing with too few RNAs per cell) — the results will not be reliable When the dataset lacks unspliced/spliced read layers or has not been preprocessed with scvelo.pp.moments When the goal is discrete cell-cycle phase labeling from marker gene scores rather than a continuous circular transcriptional phase http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Seeds and infers a continuous circular transcriptional phase (theta) for each single cell by using the atan2 of z-scored spliced and unspliced reads of a cycling base gene as the initial condition for DeepCycle's autoencoder, then training the encoder and decoder to reconstruct the unspliced-spliced patterns of cell-cycle genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8
skills.summary: Seeds and infers a continuous circular transcriptional phase (theta) for each single cell by using the atan2 of z-scored spliced and unspliced reads of a cycling base gene as the initial condition for DeepCycle's autoencoder, then training the encoder and decoder to reconstruct the unspliced-spliced patterns of cell-cycle genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no cycling genes can be found (e.g. shallow sequencing with too few RNAs per cell) — the results will not be reliable When the dataset lacks unspliced/spliced read layers or has not been preprocessed with scvelo.pp.moments When the goal is discrete cell-cycle phase labeling from marker gene scores rather than a continuous circular transcriptional phase

skills.description: Use when a Scanpy AnnData object (.h5ad or in-memory) needs to be persisted as a queryable relational DuckDB database, including unstructured uns mappings that have no natural table form.
skills.name: unstructured-annotation-serialization
skills.search_text: unstructured-annotation-serialization Use when a Scanpy AnnData object (.h5ad or in-memory) needs to be persisted as a queryable relational DuckDB database, including unstructured uns mappings that have no natural table form. The dataset is small enough to hold in memory and only transient queries are needed — an in-memory AnnSQL(adata=adata) instance avoids building the on-disk table structure The input is not an AnnData object (e.g. raw FASTQ or a flat CSV matrix) — MakeDb/BuildDb expects AnnData slots (X, obs, var, obsm, varm, obsp, uns) to serialize A performance-optimized relational schema is required for heavy production workloads — the AnnSQL schema explicitly mirrors AnnData structure instead of optimizing for performance Serialize the full slot structure of a single-cell AnnData object — X expression matrix, obs/var metadata, obsm/varm/obsp mappings, and unstructured uns annotations — into an AnnSQL/DuckDB relational database (.asql) where each slot becomes an individual SQL table mirroring the AnnData object structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf105
skills.summary: Serialize the full slot structure of a single-cell AnnData object — X expression matrix, obs/var metadata, obsm/varm/obsp mappings, and unstructured uns annotations — into an AnnSQL/DuckDB relational database (.asql) where each slot becomes an individual SQL table mirroring the AnnData object structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small enough to hold in memory and only transient queries are needed — an in-memory AnnSQL(adata=adata) instance avoids building the on-disk table structure The input is not an AnnData object (e.g. raw FASTQ or a flat CSV matrix) — MakeDb/BuildDb expects AnnData slots (X, obs, var, obsm, varm, obsp, uns) to serialize A performance-optimized relational schema is required for heavy production workloads — the AnnSQL schema explicitly mirrors AnnData structure instead of optimizing for performance

skills.description: Use when clustering raw single-cell RNA-seq count data (genes x cells matrix) with unknown cell labels, or when benchmarking scDHA against SC3, SEURAT, SINCERA, CIDR, SCANPY, or k-means on datasets with known cell types using ARI.
skills.name: unsupervised-cell-clustering
skills.search_text: unsupervised-cell-clustering Use when clustering raw single-cell RNA-seq count data (genes x cells matrix) with unknown cell labels, or when benchmarking scDHA against SC3, SEURAT, SINCERA, CIDR, SCANPY, or k-means on datasets with known cell types using ARI. The task is supervised cell classification of new labeled data — scDHA.class, not the unsupervised clustering path, is the appropriate function The analysis goal is pseudo-time or trajectory inference — use scDHA.pt on the dimension-reduction output instead of the clustering output The input is already a low-dimensional embedding; re-running the non-negative kernel autoencoder for gene/component filtering is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Unsupervised cell segregation of scRNA-seq data by projecting the expression matrix through scDHA's two-module autoencoder (non-negative kernel autoencoder + stacked Bayesian autoencoder) and assigning clusters, benchmarked against SC3, Seurat, SINCERA, CIDR, Scanpy, and k-means using adjusted Rand index. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21312-2
skills.summary: Unsupervised cell segregation of scRNA-seq data by projecting the expression matrix through scDHA's two-module autoencoder (non-negative kernel autoencoder + stacked Bayesian autoencoder) and assigning clusters, benchmarked against SC3, Seurat, SINCERA, CIDR, Scanpy, and k-means using adjusted Rand index.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is supervised cell classification of new labeled data — scDHA.class, not the unsupervised clustering path, is the appropriate function The analysis goal is pseudo-time or trajectory inference — use scDHA.pt on the dimension-reduction output instead of the clustering output The input is already a low-dimensional embedding; re-running the non-negative kernel autoencoder for gene/component filtering is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when annotating clusters in a normalized/scaled scRNA-seq matrix (e.g., a Seurat object) without a labeled reference, and only a marker database plus the expression data are available.
skills.name: unsupervised-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: unsupervised-cell-type-annotation Use when annotating clusters in a normalized/scaled scRNA-seq matrix (e.g., a Seurat object) without a labeled reference, and only a marker database plus the expression data are available. Input requires distinguishing malignant from healthy cells — use ScType's single-cell SNV calling workflow (vartrix) rather than marker-based annotation alone A labeled reference scRNA-seq training dataset is available and a supervised classifier (e.g., CaSTLe, ACTINN) is preferred The comparator method cannot accept custom markers — as with scCATCH, whose implementation does not allow custom marker input http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Annotate cell clusters in a single scRNA-seq dataset using ScType, an unsupervised method that scores clusters against cell-type-specific positive and negative marker gene sets from the ScType marker database, without any reference dataset or manual marker curation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28803-w
skills.summary: Annotate cell clusters in a single scRNA-seq dataset using ScType, an unsupervised method that scores clusters against cell-type-specific positive and negative marker gene sets from the ScType marker database, without any reference dataset or manual marker curation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input requires distinguishing malignant from healthy cells — use ScType's single-cell SNV calling workflow (vartrix) rather than marker-based annotation alone A labeled reference scRNA-seq training dataset is available and a supervised classifier (e.g., CaSTLe, ACTINN) is preferred The comparator method cannot accept custom markers — as with scCATCH, whose implementation does not allow custom marker input

skills.description: Use when you have a simulated or labeled scRNA-seq count matrix with known cell-type labels and a marker list, and you need to rank clustering-then-annotation baselines (Seurat, SC3, PhenoGraph, densityCut, dynamicTreeCut) against marker-based or eager-learning classifiers.
skills.name: unsupervised-clustering-annotation-comparison
skills.search_text: unsupervised-clustering-annotation-comparison Use when you have a simulated or labeled scRNA-seq count matrix with known cell-type labels and a marker list, and you need to rank clustering-then-annotation baselines (Seurat, SC3, PhenoGraph, densityCut, dynamicTreeCut) against marker-based or eager-learning classifiers. Input is already a cluster-to-cell-type annotation or a precomputed feature/embedding table rather than a raw count matrix with labels The goal is running a single method's assignment rather than a head-to-head benchmark across unsupervised, eager-learning and marker-learning categories No ground-truth cell-type labels (or marker list) exist, so accuracy and per-cell-type F1-score cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark unsupervised scRNA-seq cell-type identification (cluster then annotate clusters via markers) against eager-learning and marker-learning methods such as CellAssign and SCINA, scoring accuracy and mean per-cell-type F1-score. This mirrors the evaluation logic of the AutomaticCellTypeIdentification review, which quantitatively compares methods on prediction accuracy, F1-score, unlabeling rate and running time. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.10.027
skills.summary: Benchmark unsupervised scRNA-seq cell-type identification (cluster then annotate clusters via markers) against eager-learning and marker-learning methods such as CellAssign and SCINA, scoring accuracy and mean per-cell-type F1-score. This mirrors the evaluation logic of the AutomaticCellTypeIdentification review, which quantitatively compares methods on prediction accuracy, F1-score, unlabeling rate and running time.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cluster-to-cell-type annotation or a precomputed feature/embedding table rather than a raw count matrix with labels The goal is running a single method's assignment rather than a head-to-head benchmark across unsupervised, eager-learning and marker-learning categories No ground-truth cell-type labels (or marker list) exist, so accuracy and per-cell-type F1-score cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq expression matrices where all genes cannot be treated as equally significant and insignificant genes must be filtered out without using cell-type labels.
skills.name: unsupervised-feature-selection-for-scrnaseq
skills.search_text: unsupervised-feature-selection-for-scrnaseq Use when clustering scRNA-seq expression matrices where all genes cannot be treated as equally significant and insignificant genes must be filtered out without using cell-type labels. Data is not raw gene-expression scRNA-seq (e.g. already a reduced feature embedding or a cell x gene annotation table) — the autoencoder and filter methods expect a gene expression matrix. Supervised or semi-supervised feature selection is desired — all four methods (Low Variance, Laplacian Score, SPEC, MCFS) are unsupervised and do not exploit labels. Only a single feature selection method can be afforded — the article's ablation showed single-method variants (e.g. SPEC alone) were second best and were outperformed by the four-method ensemble. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reduces scRNA-seq gene sets by first pre-selecting 5000 genes with a non-negative kernel autoencoder, then applying four unsupervised feature selection methods (Low Variance, Laplacian Score, SPEC, MCFS) to derive feature subsets for downstream ensemble clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.04.023
skills.summary: Reduces scRNA-seq gene sets by first pre-selecting 5000 genes with a non-negative kernel autoencoder, then applying four unsupervised feature selection methods (Low Variance, Laplacian Score, SPEC, MCFS) to derive feature subsets for downstream ensemble clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is not raw gene-expression scRNA-seq (e.g. already a reduced feature embedding or a cell x gene annotation table) — the autoencoder and filter methods expect a gene expression matrix. Supervised or semi-supervised feature selection is desired — all four methods (Low Variance, Laplacian Score, SPEC, MCFS) are unsupervised and do not exploit labels. Only a single feature selection method can be afforded — the article's ablation showed single-method variants (e.g. SPEC alone) were second best and were outperformed by the four-method ensemble.

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq expression data has been clustered or embedded with SIMLR and you need to identify the genes that explain differences across the inferred sample populations without pre-selecting gene subsets of known function.
skills.name: unsupervised-gene-prioritization
skills.search_text: unsupervised-gene-prioritization Use when single-cell RNA-seq expression data has been clustered or embedded with SIMLR and you need to identify the genes that explain differences across the inferred sample populations without pre-selecting gene subsets of known function. The analysis goal is supervised feature selection from a pre-selected gene subset of known function — SIMLR_Feature_Ranking is unsupervised and de novo by design No SIMLR similarity has been learned yet — the ranking depends on the multi-kernel sample-to-sample similarities, so run SIMLR first The dataset is too large for the standard implementation and should instead use SIMLR_Large_Scale for the similarity learning step http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Rank genes by their concordance with the sample-to-sample similarity learned by SIMLR, using SIMLR_Feature_Ranking with graph diffusion to correct weak similarities caused by noise and dropout events. This offers a de novo, unsupervised downstream application of the learned similarities alongside dimension reduction and visualization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/pmic.201700232
skills.summary: Rank genes by their concordance with the sample-to-sample similarity learned by SIMLR, using SIMLR_Feature_Ranking with graph diffusion to correct weak similarities caused by noise and dropout events. This offers a de novo, unsupervised downstream application of the learned similarities alongside dimension reduction and visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is supervised feature selection from a pre-selected gene subset of known function — SIMLR_Feature_Ranking is unsupervised and de novo by design No SIMLR similarity has been learned yet — the ranking depends on the multi-kernel sample-to-sample similarities, so run SIMLR first The dataset is too large for the standard implementation and should instead use SIMLR_Large_Scale for the similarity learning step

skills.description: Use when you must pick a minimal gene panel (e.g. k=50 markers) from scRNA-seq data without cell-type labels, and want to benchmark unsupervised selectors on full-transcriptome reconstruction loss.
skills.name: unsupervised-marker-selection
skills.search_text: unsupervised-marker-selection Use when you must pick a minimal gene panel (e.g. k=50 markers) from scRNA-seq data without cell-type labels, and want to benchmark unsupervised selectors on full-transcriptome reconstruction loss. Cell-type labels are available and the goal is cell-type classification — use supervised (loss_tradeoff=0) or mixed (loss_tradeoff=0.5) MarkerMap instead, as in the README's three tradeoff levels The task is cluster annotation or differential expression ranking (e.g. COSG-style marker identification) rather than choosing a minimal panel predictive of the whole transcriptome Input is not single-cell expression data in an AnnData-compatible format, or the sparse-to-dense conversion (adata.X.toarray()) is infeasible because the dataset is too large for memory http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Select a small set of k gene markers without using cell labels by benchmarking unsupervised MarkerMap (loss_tradeoff=1.0) against RandomBaseline, Scanpy highly-variable genes, and unsupervised PERSIST, then judge marker quality by how well a linear regression reconstructs the full transcriptome from the k markers (average ℓ2/ℓ1 loss over 10 runs). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00339-3
skills.summary: Select a small set of k gene markers without using cell labels by benchmarking unsupervised MarkerMap (loss_tradeoff=1.0) against RandomBaseline, Scanpy highly-variable genes, and unsupervised PERSIST, then judge marker quality by how well a linear regression reconstructs the full transcriptome from the k markers (average ℓ2/ℓ1 loss over 10 runs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell-type labels are available and the goal is cell-type classification — use supervised (loss_tradeoff=0) or mixed (loss_tradeoff=0.5) MarkerMap instead, as in the README's three tradeoff levels The task is cluster annotation or differential expression ranking (e.g. COSG-style marker identification) rather than choosing a minimal panel predictive of the whole transcriptome Input is not single-cell expression data in an AnnData-compatible format, or the sparse-to-dense conversion (adata.X.toarray()) is infeasible because the dataset is too large for memory

skills.description: Use when the input is a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. 10X PBMC3k) whose initial unsupervised clusters appear heterogeneous, and rare or low-abundance cell populations must be resolved without prior labels.
skills.name: unsupervised-scrna-seq-clustering-reclustering
skills.search_text: unsupervised-scrna-seq-clustering-reclustering Use when the input is a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. 10X PBMC3k) whose initial unsupervised clusters appear heterogeneous, and rare or low-abundance cell populations must be resolved without prior labels. The goal is copy-number variation inference from scRNA-seq count tables or BAM files — that is the scope of CONICS/CONICSmat, not silhouette-driven reclustering. The dataset already has reliable fine-grained cell-type labels or the clusters show high median silhouette scores, so no heterogeneous target clusters remain for reclustering. The task is purely 2D embedding/visualization of a large transcriptome matrix (e.g. t-SNE via openTSNE) rather than partitioning cells into clusters. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Unsupervised clustering and silhouette-driven reclustering of scRNA-seq data using SCISSORS, a framework wrapped around Seurat, to uncover rare cell types and small subgroups within heterogeneous broad clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad449
skills.summary: Unsupervised clustering and silhouette-driven reclustering of scRNA-seq data using SCISSORS, a framework wrapped around Seurat, to uncover rare cell types and small subgroups within heterogeneous broad clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is copy-number variation inference from scRNA-seq count tables or BAM files — that is the scope of CONICS/CONICSmat, not silhouette-driven reclustering. The dataset already has reliable fine-grained cell-type labels or the clusters show high median silhouette scores, so no heterogeneous target clusters remain for reclustering. The task is purely 2D embedding/visualization of a large transcriptome matrix (e.g. t-SNE via openTSNE) rather than partitioning cells into clusters.

skills.description: Use when an AnnData cells-by-genes matrix needs unsupervised scETM training (e.g., MousePancreas.h5ad with 'batch_indices' and 'cell_types' in adata.obs) before embedding extraction or zero-shot transfer to a target dataset.
skills.name: unsupervised-trainer-training-loop
skills.search_text: unsupervised-trainer-training-loop Use when an AnnData cells-by-genes matrix needs unsupervised scETM training (e.g., MousePancreas.h5ad with 'batch_indices' and 'cell_types' in adata.obs) before embedding extraction or zero-shot transfer to a target dataset. The goal is supervised or reference-based annotation rather than unsupervised clustering of the target scRNA-seq data The gene embedding matrix must be fixed to a pathways-by-genes matrix (p-scETM variant with trainable_gene_emb_dim=0), which requires a different configuration path http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train the scETM topic model on a single-cell RNA-seq AnnData object using the UnsupervisedTrainer class for 12000 epochs with periodic evaluation, producing cell, gene, and topic embeddings suitable for clustering and zero-shot transfer. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25534-2
skills.summary: Train the scETM topic model on a single-cell RNA-seq AnnData object using the UnsupervisedTrainer class for 12000 epochs with periodic evaluation, producing cell, gene, and topic embeddings suitable for clustering and zero-shot transfer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is supervised or reference-based annotation rather than unsupervised clustering of the target scRNA-seq data The gene embedding matrix must be fixed to a pathways-by-genes matrix (p-scETM variant with trainable_gene_emb_dim=0), which requires a different configuration path

skills.description: Use when comparing which genes multiple DS analysis methods (pseudobulk pbDS engines vs. cell-level mmDS mixed models) call significant at FDR < 0.05, and you need to visualize set intersections across methods and replicates.
skills.name: upset-plot-method-comparison-visualization
skills.search_text: upset-plot-method-comparison-visualization Use when comparing which genes multiple DS analysis methods (pseudobulk pbDS engines vs. cell-level mmDS mixed models) call significant at FDR < 0.05, and you need to visualize set intersections across methods and replicates. The analysis goal is per-method performance metrics (TPR, FDR, AUC) rather than between-method agreement of significant calls Results come from a single method or single replicate, so there are no cross-method or cross-replicate gene sets to intersect Input is raw counts or pseudobulk aggregates rather than completed DS result tables with adjusted p-values http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Builds UpSet plots of intersection sizes between top-ranked differential state (DS) detections (Benjamini-Hochberg p_adj.loc < 0.05) from the 16 muscat DS methods, to visualize between-method concordance and isolate method-unique hits for truth assessment in simulation replicates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19894-4
skills.summary: Builds UpSet plots of intersection sizes between top-ranked differential state (DS) detections (Benjamini-Hochberg p_adj.loc < 0.05) from the 16 muscat DS methods, to visualize between-method concordance and isolate method-unique hits for truth assessment in simulation replicates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is per-method performance metrics (TPR, FDR, AUC) rather than between-method agreement of significant calls Results come from a single method or single replicate, so there are no cross-method or cross-replicate gene sets to intersect Input is raw counts or pseudobulk aggregates rather than completed DS result tables with adjusted p-values

skills.description: Use when scanning transcriptome-wide RNA sequences for candidate pseudouridine (Ψ) sites and you need to restrict deep-learning scoring to uridine-centered 51-base fragments.
skills.name: uridine-centered-fragment-filtering
skills.search_text: uridine-centered-fragment-filtering Use when scanning transcriptome-wide RNA sequences for candidate pseudouridine (Ψ) sites and you need to restrict deep-learning scoring to uridine-centered 51-base fragments. When the goal is to re-predict already experimentally documented RMBase Ψ sites rather than discover novel ones (known sites plus ±25 flanking bases should be masked first) When scoring full-length sequences without center alignment — the model expects a uridine at the fragment center for the prediction to be interpretable Generates 51-nt running windows across RNA transcript sequences and retains only fragments with a uridine at their center so that MU-PseUDeep scores every candidate Ψ site, with a >0.99 precision threshold used to call predicted pseudouridines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2020.07.010
skills.summary: Generates 51-nt running windows across RNA transcript sequences and retains only fragments with a uridine at their center so that MU-PseUDeep scores every candidate Ψ site, with a >0.99 precision threshold used to call predicted pseudouridines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to re-predict already experimentally documented RMBase Ψ sites rather than discover novel ones (known sites plus ±25 flanking bases should be masked first) When scoring full-length sequences without center alignment — the model expects a uridine at the fragment center for the prediction to be interpretable

skills.description: Use when a set of differentially expressed uTARs (e.g., Wilcoxon rank-sum hits) must be assigned functional or gene-level annotations via nucleotide sequence homology of their coverage peaks.
skills.name: utar-coverage-peak-fwhm-extraction
skills.search_text: utar-coverage-peak-fwhm-extraction Use when a set of differentially expressed uTARs (e.g., Wilcoxon rank-sum hits) must be assigned functional or gene-level annotations via nucleotide sequence homology of their coverage peaks. The regions of interest are already annotated (aTARs) with gene symbols and do not require sequence-homology annotation. No aligned BAM files or reference genome FASTA are available from which per-uTAR coverage and peak sequences can be extracted. The goal is de novo transcript assembly or ORF prediction rather than homology-based labeling of differentially expressed uTAR peaks. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Annotates differentially expressed uTARs by extracting the nucleotide sequence of their largest coverage peak (located via LOESS smoothing and FWHM coordinates) and labeling the uTAR by its top BLASTn hit against the NCBI nt database, providing sequence-homology functional labels for unannotated transcribed regions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22496-3
skills.summary: Annotates differentially expressed uTARs by extracting the nucleotide sequence of their largest coverage peak (located via LOESS smoothing and FWHM coordinates) and labeling the uTAR by its top BLASTn hit against the NCBI nt database, providing sequence-homology functional labels for unannotated transcribed regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The regions of interest are already annotated (aTARs) with gene symbols and do not require sequence-homology annotation. No aligned BAM files or reference genome FASTA are available from which per-uTAR coverage and peak sequences can be extracted. The goal is de novo transcript assembly or ORF prediction rather than homology-based labeling of differentially expressed uTAR peaks.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq alignments must be quantified against annotation-independent genomic TARs, and when deciding whether pseudo-bulk uTAR expression or single-cell PC loading better flags biologically significant uTARs.
skills.name: utar-feature-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: utar-feature-expression-analysis Use when scRNA-seq alignments must be quantified against annotation-independent genomic TARs, and when deciding whether pseudo-bulk uTAR expression or single-cell PC loading better flags biologically significant uTARs. The analysis targets annotated genes only (a well-annotated gene expression matrix) — this skill is specifically for regions outside existing annotation (uTARs) No aligned scRNA-seq data or groHMM TAR intervals exist (e.g. only a raw fastq with no from_fastqs/from_cellranger workflow run) A pseudo-bulk-only coverage ranking is sufficient — this skill shows coverage rank is uncorrelated (r2 = 4.0e-3) with cell-type-defining PC loadings http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A scRNA-seq analysis routine from the TAR-scRNA-seq workflow that builds a single-cell expression matrix over transcriptionally active regions (TARs), identifies unannotated TARs (uTARs) differentially expressed across cell clusters, and evaluates whether highly expressed uTARs (pseudo-bulk coverage) correspond to uTARs that define cell types (PC loadings). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22496-3
skills.summary: A scRNA-seq analysis routine from the TAR-scRNA-seq workflow that builds a single-cell expression matrix over transcriptionally active regions (TARs), identifies unannotated TARs (uTARs) differentially expressed across cell clusters, and evaluates whether highly expressed uTARs (pseudo-bulk coverage) correspond to uTARs that define cell types (PC loadings).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets annotated genes only (a well-annotated gene expression matrix) — this skill is specifically for regions outside existing annotation (uTARs) No aligned scRNA-seq data or groHMM TAR intervals exist (e.g. only a raw fastq with no from_fastqs/from_cellranger workflow run) A pseudo-bulk-only coverage ranking is sufficient — this skill shows coverage rank is uncorrelated (r2 = 4.0e-3) with cell-type-defining PC loadings

skills.description: Use when spatial Visium count matrices and a TAR+reference genome annotation are available and you must confirm that scRNA-seq-discovered uTARs are spatially detectable and colocalize with known marker genes.
skills.name: utar-genomic-overlap-matching
skills.search_text: utar-genomic-overlap-matching Use when spatial Visium count matrices and a TAR+reference genome annotation are available and you must confirm that scRNA-seq-discovered uTARs are spatially detectable and colocalize with known marker genes. Input is a single-cell (non-spatial) expression matrix — this skill requires per-spot Visium data with spatial coordinates Only raw FASTQs without Space Ranger count matrices or alignments are available and no alignment step is planned The organism lacks any genome annotation or TAR track, so uTAR coordinates/strandedness cannot be compared across modalities http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Matches spatial-transcriptomics uTARs to scRNA-seq uTARs by chromosome-position and strandedness overlap, then tests whether these uTARs colocalize with canonical cell-type markers by Pearson correlation of log-e-normalized spot expression. Extends annotation-independent TAR analysis from single-cell to 10X Visium spatial data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22496-3
skills.summary: Matches spatial-transcriptomics uTARs to scRNA-seq uTARs by chromosome-position and strandedness overlap, then tests whether these uTARs colocalize with canonical cell-type markers by Pearson correlation of log-e-normalized spot expression. Extends annotation-independent TAR analysis from single-cell to 10X Visium spatial data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-cell (non-spatial) expression matrix — this skill requires per-spot Visium data with spatial coordinates Only raw FASTQs without Space Ranger count matrices or alignments are available and no alignment step is planned The organism lacks any genome annotation or TAR track, so uTAR coordinates/strandedness cannot be compared across modalities

skills.description: Use when running or reproducing a phase I/II immunotherapy dose-finding trial/simulation that must pick an OBD by jointly balancing binary DLT and efficacy outcomes via a utility function, after a toxicity-exploration stage has defined an admissible dose set.
skills.name: utility-based-obd-selection
skills.search_text: utility-based-obd-selection Use when running or reproducing a phase I/II immunotherapy dose-finding trial/simulation that must pick an OBD by jointly balancing binary DLT and efficacy outcomes via a utility function, after a toxicity-exploration stage has defined an admissible dose set. The response outcome is binary but requires long follow-up to be assessed; the article states the design 'cannot be applied directly to cases in which the response outcome requires a long follow-up time to be assessed.' The trial is a drug-combination study; extending TSNP to drug-combination trials is explicitly future work, not yet done. The goal is conventional MTD-targeting phase I monotherapy dose escalation without joint toxicity-efficacy utility-based OBD selection. Stage-2 component of the TSNP two-stage nonparametric phase I/II design for immunotherapy: within the toxicity-admissible dose set, select the optimal biological dose (OBD) by maximizing a utility function U(pi_jkl_hat, omega_kl) that weights the four joint toxicity-efficacy outcomes by physician-elicited desirability scores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/pst.2075
skills.summary: Stage-2 component of the TSNP two-stage nonparametric phase I/II design for immunotherapy: within the toxicity-admissible dose set, select the optimal biological dose (OBD) by maximizing a utility function U(pi_jkl_hat, omega_kl) that weights the four joint toxicity-efficacy outcomes by physician-elicited desirability scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The response outcome is binary but requires long follow-up to be assessed; the article states the design 'cannot be applied directly to cases in which the response outcome requires a long follow-up time to be assessed.' The trial is a drug-combination study; extending TSNP to drug-combination trials is explicitly future work, not yet done. The goal is conventional MTD-targeting phase I monotherapy dose escalation without joint toxicity-efficacy utility-based OBD selection.

skills.description: Use when you need to measure whether improved 3' UTR annotation (e.g. peaks2utr output with source=peaks2utr) translates into better per-cell genes captured and UMI counts in a 10x Chromium scRNA-seq quantification pipeline.
skills.name: utr-annotation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: utr-annotation-benchmarking Use when you need to measure whether improved 3' UTR annotation (e.g. peaks2utr output with source=peaks2utr) translates into better per-cell genes captured and UMI counts in a 10x Chromium scRNA-seq quantification pipeline. The 3' UTR annotation has not yet been generated — this skill benchmarks an existing peaks2utr-augmented GFF3, it does not produce UTR annotations (run peaks2utr on the GFF + BAM first). The read data are not from a UTR-enriched single-cell protocol such as 10x Chromium; peaks2utr's signal depends on reads concentrating at UTR distal ends, so per-cell metric gains would not be interpretable for bulk or non-polyA-capture data. The goal is de novo gene discovery or transcript assembly rather than comparing quantification impact of two annotation versions of the same gene models. http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmarking skill that quantifies the downstream effect of peaks2utr-extended 3' UTR annotations by rebuilding a Cell Ranger 6.1.1 custom reference from the augmented GFF3 and comparing per-cell scRNA-seq metrics against the canonical annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad112
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill that quantifies the downstream effect of peaks2utr-extended 3' UTR annotations by rebuilding a Cell Ranger 6.1.1 custom reference from the augmented GFF3 and comparing per-cell scRNA-seq metrics against the canonical annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The 3' UTR annotation has not yet been generated — this skill benchmarks an existing peaks2utr-augmented GFF3, it does not produce UTR annotations (run peaks2utr on the GFF + BAM first). The read data are not from a UTR-enriched single-cell protocol such as 10x Chromium; peaks2utr's signal depends on reads concentrating at UTR distal ends, so per-cell metric gains would not be interpretable for bulk or non-polyA-capture data. The goal is de novo gene discovery or transcript assembly rather than comparing quantification impact of two annotation versions of the same gene models.

skills.description: Use when you have an aligned scRNA-seq BAM (e.g. 10x Chromium, UTR-enriched) plus a GFF/GTF gene model and need to annotate or reannotate 3' UTRs beyond the canonical annotation.
skills.name: utr-annotation-from-bam-reads
skills.search_text: utr-annotation-from-bam-reads Use when you have an aligned scRNA-seq BAM (e.g. 10x Chromium, UTR-enriched) plus a GFF/GTF gene model and need to annotate or reannotate 3' UTRs beyond the canonical annotation. The BAM is not from a UTR-enriched single-cell protocol (e.g. 10x Chromium) — signal concentrated at UTR distal ends is what the method relies on You already have a validated, complete 3' UTR annotation and do not want it extended, overridden or augmented You need bulk-3'-seq-style UTR quantification rather than annotation of UTR coordinates from scRNA-seq coverage peaks http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Annotate 3' UTRs by running peaks2utr, a Python CLI that calls broad read-coverage peaks with MACS3 on an aligned BAM (e.g. 10x Chromium scRNA-seq) and refines UTR end positions using polyA-tail truncation points, extending or overriding a canonical GFF/GTF annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad112
skills.summary: Annotate 3' UTRs by running peaks2utr, a Python CLI that calls broad read-coverage peaks with MACS3 on an aligned BAM (e.g. 10x Chromium scRNA-seq) and refines UTR end positions using polyA-tail truncation points, extending or overriding a canonical GFF/GTF annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The BAM is not from a UTR-enriched single-cell protocol (e.g. 10x Chromium) — signal concentrated at UTR distal ends is what the method relies on You already have a validated, complete 3' UTR annotation and do not want it extended, overridden or augmented You need bulk-3'-seq-style UTR quantification rather than annotation of UTR coordinates from scRNA-seq coverage peaks

skills.description: Use when a region set of transcriptomic features (e.g. m7G/m6A methylation sites with unknown isoform origin) must be tested for colocalization against 5'UTR or CDS regions using permutation-based null models in R/RgnTX.
skills.name: utr-cds-genomic-background-construction
skills.search_text: utr-cds-genomic-background-construction Use when a region set of transcriptomic features (e.g. m7G/m6A methylation sites with unknown isoform origin) must be tested for colocalization against 5'UTR or CDS regions using permutation-based null models in R/RgnTX. When the region set already has clear isoform association — use permTestTx/permTestTx_customPick with overlapCountsTx instead of the IA mode When a genome-based colocalization background is intended (e.g. whole-genome shuffle via regioneR/BEDTools); RgnTX null models randomize over mRNA/transcriptome space and are not interchangeable with genome-based shuffling When testing associations with region types other than 5'UTR/CDS (e.g. stop codons or threeUTR) without adapting the customPick function accordingly http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Constructs 5'UTR and CDS transcriptome-region backgrounds as customPick functions for RgnTX permutation tests, so that associations between features such as m7G (or m6A) sites and specific transcriptome regions can be assessed against a transcriptome-wide shuffling null model rather than a genome-based one. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.08.021
skills.summary: Constructs 5'UTR and CDS transcriptome-region backgrounds as customPick functions for RgnTX permutation tests, so that associations between features such as m7G (or m6A) sites and specific transcriptome regions can be assessed against a transcriptome-wide shuffling null model rather than a genome-based one.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the region set already has clear isoform association — use permTestTx/permTestTx_customPick with overlapCountsTx instead of the IA mode When a genome-based colocalization background is intended (e.g. whole-genome shuffle via regioneR/BEDTools); RgnTX null models randomize over mRNA/transcriptome space and are not interchangeable with genome-based shuffling When testing associations with region types other than 5'UTR/CDS (e.g. stop codons or threeUTR) without adapting the customPick function accordingly

skills.description: Use when you need a canonical 5'-UTR-CDS-3'-UTR metagene of CLIP (eCLIP/STAMP) binding density on mature mRNA, rather than Metadensity's custom pre-mRNA feature models such as branchpoints or polyadenylation sites.
skills.name: utr-cds-metagene-segmentation
skills.search_text: utr-cds-metagene-segmentation Use when you need a canonical 5'-UTR-CDS-3'-UTR metagene of CLIP (eCLIP/STAMP) binding density on mature mRNA, rather than Metadensity's custom pre-mRNA feature models such as branchpoints or polyadenylation sites. When the target features are non-canonical pre-mRNA sites such as branchpoints, intronic polyadenylation sites, miRNA-hosting genes, or snoRNA/lncRNA loci — Metadensity supports these but this skill covers only the mature 5'UTR-CDS-3'UTR model When you need per-feature scaling by length (e.g. transcriptome-wide scaled coverage maps) — Metadensity deliberately preserves near-nucleotide resolution instead of scaling features by length When you lack a size-matched input control for the eCLIP experiment, since IP signal normalization against background is central to the metagene computation http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Compute the canonical mature-mRNA 5'-UTR-CDS-3'-UTR metagene model with Metadensity — the regular metagene reported in Supplementary Fig. S1 — by windowing input-normalized eCLIP signal over UTR/CDS transcript features at near-nucleotide resolution and averaging across transcripts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac083
skills.summary: Compute the canonical mature-mRNA 5'-UTR-CDS-3'-UTR metagene model with Metadensity — the regular metagene reported in Supplementary Fig. S1 — by windowing input-normalized eCLIP signal over UTR/CDS transcript features at near-nucleotide resolution and averaging across transcripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the target features are non-canonical pre-mRNA sites such as branchpoints, intronic polyadenylation sites, miRNA-hosting genes, or snoRNA/lncRNA loci — Metadensity supports these but this skill covers only the mature 5'UTR-CDS-3'UTR model When you need per-feature scaling by length (e.g. transcriptome-wide scaled coverage maps) — Metadensity deliberately preserves near-nucleotide resolution instead of scaling features by length When you lack a size-matched input control for the eCLIP experiment, since IP signal normalization against background is central to the metagene computation

skills.description: Use when annotating 3' UTRs from aligned reads (e.g. 10x Chromium BAM signal concentrated at UTR distal ends) and you need to identify candidate regions of significant read coverage before UTR end determination.
skills.name: utr-enrichment-peak-detection
skills.search_text: utr-enrichment-peak-detection Use when annotating 3' UTRs from aligned reads (e.g. 10x Chromium BAM signal concentrated at UTR distal ends) and you need to identify candidate regions of significant read coverage before UTR end determination. The BAM signal is diffuse across transcript bodies rather than concentrated at UTR distal ends (the approach favours 10x Chromium-style runs) You need precise UTR end bases directly from peak calls — peaks are only the candidate regions; truncation-point pile-up is a separate downstream step http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Call broad peaks of significant read coverage from an aligned BAM file using MACS (MACS3), as the first stage of peaks2utr's pipeline for annotating novel 3' UTRs. The peaks are the candidate regions on which downstream UTR-extension criteria are applied. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad112
skills.summary: Call broad peaks of significant read coverage from an aligned BAM file using MACS (MACS3), as the first stage of peaks2utr's pipeline for annotating novel 3' UTRs. The peaks are the candidate regions on which downstream UTR-extension criteria are applied.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The BAM signal is diffuse across transcript bodies rather than concentrated at UTR distal ends (the approach favours 10x Chromium-style runs) You need precise UTR end bases directly from peak calls — peaks are only the candidate regions; truncation-point pile-up is a separate downstream step

skills.description: Use when you have a DESeq2 results data.frame and an siRNA guide sequence, and need per-gene counts of a defined seed (e.g., mer7m8) across 3'UTRs to test for seed-mediated off-target activity.
skills.name: utr-sequence-seed-match-counting
skills.search_text: utr-sequence-seed-match-counting Use when you have a DESeq2 results data.frame and an siRNA guide sequence, and need per-gene counts of a defined seed (e.g., mer7m8) across 3'UTRs to test for seed-mediated off-target activity. Input results frame lacks the gene_id, log2FoldChange, or padj columns required by SeedMatchR's res argument You need mismatch-tolerant or indel-permitting seed search (e.g., target bulges and wobbles) rather than exact vcountPattern matching Sequences are full transcripts or CDS rather than the 3'UTR features the annotation loader extracts http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Annotate a differential expression results frame with per-gene counts of siRNA seed matches (e.g., mer7m8) found in 3'UTR feature sequences, using exact-pattern counting over a reference transcriptome so seed-mediated off-target effects can be detected in RNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae011
skills.summary: Annotate a differential expression results frame with per-gene counts of siRNA seed matches (e.g., mer7m8) found in 3'UTR feature sequences, using exact-pattern counting over a reference transcriptome so seed-mediated off-target effects can be detected in RNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input results frame lacks the gene_id, log2FoldChange, or padj columns required by SeedMatchR's res argument You need mismatch-tolerant or indel-permitting seed search (e.g., target bulges and wobbles) rather than exact vcountPattern matching Sequences are full transcripts or CDS rather than the 3'UTR features the annotation loader extracts

skills.description: Use when a GFF/GTF gene annotation plus a BAM of aligned reads (e.g. 10x Chromium, where signal concentrates at UTR distal ends) must be converted into novel 3' UTR annotations.
skills.name: utr-truncation-point-pileup-annotation
skills.search_text: utr-truncation-point-pileup-annotation Use when a GFF/GTF gene annotation plus a BAM of aligned reads (e.g. 10x Chromium, where signal concentrates at UTR distal ends) must be converted into novel 3' UTR annotations. The input BAM is not from a 3'-enriched library — the peak-calling and truncation-point logic assumes signal concentrated at the distal ends of 3' or 5' UTRs (e.g. 10x Chromium) You need 5' UTR or full-length transcript isoform annotation rather than 3' UTR end designation Peak-to-gene strand/distance filtering is not applicable because the annotation lacks strand or gene features http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Annotates 3' UTRs by linking MACS3-called broad peaks of significant read coverage to same-strand genes within a maximum distance, then defining each passing UTR's precise end via pileup of polyA/soft-clip truncation points from the BAM. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad112
skills.summary: Annotates 3' UTRs by linking MACS3-called broad peaks of significant read coverage to same-strand genes within a maximum distance, then defining each passing UTR's precise end via pileup of polyA/soft-clip truncation points from the BAM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input BAM is not from a 3'-enriched library — the peak-calling and truncation-point logic assumes signal concentrated at the distal ends of 3' or 5' UTRs (e.g. 10x Chromium) You need 5' UTR or full-length transcript isoform annotation rather than 3' UTR end designation Peak-to-gene strand/distance filtering is not applicable because the annotation lacks strand or gene features

skills.description: Use when running scUTRquant on 10x Genomics or Microwell-seq-style 3'-end scRNA-seq FASTQs and a UTRome/CS-annotated target (e.g. utrome_mm10_v2) must be chosen, built, or configured for gene and 3'UTR isoform quantification.
skills.name: utrome-transcriptome-target-handling
skills.search_text: utrome-transcriptome-target-handling Use when running scUTRquant on 10x Genomics or Microwell-seq-style 3'-end scRNA-seq FASTQs and a UTRome/CS-annotated target (e.g. utrome_mm10_v2) must be chosen, built, or configured for gene and 3'UTR isoform quantification. The analysis goal is standard whole-transcript gene quantification with full-length transcriptomes (Cell Ranger) and no 3'UTR isoform resolution is needed — a standard GENCODE reference suffices Input data is full-length or 5'-end scRNA-seq that does not cover transcript 3' ends, since truncated-UTR targets are designed for 3'-end tag-based libraries A custom cleavage-site catalog is required and cannot come from GENCODE-validated 3' ends or the MWS CS atlas — txcutr-db/UTRome targets would not reflect the desired CS set http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Prepares and selects truncated-UTR transcriptome targets (e.g. utrome_mm10_v2) as the pseudoalignment reference for scUTRquant, so that kallisto|bustools can quantify 3'UTR isoforms and genes simultaneously from scRNA-seq data. Targets are built by truncating protein-coding transcripts with validated 3' ends from GENCODE plus MWS-derived cleavage sites. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Prepares and selects truncated-UTR transcriptome targets (e.g. utrome_mm10_v2) as the pseudoalignment reference for scUTRquant, so that kallisto|bustools can quantify 3'UTR isoforms and genes simultaneously from scRNA-seq data. Targets are built by truncating protein-coding transcripts with validated 3' ends from GENCODE plus MWS-derived cleavage sites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is standard whole-transcript gene quantification with full-length transcriptomes (Cell Ranger) and no 3'UTR isoform resolution is needed — a standard GENCODE reference suffices Input data is full-length or 5'-end scRNA-seq that does not cover transcript 3' ends, since truncated-UTR targets are designed for 3'-end tag-based libraries A custom cleavage-site catalog is required and cannot come from GENCODE-validated 3' ends or the MWS CS atlas — txcutr-db/UTRome targets would not reflect the desired CS set

skills.description: Use when an annotated or unannotated single-cell gene-expression matrix must be clustered and embedded without pre-specifying the number of clusters, e.g. reproducing scRNA-seq ARI benchmarks like Fig. 3A.
skills.name: vae-based-cell-embedding-clustering
skills.search_text: vae-based-cell-embedding-clustering Use when an annotated or unannotated single-cell gene-expression matrix must be clustered and embedded without pre-specifying the number of clusters, e.g. reproducing scRNA-seq ARI benchmarks like Fig. 3A. Input is not single-cell gene expression data (e.g. bulk RNA-seq, protein abundance, or already-reduced feature tables) — the VAE expects a raw count matrix Cells already have trusted curated labels and the goal is classification rather than unsupervised cluster discovery The pipeline requires cluster labels fixed before analysis with no merging or splitting (adaptive cluster merging may restructure the partition) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Applies scAce, a Python 3.8 VAE-based method that jointly learns single-cell embeddings and cluster assignments via ZINB-distribution modeling, Leiden-based cluster initialization, and adaptive cluster merging, to scRNA-seq count matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad546
skills.summary: Applies scAce, a Python 3.8 VAE-based method that jointly learns single-cell embeddings and cluster assignments via ZINB-distribution modeling, Leiden-based cluster initialization, and adaptive cluster merging, to scRNA-seq count matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not single-cell gene expression data (e.g. bulk RNA-seq, protein abundance, or already-reduced feature tables) — the VAE expects a raw count matrix Cells already have trusted curated labels and the goal is classification rather than unsupervised cluster discovery The pipeline requires cluster labels fixed before analysis with no merging or splitting (adaptive cluster merging may restructure the partition)

skills.description: Use when multi-batch scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., pancreas: 16382 cells, 14 cell types, 9 batches) must be integrated via a contrastive VAE-GAN whose decoder emits batch-corrected outputs in the original gene space.
skills.name: vae-gan-neural-network-implementation
skills.search_text: vae-gan-neural-network-implementation Use when multi-batch scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., pancreas: 16382 cells, 14 cell types, 9 batches) must be integrated via a contrastive VAE-GAN whose decoder emits batch-corrected outputs in the original gene space. CITE-seq protein data with only a few hundred features, where identifying shared features for scCobra's shared encoder is challenging Label transfer to query datasets from a different tissue type or without similar cell types, which scCobra requires for optimal performance scATAC-seq peak matrices where conversion to a gene activity matrix (e.g., via MAESTRO) may lead to information loss Reconstruct scCobra's VAE-GAN deep generative network — an encoder mapping multi-batch scRNA-seq into a unified latent space and a decoder with a Domain-Specific Batch Normalization (DSBN) layer — to batch-correct single-cell data without assuming a gene expression distribution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07692-x
skills.summary: Reconstruct scCobra's VAE-GAN deep generative network — an encoder mapping multi-batch scRNA-seq into a unified latent space and a decoder with a Domain-Specific Batch Normalization (DSBN) layer — to batch-correct single-cell data without assuming a gene expression distribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: CITE-seq protein data with only a few hundred features, where identifying shared features for scCobra's shared encoder is challenging Label transfer to query datasets from a different tissue type or without similar cell types, which scCobra requires for optimal performance scATAC-seq peak matrices where conversion to a gene activity matrix (e.g., via MAESTRO) may lead to information loss

skills.description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq for a cohort plus single-cell data for one representative sample and need single-cell-resolution profiles (e.g., .h5ad) for non-sequenced target samples.
skills.name: vae-gan-single-cell-generative-modeling
skills.search_text: vae-gan-single-cell-generative-modeling Use when you have bulk RNA-seq for a cohort plus single-cell data for one representative sample and need single-cell-resolution profiles (e.g., .h5ad) for non-sequenced target samples. Input is already cleaned/filtered mutation data with no missing VAF entries (e.g. after read_sclineager with coverage_cutoff filtering), where drop-out rates are no longer measurable The goal is lineage inference itself rather than drop-out characterization; use run_sclineager / sclineager_internal instead http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantifies expressional drop-out in single-cell genetic variant data by computing the proportion of missing variant allele frequency (VAF) observations per variant, per cell, and overall from a cells-by-variants mutation matrix, as described in the SClineager workflow (Lu et al., Cell Reports 2021). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2020.108589

skills.search_text: variant-allele-frequency-purity-proxy Use when analyzing bulk PDAC transcriptomic samples (e.g., the Puleo 2018 FFPE primary cohort in pdacR) and you need a per-sample tumor purity proxy without matched normal sequencing, to validate that a gene signature tracks tumor content. skills.summary: Uses predicted mean variant allele frequency (VAF) per sample as a tumor-cellularity proxy for bulk PDAC microarray data, then tests whether curated gene signatures (e.g., Collisson Exocrine) correlate with purity via Spearman rank correlation.

skills.description: Use when you have a Cell Ranger genome BAM from scRNA-seq data and need de novo SNV genotypes per cell — e.g. to determine host vs donor origin in post-transplant bone marrow samples without a known donor genotype.
skills.name: variant-calling-from-scrna-alignment-bam
skills.search_text: variant-calling-from-scrna-alignment-bam Use when you have a Cell Ranger genome BAM from scRNA-seq data and need de novo SNV genotypes per cell — e.g. to determine host vs donor origin in post-transplant bone marrow samples without a known donor genotype. When a reference donor/host genotype is already available and genotyping (rather than de novo discovery) suffices — this skill is for de novo calling without prior genotype knowledge When indels or structural variants are the target — the method explicitly ignores indels and calls only SNVs When expecting very low-level chimerism below ~4% of ~6,000 cells — K=1 selection only indicates the mixture fraction is below the detection level http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 De novo SNV calling directly from the genome BAM produced by single-cell 3' RNA-seq alignment, used to infer host/donor chimerism and cell genotypes without prior genotype knowledge. It repurposes transcriptome alignments (STAR-aligned Read1 cDNA inserts via Cell Ranger) as a variant-calling substrate with Freebayes 1.0.2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: De novo SNV calling directly from the genome BAM produced by single-cell 3' RNA-seq alignment, used to infer host/donor chimerism and cell genotypes without prior genotype knowledge. It repurposes transcriptome alignments (STAR-aligned Read1 cDNA inserts via Cell Ranger) as a variant-calling substrate with Freebayes 1.0.2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a reference donor/host genotype is already available and genotyping (rather than de novo discovery) suffices — this skill is for de novo calling without prior genotype knowledge When indels or structural variants are the target — the method explicitly ignores indels and calls only SNVs When expecting very low-level chimerism below ~4% of ~6,000 cells — K=1 selection only indicates the mixture fraction is below the detection level

skills.when_to_use_negative: The mixture contains fixed or non-living cells — the 10x genomics scRNA-seq platform requires live cells for successful genetic separation The goal is downstream individual identification and biogeographical ancestry assignment rather than separation — use de-goulash Snakemake step 2 (Snakefile_analysis) instead Per-cell genotype data or cluster VCFs already exist — re-running variant calling adds no information

skills.description: Use when you have a set of fine-mapped variant positions plus REF/ALT alleles and need allele-specific sequence windows centered on each variant for motif scanning (e.g., FIMO PWM analysis of binding-affinity disruption).

skills.search_text: variant-flanked-sequence-extraction Use when you have a set of fine-mapped variant positions plus REF/ALT alleles and need allele-specific sequence windows centered on each variant for motif scanning (e.g., FIMO PWM analysis of binding-affinity disruption). Variants lack both reference and alternate alleles mapped to a single GRCh38/hg38 position (e.g., only summary statistics without alleles) The goal is gene-level or locus-level attribution rather than allele-specific motif disruption analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Extracts, for each GrID-Net-linked schizophrenia variant, two ±20 bp-flanked allele sequences (reference and risk allele) from the GRCh38/hg38 reference genome so they can be scored for transcription-factor binding affinity changes with FIMO PWM scans. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Extracts, for each GrID-Net-linked schizophrenia variant, two ±20 bp-flanked allele sequences (reference and risk allele) from the GRCh38/hg38 reference genome so they can be scored for transcription-factor binding affinity changes with FIMO PWM scans.

skills.description: Use when preparing a ClinVar-derived VUS input set for RNA-seq or MRSD-based analysis of splice-altering variants, or when reproducing the paper's 352,011 -> 185,119 -> 7,507 variant curation workflow.
skills.name: variant-of-uncertain-significance-prioritization
skills.search_text: variant-of-uncertain-significance-prioritization Use when preparing a ClinVar-derived VUS input set for RNA-seq or MRSD-based analysis of splice-altering variants, or when reproducing the paper's 352,011 -> 185,119 -> 7,507 variant curation workflow. The variant set is already classified as pathogenic or likely pathogenic in ClinVar — this skill intentionally restricts to 'Uncertain significance' and 'Conflicting interpretations of pathogenicity' records. The downstream question concerns differential gene expression or allele-specific expression rather than splice junction coverage — the paper states the MRSD model cannot directly be extended to these use cases. The RNA-seq data are long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved — the paper notes no appropriate control datasets exist yet to develop corresponding MRSD models for these modalities. http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 A curation skill that extracts ClinVar variants of uncertain significance (VUS) predicted to impact splicing via SpliceAI delta-score filtering (score >= 0.5), producing a defined splice-impacting VUS set for downstream MRSD tissue-suitability analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2021.12.014
skills.summary: A curation skill that extracts ClinVar variants of uncertain significance (VUS) predicted to impact splicing via SpliceAI delta-score filtering (score >= 0.5), producing a defined splice-impacting VUS set for downstream MRSD tissue-suitability analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The variant set is already classified as pathogenic or likely pathogenic in ClinVar — this skill intentionally restricts to 'Uncertain significance' and 'Conflicting interpretations of pathogenicity' records. The downstream question concerns differential gene expression or allele-specific expression rather than splice junction coverage — the paper states the MRSD model cannot directly be extended to these use cases. The RNA-seq data are long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved — the paper notes no appropriate control datasets exist yet to develop corresponding MRSD models for these modalities.

skills.description: Use when sQTL mapping results (e.g. all-tests.nominal.tsv from sqtlseeker2-nf) must be restricted to variants overlapping annotated donor/acceptor splice-site intervals so their effect on splice-site strength can be quantified and compared.
skills.name: variant-splice-site-interval-intersection
skills.search_text: variant-splice-site-interval-intersection Use when sQTL mapping results (e.g. all-tests.nominal.tsv from sqtlseeker2-nf) must be restricted to variants overlapping annotated donor/acceptor splice-site intervals so their effect on splice-site strength can be quantified and compared. The analysis targets RNA-binding protein (RBP) motif disruption rather than splice-site sequences — the paper notes 'many more modify the binding sites of RNA-binding proteins' than splice-site sequences Variants are intronic/exonic but far from annotated donor/acceptor motifs (e.g. deep intronic or branchpoint effects), which this interval intersection will drop No transcript annotation with splice-junction coordinates is available for the genome build of the variants http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0798 A method step from the GTEx sQTL catalog analysis (Garrido-Martín et al., Nat Commun 2021) that intersects tested sQTL variant coordinates from sqtlseeker2-nf output with annotated splice-site (donor/acceptor) intervals to retain variants overlapping splice junction motifs, enabling downstream PWM-based splice-strength comparison of sQTLs vs non-sQTLs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2
skills.summary: A method step from the GTEx sQTL catalog analysis (Garrido-Martín et al., Nat Commun 2021) that intersects tested sQTL variant coordinates from sqtlseeker2-nf output with annotated splice-site (donor/acceptor) intervals to retain variants overlapping splice junction motifs, enabling downstream PWM-based splice-strength comparison of sQTLs vs non-sQTLs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets RNA-binding protein (RBP) motif disruption rather than splice-site sequences — the paper notes 'many more modify the binding sites of RNA-binding proteins' than splice-site sequences Variants are intronic/exonic but far from annotated donor/acceptor motifs (e.g. deep intronic or branchpoint effects), which this interval intersection will drop No transcript annotation with splice-junction coordinates is available for the genome build of the variants

skills.description: Use when high-dimensional, sparse, redundant scRNA-seq or proteomics matrices (AnnData-compatible TSV/CSV) must be compressed into a dense low-dimensional latent space before correlation-based network inference.
skills.name: variational-autoencoder-architecture-implementation
skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-architecture-implementation Use when high-dimensional, sparse, redundant scRNA-seq or proteomics matrices (AnnData-compatible TSV/CSV) must be compressed into a dense low-dimensional latent space before correlation-based network inference. Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or precomputed protein association network — the VAE stage exists to compress raw high-dimensional condition/sample matrices The goal is direct co-expression analysis on the original high-dimensional matrix rather than correlation in the compressed latent space Downstream analysis requires reconstructing the exact input matrix rather than learning a dense latent representation for pair scoring http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Implements FAVA's VAE dimensionality reduction stage: a single-hidden-layer encoder-decoder (ReLU hidden layers, linear mu/sigma outputs, sigmoid decoder) that compresses high-dimensional omics data into a regularized Gaussian latent space, trained with a 0.9 reconstruction / 0.1 KL loss against a N(1, 0.1) prior. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae010
skills.summary: Implements FAVA's VAE dimensionality reduction stage: a single-hidden-layer encoder-decoder (ReLU hidden layers, linear mu/sigma outputs, sigmoid decoder) that compresses high-dimensional omics data into a regularized Gaussian latent space, trained with a 0.9 reconstruction / 0.1 KL loss against a N(1, 0.1) prior.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or precomputed protein association network — the VAE stage exists to compress raw high-dimensional condition/sample matrices The goal is direct co-expression analysis on the original high-dimensional matrix rather than correlation in the compressed latent space Downstream analysis requires reconstructing the exact input matrix rather than learning a dense latent representation for pair scoring

skills.description: Use when building or reproducing an end-to-end marker selection model for single-cell RNA-seq (.h5ad / AnnData) data that must select exactly k genes and support supervised (loss_tradeoff=0), unsupervised (=1), or joint (=0.5) objectives.
skills.name: variational-autoencoder-architecture-implementation
skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-architecture-implementation Use when building or reproducing an end-to-end marker selection model for single-cell RNA-seq (.h5ad / AnnData) data that must select exactly k genes and support supervised (loss_tradeoff=0), unsupervised (=1), or joint (=0.5) objectives. You only need a fast baseline marker ranking without a trained generative model — the repository offers RandomBaseline (selects k markers at random) and RankCorr (rank-correlation-based selection) instead Input data is not single-cell expression in an AnnData/h5ad structure with a categorical group_by label column, so prepareData cannot build the dataloaders You need reproducible marker gene names for FISH panel design with binarized expression — PERSIST is designed for that spatial transcriptomics setting, not MarkerMap http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Implements the MarkerMap VAE-based marker selector: a Gumbel-Softmax layer differentiably picks k markers from a d-dimensional logit vector, a VAE branch reconstructs the full transcriptome from the selected markers, and a classification branch on the 16-dimensional latent space is combined with reconstruction via a loss_tradeoff-weighted convex loss. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00339-3
skills.summary: Implements the MarkerMap VAE-based marker selector: a Gumbel-Softmax layer differentiably picks k markers from a d-dimensional logit vector, a VAE branch reconstructs the full transcriptome from the selected markers, and a classification branch on the 16-dimensional latent space is combined with reconstruction via a loss_tradeoff-weighted convex loss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a fast baseline marker ranking without a trained generative model — the repository offers RandomBaseline (selects k markers at random) and RankCorr (rank-correlation-based selection) instead Input data is not single-cell expression in an AnnData/h5ad structure with a categorical group_by label column, so prepareData cannot build the dataloaders You need reproducible marker gene names for FISH panel design with binarized expression — PERSIST is designed for that spatial transcriptomics setting, not MarkerMap
