skills.name: variational-autoencoder-architecture-implementation
skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-architecture-implementation Use when building a dynamics-based latent-space model of RNA velocity from spliced/unspliced AnnData layers, where lineage-dependent dynamics require a latent regulatory state (zr) with state-dependent conditioning h. The analysis only needs local RNA velocity vectors under the standard spliced-unspliced model — scVelo's linear/dynamical model suffices without a learned latent space The dataset lacks spliced/unspliced layers (e.g. only a feature expression matrix or already-computed velocities), so the VAE cannot observe the gene dynamics it models http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Implement the structured latent VAE underlying LatentVelo: a PyTorch variational autoencoder with structured latent states (zu, zs, zr) whose dynamics are integrated with torchdiffeq neural ODEs, optionally extended as AnnotVAE with cell-type conditioning and batch correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100581

skills.description: Use when raw single-cell UMI/expression matrices (e.g. 10x Genomics PBMC3k, ~2700 cells with high dropout rate) need nonlinear 2D embedding to separate cell types or resolve rare sub-populations like FCGR3A+ vs CD14+ monocytes.
skills.name: variational-autoencoder-dimension-reduction
skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-dimension-reduction Use when raw single-cell UMI/expression matrices (e.g. 10x Genomics PBMC3k, ~2700 cells with high dropout rate) need nonlinear 2D embedding to separate cell types or resolve rare sub-populations like FCGR3A+ vs CD14+ monocytes. The input is bulk RNA-seq or already a low-dimensional feature embedding — VASC targets single-cell data dominated by dropout events You need deterministic, reproducible embeddings from a single run — stochastic optimization introduces run-to-run variation The sample size is very small and the co-variance matrix cannot be reliably estimated http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 VASC is a deep variational autoencoder that performs unsupervised dimension reduction and 2D visualization of scRNA-seq data by learning nonlinear hierarchical representations while explicitly modeling zero/near-zero dropout events with the Gumbel distribution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2018.08.003
skills.summary: VASC is a deep variational autoencoder that performs unsupervised dimension reduction and 2D visualization of scRNA-seq data by learning nonlinear hierarchical representations while explicitly modeling zero/near-zero dropout events with the Gumbel distribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is bulk RNA-seq or already a low-dimensional feature embedding — VASC targets single-cell data dominated by dropout events You need deterministic, reproducible embeddings from a single run — stochastic optimization introduces run-to-run variation The sample size is very small and the co-variance matrix cannot be reliably estimated

skills.description: Use when clustering single-cell RNA-seq data (tens of thousands of genes per cell) where dropout noise and high dimensionality make direct clustering unreliable, and a compressed latent cell representation is needed before network-fusion clustering.
skills.name: variational-autoencoder-dimensionality-reduction
skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-dimensionality-reduction Use when clustering single-cell RNA-seq data (tens of thousands of genes per cell) where dropout noise and high dimensionality make direct clustering unreliable, and a compressed latent cell representation is needed before network-fusion clustering. The input matrix is already low-dimensional (e.g. a pre-computed latent embedding or feature table rather than a genes-by-cells expression matrix) — the autoencoder feature filtering assumes raw high-dimensional gene expression. The data is raw/unnormalized count data that has not been log-transformed when max(data) > 100 — the pipeline expects normalized input and will not compensate on its own. The goal is supervised cell-type classification with known labels, not unsupervised clustering — the VAE latent space here is trained without labels. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Compresses noisy, high-dimensional scRNA-seq expression matrices into low-dimensional cell representations using scCAN's stacked variational autoencoder (latent d=15), preceded by min-max rescaling and non-negative-kernel autoencoder feature selection (top 5000 informative genes). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-14218-6
skills.summary: Compresses noisy, high-dimensional scRNA-seq expression matrices into low-dimensional cell representations using scCAN's stacked variational autoencoder (latent d=15), preceded by min-max rescaling and non-negative-kernel autoencoder feature selection (top 5000 informative genes).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix is already low-dimensional (e.g. a pre-computed latent embedding or feature table rather than a genes-by-cells expression matrix) — the autoencoder feature filtering assumes raw high-dimensional gene expression. The data is raw/unnormalized count data that has not been log-transformed when max(data) > 100 — the pipeline expects normalized input and will not compensate on its own. The goal is supervised cell-type classification with known labels, not unsupervised clustering — the VAE latent space here is trained without labels.

skills.description: Use when the input is a large, sparse, redundant omics matrix (scRNA-seq tsv/csv or AnnData, >0.5 million conditions/cells, or bulk proteomics) and the goal is protein functional association network inference that outperforms Pearson correlation.
skills.name: variational-autoencoder-embedding-of-omics-matrices
skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-embedding-of-omics-matrices Use when the input is a large, sparse, redundant omics matrix (scRNA-seq tsv/csv or AnnData, >0.5 million conditions/cells, or bulk proteomics) and the goal is protein functional association network inference that outperforms Pearson correlation. The goal is standard differential expression or cell-type annotation on an AnnData object — FAVA produces protein interaction networks, not per-gene statistics. The dataset is too small or dense for the sparseness/redundancy problem to matter — simple co-expression (PCC) may suffice and is cheaper. The input is not gene/protein-by-condition omics data (e.g. already a feature table or an existing interaction network), since FAVA expects high-dimensional raw omics matrices. http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compress high-dimensional scRNA-seq or proteomics matrices (e.g. 566109 HPA cells, 633 PRIDE experiments) into a dense low-dimensional latent space with FAVA's variational autoencoder, so that correlations computed in the latent space yield far more accurate functional association networks than plain co-expression (PCC) while running ~9x faster. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae010
skills.summary: Compress high-dimensional scRNA-seq or proteomics matrices (e.g. 566109 HPA cells, 633 PRIDE experiments) into a dense low-dimensional latent space with FAVA's variational autoencoder, so that correlations computed in the latent space yield far more accurate functional association networks than plain co-expression (PCC) while running ~9x faster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is standard differential expression or cell-type annotation on an AnnData object — FAVA produces protein interaction networks, not per-gene statistics. The dataset is too small or dense for the sparseness/redundancy problem to matter — simple co-expression (PCC) may suffice and is cheaper. The input is not gene/protein-by-condition omics data (e.g. already a feature table or an existing interaction network), since FAVA expects high-dimensional raw omics matrices.

skills.description: Use when training a spatial location recovery model on Visium-type ST data and the training sample is limited or the scRNA-seq query data is noisy, so synthetic ST replicates are needed to augment the training set.
skills.name: variational-autoencoder-gene-expression-augmentation
skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-gene-expression-augmentation Use when training a spatial location recovery model on Visium-type ST data and the training sample is limited or the scRNA-seq query data is noisy, so synthetic ST replicates are needed to augment the training set. When the goal is direct 2D location or spatial domain prediction on the original ST data without the optional augmentation step — the VAE replicates are an optional addition, not a requirement. When the ST data has no spot-level spatial coordinates, since each gene's 1D expression vector cannot be reshaped into the 2D matrix the convolutional VAE requires. When the training ST data comes from a single-cell-resolution platform with a small gene panel (e.g., small MERFISH/Xenium panels), where the authors note CeLEry is suboptimal and augmentation is unlikely to compensate for limited gene coverage. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Optional CeLEry data augmentation step that trains a convolutional variational autoencoder on the training spatial transcriptomics (ST) data to generate replicates whose 2D gene expression patterns resemble the original data while varying among replicates, improving robustness against scRNA-seq noise. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39895-3
skills.summary: Optional CeLEry data augmentation step that trains a convolutional variational autoencoder on the training spatial transcriptomics (ST) data to generate replicates whose 2D gene expression patterns resemble the original data while varying among replicates, improving robustness against scRNA-seq noise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is direct 2D location or spatial domain prediction on the original ST data without the optional augmentation step — the VAE replicates are an optional addition, not a requirement. When the ST data has no spot-level spatial coordinates, since each gene's 1D expression vector cannot be reshaped into the 2D matrix the convolutional VAE requires. When the training ST data comes from a single-cell-resolution platform with a small gene panel (e.g., small MERFISH/Xenium panels), where the authors note CeLEry is suboptimal and augmentation is unlikely to compensate for limited gene coverage.

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq matrix (rows = cells, columns = genes) has already been filtered by the non-negative kernel autoencoder and a low-dimensional compressed embedding is needed for clustering, visualization, classification, or pseudo-time inference.
skills.name: variational-autoencoder-implementation
skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-implementation Use when a scRNA-seq matrix (rows = cells, columns = genes) has already been filtered by the non-negative kernel autoencoder and a low-dimensional compressed embedding is needed for clustering, visualization, classification, or pseudo-time inference. skills.summary: Implements the second module of the scDHA pipeline: a Stacked Bayesian Self-learning Network, i.e. a modified Variational Autoencoder that compresses the non-negative kernel-autoencoder representation into a low-dimensional latent space while repeatedly perturbing the compressed space to reduce overfitting and learn a generalized representation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unfiltered scRNA-seq counts — the non-negative kernel autoencoder (first module) should first remove genes or components with insignificant contributions The goal is dropout imputation or ultrafast clustering without a deep-learning stack — methods like CIDR use implicit imputation and require only R >= 3.1.0 A single-cell toolkit with clustering, visualization, classification, and pseudo-time already built in is preferred over a learned embedding — the article notes scVI alone does not support clustering, visualization, classification, and pseudo-time inference

skills.description: Use when you have paired RNA + ADT (CITE-Seq/TEA-Seq) counts and want a joint low-dimensional embedding from which to cluster cells, or when benchmarking decision-level integrators (scTriangulate) against data-level VAE-based joint embedding.
skills.name: variational-autoencoder-joint-embedding
skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-joint-embedding Use when you have paired RNA + ADT (CITE-Seq/TEA-Seq) counts and want a joint low-dimensional embedding from which to cluster cells, or when benchmarking decision-level integrators (scTriangulate) against data-level VAE-based joint embedding. When the goal is decision-level integration that makes no assumption about the distributions of raw underlying values, or when mixing annotation sets from label transfer, multiple algorithms, and multiple resolutions — scTriangulate is designed for that, while TotalVI is limited to specific modalities (RNA + surface protein) When the data are single-modality only (e.g. ATAC alone); TotalVI requires RNA paired with surface protein expression When you need to reconcile conflicting pre-existing cluster labels rather than produce a joint embedding from counts http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Data-level multimodal integration in which a variational autoencoder (TotalVI, scvi-tools 0.14.3) infers a joint latent space from RNA and surface-protein (ADT) expression, on which Leiden clustering is then run. In the scTriangulate paper it serves as the state-of-the-art joint-embedding baseline benchmarked against decision-level integration on TEA-Seq PBMC data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36016-y
skills.summary: Data-level multimodal integration in which a variational autoencoder (TotalVI, scvi-tools 0.14.3) infers a joint latent space from RNA and surface-protein (ADT) expression, on which Leiden clustering is then run. In the scTriangulate paper it serves as the state-of-the-art joint-embedding baseline benchmarked against decision-level integration on TEA-Seq PBMC data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is decision-level integration that makes no assumption about the distributions of raw underlying values, or when mixing annotation sets from label transfer, multiple algorithms, and multiple resolutions — scTriangulate is designed for that, while TotalVI is limited to specific modalities (RNA + surface protein) When the data are single-modality only (e.g. ATAC alone); TotalVI requires RNA paired with surface protein expression When you need to reconcile conflicting pre-existing cluster labels rather than produce a joint embedding from counts

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq AnnData with spliced/unspliced layers exhibits multi-lineage or transient dynamics (bifurcation, trifurcation) where linear velocity models fail, and latent-space velocities or trajectories are needed.
skills.name: variational-autoencoder-latent-dynamics-inference
skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-latent-dynamics-inference Use when scRNA-seq AnnData with spliced/unspliced layers exhibits multi-lineage or transient dynamics (bifurcation, trifurcation) where linear velocity models fail, and latent-space velocities or trajectories are needed. Datasets that are well described by the linear steady-state or dynamical model with a single lineage and time-independent rates, where scVelo suffices Situations requiring a single initial latent state assumption to be violated in a known way, e.g. disconnected sparse clusters like microglia that the model misassigns as trajectory start points Analyses requiring stochastic dynamics or count normalization, which LatentVelo explicitly does not address http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Train a LatentVelo variational autoencoder to embed cells into a dynamics-based latent space and model differentiation with neural ordinary differential equations, yielding latent velocities, latent trajectories, and gene velocities that outperform linear methods like scVelo on complex topologies. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100581
skills.summary: Train a LatentVelo variational autoencoder to embed cells into a dynamics-based latent space and model differentiation with neural ordinary differential equations, yielding latent velocities, latent trajectories, and gene velocities that outperform linear methods like scVelo on complex topologies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets that are well described by the linear steady-state or dynamical model with a single lineage and time-independent rates, where scVelo suffices Situations requiring a single initial latent state assumption to be violated in a known way, e.g. disconnected sparse clusters like microglia that the model misassigns as trajectory start points Analyses requiring stochastic dynamics or count normalization, which LatentVelo explicitly does not address

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices from multiple batches (e.g., pancreas 16,382 cells, immune 33,506 cells, heart atlas 486,134 cells) need batch-corrected latent embeddings for atlas-level or cross-species integration.
skills.name: variational-autoencoder-latent-embedding-learning
skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-latent-embedding-learning Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices from multiple batches (e.g., pancreas 16,382 cells, immune 33,506 cells, heart atlas 486,134 cells) need batch-corrected latent embeddings for atlas-level or cross-species integration. The number of batches is unknown — the model assumes prior knowledge of the number of batches, and unsupervised treatment of batch information is unexplored Input is a multiomic (e.g., RNA+ATAC) dataset — the multiomic extension of scDREAMER is not yet implemented (planned future work) Batches carry a hierarchical structure (e.g., nested batch variables) — utilization of hierarchical batch structure is not yet supported http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Learn batch-ignorant low-dimensional cellular embeddings from scRNA-seq count matrices by training the scDREAMER adversarial variational autoencoder: encoder E maps {x, s} to {μz, σz, μl, σl}, a ZINB decoder D reconstructs expression, and adversarial training of a discriminator (Bhattacharyya loss) plus a batch classifier B removes batch effects while conserving biology. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43590-8
skills.summary: Learn batch-ignorant low-dimensional cellular embeddings from scRNA-seq count matrices by training the scDREAMER adversarial variational autoencoder: encoder E maps {x, s} to {μz, σz, μl, σl}, a ZINB decoder D reconstructs expression, and adversarial training of a discriminator (Bhattacharyya loss) plus a batch classifier B removes batch effects while conserving biology.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The number of batches is unknown — the model assumes prior knowledge of the number of batches, and unsupervised treatment of batch information is unexplored Input is a multiomic (e.g., RNA+ATAC) dataset — the multiomic extension of scDREAMER is not yet implemented (planned future work) Batches carry a hierarchical structure (e.g., nested batch variables) — utilization of hierarchical batch structure is not yet supported

skills.name: variational-autoencoder-latent-sampling
skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-latent-sampling Use when a generative model must select a discrete subset of k genes (or features) during training and the selection must remain differentiable — e.g., scRNA-seq AnnData in adata.X with cell-type labels in adata.obs['annotation']. When a deterministic post-hoc ranking of markers suffices (e.g. rank-correlation methods like RankCorr or cosine-similarity methods like COSG) rather than a selector jointly trained inside a generative model. When the goal is whole-transcriptome reconstruction with all genes retained rather than selection of a minimal k-marker set. When the selection step does not need to be differentiable or trained with gradient-based optimization together with a downstream objective. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Implements MarkerMap's differentiable discrete marker selector: a temperature-annealed Gumbel-Softmax-style sampling module draws γ(k) gene-subset samples inside a VAE so the selection of k markers is optimized end-to-end with the downstream predictive/reconstruction objectives. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00339-3
skills.summary: Implements MarkerMap's differentiable discrete marker selector: a temperature-annealed Gumbel-Softmax-style sampling module draws γ(k) gene-subset samples inside a VAE so the selection of k markers is optimized end-to-end with the downstream predictive/reconstruction objectives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a deterministic post-hoc ranking of markers suffices (e.g. rank-correlation methods like RankCorr or cosine-similarity methods like COSG) rather than a selector jointly trained inside a generative model. When the goal is whole-transcriptome reconstruction with all genes retained rather than selection of a minimal k-marker set. When the selection step does not need to be differentiable or trained with gradient-based optimization together with a downstream objective.

skills.description: Use when you have a high-dimensional scRNA-seq or proteomics expression matrix (e.g. tsv/csv of gene x condition values, AnnData-compatible) and need a ranked protein-protein association network, especially when simple co-expression on the raw matrix is degraded by sparseness and redundancy.

skills.summary: Infers protein functional association networks by compressing high-dimensional scRNA-seq or proteomics data into a dense, low-dimensional VAE latent space (via favapy) and ranking protein pairs by Pearson correlation of their latent representations. Rationale: raw omics data are too sparse and redundant for direct co-expression analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to retrieve existing literature-curated interactions rather than infer new associations from omics data — existing high-quality networks are heavily biased toward well-studied proteins. skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-pytorch-implementation Use when reconstructing or extending VEGA: you have a Scanpy-wrapped single-cell dataset plus a GMT gene-module file and need a PyTorch VAE whose decoder mirrors user-provided gene modules. skills.search_text: vascular-roi-annotation-and-arterial-smc-identification Use when a Visium ST section contains a vascular region of interest and you must assign SMC subtype identity (arterial vs venous) using an unpaired snRNA-seq atlas reference and single-cell-resolution decomposition output. The reference atlas does not define separate arterial and venous SMC subtypes, so the TAGLN/LGR6 signature cannot discriminate them The goal is spot-level deconvolution proportions only, not single-cell-resolution subtype localization — RCTD, Cell2location or CARD suffice The tissue lacks a histological image and only DAPI or no image is available, complicating nucleus segmentation and per-spot cell-count estimation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identifies the arterial vs venous identity of smooth muscle cells within a vascular region of interest on human heart Visium data by decomposing spots to single cells with SpatialScope and checking the TAGLN-high/LGR6-low signature against the snRNA-seq atlas-defined arterial SMC subtype. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: Identifies the arterial vs venous identity of smooth muscle cells within a vascular region of interest on human heart Visium data by decomposing spots to single cells with SpatialScope and checking the TAGLN-high/LGR6-low signature against the snRNA-seq atlas-defined arterial SMC subtype.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference atlas does not define separate arterial and venous SMC subtypes, so the TAGLN/LGR6 signature cannot discriminate them The goal is spot-level deconvolution proportions only, not single-cell-resolution subtype localization — RCTD, Cell2location or CARD suffice The tissue lacks a histological image and only DAPI or no image is available, complicating nucleus segmentation and per-spot cell-count estimation

skills.description: Use when performing allele-specific read assignment from RNA-seq FASTQ data: a per-sample VCF genotype directory and a reference FASTA are available and reads must be aligned to both haplotype-modified personal genomes.
skills.name: vcf-parsing-and-haplotype-genome-construction
skills.search_text: vcf-parsing-and-haplotype-genome-construction Use when performing allele-specific read assignment from RNA-seq FASTQ data: a per-sample VCF genotype directory and a reference FASTA are available and reads must be aligned to both haplotype-modified personal genomes. The analysis goal is standard bulk RNA-seq differential expression or splicing quantification without allele-specific assignment — a single reference-genome STAR alignment suffices and personalization adds cost The genotype data are not phased heterozygous SNVs (e.g., haploid calls, structural variants only, or a common sample lacking a per-sample VCF subdirectory matching the sample name) SNPs of interest lie within or too far from alternative exons for short reads to carry them alongside the splice event — PAIRADISE cannot analyze such SNPs even with personalized genomes http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Constructs haplotype-modified personal genomes by substituting phased heterozygous alleles from per-chromosome VCF genotype files into the hg19.fa reference sequence, then builds STAR (>= 2.6.0a) indices for each haplotype genome using the Homo_sapiens.Ensembl.GRCh37.75.gtf annotation. This is the personalization foundation of the rPGA-style pipeline that PAIRADISE uses before read assignment to haplotypes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2020.07.005
skills.summary: Constructs haplotype-modified personal genomes by substituting phased heterozygous alleles from per-chromosome VCF genotype files into the hg19.fa reference sequence, then builds STAR (>= 2.6.0a) indices for each haplotype genome using the Homo_sapiens.Ensembl.GRCh37.75.gtf annotation. This is the personalization foundation of the rPGA-style pipeline that PAIRADISE uses before read assignment to haplotypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is standard bulk RNA-seq differential expression or splicing quantification without allele-specific assignment — a single reference-genome STAR alignment suffices and personalization adds cost The genotype data are not phased heterozygous SNVs (e.g., haploid calls, structural variants only, or a common sample lacking a per-sample VCF subdirectory matching the sample name) SNPs of interest lie within or too far from alternative exons for short reads to carry them alongside the splice event — PAIRADISE cannot analyze such SNPs even with personalized genomes

skills.description: Use when consolidating variant calls from multiple callers/modules in a pipeline (e.g. ScanNeo2's SplAdder, ScanExitron, transIndel, Mutect2, Arriba outputs) into per-variant-type VCFs that must carry caller-provenance INFO keys (GRP, SRC) for source-attributed downstream analysis.
skills.name: vcf-provenance-augmentation-and-merging
skills.search_text: vcf-provenance-augmentation-and-merging Use when consolidating variant calls from multiple callers/modules in a pipeline (e.g. ScanNeo2's SplAdder, ScanExitron, transIndel, Mutect2, Arriba outputs) into per-variant-type VCFs that must carry caller-provenance INFO keys (GRP, SRC) for source-attributed downstream analysis. The input is a single caller's already-annotated final VCF with no multi-module merging or source attribution needed The workflow config has all module activate flags off or only a single caller is in use, so no cross-module provenance (GRP/SRC) needs to be maintained Downstream consumers ignore variant origin and only need a flat, caller-agnostic variant list http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A ScanNeo2 pattern in which variant calls from independent detection modules (alternative splicing, exitron-splicing, long/short indels, SNVs, gene fusions) are converted to VCF, augmented with GRP (group) and SRC (caller source) INFO keys, and merged into per-variant-type VCFs so downstream neoantigen prediction can trace every peptide back to its originating caller. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad659
skills.summary: A ScanNeo2 pattern in which variant calls from independent detection modules (alternative splicing, exitron-splicing, long/short indels, SNVs, gene fusions) are converted to VCF, augmented with GRP (group) and SRC (caller source) INFO keys, and merged into per-variant-type VCFs so downstream neoantigen prediction can trace every peptide back to its originating caller.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single caller's already-annotated final VCF with no multi-module merging or source attribution needed The workflow config has all module activate flags off or only a single caller is in use, so no cross-module provenance (GRP/SRC) needs to be maintained Downstream consumers ignore variant origin and only need a flat, caller-agnostic variant list

skills.description: Use when a deconvoluted single-cell cluster VCF (e.g. cells_merge_clusters.vcf) must be matched against a WES reference VCF to compute matching-SNP fractions and identification likelihood ratios for each contributor.
skills.name: vcf-variant-comparison-against-wes-reference
skills.search_text: vcf-variant-comparison-against-wes-reference Use when a deconvoluted single-cell cluster VCF (e.g. cells_merge_clusters.vcf) must be matched against a WES reference VCF to compute matching-SNP fractions and identification likelihood ratios for each contributor. The query is sex or bio-geographic ancestry assignment rather than individual identification — those use the 1000G population analysis and Yleaf/haplogrep branches of step 2, not WES-reference matching The reference sample has not been WES-sequenced (or similarly densely genotyped) — the paper notes that because no universal identity SNPs are used, reference datasets must contain as many SNPs as possible Cells are not living (the 10X Genomics scRNA-seq platform requires live cells for successful genetic separation, so no cluster VCF can be produced) http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_2885 Matches identity SNPs from deconvoluted scRNA-seq cell-cluster VCFs against de-novo whole-exome sequencing (WES) reference VCFs to individually identify mixture contributors with likelihood ratios far above the court-acceptable 10E+9 threshold. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04557-z
skills.summary: Matches identity SNPs from deconvoluted scRNA-seq cell-cluster VCFs against de-novo whole-exome sequencing (WES) reference VCFs to individually identify mixture contributors with likelihood ratios far above the court-acceptable 10E+9 threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query is sex or bio-geographic ancestry assignment rather than individual identification — those use the 1000G population analysis and Yleaf/haplogrep branches of step 2, not WES-reference matching The reference sample has not been WES-sequenced (or similarly densely genotyped) — the paper notes that because no universal identity SNPs are used, reference datasets must contain as many SNPs as possible Cells are not living (the 10X Genomics scRNA-seq platform requires live cells for successful genetic separation, so no cluster VCF can be produced)

skills.description: Use when you have per-tissue multi-sample VCFs (e.g., GATK HaplotypeCaller g.vcf output merged by tissue) and need to remove low-quality variants, indels, indel-proximate and multiallelic SNPs before ASE or allele-count-based testing.
skills.name: vcf-variant-filtering
skills.search_text: vcf-variant-filtering Use when you have per-tissue multi-sample VCFs (e.g., GATK HaplotypeCaller g.vcf output merged by tissue) and need to remove low-quality variants, indels, indel-proximate and multiallelic SNPs before ASE or allele-count-based testing. Your variants come from whole-genome/genotyping-array data rather than RNA-seq-aligned reads — the read-count thresholds (20 reads) and indel exclusion (75 bp read length) are calibrated to RNA-seq depth and alignment error You need multiallelic or indel-level ASE quantification — VADT explicitly removes indels, multiallelic variants, and SNPs within 75 bp of an indel Input VCFs are not in the GATK HaplotypeCaller format — the README warns VCFs from other callers 'could potentially have some bugs' http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Derive per-tissue informative biallelic SNP sets from RNA-seq-derived VCFs by combining GATK hard filters (Fisher Strand > 30.0, Quality Depth < 2.0, Depth < 100) with VADT's variant- and sample-level filtering, so that only heterozygous, well-covered SNPs are testable for allele-specific expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-83459-8
skills.summary: Derive per-tissue informative biallelic SNP sets from RNA-seq-derived VCFs by combining GATK hard filters (Fisher Strand > 30.0, Quality Depth < 2.0, Depth < 100) with VADT's variant- and sample-level filtering, so that only heterozygous, well-covered SNPs are testable for allele-specific expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your variants come from whole-genome/genotyping-array data rather than RNA-seq-aligned reads — the read-count thresholds (20 reads) and indel exclusion (75 bp read length) are calibrated to RNA-seq depth and alignment error You need multiallelic or indel-level ASE quantification — VADT explicitly removes indels, multiallelic variants, and SNPs within 75 bp of an indel Input VCFs are not in the GATK HaplotypeCaller format — the README warns VCFs from other callers 'could potentially have some bugs'

skills.description: Use when a raw multi-sample VCF (e.g., from GATK HaplotypeCaller) must be cleaned of low-confidence, indel-proximate, multiallelic, and homozygous calls before per-sample allele-based statistics such as ASE binomial tests.
skills.name: vcf-variant-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: vcf-variant-quality-filtering Use when a raw multi-sample VCF (e.g., from GATK HaplotypeCaller) must be cleaned of low-confidence, indel-proximate, multiallelic, and homozygous calls before per-sample allele-based statistics such as ASE binomial tests. The input is a genotype-array VCF needing call-rate filtering instead (e.g., remove SNPs with < 97% call rates from the 600K Axiom panel), which is a different filtering regime The VCF is already restricted to informative testable biallelic SNPs and re-filtering would discard valid variants The downstream analysis requires indel or multiallelic variants, which this filter removes by design http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 A filtering scheme for multi-sample VCFs that removes GATK-flagged variants, indels and SNPs within 75 bp of indels, multiallelic SNPs, variants with Phred quality < 20, and per-sample calls that are homozygous, low-coverage (< 20 reads), or have minor allele count < 1%, leaving only 'informative' biallelic SNPs for downstream statistical testing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-83459-8
skills.summary: A filtering scheme for multi-sample VCFs that removes GATK-flagged variants, indels and SNPs within 75 bp of indels, multiallelic SNPs, variants with Phred quality < 20, and per-sample calls that are homozygous, low-coverage (< 20 reads), or have minor allele count < 1%, leaving only 'informative' biallelic SNPs for downstream statistical testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a genotype-array VCF needing call-rate filtering instead (e.g., remove SNPs with < 97% call rates from the 600K Axiom panel), which is a different filtering regime The VCF is already restricted to informative testable biallelic SNPs and re-filtering would discard valid variants The downstream analysis requires indel or multiallelic variants, which this filter removes by design

skills.description: Use when a paired scRNA-seq + scVDJ-seq SingleCellExperiment object (e.g. Suo et al. fetal immune atlas with contig data merged via scRepertoire) must be filtered to cells with productive, unambiguous immune receptors before VDJ pseudobulking.
skills.name: vdj-chain-productivity-filtering
skills.search_text: vdj-chain-productivity-filtering Use when a paired scRNA-seq + scVDJ-seq SingleCellExperiment object (e.g. Suo et al. fetal immune atlas with contig data merged via scRepertoire) must be filtered to cells with productive, unambiguous immune receptors before VDJ pseudobulking. Input cells already lack paired VDJ contig data or only BCR sequencing is available (e.g. Bandyopadhyay et al. / Baccin et al. datasets lack BCR sequencing for B cell workflows) The dataset contains only a very small number of target cells (e.g. Tonglin et al. with 972 healthy B cells), where filtering would leave insufficient material for downstream miloR neighbourhood construction You need Dandelion's additional filtering or network-generation functionality, which dandelionR has not yet implemented http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A preprocessing skill from the dandelionR workflow that filters single-cell VDJ-seq data using dandelionR::setupVdjPseudobulk, removing cells with non-productive immune receptors and ambiguous VDJ chain status so only cells with relevant or complete VDJ information proceed to trajectory analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2025.06.047
skills.summary: A preprocessing skill from the dandelionR workflow that filters single-cell VDJ-seq data using dandelionR::setupVdjPseudobulk, removing cells with non-productive immune receptors and ambiguous VDJ chain status so only cells with relevant or complete VDJ information proceed to trajectory analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input cells already lack paired VDJ contig data or only BCR sequencing is available (e.g. Bandyopadhyay et al. / Baccin et al. datasets lack BCR sequencing for B cell workflows) The dataset contains only a very small number of target cells (e.g. Tonglin et al. with 972 healthy B cells), where filtering would leave insufficient material for downstream miloR neighbourhood construction You need Dandelion's additional filtering or network-generation functionality, which dandelionR has not yet implemented

skills.description: Use when a SingleCellExperiment with a miloR-pseudobulked VDJ feature space (e.g. pb.milo from vdjPseudobulk, mode_option='abT') needs pseudotime and CD4/CD8 branching probabilities projected back to cells.
skills.name: vdj-feature-space-trajectory-analysis
skills.search_text: vdj-feature-space-trajectory-analysis Use when a SingleCellExperiment with a miloR-pseudobulked VDJ feature space (e.g. pb.milo from vdjPseudobulk, mode_option='abT') needs pseudotime and CD4/CD8 branching probabilities projected back to cells. The dataset has a cyclic trajectory (e.g. B cell receptor editing), which cannot be represented by absorbing Markov chains. The data topology is more complex than a bifurcation or linear trajectory, since the destiny-based diffusion map limits inference to bifurcation or linear topologies. The input lacks a constructed VDJ feature space (no vdjPseudobulk Feature_space assay) and only a gene-expression matrix is available — that is the weaker baseline this skill is meant to improve upon. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Trajectory inference on a VDJ feature space in R, replicating Dandelion/Palantir's workflow by computing diffusion maps (destiny), diffusion pseudotime (DPT), and branch probabilities via an absorbing Markov chain (dandelionR::markovProbability) on pseudobulked VDJ features. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2025.06.047
skills.summary: Trajectory inference on a VDJ feature space in R, replicating Dandelion/Palantir's workflow by computing diffusion maps (destiny), diffusion pseudotime (DPT), and branch probabilities via an absorbing Markov chain (dandelionR::markovProbability) on pseudobulked VDJ features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has a cyclic trajectory (e.g. B cell receptor editing), which cannot be represented by absorbing Markov chains. The data topology is more complex than a bifurcation or linear trajectory, since the destiny-based diffusion map limits inference to bifurcation or linear topologies. The input lacks a constructed VDJ feature space (no vdjPseudobulk Feature_space assay) and only a gene-expression matrix is available — that is the weaker baseline this skill is meant to improve upon.

skills.description: Use when single-cell VDJ data has been pseudobulked into miloR neighbourhoods and you need a gene-usage feature matrix (VDJ genes x pseudobulks) for downstream PCA/diffusion-map trajectory analysis.
skills.name: vdj-gene-usage-pseudobulk-tabulation
skills.search_text: vdj-gene-usage-pseudobulk-tabulation Use when single-cell VDJ data has been pseudobulked into miloR neighbourhoods and you need a gene-usage feature matrix (VDJ genes x pseudobulks) for downstream PCA/diffusion-map trajectory analysis. Input is a raw AIRR/contig list that has not yet been combined into a SingleCellExperiment and pseudobulked into miloR neighbourhoods (use combineTCR/combineExpression and setupVdjPseudobulk first) Data contains no productive TCR information or too few cells for neighbourhood construction (e.g. only 972 healthy B cells as in Tonglin et al.) The goal is per-cell VDJ usage rather than pseudobulk-level feature space construction http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Tabulates V/D/J gene usage per miloR-derived pseudobulk neighbourhood using dandelionR::vdjPseudobulk, converting single-cell VDJ calls into a continuous VDJ feature space (160 V/D/J genes x 1516 pseudobulks on the Suo et al. abT data) that can be combined with gene expression for trajectory analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2025.06.047
skills.summary: Tabulates V/D/J gene usage per miloR-derived pseudobulk neighbourhood using dandelionR::vdjPseudobulk, converting single-cell VDJ calls into a continuous VDJ feature space (160 V/D/J genes x 1516 pseudobulks on the Suo et al. abT data) that can be combined with gene expression for trajectory analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw AIRR/contig list that has not yet been combined into a SingleCellExperiment and pseudobulked into miloR neighbourhoods (use combineTCR/combineExpression and setupVdjPseudobulk first) Data contains no productive TCR information or too few cells for neighbourhood construction (e.g. only 972 healthy B cells as in Tonglin et al.) The goal is per-cell VDJ usage rather than pseudobulk-level feature space construction

skills.description: Use when analyzing single-cell T cell scRNA-seq (Smart-Seq FASTQ) and the goal is to detect V(D)J recombination fusions marking MAIT cells that bulk RNA fusion methods miss.
skills.name: vdj-recombination-identification
skills.search_text: vdj-recombination-identification Use when analyzing single-cell T cell scRNA-seq (Smart-Seq FASTQ) and the goal is to detect V(D)J recombination fusions marking MAIT cells that bulk RNA fusion methods miss. Data are bulk RNA-seq rather than single-cell Smart-Seq scRNA-seq; scFusion is designed for Smart-Seq single-cell data, not 10X or bulk inputs FASTQ files are named *_1.fq instead of *_1.fastq, which the scFusion pipeline explicitly disallows The goal is to detect rare fusions such as TRAJ20-TRAV1-2 in a small cell population — scFusion may miss these (TRAJ20-TRAV1-2 was not identified, possibly because it was rare in MAIT cells) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 Detect invariant TCR V(D)J gene recombinations (e.g., TRAJ33-TRAV1-2, TRAJ12-TRAV1-2) from Smart-Seq scRNA-seq data using scFusion, where bulk-oriented fusion callers like STAR-Fusion fail, and validate them against the MAIT cell marker SLC4A10 via Fisher's exact test. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28661-6
skills.summary: Detect invariant TCR V(D)J gene recombinations (e.g., TRAJ33-TRAV1-2, TRAJ12-TRAV1-2) from Smart-Seq scRNA-seq data using scFusion, where bulk-oriented fusion callers like STAR-Fusion fail, and validate them against the MAIT cell marker SLC4A10 via Fisher's exact test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are bulk RNA-seq rather than single-cell Smart-Seq scRNA-seq; scFusion is designed for Smart-Seq single-cell data, not 10X or bulk inputs FASTQ files are named *_1.fq instead of *_1.fastq, which the scFusion pipeline explicitly disallows The goal is to detect rare fusions such as TRAJ20-TRAV1-2 in a small cell population — scFusion may miss these (TRAJ20-TRAV1-2 was not identified, possibly because it was rare in MAIT cells)

skills.search_text: vdj-trajectory-inference-cross-language-reproducibility Use when porting a Python-based scVDJ-seq trajectory pipeline (Dandelion/Palantir) to R (dandelionR) and you need to quantify cross-language output concordance via cell counts, Pearson/Kendall correlations, and Lin's CCC. Input data has a cyclic trajectory (e.g. B cell receptor editing) that cannot be represented by absorbing Markov chains, or a topology more complex than bifurcation/linear, since destiny-based diffusion map limits trajectory inference to bifurcation or linear topologies The dataset lacks paired BCR/TCR sequencing or has too few cells (e.g. only 972 healthy B cells in Tonglin et al.), which is insufficient for miloR neighbourhood construction You only need to run a single-language workflow and have no cross-implementation outputs to compare — concordance benchmarking requires both R and Python results on the same input data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 Reproduce and benchmark a VDJ feature-space trajectory analysis workflow (dandelionR in R) against its original Python implementation (Dandelion/Palantir) on the Suo et al. fetal immune T-cell dataset, quantifying concordance of per-cell pseudotime and branch probabilities. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2025.06.047
skills.summary: Reproduce and benchmark a VDJ feature-space trajectory analysis workflow (dandelionR in R) against its original Python implementation (Dandelion/Palantir) on the Suo et al. fetal immune T-cell dataset, quantifying concordance of per-cell pseudotime and branch probabilities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has a cyclic trajectory (e.g. B cell receptor editing) that cannot be represented by absorbing Markov chains, or a topology more complex than bifurcation/linear, since destiny-based diffusion map limits trajectory inference to bifurcation or linear topologies The dataset lacks paired BCR/TCR sequencing or has too few cells (e.g. only 972 healthy B cells in Tonglin et al.), which is insufficient for miloR neighbourhood construction You only need to run a single-language workflow and have no cross-implementation outputs to compare — concordance benchmarking requires both R and Python results on the same input data

skills.description: Use when benchmarking RNA velocity models on multi-batch data and you need to quantify whether inferred velocities remain directionally coherent after batch correction, not just whether cell states are integrated.
skills.name: velocity-directional-coherence-scoring-cbdir-iccoh
skills.search_text: velocity-directional-coherence-scoring-cbdir-iccoh Use when benchmarking RNA velocity models on multi-batch data and you need to quantify whether inferred velocities remain directionally coherent after batch correction, not just whether cell states are integrated. Single-batch datasets where batch-correction/integration metrics (kBET, iLISI, cLISI) are undefined or trivial and velocity metrics alone suffice Datasets lacking spliced/unspliced layers (e.g. only a raw count matrix), since RNA velocity scoring requires spliced_key='spliced' and unspliced_key='unspliced' Questions about trajectory shape or latent time accuracy rather than velocity directional coherence under batch correction http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Scores RNA velocity quality on batch-corrected cell states using directional-coherence metrics (CBDir, ICCoh, and nearest-neighbor velocity cosine similarity from scVelo velocity graphs), alongside batch-integration metrics (kBET, iLISI, cLISI from scib), to test whether a model such as LatentVelo batch-corrects velocities better than gene-space corrections like ComBat or scGen applied to UniTVelo. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100581
skills.summary: Scores RNA velocity quality on batch-corrected cell states using directional-coherence metrics (CBDir, ICCoh, and nearest-neighbor velocity cosine similarity from scVelo velocity graphs), alongside batch-integration metrics (kBET, iLISI, cLISI from scib), to test whether a model such as LatentVelo batch-corrects velocities better than gene-space corrections like ComBat or scGen applied to UniTVelo.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-batch datasets where batch-correction/integration metrics (kBET, iLISI, cLISI) are undefined or trivial and velocity metrics alone suffice Datasets lacking spliced/unspliced layers (e.g. only a raw count matrix), since RNA velocity scoring requires spliced_key='spliced' and unspliced_key='unspliced' Questions about trajectory shape or latent time accuracy rather than velocity directional coherence under batch correction
