skills.description: Use when you need to test whether inferred transcriptional velocities (e.g., from scKINETICS on raw UMI counts such as GSE207943) are stable under technical noise in gene expression, specifically perturbed transcript capture rates from downsampling.
skills.name: velocity-model-refitting-with-fixed-mask
skills.search_text: velocity-model-refitting-with-fixed-mask Use when you need to test whether inferred transcriptional velocities (e.g., from scKINETICS on raw UMI counts such as GSE207943) are stable under technical noise in gene expression, specifically perturbed transcript capture rates from downsampling. When testing biological (not technical) robustness — the perturbation here models transcript-capture noise via downsampling of raw counts, not biological variability between samples When the regulatory mask or model parameters should be re-optimized per fit — this skill requires a fixed mask and fixed parameters so only the count perturbation differs When velocity estimates do not yet exist for an unperturbed reference fit — the cosine deviation is always measured against the original fit http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A robustness-testing skill for dynamical velocity models: perturb raw single-cell counts (e.g., random downsampling to simulate reduced sequencing depth), refit scKINETICS with the same fixed regulatory mask and parameter settings, and quantify how far perturbed per-cell velocities deviate from the original fit via cosine deviation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: A robustness-testing skill for dynamical velocity models: perturb raw single-cell counts (e.g., random downsampling to simulate reduced sequencing depth), refit scKINETICS with the same fixed regulatory mask and parameter settings, and quantify how far perturbed per-cell velocities deviate from the original fit via cosine deviation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When testing biological (not technical) robustness — the perturbation here models transcript-capture noise via downsampling of raw counts, not biological variability between samples When the regulatory mask or model parameters should be re-optimized per fit — this skill requires a fixed mask and fixed parameters so only the count perturbation differs When velocity estimates do not yet exist for an unperturbed reference fit — the cosine deviation is always measured against the original fit

skills.description: Use when assessing whether scKINETICS-inferred per-cell velocities and GRNs are stable to user-defined hyperparameter choices (initiating sigma) or perturbation of prior inputs (coexpression matrix A^), before trusting downstream regulator calls.
skills.name: velocity-recovery-benchmarking
skills.search_text: velocity-recovery-benchmarking Use when assessing whether scKINETICS-inferred per-cell velocities and GRNs are stable to user-defined hyperparameter choices (initiating sigma) or perturbation of prior inputs (coexpression matrix A^), before trusting downstream regulator calls. The goal is accuracy benchmarking of scKINETICS against other velocity methods (e.g. RNA velocity baselines) rather than internal parameter-sensitivity testing. The coexpression prior A^ or manifold-constraint sigma will not be perturbed because a single standard fit suffices for the analysis at hand. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A robustness-benchmarking procedure for scKINETICS that quantifies how inferred per-cell velocities and the governing gene regulatory network respond to perturbation of the manifold-constraint width sigma and to Gaussian noise added to the coexpression prior A^, using cosine distance of refitted velocities against a reference fit. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: A robustness-benchmarking procedure for scKINETICS that quantifies how inferred per-cell velocities and the governing gene regulatory network respond to perturbation of the manifold-constraint width sigma and to Gaussian noise added to the coexpression prior A^, using cosine distance of refitted velocities against a reference fit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is accuracy benchmarking of scKINETICS against other velocity methods (e.g. RNA velocity baselines) rather than internal parameter-sensitivity testing. The coexpression prior A^ or manifold-constraint sigma will not be perturbed because a single standard fit suffices for the analysis at hand.

skills.description: Use when an AnnData object contains estimated velocities and cell-type labels and you need to visually verify that an inferred trajectory (e.g., OPC→OL maturation, retinal branches PR/RGC/AC-HC, Fev+→Delta transitions) is recovered.
skills.name: velocity-stream-visualization
skills.search_text: velocity-stream-visualization Use when an AnnData object contains estimated velocities and cell-type labels and you need to visually verify that an inferred trajectory (e.g., OPC→OL maturation, retinal branches PR/RGC/AC-HC, Fev+→Delta transitions) is recovered. The AnnData lacks a velocity layer because utv.run_model or scVelo has not yet been fit — run the model first Quantitative comparison across methods is the goal alone — use utv.evaluate CBDir scores rather than relying only on stream plots Only per-gene phase-portrait dynamics are needed — use utv.pl.plot_range(gene_name, adata, velo, ...) instead of embedding streams http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Render RNA velocity fields as streamline embedding plots (and latent-time scatter plots) using scVelo's plotting API on AnnData objects processed by UniTVelo or scVelo, to visually assess recovered differentiation trajectories and branch structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34188-7
skills.summary: Render RNA velocity fields as streamline embedding plots (and latent-time scatter plots) using scVelo's plotting API on AnnData objects processed by UniTVelo or scVelo, to visually assess recovered differentiation trajectories and branch structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The AnnData lacks a velocity layer because utv.run_model or scVelo has not yet been fit — run the model first Quantitative comparison across methods is the goal alone — use utv.evaluate CBDir scores rather than relying only on stream plots Only per-gene phase-portrait dynamics are needed — use utv.pl.plot_range(gene_name, adata, velo, ...) instead of embedding streams

skills.description: Use when comparing velocity inference methods (e.g. scKINETICS, scVelo, VeloVAE, UniTVelo) on the same single-cell dataset and you need a quantitative, cluster-resolved measure of velocity-field smoothness to show one method's vectors are more locally concordant.
skills.name: velocity-vector-nearest-neighbor-analysis
skills.search_text: velocity-vector-nearest-neighbor-analysis Use when comparing velocity inference methods (e.g. scKINETICS, scVelo, VeloVAE, UniTVelo) on the same single-cell dataset and you need a quantitative, cluster-resolved measure of velocity-field smoothness to show one method's vectors are more locally concordant. You have only one velocity method and no baselines to compare — the metric is a relative benchmarking measure, not an absolute quality certificate. The goal is gene regulatory network inference or regulator identification (scKINETICS's GRN/EM output) rather than velocity-field consistency assessment. Cluster annotations are unavailable or unreliable, since cluster-level aggregation is a core part of the reported analysis. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantifies local consistency of inferred single-cell RNA velocity vectors by measuring mean cosine distance between each cell's velocity and those of its k=30 nearest neighbors, per method and per cluster. This benchmarking metric exposed scKINETICS's locally concordant velocity field relative to scVelo, VeloVAE, and UniTVelo. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Quantifies local consistency of inferred single-cell RNA velocity vectors by measuring mean cosine distance between each cell's velocity and those of its k=30 nearest neighbors, per method and per cluster. This benchmarking metric exposed scKINETICS's locally concordant velocity field relative to scVelo, VeloVAE, and UniTVelo.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only one velocity method and no baselines to compare — the metric is a relative benchmarking measure, not an absolute quality certificate. The goal is gene regulatory network inference or regulator identification (scKINETICS's GRN/EM output) rather than velocity-field consistency assessment. Cluster annotations are unavailable or unreliable, since cluster-level aggregation is a core part of the reported analysis.

skills.description: Use when starting from raw single-cell RNA-seq reads (e.g. Burns et al. GSE71982, 157 neonatal mouse inner ear cells) and you need spliced/unspliced count layers for RNA velocity estimation and Cytopath trajectory inference.
skills.name: velocyto-spliced-unspliced-count-matrix-generation
skills.search_text: velocyto-spliced-unspliced-count-matrix-generation Use when starting from raw single-cell RNA-seq reads (e.g. Burns et al. GSE71982, 157 neonatal mouse inner ear cells) and you need spliced/unspliced count layers for RNA velocity estimation and Cytopath trajectory inference. Spliced/unspliced count layers already exist (e.g. a loom or h5ad from velocyto is already provided) — go directly to scvelo/Cytopath Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable and the underlying RNA velocity estimation is expected to be faulty, e.g. features with time-dependent degradation rates — the article's authors do not recommend trajectory inference in such cases http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generate spliced/unspliced/ambiguous count matrices from raw single-cell reads with velocyto, supplying the transcriptional-activity layers that RNA-velocity-based trajectory inference (scvelo + Cytopath) requires. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Generate spliced/unspliced/ambiguous count matrices from raw single-cell reads with velocyto, supplying the transcriptional-activity layers that RNA-velocity-based trajectory inference (scvelo + Cytopath) requires.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spliced/unspliced count layers already exist (e.g. a loom or h5ad from velocyto is already provided) — go directly to scvelo/Cytopath Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable and the underlying RNA velocity estimation is expected to be faulty, e.g. features with time-dependent degradation rates — the article's authors do not recommend trajectory inference in such cases

skills.description: Use when comparing lists of significant features (e.g., ASE SNPs or ASE genes) across two or more tissues or conditions and you need intersection counts, overlap fractions, and Venn diagrams to report shared vs. tissue-specific results.
skills.name: venn-diagram-overlap-visualization
skills.search_text: venn-diagram-overlap-visualization Use when comparing lists of significant features (e.g., ASE SNPs or ASE genes) across two or more tissues or conditions and you need intersection counts, overlap fractions, and Venn diagrams to report shared vs. tissue-specific results. The input is a single tissue/condition list with nothing to intersect — no multi-set overlap exists to compute The features being compared are not commensurable across tissues (e.g., different genome builds or coordinate systems not lifted over), since Bedtools intersection requires matching coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantify and visualize set overlap of allele-specific expression (ASE) results across multiple tissues at both the SNP and gene level, reproducing the broiler chicken study's 3.7% three-tissue ASE SNP overlap and its rise to 20.1% when ASE SNPs are aggregated to genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-83459-8
skills.summary: Quantify and visualize set overlap of allele-specific expression (ASE) results across multiple tissues at both the SNP and gene level, reproducing the broiler chicken study's 3.7% three-tissue ASE SNP overlap and its rise to 20.1% when ASE SNPs are aggregated to genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single tissue/condition list with nothing to intersect — no multi-set overlap exists to compute The features being compared are not commensurable across tissues (e.g., different genome builds or coordinate systems not lifted over), since Bedtools intersection requires matching coordinates

skills.description: Use when a CLASH/qCLASH workflow requires reading predicted secondary-structure data in Vienna (dot-bracket) or CT format, or pairing each fold record with its corresponding hyb record (e.g., to detect hyb/Vienna sequence mismatches before analysis).
skills.name: vienna-dot-bracket-fold-parsing
skills.search_text: vienna-dot-bracket-fold-parsing Use when a CLASH/qCLASH workflow requires reading predicted secondary-structure data in Vienna (dot-bracket) or CT format, or pairing each fold record with its corresponding hyb record (e.g., to detect hyb/Vienna sequence mismatches before analysis). Input is a plain hyb file with no associated Vienna/CT fold data and only type/miRNA or target analyses are needed — the hyb-only HybFile iterator suffices. Data are raw sequencing reads (FASTQ) or other non-hybrid formats — hybkit is specific to hyb-format chimeric RNA data from RNA proximity-ligation methods. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Parses Vienna-format files line-by-line into FoldRecord objects carrying dot-bracket secondary-structure data using the hybkit API (ViennaFile), enabling lockstep iteration with hyb records via HybFoldIter for validation and fold-aware analysis of chimeric RNA hybrid data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad721
skills.summary: Parses Vienna-format files line-by-line into FoldRecord objects carrying dot-bracket secondary-structure data using the hybkit API (ViennaFile), enabling lockstep iteration with hyb records via HybFoldIter for validation and fold-aware analysis of chimeric RNA hybrid data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a plain hyb file with no associated Vienna/CT fold data and only type/miRNA or target analyses are needed — the hyb-only HybFile iterator suffices. Data are raw sequencing reads (FASTQ) or other non-hybrid formats — hybkit is specific to hyb-format chimeric RNA data from RNA proximity-ligation methods.

skills.description: Use when a qCLASH/CLASH analysis requires each hyb-format hybrid record to carry its predicted folding pattern (dot-bracket) and energy from a paired Vienna or CT file, e.g. before Fold Analysis of miRNA folding patterns.
skills.name: vienna-fold-annotation-merging
skills.search_text: vienna-fold-annotation-merging Use when a qCLASH/CLASH analysis requires each hyb-format hybrid record to carry its predicted folding pattern (dot-bracket) and energy from a paired Vienna or CT file, e.g. before Fold Analysis of miRNA folding patterns. The hyb file has no paired Vienna/CT fold file, so records cannot be matched by identifier and no fold annotation can be merged. The goal is filtering rather than annotation — hyb_filter operations like 'any_seg_contains kshv' or duplicate/ribosomal/mitochondrial removal do not require fold merging. Input fold data is not in Vienna or CT format, since HybFoldIter pairing is defined for HybFile with ViennaFile/CTFile iterators. http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_0097 Merges predicted secondary-structure annotations (Vienna dot-bracket strings and Gibbs free-energy values) from fold files into hyb-format hybrid records using hybkit's HybFoldIter concurrent file iterator, with sequence-mismatch checking between paired hyb and fold records. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad721
skills.summary: Merges predicted secondary-structure annotations (Vienna dot-bracket strings and Gibbs free-energy values) from fold files into hyb-format hybrid records using hybkit's HybFoldIter concurrent file iterator, with sequence-mismatch checking between paired hyb and fold records.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The hyb file has no paired Vienna/CT fold file, so records cannot be matched by identifier and no fold annotation can be merged. The goal is filtering rather than annotation — hyb_filter operations like 'any_seg_contains kshv' or duplicate/ribosomal/mitochondrial removal do not require fold merging. Input fold data is not in Vienna or CT format, since HybFoldIter pairing is defined for HybFile with ViennaFile/CTFile iterators.

skills.description: Use when FiRE-scored rare PBMC cells need dendritic sub-type resolution against Villani reference signatures, e.g. when rare-cell clusters must be assigned to DC1/DC3/DC4/DC6 identities.
skills.name: villani-dendritic-subtype-classification
skills.search_text: villani-dendritic-subtype-classification Use when FiRE-scored rare PBMC cells need dendritic sub-type resolution against Villani reference signatures, e.g. when rare-cell clusters must be assigned to DC1/DC3/DC4/DC6 identities. The rare-cell set has not been produced by the upstream FiRE rareness-scoring step on the ~68k PBMC dataset — this skill operates on FiRE-detected cells, not raw counts. The goal is de novo discovery of novel rare cell types rather than assigning cells to known Villani dendritic sub-type reference signatures. Only abundant (non-rare) PBMC populations are of interest; clustering the full ~68k profile set is a different analysis. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Resolves Villani human blood dendritic cell sub-types (DC1, DC3, DC4, DC6) from FiRE-detected rare PBMC cells by clustering them with dropClust, isolating dendritic-exclusive clusters, and matching their differential genes to Villani reference signatures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07234-6
skills.summary: Resolves Villani human blood dendritic cell sub-types (DC1, DC3, DC4, DC6) from FiRE-detected rare PBMC cells by clustering them with dropClust, isolating dendritic-exclusive clusters, and matching their differential genes to Villani reference signatures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The rare-cell set has not been produced by the upstream FiRE rareness-scoring step on the ~68k PBMC dataset — this skill operates on FiRE-detected cells, not raw counts. The goal is de novo discovery of novel rare cell types rather than assigning cells to known Villani dendritic sub-type reference signatures. Only abundant (non-rare) PBMC populations are of interest; clustering the full ~68k profile set is a different analysis.

skills.description: Use when spatial scRNA-seq data with prior zone/position labels (e.g., villus zones) must be organized into a coherent linear differentiation trajectory, and PCA/UMAP alone give spatially incoherent orderings of landmark genes.
skills.name: villus-zone-trajectory-visualization
skills.search_text: villus-zone-trajectory-visualization Use when spatial scRNA-seq data with prior zone/position labels (e.g., villus zones) must be organized into a coherent linear differentiation trajectory, and PCA/UMAP alone give spatially incoherent orderings of landmark genes. Labels are unknown or an unbiased view of the data is preferable — the supervised approach is inappropriate in these situations More than ~100 features must be selected individually, since HSS is not feasible above ~100 dimensions (use PC scores as LDA predictors instead, or plain LDA) Preserving local data structure is critical — LDA maximizes class separability and comes at the expense of local structure http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Visualizes a linear differentiation trajectory of enterocytes along intestinal villi by applying LDA (without HSS feature selection) to the first 50 principal components of spatially reconstructed scRNA-seq data, using a priori villus-zone labels, and comparing the LD embedding against UMAP. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100536
skills.summary: Visualizes a linear differentiation trajectory of enterocytes along intestinal villi by applying LDA (without HSS feature selection) to the first 50 principal components of spatially reconstructed scRNA-seq data, using a priori villus-zone labels, and comparing the LD embedding against UMAP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Labels are unknown or an unbiased view of the data is preferable — the supervised approach is inappropriate in these situations More than ~100 features must be selected individually, since HSS is not feasible above ~100 dimensions (use PC scores as LDA predictors instead, or plain LDA) Preserving local data structure is critical — LDA maximizes class separability and comes at the expense of local structure

skills.description: Use when benchmarking multiple DA-testing methods on scRNA-Seq data and you need to display the full distribution of DA z-statistics per method/dataset to compare sensitivity.
skills.name: violin-plot-benchmark-visualization
skills.search_text: violin-plot-benchmark-visualization Use when benchmarking multiple DA-testing methods on scRNA-Seq data and you need to display the full distribution of DA z-statistics per method/dataset to compare sensitivity. When only point estimates or single p-values per method are available rather than distributions of z-statistics — a violin plot would convey false spread When comparing methods on different datasets or differently preprocessed inputs, since the comparison assumes identical Seurat processing (vst variable features, ScaleData, RunPCA, FindNeighbors k.param=20) per dataset http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates violin plots of differential-abundance (DA) z-statistics to visually and quantitatively compare DA-testing methods (ELVAR, DA-seq, Milo) across benchmark datasets, reproducing the paper's Fig. 5-style comparison of statistical significance and fraction of condition-enriched cells captured. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39017-z
skills.summary: Generates violin plots of differential-abundance (DA) z-statistics to visually and quantitatively compare DA-testing methods (ELVAR, DA-seq, Milo) across benchmark datasets, reproducing the paper's Fig. 5-style comparison of statistical significance and fraction of condition-enriched cells captured.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only point estimates or single p-values per method are available rather than distributions of z-statistics — a violin plot would convey false spread When comparing methods on different datasets or differently preprocessed inputs, since the comparison assumes identical Seurat processing (vst variable features, ScaleData, RunPCA, FindNeighbors k.param=20) per dataset

skills.description: Use when you have an annotated single-cell RNA-seq object (e.g. Seurat with cell-type labels) and need to determine which cell subsets show differential expression of specific marker genes.
skills.name: violin-plot-gene-expression-visualization
skills.search_text: violin-plot-gene-expression-visualization Use when you have an annotated single-cell RNA-seq object (e.g. Seurat with cell-type labels) and need to determine which cell subsets show differential expression of specific marker genes. Input is bulk RNA-seq or a processed differential-expression table with no per-cell resolution — box plots of the Streamlit app counts/anova folders are the appropriate visualization instead Clusters are not yet annotated from canonical markers; violin plots across unlabelled clusters cannot localize dysregulation to CD14+ subsets http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Visualize per-cell gene expression distributions across annotated immune cell types with Seurat's VlnPlot, as used to localize MCEMP1 upregulation and HLA-DRA downregulation to CD14+ monocytes in PBMCs of severe COVID-19 patients. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ebiom.2023.104472
skills.summary: Visualize per-cell gene expression distributions across annotated immune cell types with Seurat's VlnPlot, as used to localize MCEMP1 upregulation and HLA-DRA downregulation to CD14+ monocytes in PBMCs of severe COVID-19 patients.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-seq or a processed differential-expression table with no per-cell resolution — box plots of the Streamlit app counts/anova folders are the appropriate visualization instead Clusters are not yet annotated from canonical markers; violin plots across unlabelled clusters cannot localize dysregulation to CD14+ subsets

skills.description: Use when you need to visually confirm that specific genes (e.g., DEFA1/DEFA3) are expressed exclusively in one subset of cells grouped by a metadata variable such as tissue, after a pathway or differential analysis flags them.
skills.name: violin-plot-gene-expression-visualization
skills.search_text: violin-plot-gene-expression-visualization Use when you need to visually confirm that specific genes (e.g., DEFA1/DEFA3) are expressed exclusively in one subset of cells grouped by a metadata variable such as tissue, after a pathway or differential analysis flags them. The input is already aggregated pseudobulk or a feature table rather than single-cell level expression, so per-cell distribution violins are not meaningful. You need statistical testing of expression differences rather than visual confirmation — use SCPA compare_pathways qval-based analysis instead. The gene set of interest spans pathway-level activity rather than individual marker genes; violin plots of single genes cannot represent multivariate pathway distribution shifts. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Visualize single-cell gene expression distributions with Seurat/ggplot2 violin plots grouped by metadata (e.g., tissue, stimulation) to localize marker expression to specific populations — as used to show DEFA1/DEFA3 alpha-defensin expression restricted to bone-marrow-derived T cells in the Szabo T cell dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2022.111697
skills.summary: Visualize single-cell gene expression distributions with Seurat/ggplot2 violin plots grouped by metadata (e.g., tissue, stimulation) to localize marker expression to specific populations — as used to show DEFA1/DEFA3 alpha-defensin expression restricted to bone-marrow-derived T cells in the Szabo T cell dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already aggregated pseudobulk or a feature table rather than single-cell level expression, so per-cell distribution violins are not meaningful. You need statistical testing of expression differences rather than visual confirmation — use SCPA compare_pathways qval-based analysis instead. The gene set of interest spans pathway-level activity rather than individual marker genes; violin plots of single genes cannot represent multivariate pathway distribution shifts.

skills.description: Use when you need to visually assess whether one marker gene's expression distribution discriminates cell cycle stages in single-cell RNA-seq data (overlapping violins = insufficient marker).
skills.name: violin-plot-visualization-of-stage-distributions
skills.search_text: violin-plot-visualization-of-stage-distributions Use when you need to visually assess whether one marker gene's expression distribution discriminates cell cycle stages in single-cell RNA-seq data (overlapping violins = insufficient marker). You need reliable per-cell stage assignment from expression — the violins show distributions overlap, so a single marker gene cannot determine a single cell's stage; use the reCAT TSP+HMM pipeline instead Your data is bulk RNA-seq or synchronized-cell data, where stage is already known or averaged out http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Draw ggplot2 violin plots of individual cell cycle marker gene expression (Ccne1, Pcna, Cdc6, Hjurp) split by reCAT-assigned cell cycle stage (G1, S, G2/M) on the mESC-SMARTer scRNA-seq data, to demonstrate that a single marker gene is insufficient to determine a single cell's stage. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-00039-z
skills.summary: Draw ggplot2 violin plots of individual cell cycle marker gene expression (Ccne1, Pcna, Cdc6, Hjurp) split by reCAT-assigned cell cycle stage (G1, S, G2/M) on the mESC-SMARTer scRNA-seq data, to demonstrate that a single marker gene is insufficient to determine a single cell's stage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need reliable per-cell stage assignment from expression — the violins show distributions overlap, so a single marker gene cannot determine a single cell's stage; use the reCAT TSP+HMM pipeline instead Your data is bulk RNA-seq or synchronized-cell data, where stage is already known or averaged out

skills.description: Use when building infected-host metabolic models that must carry a viral biomass reaction (e.g. for FBA-based viral essentiality or drug repositioning), starting from a generic reconstruction plus a published VBOF.
skills.name: viral-biomass-objective-integration
skills.search_text: viral-biomass-objective-integration Use when building infected-host metabolic models that must carry a viral biomass reaction (e.g. for FBA-based viral essentiality or drug repositioning), starting from a generic reconstruction plus a published VBOF. When the goal is to model the virus through direct docking or viral-proteome network effects — here the virus is represented only through its biomass function on the host model When the reconstruction is already flux-consistent and already carries the VBOF; re-running identifier harmonization and FASTCC is redundant For non-viral context-specific reconstructions where a host biomass function alone suffices (plain rFASTCORMICS with a host biomass reaction is the correct path) http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Augments a generic genome-scale metabolic reconstruction (Recon2.04, Recon3D_01) with the SARS-CoV-2 viral biomass objective function (VBOF, BioModels MODEL2003020001) and removes flux-inconsistent reactions with FASTCC, yielding consistent infected and control generic models that serve as inputs for context-specific (rFASTCORMICS) reconstruction and viral-essentiality analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103331
skills.summary: Augments a generic genome-scale metabolic reconstruction (Recon2.04, Recon3D_01) with the SARS-CoV-2 viral biomass objective function (VBOF, BioModels MODEL2003020001) and removes flux-inconsistent reactions with FASTCC, yielding consistent infected and control generic models that serve as inputs for context-specific (rFASTCORMICS) reconstruction and viral-essentiality analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to model the virus through direct docking or viral-proteome network effects — here the virus is represented only through its biomass function on the host model When the reconstruction is already flux-consistent and already carries the VBOF; re-running identifier harmonization and FASTCC is redundant For non-viral context-specific reconstructions where a host biomass function alone suffices (plain rFASTCORMICS with a host biomass reaction is the correct path)

skills.description: Use when you have infected context-specific genome-scale metabolic models with a VBOF (e.g. SARS-CoV-2 lung models) and need to enumerate essential genes or synergistic gene pairs as drug-target candidates.
skills.name: viral-biomass-objective-knockout-scoring
skills.search_text: viral-biomass-objective-knockout-scoring Use when you have infected context-specific genome-scale metabolic models with a VBOF (e.g. SARS-CoV-2 lung models) and need to enumerate essential genes or synergistic gene pairs as drug-target candidates. The model does not carry a viral biomass objective function — knockouts then only probe host biomass, not virus-specific essentiality The goal is direct docking or antiviral targeting of the viral proteome; this skill identifies host metabolic targets via network effects on the host metabolome only You need experimentally validated essentiality rather than in silico predictions — in vitro single- and double-gene deletion studies are required to confirm the predictions http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Systematically performs in silico single- and double-gene knockouts on context-specific metabolic models carrying a viral biomass objective function (VBOF), scoring each knockout by the resulting viral biomass production flux to identify host genes whose loss reduces viral biomass without affecting host biomass maintenance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103331
skills.summary: Systematically performs in silico single- and double-gene knockouts on context-specific metabolic models carrying a viral biomass objective function (VBOF), scoring each knockout by the resulting viral biomass production flux to identify host genes whose loss reduces viral biomass without affecting host biomass maintenance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model does not carry a viral biomass objective function — knockouts then only probe host biomass, not virus-specific essentiality The goal is direct docking or antiviral targeting of the viral proteome; this skill identifies host metabolic targets via network effects on the host metabolome only You need experimentally validated essentiality rather than in silico predictions — in vitro single- and double-gene deletion studies are required to confirm the predictions

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data of virus-specific T cells (e.g. P14 cells from LCMV chronic infection under perturbations like CD4 T cell depletion) must be assigned to reference subtypes (SLEC, Tpex, Tex) and their composition compared between conditions.
skills.name: viral-infection-t-cell-subtype-composition-analysis
skills.search_text: viral-infection-t-cell-subtype-composition-analysis Use when scRNA-seq data of virus-specific T cells (e.g. P14 cells from LCMV chronic infection under perturbations like CD4 T cell depletion) must be assigned to reference subtypes (SLEC, Tpex, Tex) and their composition compared between conditions. skills.summary: Quantify the subtype composition of virus-specific CD8+ T cells (e.g. LCMV P14 query data) by projecting scRNA-seq query expression matrices onto the mouse acute/chronic viral infection CD8 T cell reference atlas with ProjecTILs, then comparing subtype frequencies and gene expression (e.g. Pdcd1) across conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query contains cell types absent from the reference (e.g. γδ T cells or CD4+ TILs, which are not represented in the viral CD8 T cell atlas) The goal is de novo clustering/annotation of query data without a suitable reference atlas — unsupervised annotation would be required instead UMAP-based quantitative claims (cell-cell distances/densities) are intended, since ProjecTILs performs cell state quantifications in PCA space and UMAP distances are highly distorted

skills.description: Use when building or retraining an alignment-free viral-read classifier on fixed-length RNA-seq fragments (e.g., 48 bp), or when all models must be retrained on identical training fragments for a fair comparison on a shared test set.
skills.name: viral-read-classification-model-training
skills.search_text: viral-read-classification-model-training Use when building or retraining an alignment-free viral-read classifier on fixed-length RNA-seq fragments (e.g., 48 bp), or when all models must be retrained on identical training fragments for a fair comparison on a shared test set. Reads are not from human RNA-seq samples — the article notes model predictions for sequences from organisms other than human/viral are not defined; models for other organisms are future work Only a handful of viral reads (<5) are expected in a sample — the sensitivity guarantee is stated only for cases with more than five viral reads present The goal is read alignment/mapping rather than alignment-free classification — map reads to the human genome first and apply this model only to unmapped reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Train a TensorFlow/Keras deep learning model (viRNAtrap-style) to discriminate viral from human RNA-seq reads, using 48 bp fragments segmented from positive (viral) and negative (human) transcripts split into shared training and test sets, so the model can score unmapped reads and enable viral contig assembly and fair benchmarking against methods like DeepVirFinder, DeepViFi, ViraMiner, and Seq2Seq. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36336-z
skills.summary: Train a TensorFlow/Keras deep learning model (viRNAtrap-style) to discriminate viral from human RNA-seq reads, using 48 bp fragments segmented from positive (viral) and negative (human) transcripts split into shared training and test sets, so the model can score unmapped reads and enable viral contig assembly and fair benchmarking against methods like DeepVirFinder, DeepViFi, ViraMiner, and Seq2Seq.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are not from human RNA-seq samples — the article notes model predictions for sequences from organisms other than human/viral are not defined; models for other organisms are future work Only a handful of viral reads (<5) are expected in a sample — the sensitivity guarantee is stated only for cases with more than five viral reads present The goal is read alignment/mapping rather than alignment-free classification — map reads to the human genome first and apply this model only to unmapped reads

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are still aligned to the human genome — viRNAtrap is applied only to unaligned RNA reads (not mapped to hg19 or phiX) to reduce running time Sequences come from organisms other than human/viral — model predictions for such sequences are not defined and other-organism models are future work You expect to overwrite or append to existing output files — virnatrap-predict refuses to overwrite pre-existing outputs

skills.description: Use when running scPathoQuant on 10x cellranger output and a pathogen (e.g. HIV, SARS-CoV-2, metapneumovirus) reference genome must be packaged into the -p2genome folder with clean FASTA headers.
skills.name: viral-reference-genome-preparation
skills.search_text: viral-reference-genome-preparation Use when running scPathoQuant on 10x cellranger output and a pathogen (e.g. HIV, SARS-CoV-2, metapneumovirus) reference genome must be packaged into the -p2genome folder with clean FASTA headers. The analysis target is not a 10x scRNAseq pathogen-quantification run (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or metagenomic assembly) — this folder format is specific to scPathoQuant's -p2genome argument. A host genome reference is needed: scPathoQuant expects the host alignment to already be done by cellranger count; the -p2genome folder must contain only pathogen sequences, not the host genome. Per-gene pathogen counts are not required and no GTF is available — a FASTA-only folder still works, so blocking on GTF creation is unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assembles the pathogen reference folder that scPathoQuant consumes via -p2genome: a simplified-header FASTA (and optionally a GTF) per viral genome, capped at 2 files, since the FASTA header is the key under which total pathogen reads are quantified. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae145
skills.summary: Assembles the pathogen reference folder that scPathoQuant consumes via -p2genome: a simplified-header FASTA (and optionally a GTF) per viral genome, capped at 2 files, since the FASTA header is the key under which total pathogen reads are quantified.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis target is not a 10x scRNAseq pathogen-quantification run (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or metagenomic assembly) — this folder format is specific to scPathoQuant's -p2genome argument. A host genome reference is needed: scPathoQuant expects the host alignment to already be done by cellranger count; the -p2genome folder must contain only pathogen sequences, not the host genome. Per-gene pathogen counts are not required and no GTF is available — a FASTA-only folder still works, so blocking on GTF creation is unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when a SNP-by-cell AD/DP mtDNA matrix (from cellsnp-lite/cellSNP) has been filtered by MQuad and you need per-cell clone labels from mitochondrial variants.
skills.name: vireosnp-clonal-assignment
skills.search_text: vireosnp-clonal-assignment Use when a SNP-by-cell AD/DP mtDNA matrix (from cellsnp-lite/cellSNP) has been filtered by MQuad and you need per-cell clone labels from mitochondrial variants. Variant calling and informativeness filtering have not yet been done — run MQuad first; vireoSNP expects selected SNPs, not raw pile-ups. Input data are nuclear SNVs or CNV-derived subclones where the diploid context applies — the mtDNA-specific pipeline violates diploid assumptions. Per-cell mitochondrial read depth is far below ~3,000 reads, where assignable cells, informative variants, and concordance drop linearly and assignments become unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstruct clonal substructure from single-cell mtDNA variant data by running vireoSNP (v0.5.3) variational inference on the MQuad-selected informative mitochondrial SNPs, assigning each cell to a clone in the cellSNP-MQuad-VireoSNP pipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28845-0
skills.summary: Reconstruct clonal substructure from single-cell mtDNA variant data by running vireoSNP (v0.5.3) variational inference on the MQuad-selected informative mitochondrial SNPs, assigning each cell to a clone in the cellSNP-MQuad-VireoSNP pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Variant calling and informativeness filtering have not yet been done — run MQuad first; vireoSNP expects selected SNPs, not raw pile-ups. Input data are nuclear SNVs or CNV-derived subclones where the diploid context applies — the mtDNA-specific pipeline violates diploid assumptions. Per-cell mitochondrial read depth is far below ~3,000 reads, where assignable cells, informative variants, and concordance drop linearly and assignments become unreliable.

skills.description: Use when reimplementing or verifying scPhere's hyperspherical VAE: you need vMF posterior sampling, the closed-form vMF-vs-uniform-sphere KL, or the NB observation model with softmax means.
skills.name: vmf-distribution-sampling
skills.search_text: vmf-distribution-sampling Use when reimplementing or verifying scPhere's hyperspherical VAE: you need vMF posterior sampling, the closed-form vMF-vs-uniform-sphere KL, or the NB observation model with softmax means. The latent geometry is hyperbolic rather than spherical — scPhere uses latent_dist='wn' (wrapped normal) for hyperbolic (Lorentz-model/Poincaré-disk) embeddings, not the vMF machinery. You need a Euclidean-latent VAE baseline (standard multidimensional normal prior); the vMF sampling and hyperspherical KL do not apply. You need scPhere's future extensions (imputation of missing counts, ambient RNA removal, perturbation modeling, multimodal integration) — these are explicitly not implemented. Reconstructs the von Mises–Fisher (vMF) latent machinery of scPhere: rejection-sampled vMF draws mapped to arbitrary mean directions via Householder rotations, the closed-form KL divergence to a uniform prior on the unit hypersphere, and the negative-binomial decoder used with z_dim=2 spherical embeddings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22851-4
skills.summary: Reconstructs the von Mises–Fisher (vMF) latent machinery of scPhere: rejection-sampled vMF draws mapped to arbitrary mean directions via Householder rotations, the closed-form KL divergence to a uniform prior on the unit hypersphere, and the negative-binomial decoder used with z_dim=2 spherical embeddings.
