skills.name: weighted-overlap-colocalization-measure
skills.search_text: weighted-overlap-colocalization-measure Use when testing association between transcriptome region sets where the query features lack clear isoform association (e.g. miCLIP-seq m6A sites) and isoform-derived regions such as stop codons, and you need a TxIA-aware weighted overlap statistic rather than a raw genomic overlap count. Features already carry clear isoform/transcript association — use permTestTx or permTestTx_customPick with overlapCountsTx instead of the TxIA (isoform-ambiguity) variant The comparison is purely genome-based (no transcriptome annotation involved) — genome-only tools like regioneR or BEDTools overlap workflows are the appropriate scope The region of interest is directly provided as a region set rather than derived by a customPick function from transcripts http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A colocalization measure used with RgnTX permutation tests that counts overlaps between a query region set (e.g. miCLIP-seq m6A methylation sites with isoform ambiguity) and target transcriptome regions (e.g. UCSC hg19 stop codons), weighting counts when a region maps to multiple isoforms. It yields an observed weighted overlap, a random-overlap null mean, a permutation p-value, and a z-score. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.08.021
skills.summary: A colocalization measure used with RgnTX permutation tests that counts overlaps between a query region set (e.g. miCLIP-seq m6A methylation sites with isoform ambiguity) and target transcriptome regions (e.g. UCSC hg19 stop codons), weighting counts when a region maps to multiple isoforms. It yields an observed weighted overlap, a random-overlap null mean, a permutation p-value, and a z-score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features already carry clear isoform/transcript association — use permTestTx or permTestTx_customPick with overlapCountsTx instead of the TxIA (isoform-ambiguity) variant The comparison is purely genome-based (no transcriptome annotation involved) — genome-only tools like regioneR or BEDTools overlap workflows are the appropriate scope The region of interest is directly provided as a region set rather than derived by a customPick function from transcripts

skills.description: Use when bulk expression samples must be decomposed into cell-type relative abundances but no single-cell reference profile is available—only marker genes with per-gene weights (e.g., log fold-change) per cell type.
skills.name: weighted-principal-component-analysis
skills.search_text: weighted-principal-component-analysis Use when bulk expression samples must be decomposed into cell-type relative abundances but no single-cell reference profile is available—only marker genes with per-gene weights (e.g., log fold-change) per cell type. A matched single-cell reference profile is available — use reference-based decomposition (ReferenceBasedDecomposition) instead, which is more accurate when scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq data exist Absolute proportions comparable across cell types are needed — BisqueMarker only estimates relative abundance differences that cannot be compared between cell types http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A semi-supervised decomposition technique used by BisqueMarker: each cell type's marker-gene expression matrix from bulk RNA-seq samples is scaled by marker weights (e.g., avg_logFC) and reduced via PCA (svd/prcomp), with the first principal component serving as a relative cell-type abundance estimate after correcting for the first global expression PC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15816-6
skills.summary: A semi-supervised decomposition technique used by BisqueMarker: each cell type's marker-gene expression matrix from bulk RNA-seq samples is scaled by marker weights (e.g., avg_logFC) and reduced via PCA (svd/prcomp), with the first principal component serving as a relative cell-type abundance estimate after correcting for the first global expression PC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A matched single-cell reference profile is available — use reference-based decomposition (ReferenceBasedDecomposition) instead, which is more accurate when scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq data exist Absolute proportions comparable across cell types are needed — BisqueMarker only estimates relative abundance differences that cannot be compared between cell types

skills.description: Use when benchmarking clustering or dimensionality reduction tools needs datasets with known cell-type composition, by subsampling pre-sorted cells (e.g., Zheng mixtures) at controlled cluster sizes and ratios.
skills.name: weighted-random-cell-subsampling
skills.search_text: weighted-random-cell-subsampling Use when benchmarking clustering or dimensionality reduction tools needs datasets with known cell-type composition, by subsampling pre-sorted cells (e.g., Zheng mixtures) at controlled cluster sizes and ratios. The goal is to evaluate method performance on real datasets with biologically authentic cluster proportions rather than controlled mixtures The reference cell types lack independent, assay-independent labels, so ground truth for ECS/SIL computation would be unreliable You need simulation of new expression profiles rather than resampling of measured cells (use a simulator like scDesign2 instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Constructs simulated scRNA-seq mixture datasets by mixing pre-sorted cells from a reference dataset (e.g., Zheng blood cell types) via weighted random sampling according to target cluster sizes and ratios, enabling ground-truth-controlled benchmarking of dimensionality reduction methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47884-3
skills.summary: Constructs simulated scRNA-seq mixture datasets by mixing pre-sorted cells from a reference dataset (e.g., Zheng blood cell types) via weighted random sampling according to target cluster sizes and ratios, enabling ground-truth-controlled benchmarking of dimensionality reduction methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to evaluate method performance on real datasets with biologically authentic cluster proportions rather than controlled mixtures The reference cell types lack independent, assay-independent labels, so ground truth for ECS/SIL computation would be unreliable You need simulation of new expression profiles rather than resampling of measured cells (use a simulator like scDesign2 instead)

skills.description: Use when scUTRquant SingleCellExperiment outputs (gene + 3'UTR isoform count matrices) cover multi-UTR genes across two or more cell types or perturbations and differentially used/lengthened 3' ends must be called and compared to DGE gene sets.
skills.name: weighted-utr-isoform-usage-analysis
skills.search_text: weighted-utr-isoform-usage-analysis Use when scUTRquant SingleCellExperiment outputs (gene + 3'UTR isoform count matrices) cover multi-UTR genes across two or more cell types or perturbations and differentially used/lengthened 3' ends must be called and compared to DGE gene sets. Input data are raw 10x Genomics reads that have not yet been processed through scUTRquant — most 10x reads do not span 3' end cleavage sites, so WUI testing needs scUTRquant isoform quantification first Genes of interest are single-UTR genes with only one major 3' end; isoform usage analysis requires multi-UTR genes Bulk RNA-seq or full-length protocols where standard 3'UTR isoform quantification assumptions (3'-end tag data, truncated-transcript targets) do not hold http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Statistical detection of differential 3'UTR isoform usage (lengthening/shortening) from scUTRquant SingleCellExperiment outputs using the scUTRboot weighted UTR isoform (WUI) test, complementing differential gene expression to show mRNA abundance and 3'UTR length are largely independent regulatory axes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Statistical detection of differential 3'UTR isoform usage (lengthening/shortening) from scUTRquant SingleCellExperiment outputs using the scUTRboot weighted UTR isoform (WUI) test, complementing differential gene expression to show mRNA abundance and 3'UTR length are largely independent regulatory axes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are raw 10x Genomics reads that have not yet been processed through scUTRquant — most 10x reads do not span 3' end cleavage sites, so WUI testing needs scUTRquant isoform quantification first Genes of interest are single-UTR genes with only one major 3' end; isoform usage analysis requires multi-UTR genes Bulk RNA-seq or full-length protocols where standard 3'UTR isoform quantification assumptions (3'-end tag data, truncated-transcript targets) do not hold

skills.description: Use when metacell-level (rather than single-cell-level) differential expression, differential abundance, or dimensionality reduction is planned and metacells have unequal sizes, to quantify and visualize the type I/II errors introduced by disregarding metacell size weights.
skills.name: weighted-vs-unweighted-artifact-comparison-visualization
skills.search_text: weighted-vs-unweighted-artifact-comparison-visualization Use when metacell-level (rather than single-cell-level) differential expression, differential abundance, or dimensionality reduction is planned and metacells have unequal sizes, to quantify and visualize the type I/II errors introduced by disregarding metacell size weights. When metacells are constructed with a fixed target size so all metacells contain approximately the same number of cells — weighting then has little effect When the analysis goal is single-cell-level differential expression, where the single-cell reference itself is the output and no metacell weighting is involved When building or quality-controlling metacells (purity, compactness, separation, INV) rather than performing weighted downstream analyses http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduces and visualizes the downstream-analysis artifacts that arise when metacell size (number of constituent single cells) is ignored in metacell-level differential expression, differential abundance, and PCA/clustering analyses. It contrasts unweighted vs size-weighted results against a single-cell-level reference to expose type I (Gene B) and type II (Gene C) errors, as in Fig 7B. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-024-00045-6
skills.summary: Reproduces and visualizes the downstream-analysis artifacts that arise when metacell size (number of constituent single cells) is ignored in metacell-level differential expression, differential abundance, and PCA/clustering analyses. It contrasts unweighted vs size-weighted results against a single-cell-level reference to expose type I (Gene B) and type II (Gene C) errors, as in Fig 7B.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When metacells are constructed with a fixed target size so all metacells contain approximately the same number of cells — weighting then has little effect When the analysis goal is single-cell-level differential expression, where the single-cell reference itself is the output and no metacell weighting is involved When building or quality-controlling metacells (purity, compactness, separation, INV) rather than performing weighted downstream analyses

skills.description: Use when comparing whether peak-gene pairs ranked by a Granger-causal method show significantly longer chromatin-to-expression pseudotime lags than pairs ranked by Pearson or pseudocell correlation.
skills.name: welch-t-test-asynchrony-comparison
skills.search_text: welch-t-test-asynchrony-comparison Use when comparing whether peak-gene pairs ranked by a Granger-causal method show significantly longer chromatin-to-expression pseudotime lags than pairs ranked by Pearson or pseudocell correlation. Static or non-trajectory multimodal data with no meaningful pseudotime ordering, since lag computation depends on a cell-state DAG and diffusion pseudotime Peak-gene pairs outside the prioritized top/bottom 1% groups when the goal is to replicate the reported Fig. 2d,e group comparison Datasets where candidate pairs were assembled with the default 1 Mb cutoff instead of the 10x Multiome 250 kb cutoff, since lag statistics are not directly comparable to the reported result http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Statistical test comparing pseudotime lag ('asynchrony') distributions between GrID-Net-prioritized peak-gene pairs and correlation-prioritized pairs on the 10x Multiome corticogenesis dataset, using a Welch one-tailed t-test to establish the cell-state parallax effect (P < 10^-26). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Statistical test comparing pseudotime lag ('asynchrony') distributions between GrID-Net-prioritized peak-gene pairs and correlation-prioritized pairs on the 10x Multiome corticogenesis dataset, using a Welch one-tailed t-test to establish the cell-state parallax effect (P < 10^-26).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Static or non-trajectory multimodal data with no meaningful pseudotime ordering, since lag computation depends on a cell-state DAG and diffusion pseudotime Peak-gene pairs outside the prioritized top/bottom 1% groups when the goal is to replicate the reported Fig. 2d,e group comparison Datasets where candidate pairs were assembled with the default 1 Mb cutoff instead of the 10x Multiome 250 kb cutoff, since lag statistics are not directly comparable to the reported result

skills.description: Use when PILOT's Wasserstein-distance-based Leiden clustering has assigned patient samples to clusters (e.g., the PDAC 11 control / 14 Tumor 1 / 10 Tumor 2 split) and you need to test which cell-type proportions differ between clusters.
skills.name: welch-t-test-cell-proportion-testing
skills.search_text: welch-t-test-cell-proportion-testing Use when PILOT's Wasserstein-distance-based Leiden clustering has assigned patient samples to clusters (e.g., the PDAC 11 control / 14 Tumor 1 / 10 Tumor 2 split) and you need to test which cell-type proportions differ between clusters. The goal is differential gene expression between clusters rather than cell-population changes — use PILOT's limma empirical-Bayes or Wald-statistic testing instead. Clusters have not yet been defined: the Welch t-test requires patient-level cluster labels (e.g., from select_best_sil followed by clustering_emd), not raw per-cell data. Each cluster contains only one or very few samples, so between-cluster variance in proportions cannot be estimated reliably. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Statistically compares cell-type composition between PILOT-detected patient clusters by applying a Welch t-test to per-cluster cell-type proportions, identifying which populations (e.g., ductal cell 1, ductal cell 2, stellate) differ significantly (p < 0.05) across patient subgroups. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-023-00003-8
skills.summary: Statistically compares cell-type composition between PILOT-detected patient clusters by applying a Welch t-test to per-cluster cell-type proportions, identifying which populations (e.g., ductal cell 1, ductal cell 2, stellate) differ significantly (p < 0.05) across patient subgroups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is differential gene expression between clusters rather than cell-population changes — use PILOT's limma empirical-Bayes or Wald-statistic testing instead. Clusters have not yet been defined: the Welch t-test requires patient-level cluster labels (e.g., from select_best_sil followed by clustering_emd), not raw per-cell data. Each cluster contains only one or very few samples, so between-cluster variance in proportions cannot be estimated reliably.

skills.description: Use when a clustered single-cell RNA-seq AnnData object needs a per-cluster DE profile to assign a cell type, e.g. testing one Leiden cluster against the rest before GO/KEGG/MSigDB enrichment.
skills.name: welch-t-test-de-testing
skills.search_text: welch-t-test-de-testing Use when a clustered single-cell RNA-seq AnnData object needs a per-cluster DE profile to assign a cell type, e.g. testing one Leiden cluster against the rest before GO/KEGG/MSigDB enrichment. The data are not yet clustered into cell groups — Welch's t-test of cluster vs. rest requires a prior Leiden/clustering step The goal is bulk RNA-seq differential expression across conditions rather than single-cell cluster-vs-rest testing (the unmaintained diffxpy README suggests PyDESeq2 for pure-python bulk DE analysis) Only marker-based annotation without enrichment is needed — marker set intersection may be more appropriate than a ranked fold-change gene list http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Differential expression analysis of a single Leiden cluster versus all remaining cells using diffxpy's Welch's t-test, followed by selection of the top fold-change genes for downstream enrichment. In the Cellar paper this workflow assigned spleen cluster 0 (HBMP3-spleen data) to B-cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29744-0
skills.summary: Differential expression analysis of a single Leiden cluster versus all remaining cells using diffxpy's Welch's t-test, followed by selection of the top fold-change genes for downstream enrichment. In the Cellar paper this workflow assigned spleen cluster 0 (HBMP3-spleen data) to B-cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not yet clustered into cell groups — Welch's t-test of cluster vs. rest requires a prior Leiden/clustering step The goal is bulk RNA-seq differential expression across conditions rather than single-cell cluster-vs-rest testing (the unmaintained diffxpy README suggests PyDESeq2 for pure-python bulk DE analysis) Only marker-based annotation without enrichment is needed — marker set intersection may be more appropriate than a ranked fold-change gene list

skills.description: Use when each cell in a single-cell dataset (scRNA-seq or a scATAC-seq cell-by-gene activity matrix) already has cluster labels and you must identify marker genes per cluster via one-vs-rest testing, ranked by fold-change for marker or enrichment analysis.
skills.name: welch-t-test-differential-expression
skills.search_text: welch-t-test-differential-expression Use when each cell in a single-cell dataset (scRNA-seq or a scATAC-seq cell-by-gene activity matrix) already has cluster labels and you must identify marker genes per cluster via one-vs-rest testing, ranked by fold-change for marker or enrichment analysis. The input is still a cell-by-peak chromatin-accessibility matrix with no gene-level representation — derive topics (cisTopic) or a gene activity score first. The goal is reference-based label transfer/annotation rather than de novo marker discovery — use scanpy Ingest or SingleR instead. Differential expression results already exist and the task is downstream GO-term enrichment — feed the top 500 fold-change genes directly to GSEApy. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Performs one-vs-rest differential gene expression testing for each Leiden cluster using diffxpy's Welch's t-test, ranking genes by log fold-change to surface cluster markers (e.g., KLRD1 for NK cells, SLC5A12 for proximal tubule cells) in Cellar-style single-cell workflows. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29744-0
skills.summary: Performs one-vs-rest differential gene expression testing for each Leiden cluster using diffxpy's Welch's t-test, ranking genes by log fold-change to surface cluster markers (e.g., KLRD1 for NK cells, SLC5A12 for proximal tubule cells) in Cellar-style single-cell workflows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is still a cell-by-peak chromatin-accessibility matrix with no gene-level representation — derive topics (cisTopic) or a gene activity score first. The goal is reference-based label transfer/annotation rather than de novo marker discovery — use scanpy Ingest or SingleR instead. Differential expression results already exist and the task is downstream GO-term enrichment — feed the top 500 fold-change genes directly to GSEApy.

skills.description: Use when cells have been assigned intact or mutant gRNAs by GiRAFR and you need to test whether mutant gRNA cells fail to downregulate their target genes relative to intact gRNA cells.
skills.name: welch-two-sample-t-testing
skills.search_text: welch-two-sample-t-testing Use when cells have been assigned intact or mutant gRNAs by GiRAFR and you need to test whether mutant gRNA cells fail to downregulate their target genes relative to intact gRNA cells. When gRNA-to-cell labels come from tools that do not detect mutant gRNAs (e.g., Cell Ranger labels gRNAs with 1 Hamming distance as intact), since mislabeled cells attenuate the intact-vs-mutant expression contrast When the question is which gRNA mutation types or positions are tolerable or damaging — the article declares this fine-grained appraisal beyond its scope When the input is already a summarized table of expression statistics rather than per-cell count values http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Welch two-sample t-testing of single-cell target gene expression between gRNA classes (intact vs spacer-mutant vs scaffold-mutant) to demonstrate that mutant gRNAs are dysfunctional. It reproduces the GiRAFR paper's functional impact analysis (Figure 2b, P = 8.2e-6). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05351-7
skills.summary: Welch two-sample t-testing of single-cell target gene expression between gRNA classes (intact vs spacer-mutant vs scaffold-mutant) to demonstrate that mutant gRNAs are dysfunctional. It reproduces the GiRAFR paper's functional impact analysis (Figure 2b, P = 8.2e-6).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When gRNA-to-cell labels come from tools that do not detect mutant gRNAs (e.g., Cell Ranger labels gRNAs with 1 Hamming distance as intact), since mislabeled cells attenuate the intact-vs-mutant expression contrast When the question is which gRNA mutation types or positions are tolerable or damaging — the article declares this fine-grained appraisal beyond its scope When the input is already a summarized table of expression statistics rather than per-cell count values

skills.description: Use when paired WGS and WES SNV catalogs exist for the same samples and you need to test whether exome capture regions distort COSMIC v3.1 signature contributions (e.g. non-coding signatures like SBS9 or flat signatures like SBS-MM1) before reporting WES-based fits.
skills.name: wes-vs-wgs-signature-concordance-evaluation
skills.search_text: wes-vs-wgs-signature-concordance-evaluation Use when paired WGS and WES SNV catalogs exist for the same samples and you need to test whether exome capture regions distort COSMIC v3.1 signature contributions (e.g. non-coding signatures like SBS9 or flat signatures like SBS-MM1) before reporting WES-based fits. When the input is from targeted capture panels covering only a few megabases — mutational burdens are too low for meaningful individual-patient signature fitting, even in WGS When catalogs contain fewer than ~500 mutations, since mmsig's built-in error-suppression and bootstrap CIs only reach excellent sensitivity and specificity on larger catalogs When the question is de novo signature discovery rather than fitting against a fixed COSMIC v3.1 reference set http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 A paired evaluation skill that refits mutational signatures with mmsig::mm_fit_signatures on both whole-genome SNV catalogs and exome-restricted catalogs (SureSelect V6 + UTR capture intervals) to quantify how capture-region restriction biases signature estimates, e.g. the ~12% underestimation of the non-coding AID signature SBS9 in CLL. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-01938-0
skills.summary: A paired evaluation skill that refits mutational signatures with mmsig::mm_fit_signatures on both whole-genome SNV catalogs and exome-restricted catalogs (SureSelect V6 + UTR capture intervals) to quantify how capture-region restriction biases signature estimates, e.g. the ~12% underestimation of the non-coding AID signature SBS9 in CLL.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is from targeted capture panels covering only a few megabases — mutational burdens are too low for meaningful individual-patient signature fitting, even in WGS When catalogs contain fewer than ~500 mutations, since mmsig's built-in error-suppression and bootstrap CIs only reach excellent sensitivity and specificity on larger catalogs When the question is de novo signature discovery rather than fitting against a fixed COSMIC v3.1 reference set

skills.description: Use when a tumor-normal WES/WGS pipeline needs patient HLA class I typing from sequencing reads (not clinical HLA reports) so that pMHC binding/immunogenicity prediction can be restricted to the patient's own HLA alleles.
skills.name: wes-wgs-read-based-genotyping
skills.search_text: wes-wgs-read-based-genotyping Use when a tumor-normal WES/WGS pipeline needs patient HLA class I typing from sequencing reads (not clinical HLA reports) so that pMHC binding/immunogenicity prediction can be restricted to the patient's own HLA alleles. Clinical-grade HLA typing results are already available (e.g., the TESLA dataset provides clinical-grade HLA typing), making read-based inference redundant The input is RNA-Seq rather than WES/WGS reads from a tumor-normal pair, or HLA class II typing is required (OptiType as embedded here covers class I only) http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Identify 4-digit HLA class I (HLA-A/-B/-C) alleles from trimmed tumor-normal FASTQ reads using OptiType v1.3.5, as embedded in the TSNAD v2.0.1 neoantigen prediction pipeline, producing per-sample genotype calls that feed the DeepHLApan-based neoantigen prediction module. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.016
skills.summary: Identify 4-digit HLA class I (HLA-A/-B/-C) alleles from trimmed tumor-normal FASTQ reads using OptiType v1.3.5, as embedded in the TSNAD v2.0.1 neoantigen prediction pipeline, producing per-sample genotype calls that feed the DeepHLApan-based neoantigen prediction module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clinical-grade HLA typing results are already available (e.g., the TESLA dataset provides clinical-grade HLA typing), making read-based inference redundant The input is RNA-Seq rather than WES/WGS reads from a tumor-normal pair, or HLA class II typing is required (OptiType as embedded here covers class I only)

skills.description: Use when you have an RNA-seq table of counts plus sample phenotype metadata (e.g., mutant/wild-type Lafora disease samples) and want to find co-expressed gene groups (CEGs) that correlate with phenotypic data.
skills.name: wgcna-co-expression-module-detection
skills.search_text: wgcna-co-expression-module-detection Use when you have an RNA-seq table of counts plus sample phenotype metadata (e.g., mutant/wild-type Lafora disease samples) and want to find co-expressed gene groups (CEGs) that correlate with phenotypic data. Input is raw reads or FASTQ rather than a processed table of counts — the count matrix must already be produced by upstream RNA-seq initial data analysis. The analysis goal is only differential expression detection without phenotypic correlation of gene groups — use the DEgenes Hunter DEG combination workflow instead. No sample phenotype/trait metadata exists to correlate modules against, since the method searches for CEGs that correlate with phenotypic data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Detect co-expression modules in RNA-seq data via WGCNA within the ExpHunter Suite and correlate module eigen-genes with a phenotypic trait (e.g., mutant vs wild-type in the Lafora disease dataset) to link gene networks to phenotype, followed by functional enrichment of module gene lists. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-94343-w
skills.summary: Detect co-expression modules in RNA-seq data via WGCNA within the ExpHunter Suite and correlate module eigen-genes with a phenotypic trait (e.g., mutant vs wild-type in the Lafora disease dataset) to link gene networks to phenotype, followed by functional enrichment of module gene lists.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or FASTQ rather than a processed table of counts — the count matrix must already be produced by upstream RNA-seq initial data analysis. The analysis goal is only differential expression detection without phenotypic correlation of gene groups — use the DEgenes Hunter DEG combination workflow instead. No sample phenotype/trait metadata exists to correlate modules against, since the method searches for CEGs that correlate with phenotypic data.

skills.description: Use when input is a processed single-cell expression matrix with cell-level metadata and the goal is to infer co-expression modules and identify which modules track a trait such as patient survival status.
skills.name: wgcna-co-expression-module-detection
skills.search_text: wgcna-co-expression-module-detection Use when input is a processed single-cell expression matrix with cell-level metadata and the goal is to infer co-expression modules and identify which modules track a trait such as patient survival status. Input is bulk RNA-seq or an already-aggregated bulk expression matrix rather than single-cell data requiring pseudo-bulk aggregation across neighboring cells. The goal is transcription-factor regulatory network (GRN) reconstruction or drug–gene interaction repurposing rather than co-expression module detection and module–trait correlation. The network is already inferred and modules already detected — use downstream skills for hub detection or GRN/drug analysis instead of re-running module detection. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Detects trait- and cell-type-specific co-expression gene modules from scRNA-seq data by building a signed gene co-expression network (GCN) with a modified WGCNA implementation inside SCANet, then correlating detected modules against sample-level trait metadata (e.g. patient outcome). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad644
skills.summary: Detects trait- and cell-type-specific co-expression gene modules from scRNA-seq data by building a signed gene co-expression network (GCN) with a modified WGCNA implementation inside SCANet, then correlating detected modules against sample-level trait metadata (e.g. patient outcome).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-seq or an already-aggregated bulk expression matrix rather than single-cell data requiring pseudo-bulk aggregation across neighboring cells. The goal is transcription-factor regulatory network (GRN) reconstruction or drug–gene interaction repurposing rather than co-expression module detection and module–trait correlation. The network is already inferred and modules already detected — use downstream skills for hub detection or GRN/drug analysis instead of re-running module detection.

skills.description: Use when the input is a preprocessed single-cell expression matrix (e.g. .h5ad/HDF5/loom) with cell metadata and the goal is to infer gene co-expression modules and hubs for specific cell types or conditions.
skills.name: wgcna-coexpression-network-inference
skills.search_text: wgcna-coexpression-network-inference Use when the input is a preprocessed single-cell expression matrix (e.g. .h5ad/HDF5/loom) with cell metadata and the goal is to infer gene co-expression modules and hubs for specific cell types or conditions. The goal is directed gene regulatory network reconstruction rather than co-expression — GCNs rely on correlation, not causation; use downstream GRN inference (e.g. GRNBoost2 + RcisTarget) instead Data are already bulk RNA-seq or an aggregated feature table — pseudo-bulk sub-clustering of single cells is unnecessary A full-connection co-expression method specific to single cells is required and other dedicated tools (COTAN, scLink, fcoex) may be more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Infer gene co-expression networks (GCNs) and detect co-expression gene modules from scRNA-seq data using a modified WGCNA implementation (via BioNERO) inside SCANet, after pseudo-bulk aggregation of cells. This converts high-dimensional single-cell expression into trait/cell-type-associated gene modules. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad644
skills.summary: Infer gene co-expression networks (GCNs) and detect co-expression gene modules from scRNA-seq data using a modified WGCNA implementation (via BioNERO) inside SCANet, after pseudo-bulk aggregation of cells. This converts high-dimensional single-cell expression into trait/cell-type-associated gene modules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is directed gene regulatory network reconstruction rather than co-expression — GCNs rely on correlation, not causation; use downstream GRN inference (e.g. GRNBoost2 + RcisTarget) instead Data are already bulk RNA-seq or an aggregated feature table — pseudo-bulk sub-clustering of single cells is unnecessary A full-connection co-expression method specific to single cells is required and other dedicated tools (COTAN, scLink, fcoex) may be more appropriate

skills.description: Use when a cell-type-specific co-expression matrix (e.g., from CS-CORE or diff_CSCORE) needs to be partitioned into co-expressed gene modules for downstream GO enrichment of disease-relevant pathways.
skills.name: wgcna-gene-module-detection
skills.search_text: wgcna-gene-module-detection Use when a cell-type-specific co-expression matrix (e.g., from CS-CORE or diff_CSCORE) needs to be partitioned into co-expressed gene modules for downstream GO enrichment of disease-relevant pathways. Input is raw UMI counts rather than an inferred co-expression matrix — run CS-CORE/CSCORE first, as naive correlation-based modules are confounded by sequencing depth and measurement error The analysis goal is single gene-pair significance testing rather than module-level structure discovery Cell types are not subsetted and all cells are pooled — the paper warns this risks Simpson's paradox in co-expression inference http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Extracts co-expressed gene modules from CS-CORE-inferred cell-type-specific co-expression matrices by thresholding non-significant pairs, building a WGCNA adjacency and topological overlap matrix, and cutting the hierarchical clustering tree with dynamicTreeCut. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40503-7
skills.summary: Extracts co-expressed gene modules from CS-CORE-inferred cell-type-specific co-expression matrices by thresholding non-significant pairs, building a WGCNA adjacency and topological overlap matrix, and cutting the hierarchical clustering tree with dynamicTreeCut.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw UMI counts rather than an inferred co-expression matrix — run CS-CORE/CSCORE first, as naive correlation-based modules are confounded by sequencing depth and measurement error The analysis goal is single gene-pair significance testing rather than module-level structure discovery Cell types are not subsetted and all cells are pooled — the paper warns this risks Simpson's paradox in co-expression inference

skills.description: Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq count matrix across many samples (e.g. 38 female hippocampus 3xTg-AD/WT samples) and need to find co-expressed gene modules and correlate them with external traits.
skills.name: wgcna-module-detection
skills.search_text: wgcna-module-detection Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq count matrix across many samples (e.g. 38 female hippocampus 3xTg-AD/WT samples) and need to find co-expressed gene modules and correlate them with external traits. You need single-cell co-expression or differential expression rather than bulk-sample co-expression modules — PyWGCNA is designed for bulk RNA-seq datasets with many samples You only need pairwise gene correlations or a small pre-selected gene list analysis rather than unsupervised module discovery across the whole transcriptome Input is not a gene-by-sample count/normalized expression matrix (e.g. already-aggregated module statistics or a feature table) — the Data_format preprocessing step expects raw count-level input http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Detect co-expression modules from bulk RNA-seq count matrices using PyWGCNA, the Python implementation of weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). It identifies clusters of highly correlated genes, summarizes them as module eigengenes, and relates modules to sample traits such as genotype and age. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad415
skills.summary: Detect co-expression modules from bulk RNA-seq count matrices using PyWGCNA, the Python implementation of weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). It identifies clusters of highly correlated genes, summarizes them as module eigengenes, and relates modules to sample traits such as genotype and age.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need single-cell co-expression or differential expression rather than bulk-sample co-expression modules — PyWGCNA is designed for bulk RNA-seq datasets with many samples You only need pairwise gene correlations or a small pre-selected gene list analysis rather than unsupervised module discovery across the whole transcriptome Input is not a gene-by-sample count/normalized expression matrix (e.g. already-aggregated module statistics or a feature table) — the Data_format preprocessing step expects raw count-level input

skills.description: Use when a PyWGCNA co-expression network has already been built and you need module–trait correlations (e.g., module eigengene vs. genotype or age/time point) plus GO/KEGG/REACTOME enrichment of the correlated module.
skills.name: wgcna-module-trait-association-testing
skills.search_text: wgcna-module-trait-association-testing Use when a PyWGCNA co-expression network has already been built and you need module–trait correlations (e.g., module eigengene vs. genotype or age/time point) plus GO/KEGG/REACTOME enrichment of the correlated module. No co-expression modules have been detected yet — module identification (task_003-style WGCNA network construction) must come first Input is a single-gene differential expression table rather than a PyWGCNA object with eigengenes; use standard DE tools instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 PyWGCNA-based workflow for correlating co-expression module eigengenes with external sample traits (e.g., genotype and 18-month time point in 5xFAD/3xTg-AD brain bulk RNA-seq) and for running GO/KEGG/REACTOME functional enrichment on trait-associated modules such as the dark gray module containing Csf1, Tyrobp, and Trem2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad415
skills.summary: PyWGCNA-based workflow for correlating co-expression module eigengenes with external sample traits (e.g., genotype and 18-month time point in 5xFAD/3xTg-AD brain bulk RNA-seq) and for running GO/KEGG/REACTOME functional enrichment on trait-associated modules such as the dark gray module containing Csf1, Tyrobp, and Trem2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No co-expression modules have been detected yet — module identification (task_003-style WGCNA network construction) must come first Input is a single-gene differential expression table rather than a PyWGCNA object with eigengenes; use standard DE tools instead

skills.description: Use when raw tumor-normal WES/WGS FASTQ reads are about to be mapped to a reference genome (GRCh37/GRCh38) and adapter or low-quality artifacts must be removed first.
skills.name: wgs-read-quality-trimming
skills.search_text: wgs-read-quality-trimming Use when raw tumor-normal WES/WGS FASTQ reads are about to be mapped to a reference genome (GRCh37/GRCh38) and adapter or low-quality artifacts must be removed first. Input reads are already aligned (BAM/SAM) — trimming applies only to raw reads at the start of the pipeline The data is RNA-Seq rather than WES/WGS — TSNAD v2.0 handles RNA-Seq with the separate STAR/Arriba module instead Reads are synthetic or pre-cleaned test data with no adapters, where trimming adds no value before alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Quality/adapter trimming of raw WES/WGS reads as the first step of the TSNAD v2.0 neoantigen pipeline, using Trimmomatic v0.39 to remove adapter artifacts before alignment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.016
skills.summary: Quality/adapter trimming of raw WES/WGS reads as the first step of the TSNAD v2.0 neoantigen pipeline, using Trimmomatic v0.39 to remove adapter artifacts before alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already aligned (BAM/SAM) — trimming applies only to raw reads at the start of the pipeline The data is RNA-Seq rather than WES/WGS — TSNAD v2.0 handles RNA-Seq with the separate STAR/Arriba module instead Reads are synthetic or pre-cleaned test data with no adapters, where trimming adds no value before alignment

skills.description: Use when constructing synthetic benchmark RNA-seq datasets with known fusion transcripts at graded expression/coverage levels, or when evaluating fusion-detection sensitivity across low-to-high sequencing depth.
skills.name: wgsim-read-simulation-coverage-scaling
skills.search_text: wgsim-read-simulation-coverage-scaling Use when constructing synthetic benchmark RNA-seq datasets with known fusion transcripts at graded expression/coverage levels, or when evaluating fusion-detection sensitivity across low-to-high sequencing depth. When evaluating de novo fusion discovery rather than targeted (anchored) detection — the simulated fusions are user-specified partner pairs When the input is already real tumor RNA-seq with validated fusions (e.g., CCLE/SRA:SRP186687 benchmarks) — simulation is unnecessary and may not capture real background complexity For single-end RNA-seq or whole-genome/exome data, since the downstream detection requires paired-end RNA-seq http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Simulate paired-end reads from constructed fusion-transcript references using wgsim across a doubling coverage ladder (2x to 128x), then spike the simulated fusion reads into real GM12878 RNA-seq background to build benchmark test datasets for targeted fusion detection (Anchored-fusion). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100733
skills.summary: Simulate paired-end reads from constructed fusion-transcript references using wgsim across a doubling coverage ladder (2x to 128x), then spike the simulated fusion reads into real GM12878 RNA-seq background to build benchmark test datasets for targeted fusion detection (Anchored-fusion).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When evaluating de novo fusion discovery rather than targeted (anchored) detection — the simulated fusions are user-specified partner pairs When the input is already real tumor RNA-seq with validated fusions (e.g., CCLE/SRA:SRP186687 benchmarks) — simulation is unnecessary and may not capture real background complexity For single-end RNA-seq or whole-genome/exome data, since the downstream detection requires paired-end RNA-seq

skills.description: Use when you have a curated list of wheat (Triticum aestivum) miRNA precursors with genomic coordinates and need to quantify their A/B/D subgenome distribution and homologous-group (triad) structure.
skills.name: wheat-microrna-precursor-subgenome-assignment
skills.search_text: wheat-microrna-precursor-subgenome-assignment Use when you have a curated list of wheat (Triticum aestivum) miRNA precursors with genomic coordinates and need to quantify their A/B/D subgenome distribution and homologous-group (triad) structure. sRNA-Seq data or precursor candidates from species without a reference genome — iwa-miRNA 'cannot handle sRNA-Seq data from species without genome sequences' Sequences/reads that do not map to the reference genome — the current iwa-miRNA version ignores unmapped reads Species with a single (non-homeologous) genome, where A/B/D subgenome assignment and homologous-group triad analysis are meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Assigns wheat miRNA precursors (exported from the iwa-miRNA Manual Curation module) to the A, B, and D subgenomes of hexaploid bread wheat using GFF3/GTF coordinates, then clusters sequence-similar precursors into homologous groups and flags complete A:B:D triads to reveal homeologous-group structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.02.010
skills.summary: Assigns wheat miRNA precursors (exported from the iwa-miRNA Manual Curation module) to the A, B, and D subgenomes of hexaploid bread wheat using GFF3/GTF coordinates, then clusters sequence-similar precursors into homologous groups and flags complete A:B:D triads to reveal homeologous-group structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: sRNA-Seq data or precursor candidates from species without a reference genome — iwa-miRNA 'cannot handle sRNA-Seq data from species without genome sequences' Sequences/reads that do not map to the reference genome — the current iwa-miRNA version ignores unmapped reads Species with a single (non-homeologous) genome, where A/B/D subgenome assignment and homologous-group triad analysis are meaningless

skills.description: Use when multiple independent white adipose tissue (or comparable multi-donor tissue) scRNA-seq datasets must be uniformly annotated and integrated into a single reference atlas with cell type/state labels.
skills.name: white-adipose-tissue-reference-atlas-construction
skills.search_text: white-adipose-tissue-reference-atlas-construction Use when multiple independent white adipose tissue (or comparable multi-donor tissue) scRNA-seq datasets must be uniformly annotated and integrated into a single reference atlas with cell type/state labels. The task is single-dataset clustering or batch correction within one sample set rather than cross-study atlas construction Input data are not single-cell transcriptomes of adipose tissue (or a tissue where re-using WATLAS labels is not biologically defensible) A quick supervised label transfer suffices and there is no need to re-annotate and re-integrate the six source studies http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs WATLAS, a white adipose tissue reference atlas, by annotating cells from six independent scRNA-seq datasets (Tabula Sapiens, Jaitin GSE128518, Vijay GSE129363, Hildreth GSE155960, Emont SCP1376, Barboza) with JOINTLY and integrating them with scANVI into a consensus annotation of ~300,000 VAT/SAT cells at 17 major-type and 43 subtype resolution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44279-8
skills.summary: Constructs WATLAS, a white adipose tissue reference atlas, by annotating cells from six independent scRNA-seq datasets (Tabula Sapiens, Jaitin GSE128518, Vijay GSE129363, Hildreth GSE155960, Emont SCP1376, Barboza) with JOINTLY and integrating them with scANVI into a consensus annotation of ~300,000 VAT/SAT cells at 17 major-type and 43 subtype resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is single-dataset clustering or batch correction within one sample set rather than cross-study atlas construction Input data are not single-cell transcriptomes of adipose tissue (or a tissue where re-using WATLAS labels is not biologically defensible) A quick supervised label transfer suffices and there is no need to re-annotate and re-integrate the six source studies

skills.description: Use when you have noisy long-read single-cell RNA-seq data with discovered cellular barcodes and a short-read-derived whitelist, and need to filter against the whitelist and remove empty droplets.
skills.name: whitelist-filtering-of-cellular-barcodes
skills.search_text: whitelist-filtering-of-cellular-barcodes Use when you have noisy long-read single-cell RNA-seq data with discovered cellular barcodes and a short-read-derived whitelist, and need to filter against the whitelist and remove empty droplets. When barcodes are already known and the task is read demultiplexing/assignment rather than discovery and whitelist filtering (use known-sequence mode with a preset such as -d 10x3v3). When no short-read-derived whitelist or ground-truth barcode set exists to filter against. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Filter discovered or demultiplexed cellular barcodes against a short-read-derived whitelist and remove empty droplets using the inflection point method with flexiplex-filter, producing validated barcode frequency lists for benchmarking barcode discovery. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae102
skills.summary: Filter discovered or demultiplexed cellular barcodes against a short-read-derived whitelist and remove empty droplets using the inflection point method with flexiplex-filter, producing validated barcode frequency lists for benchmarking barcode discovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When barcodes are already known and the task is read demultiplexing/assignment rather than discovery and whitelist filtering (use known-sequence mode with a preset such as -d 10x3v3). When no short-read-derived whitelist or ground-truth barcode set exists to filter against.

skills.description: Use when running XClone's combine module on merged RDR and BAF results from scRNA-seq data and you need to check whether allele-specific CNA patterns (e.g., widespread LOH plus copy gains) indicate whole-genome duplication.
skills.name: whole-genome-duplication-warning
skills.search_text: whole-genome-duplication-warning Use when running XClone's combine module on merged RDR and BAF results from scRNA-seq data and you need to check whether allele-specific CNA patterns (e.g., widespread LOH plus copy gains) indicate whole-genome duplication. Input is raw scRNA-seq counts without prior RDR and BAF module outputs — the combine/WGD check requires both module results Sample is copy-number neutral (e.g., normal reference cells like ref_celltype='N'); WGD signatures will not be present and the warning is not expected http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Detects and flags whole-genome duplication (WGD) signatures when combining XClone's RDR and BAF modules: the combine step emits four-state CNA calls and raises a WGD warning when duplication signatures are present in the per-gene-per-cell CNA states. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51026-0
skills.summary: Detects and flags whole-genome duplication (WGD) signatures when combining XClone's RDR and BAF modules: the combine step emits four-state CNA calls and raises a WGD warning when duplication signatures are present in the per-gene-per-cell CNA states.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw scRNA-seq counts without prior RDR and BAF module outputs — the combine/WGD check requires both module results Sample is copy-number neutral (e.g., normal reference cells like ref_celltype='N'); WGD signatures will not be present and the warning is not expected

skills.description: Use when a wide-format scRNA-seq count matrix (cells x genes, .csv) must be converted into a Spark-optimized tall (cell, gene, count) format before downstream filtering or normalization.
skills.name: wide-to-tall-dataframe-reshaping
skills.search_text: wide-to-tall-dataframe-reshaping Use when a wide-format scRNA-seq count matrix (cells x genes, .csv) must be converted into a Spark-optimized tall (cell, gene, count) format before downstream filtering or normalization. Input is already a tall cell-gene-count dataframe or an existing .parquet file produced by a prior melt Downstream step is not Spark-based (e.g., a Seurat or Scanpy in-memory pipeline), where wide in-memory matrices are expected Dataset fits comfortably in RAM and does not need Spark/Parquet optimization http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Stage-1 preprocessing skill from scSPARKL that reshapes a wide-format scRNA-seq count matrix (.csv) into a tall cell-gene-count Spark dataframe via melt_Spark() and persists it as compressed Apache Parquet, reducing the columnar load so analysis can run on commodity hardware with as little as 4 GB RAM. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-025-12897-5
skills.summary: Stage-1 preprocessing skill from scSPARKL that reshapes a wide-format scRNA-seq count matrix (.csv) into a tall cell-gene-count Spark dataframe via melt_Spark() and persists it as compressed Apache Parquet, reducing the columnar load so analysis can run on commodity hardware with as little as 4 GB RAM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a tall cell-gene-count dataframe or an existing .parquet file produced by a prior melt Downstream step is not Spark-based (e.g., a Seurat or Scanpy in-memory pipeline), where wide in-memory matrices are expected Dataset fits comfortably in RAM and does not need Spark/Parquet optimization

skills.description: Use when you need cell-type-specific marker gene sets from scRNA-seq cluster data — e.g., ten highly specific plus ten low-specificity markers per cell type via Wilcoxon rank-sum — as input to ScType gene_sets_prepare/sctype_score.
skills.name: wilcoxon-differential-expression-marker-selection
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-differential-expression-marker-selection Use when you need cell-type-specific marker gene sets from scRNA-seq cluster data — e.g., ten highly specific plus ten low-specificity markers per cell type via Wilcoxon rank-sum — as input to ScType gene_sets_prepare/sctype_score. No prior cell-type grouping or labels exist and markers must be selected purely from cluster-wide averages without DE testing (e.g., scCATCH-style workflows that cannot accept custom markers) The goal is variant/SNV calling rather than marker-based annotation (use VarTrix instead) Input is already a curated marker gene set — skip DE selection and pass markers directly to gene_sets_prepare http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Selects cell-type marker genes by Wilcoxon rank-sum differential expression between cell types, picking ten highly specific and ten low-specificity markers per cell type to build ScType positive and negative marker sets for annotation and dropout-robustness benchmarks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28803-w
skills.summary: Selects cell-type marker genes by Wilcoxon rank-sum differential expression between cell types, picking ten highly specific and ten low-specificity markers per cell type to build ScType positive and negative marker sets for annotation and dropout-robustness benchmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No prior cell-type grouping or labels exist and markers must be selected purely from cluster-wide averages without DE testing (e.g., scCATCH-style workflows that cannot accept custom markers) The goal is variant/SNV calling rather than marker-based annotation (use VarTrix instead) Input is already a curated marker gene set — skip DE selection and pass markers directly to gene_sets_prepare

skills.description: Use when preparing scRNA-seq data for CellChat communication inference: clustered cell groups exist and over-expressed signaling genes must be identified before computing ligand-receptor communication probabilities.
skills.name: wilcoxon-differential-signaling-gene-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-differential-signaling-gene-testing Use when preparing scRNA-seq data for CellChat communication inference: clustered cell groups exist and over-expressed signaling genes must be identified before computing ligand-receptor communication probabilities. Cell groups are not yet defined (cell clustering is a pre-requisite for CellChat analysis) The goal is differential expression of all genes, not specifically signaling genes curated in a ligand-receptor database Data are spatial transcriptomics at single-cell resolution where Spatial CellChat (CellChat v3) with spatial constraints is more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Identify differentially expressed signaling genes (ligands, receptors, cofactors) across cell groups in an scRNA-seq dataset using the Wilcoxon rank sum test at significance level 0.05, as the first statistical filter in the CellChat cell-cell communication inference pipeline prior to ligand-receptor interaction inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9
skills.summary: Identify differentially expressed signaling genes (ligands, receptors, cofactors) across cell groups in an scRNA-seq dataset using the Wilcoxon rank sum test at significance level 0.05, as the first statistical filter in the CellChat cell-cell communication inference pipeline prior to ligand-receptor interaction inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell groups are not yet defined (cell clustering is a pre-requisite for CellChat analysis) The goal is differential expression of all genes, not specifically signaling genes curated in a ligand-receptor database Data are spatial transcriptomics at single-cell resolution where Spatial CellChat (CellChat v3) with spatial constraints is more appropriate

skills.description: Use when bulk tumor expression profiles have been projected through a single-cell-trained Miscell encoder (moco-dim 64) and you must test each latent feature for responder-vs-non-responder differences in an ICB cohort, or generally when comparing two patient groups on non-normal feature scores.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-association-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-association-testing Use when bulk tumor expression profiles have been projected through a single-cell-trained Miscell encoder (moco-dim 64) and you must test each latent feature for responder-vs-non-responder differences in an ICB cohort, or generally when comparing two patient groups on non-normal feature scores. Datasets are small — Miscell demands a large sample size to obtain good performance, so features from small cohorts will be unreliable Batch effects are present and uncorrected — Miscell does not internally include batch-correction methods, so running it directly will confound the latent features A practitioner needs interpretable features — the clinically significant latent features extracted by Miscell lack explainability http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Score bulk tumor RNA-seq-derived Miscell latent features (e.g., 64 features per patient from the 298-patient urothelial carcinoma ICB cohort of Mariathasan et al., 2018) for association with immune checkpoint blockade therapy response using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test, the differential analysis adopted by Seurat and Scanpy, followed by multiple-testing correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103200
skills.summary: Score bulk tumor RNA-seq-derived Miscell latent features (e.g., 64 features per patient from the 298-patient urothelial carcinoma ICB cohort of Mariathasan et al., 2018) for association with immune checkpoint blockade therapy response using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test, the differential analysis adopted by Seurat and Scanpy, followed by multiple-testing correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets are small — Miscell demands a large sample size to obtain good performance, so features from small cohorts will be unreliable Batch effects are present and uncorrected — Miscell does not internally include batch-correction methods, so running it directly will confound the latent features A practitioner needs interpretable features — the clinically significant latent features extracted by Miscell lack explainability

skills.description: Use when a processed Seurat scRNA-seq object with cluster/subcluster labels (e.g. PBMC3k) needs a cluster-specific marker gene list, and genes shared with background clusters must be excluded.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-cluster-comparison
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-cluster-comparison Use when a processed Seurat scRNA-seq object with cluster/subcluster labels (e.g. PBMC3k) needs a cluster-specific marker gene list, and genes shared with background clusters must be excluded. The Seurat object has no cluster or subcluster annotations, so no target-vs-background comparison can be defined The goal is reclustering or rare-cell discovery (use SCISSORS' silhouette scoring and semi-supervised reclustering steps, e.g. ComputeSilhouetteScores/getClusters, not marker filtering) Differential expression against a bulk or cross-dataset comparison is needed rather than a within-dataset cluster-vs-background contrast http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 SCISSORS' marker gene identification module: a candidate list is generated by Wilcoxon rank-sum differential expression of a target cluster or subcluster against background (rest-of-clusters or closely related subclusters), then filtered by expression percentile in non-target clusters to retain only genes of high specificity to the cell type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad449
skills.summary: SCISSORS' marker gene identification module: a candidate list is generated by Wilcoxon rank-sum differential expression of a target cluster or subcluster against background (rest-of-clusters or closely related subclusters), then filtered by expression percentile in non-target clusters to retain only genes of high specificity to the cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The Seurat object has no cluster or subcluster annotations, so no target-vs-background comparison can be defined The goal is reclustering or rare-cell discovery (use SCISSORS' silhouette scoring and semi-supervised reclustering steps, e.g. ComputeSilhouetteScores/getClusters, not marker filtering) Differential expression against a bulk or cross-dataset comparison is needed rather than a within-dataset cluster-vs-background contrast

skills.description: Use when you need cluster-level DEGs from a single-dataset scRNA-seq Seurat object and want per-gene discrimination metrics (AUC, sensitivity, specificity), e.g. to benchmark a binary marker method like CDI against a standard Wilcoxon baseline.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-deg-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-deg-testing Use when you need cluster-level DEGs from a single-dataset scRNA-seq Seurat object and want per-gene discrimination metrics (AUC, sensitivity, specificity), e.g. to benchmark a binary marker method like CDI against a standard Wilcoxon baseline. When the goal is to identify binary (on/off) cluster-discriminating markers with maximum cluster specificity — the article's CDI-based findCDIMarkers approach outperformed Wilcoxon on specificity (0.95 vs 0.75) When the analysis requires modeling variation across biological replicates — the article notes existing DE methods for scRNA-seq fail to account for this http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Rank-sum based differential expression testing per cell cluster in a Seurat object via scMiko's getDEG(), which returns per-marker AUC, sensitivity, and specificity indices alongside DEG calls, enabling benchmarking of DE methods such as CDI. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04093-2
skills.summary: Rank-sum based differential expression testing per cell cluster in a Seurat object via scMiko's getDEG(), which returns per-marker AUC, sensitivity, and specificity indices alongside DEG calls, enabling benchmarking of DE methods such as CDI.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to identify binary (on/off) cluster-discriminating markers with maximum cluster specificity — the article's CDI-based findCDIMarkers approach outperformed Wilcoxon on specificity (0.95 vs 0.75) When the analysis requires modeling variation across biological replicates — the article notes existing DE methods for scRNA-seq fail to account for this

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq cell population has been binarized by pathway activity (e.g., GSDensity compute.cell.label PAL labels) and you must test whether a gene of interest is differentially expressed between the pathway-positive and pathway-negative cells.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-differential-expression-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-differential-expression-testing Use when a scRNA-seq cell population has been binarized by pathway activity (e.g., GSDensity compute.cell.label PAL labels) and you must test whether a gene of interest is differentially expressed between the pathway-positive and pathway-negative cells.
