skills.summary: Wilcoxon rank-sum testing of a marker gene (e.g., MKI67, TYRO3) between pathway-binarized tumor cell groups defined by GSDensity PAL binarization (G2M checkpoint-positive vs. negative), used to validate that dividing TNBC tumor cells preferentially express proliferation and GAS6-TYRO3 markers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input gene set has not passed the GSDensity coordination test (compute.kld significance); the article recommends performing binarization only on gene sets that pass the coordination test The data are targeted-gene panels with limited numbers of genes — GSDensity-based binarization feeding the test is unsuitable there Cells are not labeled by pathway activity (no PAL binarization) — the test needs a two-group grouping grounded in the pathway activity distribution

skills.description: Use when you have per-spot/per-cell normalized spatial transcriptomics expression with assigned spatial-domain labels and need domain-enriched genes or SVG candidates, e.g. recovering DLPFC cortical-layer SVGs.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-gene-screening
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-gene-screening Use when you have per-spot/per-cell normalized spatial transcriptomics expression with assigned spatial-domain labels and need domain-enriched genes or SVG candidates, e.g. recovering DLPFC cortical-layer SVGs. Spatial domain labels have not yet been assigned — Splane domain identification (after Spoint deconvolution for seq-based data like 10X Visium) must precede the per-domain differential test The goal is nonlinear slice alignment or 3D stacking rather than domain-enriched gene detection http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Screens genes enriched in identified spatial domains by running a Wilcoxon rank-sum differential expression test on the normalized expression matrix (scanpy rank_genes_groups), filtering DEGs at logFC > 0.5 and P < 0.01 to recover spatially variable genes (SVGs) matching known cortical-layer markers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43220-3
skills.summary: Screens genes enriched in identified spatial domains by running a Wilcoxon rank-sum differential expression test on the normalized expression matrix (scanpy rank_genes_groups), filtering DEGs at logFC > 0.5 and P < 0.01 to recover spatially variable genes (SVGs) matching known cortical-layer markers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spatial domain labels have not yet been assigned — Splane domain identification (after Spoint deconvolution for seq-based data like 10X Visium) must precede the per-domain differential test The goal is nonlinear slice alignment or 3D stacking rather than domain-enriched gene detection

skills.description: Use when comparing a continuous per-region metric (e.g. novel/structured RNA fraction of dsRID-predicted dsRNA regions) between two independent sample groups such as AD and control brain, without assuming normality.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-group-comparison
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-group-comparison Use when comparing a continuous per-region metric (e.g. novel/structured RNA fraction of dsRID-predicted dsRNA regions) between two independent sample groups such as AD and control brain, without assuming normality. When the comparison involves only categorical overlap counts (shared vs group-specific regions) — use Fisher's exact test on the contingency table, as the study does When the two sample groups are paired or matched rather than independent AD and control cohorts — the rank-sum test assumes independent samples When input is raw read data rather than per-region dsRID predictions — the test operates on computed per-region/per-sample fractions, not on BAM files directly http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Non-parametric two-group comparison of region-level continuous metrics — here, the novel/structured RNA fractions of candidate dsRNA regions predicted by dsRID in AD versus control brain samples from the ENCODE consortium PacBio long-read RNA-seq cohort — used alongside Fisher's exact test on the shared/AD-specific/control-specific overlap contingency. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad649
skills.summary: Non-parametric two-group comparison of region-level continuous metrics — here, the novel/structured RNA fractions of candidate dsRNA regions predicted by dsRID in AD versus control brain samples from the ENCODE consortium PacBio long-read RNA-seq cohort — used alongside Fisher's exact test on the shared/AD-specific/control-specific overlap contingency.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the comparison involves only categorical overlap counts (shared vs group-specific regions) — use Fisher's exact test on the contingency table, as the study does When the two sample groups are paired or matched rather than independent AD and control cohorts — the rank-sum test assumes independent samples When input is raw read data rather than per-region dsRID predictions — the test operates on computed per-region/per-sample fractions, not on BAM files directly

skills.description: Use when you have a per-sample table with a binary viral-status grouping (e.g., IIV31-positive vs -negative from Source Data file 4) and continuous per-sample quantities (TMB, CNA burden, immune fractions) whose between-group differences must be tested without distributional assumptions.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-group-comparison
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-group-comparison Use when you have a per-sample table with a binary viral-status grouping (e.g., IIV31-positive vs -negative from Source Data file 4) and continuous per-sample quantities (TMB, CNA burden, immune fractions) whose between-group differences must be tested without distributional assumptions. The outcome is binary (e.g., Trichomonas vaginalis positivity) rather than a continuous measurement — a Fisher exact test on the 2x2 contingency table is required instead The comparison involves survival curves rather than per-sample scalar values — a two-sided log-rank test on Kaplan-Meier curves is required instead Per-sample grouping labels (IIV31 status) have not yet been generated from viRNAtrap viral-read detection and expert verification http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Non-parametric (two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum / Mann-Whitney) comparison of continuous measurements between IIV31-positive and IIV31-negative UCEC groups, used in the divergent-virus association analysis (Fig. 4b-e) to test TMB, chromosome-level CNA burden, and CIBERSORT CD8+ T-cell/Treg fractions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36336-z
skills.summary: Non-parametric (two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum / Mann-Whitney) comparison of continuous measurements between IIV31-positive and IIV31-negative UCEC groups, used in the divergent-virus association analysis (Fig. 4b-e) to test TMB, chromosome-level CNA burden, and CIBERSORT CD8+ T-cell/Treg fractions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The outcome is binary (e.g., Trichomonas vaginalis positivity) rather than a continuous measurement — a Fisher exact test on the 2x2 contingency table is required instead The comparison involves survival curves rather than per-sample scalar values — a two-sided log-rank test on Kaplan-Meier curves is required instead Per-sample grouping labels (IIV31 status) have not yet been generated from viRNAtrap viral-read detection and expert verification

skills.description: Use when you need a clustering-based DEG baseline for benchmarking: cells can be clustered into biologically meaningful groups and per-cluster marker genes (e.g. via FindAllMarkers) must be ranked by p-value to compare against an alternative method.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-marker-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-marker-testing Use when you need a clustering-based DEG baseline for benchmarking: cells can be clustered into biologically meaningful groups and per-cluster marker genes (e.g. via FindAllMarkers) must be ranked by p-value to compare against an alternative method. The goal is clustering-independent DEG prediction without defining cell clusters — use singleCellHaystack's `haystack()` directly instead of cluster-restricted marker testing Clusters are not biologically interpretable or the number of relevant clusters is unclear, which the paper identifies as a major problem for clustering-based DEG prediction The input is spatial transcriptomics data where the aim is to test genes against actual 2D tissue coordinates rather than per-cluster markers http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Cluster-wise differential expression testing with Seurat's FindAllMarkers using the default Wilcoxon rank-sum test, used in this paper as the clustering-based baseline against which singleCellHaystack's clustering-independent DEG prediction is compared on the Tabula Muris bone marrow dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17900-3
skills.summary: Cluster-wise differential expression testing with Seurat's FindAllMarkers using the default Wilcoxon rank-sum test, used in this paper as the clustering-based baseline against which singleCellHaystack's clustering-independent DEG prediction is compared on the Tabula Muris bone marrow dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is clustering-independent DEG prediction without defining cell clusters — use singleCellHaystack's `haystack()` directly instead of cluster-restricted marker testing Clusters are not biologically interpretable or the number of relevant clusters is unclear, which the paper identifies as a major problem for clustering-based DEG prediction The input is spatial transcriptomics data where the aim is to test genes against actual 2D tissue coordinates rather than per-cluster markers

skills.description: Use when you need to derive a robust, pan-dataset malignant-vs-non-malignant marker gene feature set by intersecting statistically significant DEGs across multiple annotated cancer scRNA-seq training datasets.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-multiple-testing-correction Use when you need to derive a robust, pan-dataset malignant-vs-non-malignant marker gene feature set by intersecting statistically significant DEGs across multiple annotated cancer scRNA-seq training datasets. The goal is to annotate non-cancer cell subpopulations (immune, stromal, epithelial) — PreCanCell's DEG features are limited to binary cancer vs non-cancer annotation Only one dataset is available for differential expression, since the TMG/NMG sets require genes to pass significance and fold-change criteria in all five training datasets Expression data are raw counts without library-depth normalization (e.g. TPM/CPM), since FindMarkers() is applied to normalized values produced via Seurat's NormalizeData() http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies genes differentially expressed between malignant and non-malignant cells in each of five cancer scRNA-seq training datasets (RCC, HNSCC, melanoma, LUAD, BC) using Seurat's FindMarkers() with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test, Bonferroni-adjusted P < 0.05, and a 10% detection / logFC > 0.25 upregulation filter, then intersects results across datasets to form the 73-TMG and 186-NMG feature sets for PreCanCell. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.07.009
skills.summary: Identifies genes differentially expressed between malignant and non-malignant cells in each of five cancer scRNA-seq training datasets (RCC, HNSCC, melanoma, LUAD, BC) using Seurat's FindMarkers() with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test, Bonferroni-adjusted P < 0.05, and a 10% detection / logFC > 0.25 upregulation filter, then intersects results across datasets to form the 73-TMG and 186-NMG feature sets for PreCanCell.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to annotate non-cancer cell subpopulations (immune, stromal, epithelial) — PreCanCell's DEG features are limited to binary cancer vs non-cancer annotation Only one dataset is available for differential expression, since the TMG/NMG sets require genes to pass significance and fold-change criteria in all five training datasets Expression data are raw counts without library-depth normalization (e.g. TPM/CPM), since FindMarkers() is applied to normalized values produced via Seurat's NormalizeData()

skills.description: Use when comparing two methods' distributions of per-run statistical significance (e.g. DA-test P-values over 100 simulation replicates) and you need a non-parametric rank-based test of whether one method attains systematically smaller P-values.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-significance-comparison
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-significance-comparison Use when comparing two methods' distributions of per-run statistical significance (e.g. DA-test P-values over 100 simulation replicates) and you need a non-parametric rank-based test of whether one method attains systematically smaller P-values. When the per-run significance values are paired across runs rather than independent samples — a rank-sum test on independent samples would be inappropriate When only single point-estimate statistics per method exist (no replicate-run distributions), since the rank-sum test requires distributions of values to compare When the goal is a parametric comparison of means with verified normality; a t-test would have more power in that setting http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmarking skill from the ELVAR paper: apply one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests to compare distributions of negative-binomial-regression DA-test P-values produced over 100 simulation runs, establishing whether cell-attribute aware EVA clustering (ELVAR) yields significantly stronger differential-abundance significance than Louvain-based baselines (LVdet, LVnonseq). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39017-z
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill from the ELVAR paper: apply one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests to compare distributions of negative-binomial-regression DA-test P-values produced over 100 simulation runs, establishing whether cell-attribute aware EVA clustering (ELVAR) yields significantly stronger differential-abundance significance than Louvain-based baselines (LVdet, LVnonseq).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the per-run significance values are paired across runs rather than independent samples — a rank-sum test on independent samples would be inappropriate When only single point-estimate statistics per method exist (no replicate-run distributions), since the rank-sum test requires distributions of values to compare When the goal is a parametric comparison of means with verified normality; a t-test would have more power in that setting

skills.description: Use when you have per-pair predicted scores (e.g. DeepHLApan binding/immunogenicity scores) plus binary experimental labels and must test whether the scores separate the labeled groups non-parametrically.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-significance-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-significance-testing Use when you have per-pair predicted scores (e.g. DeepHLApan binding/immunogenicity scores) plus binary experimental labels and must test whether the scores separate the labeled groups non-parametrically. Data are paired/matched measurements rather than two independent groups — use a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test instead Scores are already validated against the same labels and only thresholded neoantigen calls are needed (binding score >0.5 and immunogenic score >0.5 filter), with no group-difference hypothesis to test Input is raw WES/WGS/RNA-seq data requiring the TSNAD prediction pipeline first, rather than a scored pMHC table http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Applies Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann–Whitney U) tests to compare predicted neoantigen score distributions between immunogenic and non-immunogenic pMHC pairs, as demonstrated when validating TSNAD v2.0's DeepHLApan immunogenicity scores on the 608-pair TESLA benchmark. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.016
skills.summary: Applies Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann–Whitney U) tests to compare predicted neoantigen score distributions between immunogenic and non-immunogenic pMHC pairs, as demonstrated when validating TSNAD v2.0's DeepHLApan immunogenicity scores on the 608-pair TESLA benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are paired/matched measurements rather than two independent groups — use a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test instead Scores are already validated against the same labels and only thresholded neoantigen calls are needed (binding score >0.5 and immunogenic score >0.5 filter), with no group-difference hypothesis to test Input is raw WES/WGS/RNA-seq data requiring the TSNAD prediction pipeline first, rather than a scored pMHC table

skills.description: Use when per-cell NFE (or similar potency) scores have been computed for cells grouped into developmental stages and you need a non-parametric statistical test of whether earlier-stage cells are systematically more potent than mature-stage cells.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-stage-comparison
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-stage-comparison Use when per-cell NFE (or similar potency) scores have been computed for cells grouped into developmental stages and you need a non-parametric statistical test of whether earlier-stage cells are systematically more potent than mature-stage cells. The input is already a cell-level gene expression matrix without any network/entropy transformation — apply c-CSN to build CCSN and compute NFE before testing Stages are not ordered along a differentiation trajectory and a two-sided or non-directional test is required The goal is clustering or dimension reduction (CNDM analyses), not potency comparison across stages http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Statistical comparison of c-CSN-derived network flow entropy (NFE) scores between differentiation stages using one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, to verify that NFE is higher in progenitors (e.g. Wang Day 0/Day 1 vs Day 30 mature neurons) and thus resolves differentiation trajectory direction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.05.005
skills.summary: Statistical comparison of c-CSN-derived network flow entropy (NFE) scores between differentiation stages using one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, to verify that NFE is higher in progenitors (e.g. Wang Day 0/Day 1 vs Day 30 mature neurons) and thus resolves differentiation trajectory direction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a cell-level gene expression matrix without any network/entropy transformation — apply c-CSN to build CCSN and compute NFE before testing Stages are not ordered along a differentiation trajectory and a two-sided or non-directional test is required The goal is clustering or dimension reduction (CNDM analyses), not potency comparison across stages

skills.description: Use when comparing two independent score or expression distributions without distributional assumptions — e.g., testing whether 800-gene-set AUROCs exceed 100-gene-set AUROCs, or identifying marker genes by comparing subtype cells against all other interneurons within one study.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing Use when comparing two independent score or expression distributions without distributional assumptions — e.g., testing whether 800-gene-set AUROCs exceed 100-gene-set AUROCs, or identifying marker genes by comparing subtype cells against all other interneurons within one study. The comparison involves more than two independent groups (e.g., testing AUROC across >2 gene-set size bins), where a Kruskal-Wallis test or analogous multi-group method is required instead. Subtype assignments are not yet validated across datasets (no reciprocal top hits with AUROC >= 0.9 from MetaNeighborUS), so the subtype-vs-rest contrast has no replicated cell identity to test against. Count-level modeling with library-size and dispersion control is required (e.g., raw UMI counts requiring a negative-binomial framework) rather than rank-based testing on RPKM values. Non-parametric Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann-Whitney) testing used in the MetaNeighbor replicability framework both to compare AUROC distributions (e.g., 100-gene vs 800-gene sets) and to run one-sided per-study differential expression tests that are combined across studies with Fisher's method to recover interneuron subtype marker genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03282-0
skills.summary: Non-parametric Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann-Whitney) testing used in the MetaNeighbor replicability framework both to compare AUROC distributions (e.g., 100-gene vs 800-gene sets) and to run one-sided per-study differential expression tests that are combined across studies with Fisher's method to recover interneuron subtype marker genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The comparison involves more than two independent groups (e.g., testing AUROC across >2 gene-set size bins), where a Kruskal-Wallis test or analogous multi-group method is required instead. Subtype assignments are not yet validated across datasets (no reciprocal top hits with AUROC >= 0.9 from MetaNeighborUS), so the subtype-vs-rest contrast has no replicated cell identity to test against. Count-level modeling with library-size and dispersion control is required (e.g., raw UMI counts requiring a negative-binomial framework) rather than rank-based testing on RPKM values.

skills.description: Use when identifying per-cluster marker genes from a clustered single-cell RNA-seq matrix prior to cell type annotation, and when avoiding pseudo marker genes that are upregulated in multiple clusters.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing Use when identifying per-cluster marker genes from a clustered single-cell RNA-seq matrix prior to cell type annotation, and when avoiding pseudo marker genes that are upregulated in multiple clusters. Input is already a curated marker gene list or feature table rather than a raw expression matrix with cluster labels The goal is one-against-all differential expression rather than scCATCH's paired one-against-one comparison to eliminate pseudo marker genes upregulated in multiple clusters Clusters are inadequately resolved (too many or too few clusters), which the article notes introduces errors into downstream cell type annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies Wilcoxon rank-sum (Wilcoxon rank-sum/one-against-one paired cluster) testing within scCATCH's findmarkergene step to identify genes significantly upregulated in only one cluster, filtering by log10 fold change >= 0.25, p < 0.05, and expression in >= 25% of cells. This paired-comparison design avoids pseudo marker genes produced by one-against-all approaches. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100882
skills.summary: Applies Wilcoxon rank-sum (Wilcoxon rank-sum/one-against-one paired cluster) testing within scCATCH's findmarkergene step to identify genes significantly upregulated in only one cluster, filtering by log10 fold change >= 0.25, p < 0.05, and expression in >= 25% of cells. This paired-comparison design avoids pseudo marker genes produced by one-against-all approaches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated marker gene list or feature table rather than a raw expression matrix with cluster labels The goal is one-against-all differential expression rather than scCATCH's paired one-against-one comparison to eliminate pseudo marker genes upregulated in multiple clusters Clusters are inadequately resolved (too many or too few clusters), which the article notes introduces errors into downstream cell type annotation

skills.description: Use when you have per-cell state labels from a single-cell classifier (e.g. TILPRED on GSE120575 CD8 T cells) paired pre/post treatment across a handful of patients, and need a p-value for state-proportion shifts between responder and non-responder groups.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing-of-cell-proportions
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing-of-cell-proportions Use when you have per-cell state labels from a single-cell classifier (e.g. TILPRED on GSE120575 CD8 T cells) paired pre/post treatment across a handful of patients, and need a p-value for state-proportion shifts between responder and non-responder groups. Input is raw counts or unclassified cells — you must first assign per-cell states (e.g. with TILPRED) before computing state proportions The data are murine (e.g. B16CD8TIL_SCE example SCE) — predictTilState must be run with human=FALSE; the GSE120575 responder-analysis workflow assumes human=TRUE You have many matched samples and can assume normality of proportion differences — a paired parametric test would be more appropriate than a rank-sum test on 7 patients http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Non-parametric one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test on per-patient proportions of a predicted CD8 TIL state (e.g. EM-like, as assigned by TILPRED) before versus after ICB therapy, comparing responders to non-responders to determine whether treatment induces expansion of that state. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2020.1737369
skills.summary: Non-parametric one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test on per-patient proportions of a predicted CD8 TIL state (e.g. EM-like, as assigned by TILPRED) before versus after ICB therapy, comparing responders to non-responders to determine whether treatment induces expansion of that state.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw counts or unclassified cells — you must first assign per-cell states (e.g. with TILPRED) before computing state proportions The data are murine (e.g. B16CD8TIL_SCE example SCE) — predictTilState must be run with human=FALSE; the GSE120575 responder-analysis workflow assumes human=TRUE You have many matched samples and can assume normality of proportion differences — a paired parametric test would be more appropriate than a rank-sum test on 7 patients

skills.description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq or microarray samples from multiple pancreatic compartments (normal pancreas, primary PDAC, PDX, CAF lines, metastasis) and need to test which tissue types drive a curated gene signature's expression.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing-of-tissue-type-expression
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing-of-tissue-type-expression Use when you have bulk RNA-seq or microarray samples from multiple pancreatic compartments (normal pancreas, primary PDAC, PDX, CAF lines, metastasis) and need to test which tissue types drive a curated gene signature's expression. Input is single-cell data (e.g., the rmoffitt/scOh atlas) — this skill is defined for bulk transcriptomics, where the article notes 'we are limited in our ability to fully separate cellular populations'; use the single-cell classifier instead Samples must be merged across platforms (bulk RNA-seq + microarrays) into one matrix — the article explicitly found data aggregation 'introduced more problems than it solved' The goal is survival or therapy-response prediction rather than two-group expression comparison — use PurIST subtyping and the survival/Cox tabs instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compares gene-signature scores (e.g., ADEX, Exocrine, Immunogenic) between tissue/cell-type groups in bulk PDAC expression datasets using Wilcoxon rank-sum tests to determine whether a signature is tissue-of-origin intrinsic or tumor-cell intrinsic, as in the Moffitt 2015 normal-pancreas-vs-PDAC analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04461-6
skills.summary: Compares gene-signature scores (e.g., ADEX, Exocrine, Immunogenic) between tissue/cell-type groups in bulk PDAC expression datasets using Wilcoxon rank-sum tests to determine whether a signature is tissue-of-origin intrinsic or tumor-cell intrinsic, as in the Moffitt 2015 normal-pancreas-vs-PDAC analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell data (e.g., the rmoffitt/scOh atlas) — this skill is defined for bulk transcriptomics, where the article notes 'we are limited in our ability to fully separate cellular populations'; use the single-cell classifier instead Samples must be merged across platforms (bulk RNA-seq + microarrays) into one matrix — the article explicitly found data aggregation 'introduced more problems than it solved' The goal is survival or therapy-response prediction rather than two-group expression comparison — use PurIST subtyping and the survival/Cox tabs instead

skills.description: Use when a single-cell gene expression matrix has cells split into exactly two user-defined groups and in-session differential expression markers are needed to order a heatmap.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-two-group-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-two-group-testing Use when a single-cell gene expression matrix has cells split into exactly two user-defined groups and in-session differential expression markers are needed to order a heatmap. The contrast involves more than two groups without a defined pairwise split — the workflow defines a two-group Wilcoxon rank-sum test between selected cell groups. The task is only visualizing or clustering a pre-existing marker gene list with no two-group differential-expression contrast to compute. The input is not per-cell gene expression with cell-group labels (e.g. bulk expression with one value per condition has no per-cell rank-sum structure). http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identifies differentially expressed marker genes between two user-defined cell groups by running a per-gene two-group Wilcoxon rank-sum test (implemented in C++ for speed in CellexalVR), Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, and ranking the top 250 marker genes for heatmap hierarchical clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103251
skills.summary: Identifies differentially expressed marker genes between two user-defined cell groups by running a per-gene two-group Wilcoxon rank-sum test (implemented in C++ for speed in CellexalVR), Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, and ranking the top 250 marker genes for heatmap hierarchical clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The contrast involves more than two groups without a defined pairwise split — the workflow defines a two-group Wilcoxon rank-sum test between selected cell groups. The task is only visualizing or clustering a pre-existing marker gene list with no two-group differential-expression contrast to compute. The input is not per-cell gene expression with cell-group labels (e.g. bulk expression with one value per condition has no per-cell rank-sum structure).

skills.description: Use when comparing clustering quality between two or more single-cell clustering solutions — e.g., per-cell silhouette scores from SCISSORS, Seurat, SAFE, or GiniClust3 — and you need paired significance testing on the score distributions.
skills.name: wilcoxon-ranked-significance-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-ranked-significance-testing Use when comparing clustering quality between two or more single-cell clustering solutions — e.g., per-cell silhouette scores from SCISSORS, Seurat, SAFE, or GiniClust3 — and you need paired significance testing on the score distributions. Cluster-level averaged silhouette values are used instead of per-cell scores (avg = TRUE or cluster::silhouette with average=TRUE), since pairing is lost and the test loses power for rare subclusters Clusterings partition different sets of cells, so no valid cell-level pairing exists between the score distributions The goal is differential expression testing between cell clusters rather than comparison of clustering-quality metrics http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Applies paired Wilcoxon rank-sum tests (wilcox.test) to per-cell silhouette score distributions to statistically compare the clustering quality of competing scRNA-seq clusterings (e.g., SCISSORS vs. Seurat, SAFE, GiniClust3), with results annotated as significance levels on violin plots via ggsignif. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad449
skills.summary: Applies paired Wilcoxon rank-sum tests (wilcox.test) to per-cell silhouette score distributions to statistically compare the clustering quality of competing scRNA-seq clusterings (e.g., SCISSORS vs. Seurat, SAFE, GiniClust3), with results annotated as significance levels on violin plots via ggsignif.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cluster-level averaged silhouette values are used instead of per-cell scores (avg = TRUE or cluster::silhouette with average=TRUE), since pairing is lost and the test loses power for rare subclusters Clusterings partition different sets of cells, so no valid cell-level pairing exists between the score distributions The goal is differential expression testing between cell clusters rather than comparison of clustering-quality metrics

skills.description: Use when you have a gene expression matrix plus scBGEDA cluster assignments (e.g. the QS_Heart dataset) and need to nominate per-cluster marker genes for cell-type annotation via known marker databases.
skills.name: wilcoxon-ranksum-per-cluster-deg-calling
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-ranksum-per-cluster-deg-calling Use when you have a gene expression matrix plus scBGEDA cluster assignments (e.g. the QS_Heart dataset) and need to nominate per-cluster marker genes for cell-type annotation via known marker databases. skills.summary: Identifies cell-type marker genes from scBGEDA-predicted cluster labels by running the Wilcoxon rank-sum test per cluster in scanpy, retaining the top 20 DEGs per cluster at P<0.05 and matching them against the CellMark marker database.

skills.description: Use when two paired measurements were taken on the same samples (e.g., silhouette widths in deep-feature space vs. the 273-gene CMS signature space) and you must test whether one representation is significantly more compact/separated than the other without assuming normality.
skills.name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-hypothesis-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-signed-rank-hypothesis-testing Use when two paired measurements were taken on the same samples (e.g., silhouette widths in deep-feature space vs. the 273-gene CMS signature space) and you must test whether one representation is significantly more compact/separated than the other without assuming normality. When the two groups of measurements are not paired (independent samples) — the signed-rank test requires paired differences on the same samples When the goal is unsupervised clustering of cancer patients — the article states DeepCC is 'specifically developed for addressing current challenges in classification but not clustering of cancer patients' When the input is already a prediction/label vector rather than paired continuous per-sample scores — use a classifier performance comparison instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Non-parametric paired significance test used in the DeepCC CRC study to verify that per-sample average silhouette widths computed in the 10-dimensional deep-feature space of the trained CRC_TCGA ANN significantly exceed those computed in the 273-gene CMS signature space at P < 0.01. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-019-0157-8
skills.summary: Non-parametric paired significance test used in the DeepCC CRC study to verify that per-sample average silhouette widths computed in the 10-dimensional deep-feature space of the trained CRC_TCGA ANN significantly exceed those computed in the 273-gene CMS signature space at P < 0.01.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the two groups of measurements are not paired (independent samples) — the signed-rank test requires paired differences on the same samples When the goal is unsupervised clustering of cancer patients — the article states DeepCC is 'specifically developed for addressing current challenges in classification but not clustering of cancer patients' When the input is already a prediction/label vector rather than paired continuous per-sample scores — use a classifier performance comparison instead

skills.description: Use when two methods are each evaluated on the same paired set of datasets (e.g., 44 atlas-scale normal/cancer tissues with per-dataset F1, balanced accuracy, or overall accuracy) and a nonparametric significance test of the metric differences is required.
skills.name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-paired-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-signed-rank-paired-testing Use when two methods are each evaluated on the same paired set of datasets (e.g., 44 atlas-scale normal/cancer tissues with per-dataset F1, balanced accuracy, or overall accuracy) and a nonparametric significance test of the metric differences is required. The two methods were evaluated on different, non-paired datasets — the signed-rank test requires pairwise differences on identical observations; use an unpaired test instead Only very few paired observations (e.g., fewer than ~6 datasets) are available, so signed-rank inference is underpowered The outcome of interest is runtime throughput alone, where the article's significant differences favored scType and the paired test should be reported rather than assumed favorable to Census http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Nonparametric paired Wilcoxon signed-rank testing of per-dataset metric differences between two annotation methods (e.g., Census vs scType overall accuracy across 44 held-out human/mouse tissue datasets), implemented in R with ggpubr's stat_compare_means. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad714
skills.summary: Nonparametric paired Wilcoxon signed-rank testing of per-dataset metric differences between two annotation methods (e.g., Census vs scType overall accuracy across 44 held-out human/mouse tissue datasets), implemented in R with ggpubr's stat_compare_means.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two methods were evaluated on different, non-paired datasets — the signed-rank test requires pairwise differences on identical observations; use an unpaired test instead Only very few paired observations (e.g., fewer than ~6 datasets) are available, so signed-rank inference is underpowered The outcome of interest is runtime throughput alone, where the article's significant differences favored scType and the paired test should be reported rather than assumed favorable to Census

skills.description: Use when two paired measurements over the same items (e.g., CIEDE2000 color differences per adjacent cell-type pair under two palettes) must be compared without assuming normality, and a one-sided ity claim is needed.
skills.name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-paired-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-signed-rank-paired-testing Use when two paired measurements over the same items (e.g., CIEDE2000 color differences per adjacent cell-type pair under two palettes) must be compared without assuming normality, and a one-sided ity claim is needed. The two samples are independent or unpaired (e.g., color differences computed over different cell-type-pair sets) — the signed-rank pairing is invalid The goal is testing mean differences of approximately normal paired data where a paired t-test is appropriate and more powerful The underlying palette colors are not derived from spatial relationships (no CI-graph), so no spatially aware comparison exists to test Applies a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test to paired, non-normal distributions, as used in the Spaco paper to show that the adaptive (graph-guided) palette has significantly higher pairwise CIEDE2000 color differences than a pre-defined (Scanpy default) palette (p = 1.27e-11) on the Stereo-seq axolotl brain dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100915
skills.summary: Applies a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test to paired, non-normal distributions, as used in the Spaco paper to show that the adaptive (graph-guided) palette has significantly higher pairwise CIEDE2000 color differences than a pre-defined (Scanpy default) palette (p = 1.27e-11) on the Stereo-seq axolotl brain dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two samples are independent or unpaired (e.g., color differences computed over different cell-type-pair sets) — the signed-rank pairing is invalid The goal is testing mean differences of approximately normal paired data where a paired t-test is appropriate and more powerful The underlying palette colors are not derived from spatial relationships (no CI-graph), so no spatially aware comparison exists to test

skills.description: Use when comparing paired per-replicate runtime (or other paired measurement) values across methods — e.g. three replicate subsamples per tool — and you need a distribution-free significance call without assuming normality.
skills.name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-significance-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-signed-rank-significance-testing Use when comparing paired per-replicate runtime (or other paired measurement) values across methods — e.g. three replicate subsamples per tool — and you need a distribution-free significance call without assuming normality. Measurements are independent/unpaired across conditions rather than paired on identical inputs — the signed-rank test requires paired observations The variable of interest is categorical or the sample provides no replicate pairing (e.g. a single runtime per method), making rank-based paired testing undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 A non-parametric paired significance test used in the dsCellNet benchmarking study to verify that dsCellNet's ~12 min runtime for 10,000 E15.5 cells is significantly faster than NATMI, CellPhoneDB, and SingleCellSignalR at p < 0.01. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.047
skills.summary: A non-parametric paired significance test used in the dsCellNet benchmarking study to verify that dsCellNet's ~12 min runtime for 10,000 E15.5 cells is significantly faster than NATMI, CellPhoneDB, and SingleCellSignalR at p < 0.01.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Measurements are independent/unpaired across conditions rather than paired on identical inputs — the signed-rank test requires paired observations The variable of interest is categorical or the sample provides no replicate pairing (e.g. a single runtime per method), making rank-based paired testing undefined

skills.description: Use when two or more classifiers have been run on the identical reference and validation datasets and per-sample (paired) performance scores exist, and you must test whether the performance gap for one class (e.g., cancer-cell F1) is significant.
skills.name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-significance-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-signed-rank-significance-testing Use when two or more classifiers have been run on the identical reference and validation datasets and per-sample (paired) performance scores exist, and you must test whether the performance gap for one class (e.g., cancer-cell F1) is significant. Scores are not paired — the tools were tested on different samples or datasets, so a signed-rank test on differences is invalid Only aggregated summary statistics (e.g., a single median F1 per tool) are available with no per-biopsy values to pair The comparison targets a single proportion or two-group continuous outcome with a different design — a t-test or unpaired rank-sum test is the appropriate choice http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Applies a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test to per-sample F1 scores from a controlled classifier benchmark, testing whether scATOMIC's cancer-cell classification advantage over six comparators (SingleR, Seurat, SingleCellNet, scmap-cell, CHETAH, scType) is statistically significant as reported for Fig. 2c. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-37353-8
skills.summary: Applies a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test to per-sample F1 scores from a controlled classifier benchmark, testing whether scATOMIC's cancer-cell classification advantage over six comparators (SingleR, Seurat, SingleCellNet, scmap-cell, CHETAH, scType) is statistically significant as reported for Fig. 2c.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Scores are not paired — the tools were tested on different samples or datasets, so a signed-rank test on differences is invalid Only aggregated summary statistics (e.g., a single median F1 per tool) are available with no per-biopsy values to pair The comparison targets a single proportion or two-group continuous outcome with a different design — a t-test or unpaired rank-sum test is the appropriate choice

skills.description: Use when comparing two methods' per-sample performance metrics (e.g., CCC/Pearson/RMSE over the same 124 pseudobulk samples) and a paired, one-sided significance assessment of whether one method outperforms the other is required.
skills.name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-significance-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-signed-rank-significance-testing Use when comparing two methods' per-sample performance metrics (e.g., CCC/Pearson/RMSE over the same 124 pseudobulk samples) and a paired, one-sided significance assessment of whether one method outperforms the other is required. Metric vectors are unpaired (different samples per method), where a paired signed-rank test is invalid and an unpaired test would be required The comparison involves more than two related conditions simultaneously, requiring a different omnibus procedure rather than pairwise Wilcoxon tests The analysis goal is deconvolution itself rather than significance assessment of already-computed metric differences http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 One-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test implemented in SciPy, used in the scSemiProfiler COVID-19 deconvolution benchmark to assess pairwise statistical significance of deconvolution accuracy differences (Lin's CCC, Pearson correlation, RMSE) between methods across the 124 pseudobulk samples. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50150-1
skills.summary: One-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test implemented in SciPy, used in the scSemiProfiler COVID-19 deconvolution benchmark to assess pairwise statistical significance of deconvolution accuracy differences (Lin's CCC, Pearson correlation, RMSE) between methods across the 124 pseudobulk samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Metric vectors are unpaired (different samples per method), where a paired signed-rank test is invalid and an unpaired test would be required The comparison involves more than two related conditions simultaneously, requiring a different omnibus procedure rather than pairwise Wilcoxon tests The analysis goal is deconvolution itself rather than significance assessment of already-computed metric differences

skills.description: Use when reproducing the decoupleR perturbation-benchmark weights ablation, i.e. when paired per-method with-weights vs without-weights perturbed-regulator recovery scores are available and a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test must be run on the paired deltas.
skills.name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-test-reproduction
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-signed-rank-test-reproduction Use when reproducing the decoupleR perturbation-benchmark weights ablation, i.e. when paired per-method with-weights vs without-weights perturbed-regulator recovery scores are available and a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test must be run on the paired deltas. Scores are unpaired (e.g. comparing disjoint method families or independent datasets) — the Wilcoxon signed-rank test requires matched with-weights/without-weights pairs per dataset/regulator combination. The goal is the manuscript's overall method ranking (e.g. simple linear models and the consensus score across top methods) rather than the Supplementary Fig. S4 weights ablation. No decoupleRBench outputs exist yet; the raw count table and metadata must first be processed through run_rna_bench.R / run_php_bench.R before the paired deltas can be tested. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduces the decoupleR manuscript's paired benchmark analysis showing that methods leveraging interaction weights perform significantly better when those weights are taken into account (one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, P < 2.2e-16; Supplementary Fig. S4). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac016
skills.summary: Reproduces the decoupleR manuscript's paired benchmark analysis showing that methods leveraging interaction weights perform significantly better when those weights are taken into account (one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, P < 2.2e-16; Supplementary Fig. S4).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Scores are unpaired (e.g. comparing disjoint method families or independent datasets) — the Wilcoxon signed-rank test requires matched with-weights/without-weights pairs per dataset/regulator combination. The goal is the manuscript's overall method ranking (e.g. simple linear models and the consensus score across top methods) rather than the Supplementary Fig. S4 weights ablation. No decoupleRBench outputs exist yet; the raw count table and metadata must first be processed through run_rna_bench.R / run_php_bench.R before the paired deltas can be tested.

skills.description: Use when per-event predictions from CLOUDe (classifications and theta1, theta2, log10(sigmaSq/(2*alpha)) values) must be statistically compared across deletion classes or against simulated expression distributions.
skills.name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing Use when per-event predictions from CLOUDe (classifications and theta1, theta2, log10(sigmaSq/(2*alpha)) values) must be statistically compared across deletion classes or against simulated expression distributions. Input is raw expression data before CLOUDe classification/prediction — no per-event parameters exist to compare yet The data are paired by design across more than two conditions requiring repeated-measures structure rather than a two-class rank comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 Apply Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann-Whitney U nonparametric tests in R to assess whether CLOUDe's predicted evolutionary parameters (|theta1−theta2| and log10(sigmaSq/(2*alpha))) differ between 'Redundant' and 'Unique' Drosophila deletion classes, and to compare empirical lost-gene expression against simulated expectations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae002
skills.summary: Apply Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann-Whitney U nonparametric tests in R to assess whether CLOUDe's predicted evolutionary parameters (|theta1−theta2| and log10(sigmaSq/(2*alpha))) differ between 'Redundant' and 'Unique' Drosophila deletion classes, and to compare empirical lost-gene expression against simulated expectations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw expression data before CLOUDe classification/prediction — no per-event parameters exist to compare yet The data are paired by design across more than two conditions requiring repeated-measures structure rather than a two-class rank comparison

skills.description: Use when you have paired perturbed/unperturbed expression samples from matched cells (e.g., GRouNdGAN knockout vs control) and need per-edge significance of TF-gene regulation with multiple-testing correction.
skills.name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing Use when you have paired perturbed/unperturbed expression samples from matched cells (e.g., GRouNdGAN knockout vs control) and need per-edge significance of TF-gene regulation with multiple-testing correction. You want to predict whether TF knockout will change expression in real, non-simulated cells — GRouNdGAN is generative, not predictive, and would need retraining and a high-quality GRN plus data modalities such as scATAC-seq or TF ChIP-seq Perturbed and control cells are not matched (independently sampled), since the signed-rank test assumes paired differences The GRN contains multi-layer TF-TF-gene structure — the current GRouNdGAN version only supports bipartite GRNs http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies whether in silico TF knockout in GRouNdGAN-simulated cells significantly alters target-gene expression by applying two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests to matched perturbed-vs-control expression, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction over TF-gene edges. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48516-6
skills.summary: Quantifies whether in silico TF knockout in GRouNdGAN-simulated cells significantly alters target-gene expression by applying two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests to matched perturbed-vs-control expression, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction over TF-gene edges.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to predict whether TF knockout will change expression in real, non-simulated cells — GRouNdGAN is generative, not predictive, and would need retraining and a high-quality GRN plus data modalities such as scATAC-seq or TF ChIP-seq Perturbed and control cells are not matched (independently sampled), since the signed-rank test assumes paired differences The GRN contains multi-layer TF-TF-gene structure — the current GRouNdGAN version only supports bipartite GRNs

skills.description: Use when comparing a paired metric (e.g., recall of GTEx eQTL-supported enhancer-gene pairs) between two scoring methods measured on the same small set of units (four heart cell types plus K562) and a non-parametric paired significance test is needed.
skills.name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing Use when comparing a paired metric (e.g., recall of GTEx eQTL-supported enhancer-gene pairs) between two scoring methods measured on the same small set of units (four heart cell types plus K562) and a non-parametric paired significance test is needed. The samples are independent rather than paired across the same cell types — use an unpaired (Mann-Whitney) test instead More than two scoring methods must be compared simultaneously on the same units — a Friedman-type test or per-pair tests with correction are needed The comparison target is the interaction score distribution itself rather than a derived per-cell-type statistic like eQTL-pair recall http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test used to compare per-cell-type eQTL-pair recall between the gABC (adapted-activity, all-TSS) and regular ABC enhancer-gene scoring methods, yielding the headline result P ≈ 0.0005 that gABC recovers significantly more eQTL-supported enhancer-gene pairs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad062
skills.summary: Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test used to compare per-cell-type eQTL-pair recall between the gABC (adapted-activity, all-TSS) and regular ABC enhancer-gene scoring methods, yielding the headline result P ≈ 0.0005 that gABC recovers significantly more eQTL-supported enhancer-gene pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The samples are independent rather than paired across the same cell types — use an unpaired (Mann-Whitney) test instead More than two scoring methods must be compared simultaneously on the same units — a Friedman-type test or per-pair tests with correction are needed The comparison target is the interaction score distribution itself rather than a derived per-cell-type statistic like eQTL-pair recall

skills.name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing Use when comparing two methods evaluated on the same set of benchmark datasets and you need a paired, non-parametric significance test on per-dataset scores (e.g. mean ARIs of scISR 0.571 vs raw 0.504, MAGIC 0.461, scImpute 0.286, SAVER 0.423, scScope 0.165, scGNN 0.279). Scores are not paired by dataset (independent samples from different benchmark sets) — use an unpaired test instead Per-dataset score vectors are incomplete, so scISR and the comparator cannot be aligned one-to-one across the 25 datasets The claim being tested is a two-sided difference with no directional hypothesis — a one-sided test would overstate significance http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 One-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank testing on paired per-dataset performance scores (ARI, Purity Index) to statistically validate that scISR's subspace-regression imputation beats competing imputation methods and raw data across the 25 scRNA-seq benchmark datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-06500-4
skills.summary: One-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank testing on paired per-dataset performance scores (ARI, Purity Index) to statistically validate that scISR's subspace-regression imputation beats competing imputation methods and raw data across the 25 scRNA-seq benchmark datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Scores are not paired by dataset (independent samples from different benchmark sets) — use an unpaired test instead Per-dataset score vectors are incomplete, so scISR and the comparator cannot be aligned one-to-one across the 25 datasets The claim being tested is a two-sided difference with no directional hypothesis — a one-sided test would overstate significance

skills.description: Use when scTriangulate has produced per-cell winning annotations and raw winning clusters need filtering by winning fraction (win_fraction_cutoff) or minimum size (abs_thresh) before downstream analysis.

skills.search_text: winning-fraction-cluster-pruning Use when scTriangulate has produced per-cell winning annotations and raw winning clusters need filtering by winning fraction (win_fraction_cutoff) or minimum size (abs_thresh) before downstream analysis. When the analysis goal is a consensus/ensemble clustering rather than decision-level integration — ensemble approaches like ClusterEnsembles select the consensus instead of pruning by stability. When fewer than two conflicting annotation columns exist in adata.obs, since pruning operates on reconciled multi-annotation winning clusters. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Prunes unstable or undersized winning clusters produced by scTriangulate's Shapley-based cell assignment, then reclassifies their cells to a nearest-neighbor cluster label, yielding a cleaned final clustering solution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36016-y
skills.summary: Prunes unstable or undersized winning clusters produced by scTriangulate's Shapley-based cell assignment, then reclassifies their cells to a nearest-neighbor cluster label, yielding a cleaned final clustering solution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is a consensus/ensemble clustering rather than decision-level integration — ensemble approaches like ClusterEnsembles select the consensus instead of pruning by stability. When fewer than two conflicting annotation columns exist in adata.obs, since pruning operates on reconciled multi-annotation winning clusters.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking perturbation-prediction methods on multi-batch scRNA-seq data where the held-out matrix may differ in batch from the input, and you must separate condition-only accuracy from condition+batch accuracy.
skills.name: within-batch-versus-cross-batch-evaluation-design
skills.search_text: within-batch-versus-cross-batch-evaluation-design Use when benchmarking perturbation-prediction methods on multi-batch scRNA-seq data where the held-out matrix may differ in batch from the input, and you must separate condition-only accuracy from condition+batch accuracy. Each batch is measured under only one condition, so batch and condition effects cannot be disentangled and the cross-batch scenario is not meaningful All input and held-out matrices come from the same batch, in which case only the within-batch scenario applies and a batch-aware model offers no advantage The goal is batch effect removal or key gene detection rather than perturbation prediction accuracy benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 An evaluation design for perturbation prediction that scores each method twice: once for a within-batch scenario (condition effect only) and once for a cross-batch scenario (condition plus batch effect), to expose methods that fail to account for batch effects between input and held-out matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45227-w
skills.summary: An evaluation design for perturbation prediction that scores each method twice: once for a within-batch scenario (condition effect only) and once for a cross-batch scenario (condition plus batch effect), to expose methods that fail to account for batch effects between input and held-out matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Each batch is measured under only one condition, so batch and condition effects cannot be disentangled and the cross-batch scenario is not meaningful All input and held-out matrices come from the same batch, in which case only the within-batch scenario applies and a batch-aware model offers no advantage The goal is batch effect removal or key gene detection rather than perturbation prediction accuracy benchmarking

Expression data is transcriptome-only without paired ADT measurements — there are no measured protein levels to plot against Expression input is TPM/RPKM rather than UMI-based counts, which cTP-net cannot be applied to Cells are not of hematopoietic lineage — generalization of imputation was not tested outside immune cells http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Renders per-cell-type scatter plots of CITE-seq-measured versus imputed (cTP-net or Seurat v3) surface protein abundance to visually assess imputation fidelity within each PBMC cell type, reproducing Fig. 2b-c of the cTP-net paper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14391-0

skills.description: Use when building a predefined external gene-by-subtype centroid reference for PAM50-style classification of RNA-seq breast cancer samples, and you need the reference to be independent of the arbitrary composition of the training cohort.
skills.name: within-class-mean-averaging-across-cohorts
skills.search_text: within-class-mean-averaging-across-cohorts Use when building a predefined external gene-by-subtype centroid reference for PAM50-style classification of RNA-seq breast cancer samples, and you need the reference to be independent of the arbitrary composition of the training cohort. The goal is a single-sample classifier without any external reference (e.g. the paper's mLR approach reached 90% concordance with PAM50 'without need of reference sample') Input expression data are not normalized on the same platform/scale as the training cohorts (the authors applied AWCA separately to RNA-seq and to Affymetrix log2-transformed data such as GSE4922) A quick one-off within-cohort PAM50 run is acceptable and reference portability/reproducibility across cohorts is not a requirement http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs a cohort-composition-independent PAM50 subtype reference by computing per-gene within-class (subtype) mean expression in each training cohort and averaging those class means across cohorts — the 'average of within-class averages' (AWCA) step of the AWCA-PAM50 method. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-70832-2
skills.summary: Constructs a cohort-composition-independent PAM50 subtype reference by computing per-gene within-class (subtype) mean expression in each training cohort and averaging those class means across cohorts — the 'average of within-class averages' (AWCA) step of the AWCA-PAM50 method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a single-sample classifier without any external reference (e.g. the paper's mLR approach reached 90% concordance with PAM50 'without need of reference sample') Input expression data are not normalized on the same platform/scale as the training cohorts (the authors applied AWCA separately to RNA-seq and to Affymetrix log2-transformed data such as GSE4922) A quick one-off within-cohort PAM50 run is acceptable and reference portability/reproducibility across cohorts is not a requirement

skills.description: Use when one or more candidate spatial-domain clusterings of ST/Visium spots (e.g., Mclust automated scribbles or ScribbleDom model outputs over an alpha_options grid) must be ranked by a single scalar score in the absence of ground-truth labels for ARI.
skills.name: within-cluster-variance-penalty-computation
skills.search_text: within-cluster-variance-penalty-computation Use when one or more candidate spatial-domain clusterings of ST/Visium spots (e.g., Mclust automated scribbles or ScribbleDom model outputs over an alpha_options grid) must be ranked by a single scalar score in the absence of ground-truth labels for ARI. Ground-truth domain annotations are available and adjusted Rand index can be computed directly — use ARI-based evaluation instead of this proxy score. The input is not a spatial spot-level clustering with coordinates (e.g., non-spatial single-cell clusters), since the Potts-model neighborhood term is undefined. Raw count matrices have not yet been preprocessed into PCs of the top 2000 highly variable genes — run the preprocessing step first. Computes ScribbleDom's ARI-independent goodness score v(y,Cα) = q(y,Cα)·∏ᵢ p(yᵢ|Cᵢα)·p(Cᵢα), which multiplies the Gaussian likelihood of spot PCs under their assigned cluster, a Potts-model prior over the spot neighborhood graph (gamma=2 for ST, gamma=3 for Visium), and a quasi-likelihood penalty q(y,Cα) on within-cluster PC variance (lambda=100), so optimal hyperparameters can be chosen without manual annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad594
skills.summary: Computes ScribbleDom's ARI-independent goodness score v(y,Cα) = q(y,Cα)·∏ᵢ p(yᵢ|Cᵢα)·p(Cᵢα), which multiplies the Gaussian likelihood of spot PCs under their assigned cluster, a Potts-model prior over the spot neighborhood graph (gamma=2 for ST, gamma=3 for Visium), and a quasi-likelihood penalty q(y,Cα) on within-cluster PC variance (lambda=100), so optimal hyperparameters can be chosen without manual annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Ground-truth domain annotations are available and adjusted Rand index can be computed directly — use ARI-based evaluation instead of this proxy score. The input is not a spatial spot-level clustering with coordinates (e.g., non-spatial single-cell clusters), since the Potts-model neighborhood term is undefined. Raw count matrices have not yet been preprocessed into PCs of the top 2000 highly variable genes — run the preprocessing step first.

skills.description: Use when upregulated genes from a clone-versus-normal differential expression comparison (e.g., Clone 1 vs Normal in XClone-annotated TNBC1 scRNA-seq data) need to be tested for significant Wnt-pathway over-representation via an over-representation test.
skills.name: wnt-pathway-overrepresentation-enrichment
skills.search_text: wnt-pathway-overrepresentation-enrichment Use when upregulated genes from a clone-versus-normal differential expression comparison (e.g., Clone 1 vs Normal in XClone-annotated TNBC1 scRNA-seq data) need to be tested for significant Wnt-pathway over-representation via an over-representation test. skills.summary: Over-representation test of the Wnt signaling pathway on upregulated Clone 1 differentially expressed genes in the TNBC1 sample, following stratification of DEGs by XClone-detected LOH versus non-LOH regions. skills.description: Use when the goal is to detect subtype-downregulated genes (SDG) from batch-corrected gene-by-sample expression data — i.e., genes with near-zero mean expression in exactly one subtype and elevated expression in every other subtype.
skills.name: xor-basis-cosine-statistic-computation
skills.search_text: xor-basis-cosine-statistic-computation Use when the goal is to detect subtype-downregulated genes (SDG) from batch-corrected gene-by-sample expression data — i.e., genes with near-zero mean expression in exactly one subtype and elevated expression in every other subtype. When the target is subtype-enriched marker genes (upregulated in one subtype) — use the standard COT ideal-MG reference vector instead of the XOR variant When the input matrix is not batch-corrected — COT explicitly requires batch-corrected input When only a very small number of genes are being tested and p-value estimation is required — COT cannot calculate p-values due to limited gene numbers in that case http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A modification of the COT cosine-based one-sample test in which the ideal-MG reference vector is replaced by an exclusive disjunction (XOR) with 1, so the reference is 0 in exactly one subtype and 1 in all others. This reorients the statistic to detect subtype-downregulated genes (SDG) — genes silent only in a given subtype but expressed in all others — with the resulting statistic bounded as 1/(K-1) < t_COT(i) < 1. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac037
skills.summary: A modification of the COT cosine-based one-sample test in which the ideal-MG reference vector is replaced by an exclusive disjunction (XOR) with 1, so the reference is 0 in exactly one subtype and 1 in all others. This reorients the statistic to detect subtype-downregulated genes (SDG) — genes silent only in a given subtype but expressed in all others — with the resulting statistic bounded as 1/(K-1) < t_COT(i) < 1.

skills.name: zdwi-utr-usage-statistical-testing
skills.search_text: zdwi-utr-usage-statistical-testing Use when scRNA-seq data has been quantified at 3'UTR isoform level (e.g. SingleCellExperiment from scUTRquant with the utrome_hg38_v1 target) and you need to test which genes show significant 3'UTR shortening/lengthening per condition or perturbation relative to controls. skills.description: Use when integrating multiple zebrafish embryo scRNA-seq time-course datasets (e.g., Wagner et al. and Farrell et al.) against an end-point reference marker list to recover lineage emergence timings across developmental stages.
skills.name: zebrafish-embryo-lineage-annotation
skills.search_text: zebrafish-embryo-lineage-annotation Use when integrating multiple zebrafish embryo scRNA-seq time-course datasets (e.g., Wagner et al. and Farrell et al.) against an end-point reference marker list to recover lineage emergence timings across developmental stages. The query data contains cell types not present in the end-point reference — MASI alone cannot annotate unseen cell types and would need to be combined with SCCAF to identify subtypes. The goal is batch-corrected latent-space integration (e.g., Seurat, Harmony, LIGER) rather than fast marker-based label transfer — MASI deliberately skips HVG selection and model training. No high-quality reference with cell-type markers at matching resolution is available, since MASI annotation accuracy depends on reference quality. http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Reproduce zebrafish embryo lineage-emergence timings by integrating Wagner et al. and Farrell et al. datasets with MASI's marker-based cell-type scoring and MACA label transfer, using end-point zebrafish data as the reference. Demonstrates that a model-free marker approach recovers germline at 3 hpf, epidermis at 3 hpf, notochord around 7 hpf, and non-neural ectoderm separation at 12 hpf (Fig. 1b–d). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04820-3
skills.summary: Reproduce zebrafish embryo lineage-emergence timings by integrating Wagner et al. and Farrell et al. datasets with MASI's marker-based cell-type scoring and MACA label transfer, using end-point zebrafish data as the reference. Demonstrates that a model-free marker approach recovers germline at 3 hpf, epidermis at 3 hpf, notochord around 7 hpf, and non-neural ectoderm separation at 12 hpf (Fig. 1b–d).

skills.description: Use when modeling continuous scRNA-seq expression of a target gene as a mixture over candidate TF logic combinations, where scRNA-seq dropouts require a point mass at zero and per-rule likelihoods (as in Loregic/LogicTRN) would be computationally prohibitive.
skills.name: zero-inflated-mixture-likelihood-fitting
skills.search_text: zero-inflated-mixture-likelihood-fitting Use when modeling continuous scRNA-seq expression of a target gene as a mixture over candidate TF logic combinations, where scRNA-seq dropouts require a point mass at zero and per-rule likelihoods (as in Loregic/LogicTRN) would be computationally prohibitive. The candidate TF subset exceeds ~5 regulators (k > 5), where the 2^k mixture and EM fitting overfit — the paper states decoding high-order logic with >5 regulators 'remains challenging, where overfitting is a major concern' The gene set is large-scale without prior TF selection — scGATE is applicable only to a small (<200) subset of genes with a refined candidate TF list based on external hints Data are pseudotime-sorted along differentiation trajectories or require temporal delay modeling — scGATE does not yet handle these http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 scGATE's core statistical routine: instead of computing a separate likelihood for each Boolean rule (AND, OR, XOR), it fits a zero-inflated mixture density — a point mass at zero for dropouts plus a normal density centered on each TF combination's Hill-transformed output — to a target gene's scRNA-seq profile, then estimates prior weights w_v over the 2^k logic combinations by EM and selects the gate a posteriori via a Bayes factor. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180

skills.description: Use when comparing single-cell Hi-C normalized read counts between two conditions (rows = bin pairs, columns = cells) and you need statistically principled DCI calls that handle the excessive zeros typical of scHi-C data.
skills.name: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-regression
skills.search_text: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-regression Use when comparing single-cell Hi-C normalized read counts between two conditions (rows = bin pairs, columns = cells) and you need statistically principled DCI calls that handle the excessive zeros typical of scHi-C data. The input is raw (unnormalized) scHi-C data — apply the scHiCDiff.norm normalization using local features (effective length, GC content, mappability) first, since scHiCDiff.ZINB expects normalized read counts Only bulk Hi-C data without excessive zeros is available — the article states negative binomial (NB) is the common assumption for bulk Hi-C, while ZINB is 'specially designated for the interaction comparison at single-cell level' No distributional assumptions can be justified — the non-parametric KS or CVM tests (scHiCDiff.KS / scHiCDiff.CVM) are designed for detecting DCIs 'without any assumption on data distribution' http://edamontology.org/topic_0611 A parametric likelihood-ratio-test DCI detector from the scHiCDiff R package that fits zero-inflated negative binomial (mu, theta, pi) regression models per condition to single-cell Hi-C bin-pair count matrices and calls differential chromatin interactions. It is designed for single-cell interaction comparison because it explicitly accounts for excessive zeros in scHi-C counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad625
skills.summary: A parametric likelihood-ratio-test DCI detector from the scHiCDiff R package that fits zero-inflated negative binomial (mu, theta, pi) regression models per condition to single-cell Hi-C bin-pair count matrices and calls differential chromatin interactions. It is designed for single-cell interaction comparison because it explicitly accounts for excessive zeros in scHi-C counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw (unnormalized) scHi-C data — apply the scHiCDiff.norm normalization using local features (effective length, GC content, mappability) first, since scHiCDiff.ZINB expects normalized read counts Only bulk Hi-C data without excessive zeros is available — the article states negative binomial (NB) is the common assumption for bulk Hi-C, while ZINB is 'specially designated for the interaction comparison at single-cell level' No distributional assumptions can be justified — the non-parametric KS or CVM tests (scHiCDiff.KS / scHiCDiff.CVM) are designed for detecting DCIs 'without any assumption on data distribution'

skills.description: Use when a task requires implementing or refitting a zero-inflated negative binomial regression to distinguish true fusion candidates from background technical chimeric-read noise in per-cell scRNA-seq candidate feature tables with expression and GC-content covariates.
skills.name: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-regression-implementation
skills.search_text: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-regression-implementation Use when a task requires implementing or refitting a zero-inflated negative binomial regression to distinguish true fusion candidates from background technical chimeric-read noise in per-cell scRNA-seq candidate feature tables with expression and GC-content covariates. Input data are 10X droplet-based scRNA-seq reads — scFusion's pipeline (and thus this statistical step) targets Smart-Seq data with *_1.fastq/*_2.fastq files Input is already a scored candidate list with p-values/FDR, or bulk RNA-seq data where the per-cell zero-inflation (dropout) component and joint multi-cell analysis do not apply The goal is candidate fusion calling from raw reads (alignment, chimera detection) rather than statistical significance testing of an existing candidate feature table http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstruction of scFusion's statistical significance model for scRNA-seq gene fusion candidates: a zero-inflated negative binomial regression in which supporting chimeric read counts are modeled with a logit link for the zero-inflation (dropout) component and a log link for the count-mean component, using linear gene-expression covariates and spline terms for local GC content, followed by resampling-based p-values and FDR control. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28661-6
skills.summary: Reconstruction of scFusion's statistical significance model for scRNA-seq gene fusion candidates: a zero-inflated negative binomial regression in which supporting chimeric read counts are modeled with a logit link for the zero-inflation (dropout) component and a log link for the count-mean component, using linear gene-expression covariates and spline terms for local GC content, followed by resampling-based p-values and FDR control.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are 10X droplet-based scRNA-seq reads — scFusion's pipeline (and thus this statistical step) targets Smart-Seq data with *_1.fastq/*_2.fastq files Input is already a scored candidate list with p-values/FDR, or bulk RNA-seq data where the per-cell zero-inflation (dropout) component and joint multi-cell analysis do not apply The goal is candidate fusion calling from raw reads (alignment, chimera detection) rather than statistical significance testing of an existing candidate feature table

skills.search_text: zero-inflated-poisson-count-downsampling Use when you need to synthetically downsample scRNA-seq count profiles to create a degraded input (with a known ground-truth full-depth counterpart) for benchmarking denoising methods such as scPRINT, MAGIC, or KNNsmoothing2. When the goal is gene network inference rather than denoising benchmarking — scPRINT's GN inference benchmarks (BeeLine, MCalla et al., gwps K562) do not use this downsampling step When you already hold matched low-depth and high-depth measurements of the same cells — an empirical degradation control is preferable to simulated downsampling When the input data are not raw integer counts (e.g. normalized or log-transformed matrices) — the zero-inflated Poisson sampling of reads per gene assumes raw counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3934 A controlled transcript-count perturbation procedure from the scPRINT paper that removes a defined fraction of counts per cell (e.g. 70%) using a zero-inflated Poisson model, splitting drops between Poisson-sampled reads per gene and complete gene dropouts.
