It provides a reproducible degradation step for evaluating denoising methods against true full-depth profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is gene network inference rather than denoising benchmarking — scPRINT's GN inference benchmarks (BeeLine, MCalla et al., gwps K562) do not use this downsampling step When you already hold matched low-depth and high-depth measurements of the same cells — an empirical degradation control is preferable to simulated downsampling When the input data are not raw integer counts (e.g. normalized or log-transformed matrices) — the zero-inflated Poisson sampling of reads per gene assumes raw counts

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq normalized expression matrix shows extreme sparsity/dropout (zeros can exceed 90% with droplet techniques) and you need marker-gene recovery that preserves biological zeros at exactly zero.
skills.name: zero-preserving-low-rank-matrix-imputation
skills.search_text: zero-preserving-low-rank-matrix-imputation Use when a scRNA-seq normalized expression matrix shows extreme sparsity/dropout (zeros can exceed 90% with droplet techniques) and you need marker-gene recovery that preserves biological zeros at exactly zero. When all zeros should be treated as missing data — methods like DCA or MAGIC fill every entry, whereas ALRA deliberately keeps true biological zeros at zero When the input is not a normalized gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix (ALRA assumes non-negativity, low-rank structure, and many biological zeros) When you need only one of the alternate imputers (SAVER, scImpute) — note the article reports those can be extremely slow on datasets over 100,000 cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 ALRA (Adaptively thresholded Low-Rank Approximation) imputes technical (false) zeros in scRNA-seq count matrices via randomized-SVD low-rank approximation followed by per-gene adaptive thresholding, restoring true biological zeros at exactly zero. It recovers marker-gene expression (e.g., NCAM1, CR2) that dropout hides in raw data while remaining fast on very large datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27729-z
skills.summary: ALRA (Adaptively thresholded Low-Rank Approximation) imputes technical (false) zeros in scRNA-seq count matrices via randomized-SVD low-rank approximation followed by per-gene adaptive thresholding, restoring true biological zeros at exactly zero. It recovers marker-gene expression (e.g., NCAM1, CR2) that dropout hides in raw data while remaining fast on very large datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When all zeros should be treated as missing data — methods like DCA or MAGIC fill every entry, whereas ALRA deliberately keeps true biological zeros at zero When the input is not a normalized gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix (ALRA assumes non-negativity, low-rank structure, and many biological zeros) When you need only one of the alternate imputers (SAVER, scImpute) — note the article reports those can be extremely slow on datasets over 100,000 cells

skills.description: Use when a pretrained single-cell embedding model (e.g. scETM trained on MousePancreas.h5ad) must be applied to an aligned target dataset without retraining, and clustering quality of the transferred embeddings must be benchmarked.
skills.name: zero-shot-cell-embedding-transfer
skills.search_text: zero-shot-cell-embedding-transfer Use when a pretrained single-cell embedding model (e.g. scETM trained on MousePancreas.h5ad) must be applied to an aligned target dataset without retraining, and clustering quality of the transferred embeddings must be benchmarked. Source and target datasets are unaligned (different gene sets): prepare_for_transfer discards source-unique-gene parameters and the model usually requires fine-tuning before target evaluation, so pure zero-shot transfer is not appropriate. The goal is de novo clustering of a single dataset rather than benchmarking transferability across datasets — a standard single-dataset scETM training/evaluation workflow is the right choice. The model must correct multiple categorical batch variables or integrate multi-omic data (scRNA-seq + protein/scATAC-seq): the article states these extensions are not yet implemented. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reproduce scETM's zero-shot cross-tissue and cross-species transfer-learning evaluation (Fig 4): train the scETM encoder on a source AnnData dataset, apply the frozen model to a target dataset without retraining, and score transfer quality against scVI and scVI-LD using ARI and kBET. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25534-2
skills.summary: Reproduce scETM's zero-shot cross-tissue and cross-species transfer-learning evaluation (Fig 4): train the scETM encoder on a source AnnData dataset, apply the frozen model to a target dataset without retraining, and score transfer quality against scVI and scVI-LD using ARI and kBET.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Source and target datasets are unaligned (different gene sets): prepare_for_transfer discards source-unique-gene parameters and the model usually requires fine-tuning before target evaluation, so pure zero-shot transfer is not appropriate. The goal is de novo clustering of a single dataset rather than benchmarking transferability across datasets — a standard single-dataset scETM training/evaluation workflow is the right choice. The model must correct multiple categorical batch variables or integrate multi-omic data (scRNA-seq + protein/scATAC-seq): the article states these extensions are not yet implemented.

The evaluation target is denoising or cell label prediction rather than batch effect correction measured by scIB avgBIO. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmark single-cell foundation models (scPRINT, scGPT, Geneformer, scFoundation) on batch effect correction by computing zero-shot cell embeddings and scoring them with the scIB aggregated avgBIO metric on the human pancreas and lung open-problems datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-58699-1

The evaluation target is denoising or cell label prediction rather than batch effect correction measured by scIB avgBIO.

skills.search_text: zga-gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when a curated list of ligand-receptor pair genes (e.g. eLRs from early embryo scRNA-seq analysis) must be validated against reference gene sets (essential, housekeeping, ZGA) with over-representation tests. skills.description: Use when you have an scRNA-seq dataset plus a marker gene set defining expected cell types, and you need a low-dimensional marker-gene embedding to seed pseudo-labels and pairwise constraints for constrained clustering.
skills.name: zifa-latent-embedding-of-marker-genes
skills.search_text: zifa-latent-embedding-of-marker-genes Use when you have an scRNA-seq dataset plus a marker gene set defining expected cell types, and you need a low-dimensional marker-gene embedding to seed pseudo-labels and pairwise constraints for constrained clustering. The analysis goal is purely unsupervised clustering with no marker gene set or domain knowledge available to define constraints (the article notes existing algorithms 'only support clustering in an unsupervised fashion' and scDCC's value comes from integrating prior information). skills.search_text: zinq-reconstruction-loss-optimization Use when integrating scRNA-seq batches where some (10/20/50%) or all cell type labels are available and the latent embedding must be guided by a cell type classifier loss on top of an adversarial VAE ELBO. No cell type annotations are available for any cells — use the unsupervised scDREAMER backbone instead of scDREAMER-Sup The number of batches is unknown and cannot be supplied — the model assumes prior knowledge of the number of batches Multiomic (e.g. RNA + ATAC) datasets — the authors state the multiomic extension is not yet implemented and is planned future work http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstructs the scDREAMER-Sup objective: an adversarial VAE backbone whose ZINB decoder reconstruction and KL terms are maximized via an extended ELBO, augmented with a second VAE (AY = {Ey, Dy}) and a feed-forward cell type classifier C trained by cross-entropy on available annotations. This couples latent-space batch correction with annotation-guided (supervised/semi-supervised) inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43590-8
skills.summary: Reconstructs the scDREAMER-Sup objective: an adversarial VAE backbone whose ZINB decoder reconstruction and KL terms are maximized via an extended ELBO, augmented with a second VAE (AY = {Ey, Dy}) and a feed-forward cell type classifier C trained by cross-entropy on available annotations. This couples latent-space batch correction with annotation-guided (supervised/semi-supervised) inference.

Other tools, such as CellChat, allow the generation of scores at the signaling pathway level instead of LR pairs. Here we develop CellChat, an open source R package (https://github.com/sqjin/CellChat) to infer, visualize and analyze intercellular communications from scRNA-seq data. CellChat is an R package designed for inference, analysis, and visualization of cell-cell communication from single-cell and spatially resolved transcriptomics. CellChat v1/v2 R package can be easily installed from Github using devtools: CellChat v1/v2 R package can be easily installed from Github using devtools CellChat R package is a versatile and easy-to-use toolkit for inferring, analyzing and visualizing cell–cell communication from any given scRNA-seq data. We used CellChat to detect LRI among different tissues of the SC mouse embryo data using gene expression only. devtools::install_github("sqjin/CellChat") either CCI data generated by InterCellar-supported tools (CellChat12, CellPhoneDB11, ICELLNET15, or SingleCellSignalR16) sqjin/CellChat CellChat#14CellChatDB(1) Probability—based on the expression of differentially expressed transmitter and receiver genes and their mediators Considering that [CellChatDB](https://github.com/sqjin/CellChat) L-R database contains both human and mouse ligand-receptor information many methods have been developed for cell-cell communication, such as CellPhoneDB,7 CellChat,4 and iTALK.8 computational methods have been developed for inferring cell-cell communication networks from coordinated expressions of ligand-receptor interaction pairs6–12 such as CellChat9 library(CellChat) library(NeuronChat)
library(CellChat) We conducted cell-cell interaction analyses on both real-profiled and semi-profiled datasets using the R package CellChat28. the interaction between CAF1 and myeloid cells by CellPhoneDB, NicheNet, CellChat, and InterCellDB was analyzed.
